This approach is used to collect a dataset of 25413 samples to finetune an object detection and a segmentation model, which are combined to assign detected cards to game-relevant zones and infer the game state. When evaluated on a real NICO humanoid robot, our pipeline achieves an F1-score of 0.906 for card-to-zone assignment, thus providing the perceptual foundation for a robot that can autonomously play Chef's Hat against human players.
2611.15524.comment: Presented at the Dungeons, Neurons, and Dialogues workshop (DnD-SIDC 2026) at ICANN 2026, https://dnd-sidc.github.io/

llm.title_ja: テーブルの読み取り：シェフズハットカードゲームのためのSim-to-Realゲーム状態検出
llm.tldr_ja: 実世界のアノテーションコストが高いゲームオブジェクトの認識課題に対し、完全に自動化された合成データ収集パイプラインとドメインランダム化を開発し、NICOヒューマノイドロボットの実機で高いF1スコアを達成した。
llm.problem: 高価な実世界アノテーションを必要とする、類似したゲームオブジェクトの正確な検出。
llm.method: 3D座標の再投影を用いた完全自動の合成データ収集とドメインランダム化によるSim-to-Real学習。
llm.result: 実機のNICOヒューマノイドロボットにおいて、カードとゾーンの割り当てで0.906のF1スコアを達成。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット
テーブルトップゲーム

2611.15491.title: What Makes a VLA Reactive? A Study of Execution Strategies for Dynamic Manipulation
2611.15491.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models predict chunks of future actions, and when objects move, those chunks go stale before they are executed. We study what makes a pretrained VLA reactive, using \pihalf{} on two dynamic simulation benchmarks and three real-robot tasks. We vary the prediction and execution horizons, compare synchronous and asynchronous inference, test methods that deliver actions sooner or keep successive chunks continuous, and adapt the policy with motion cues and latent-space reinforcement learning. The best prediction horizon is about one second, and the best execution horizon depends on the checkpoint. Short horizons help more with asynchronous execution, and methods that keep the trajectory continuous outperform those that only reduce latency. Adapting the policy repairs targeted failures, but on the conveyor task changing the execution horizon gained as much. Reactivity depends on the execution pipeline as much as on the policy, so both should be evaluated together.
2611.15491.comment: 13 pages, 7 figures, Efficient Foundation Models for Real-Time Embodied AI, CoRL 2026 Workshop

2611.15490.title: ActionCodec2: A Streaming Action Tokenizer
2611.15490.abstract: Most action tokenizers for autoregressive vision language action (VLA) models compress motion into chunks that must be decoded in full before their actions become executable. We introduce ActionCodec2, a non-neural streaming tokenizer that releases actions incrementally while keeping trajectory reconstruction error within a prescribed tolerance. Its encoder quantizes each step relative to the decoder's reconstructed state, so the selected motion primitive corrects residual error rather than allowing errors from independently quantized increments to accumulate. Finding the smallest such primitive set is a geometric covering problem; we derive the exact minimum for translation and constant-factor-tight bounds for rotation. Set-BPE then losslessly merges co-occurring primitive symbols across coordinates and neighboring steps, without a fixed coordinate ordering. A universal version fitted on 20k hours of data from 24 embodiments averages 8.8 tokens per second for 15 Hz end-effector motion on this corpus. With the same VLA backbone, ActionCodec2 outperforms the compared tokenizers on three simulation benchmarks and in zero-shot real-robot evaluation. Its streaming representation allows policies to incorporate state feedback within an action chunk, substantially improving performance over open-loop execution under randomized dynamics, external disturbances, and moving objects. The same tokens also can serve as a direct control interface for VLM agents, which compose successful action sequences into reusable macros. These agent-built macros reduce control decisions and thinking-token usage across attempts and transfer to a held-out task. More results are available at https://zibindong.github.io/actioncodec2-page/

llm.title_ja: ActionCodec2：ストリーミング行動トークナイザー
llm.tldr_ja: 誤差の蓄積を防ぎつつ軌道再構成誤差を許容範囲内に抑えながら段階的に行動を出力する非神経ストリーミングトークナイザー「ActionCodec2」を提案し、シミュレーションと実機で優れた性能を示した。
llm.problem: 従来の行動トークナイザーは完全なデコードを必要とし、動的環境での応答性が低いこと。
llm.method: 状態に対する相対量子化、幾何学的被覆問題としての最小プリミティブ集合の導出、Set-BPEによるマージを行う非神経ストリーミングトークナイザーの開発。
llm.result: 複数のシミュレーションおよびゼロショット実機評価において既存のトークナイザーを上回る性能を達成した。

2611.15488.title: FloCOS: Predicting Compact Forward Occupancy Sets of Surrounding Vehicles via Conditional Flow Matching
2611.15488.abstract: Existing methods for predicting surrounding vehicles' forward occupancy may under-approximate the ground-truth occupancy, exposing the ego vehicle to collision risk, or produce overly conservative regions that unnecessarily restrict feasible space and cause planning failures. To address these issues, we propose FloCOS, a conditional flow-matching framework that predicts compact forward occupancy sets with high occupancy coverage. FloCOS represents the forward occupancy set as a time-varying union of half-space convex polygons parameterized by temporal basis coefficients. Conditional flow matching captures the conditional distribution of these coefficients to govern the temporal evolution of the convex components, trained under coverage and union-area losses that penalize missed occupancy and excess area. For downstream trajectory optimization, the predicted nonconvex union is directly incorporated into hyperplane-based collision-avoidance constraints. Evaluations on the Waymo Open Motion Dataset show that FloCOS generates compact forward occupancy sets with high coverage and achieves a higher interaction completion rate than evaluated baselines. Real-world vehicle experiments further confirm its ability to support collision-free planning in interactive scenarios.

llm.title_ja: FloCOS：条件付きフローマッチングによる周辺車両のコンパクトな前方占有集合の予測
llm.tldr_ja: 周辺車両の前方占有を高精度かつコンパクトに予測する条件付きフローマッチングフレームワーク「FloCOS」を提案し、衝突回避制約を考慮した安全な計画を実現した。
llm.problem: 既存の予測手法が過小評価による衝突リスクや、過度に保守的な領域による計画失敗を引き起こすこと。
llm.method: 時間的基底係数でパラメータ化された半空間凸多角形の時間変化する和集合として前方占有集合を表現し、条件付きフローマッチングで予測する。
llm.result: Waymo Open Motion Datasetにおいて高い網羅率とコンパクトな占有集合生成を実現し、インタラクティブなシナリオで衝突回避計画を実証した。

2611.15443.title: SPARC: RoboCup Standard Platform for Autonomous Rescue Competition with Initial Datasets, Software, and Simulation Environments
2611.15443.abstract: The RoboCup Standard Platform for Autonomous Rescue Competition (SPARC) is a new competition under development of the RoboCup Rescue Robot League that uses the Unitree A2-W as a common robot platform. SPARC aims to make research on artificial intelligence for autonomous rescue robots accessible to a broader research community, including groups without expertise in developing and maintaining custom robot hardware. By providing a capable standard platform and established benchmark environments, researchers can focus on autonomous navigation, perception, manipulation, and embodied AI for challenging disaster-response scenarios. This paper introduces the SPARC competition, its benchmark environment, and the Unitree A2-W standard platform. Furthermore, we present the first open SPARC datasets collected during the IEEE ICRA 2026 Legged Robot Challenges and RoboCup Rescue 2026, release an open-source software stack for autonomous navigation, and provide initial simulation assets representing RoboCup Rescue test environments. Together, these resources aim to lower the barrier to entry for autonomous rescue robotics and facilitate reproducible research and collaborative development on a common hardware platform.

llm.title_ja: SPARC：初期データセット、ソフトウェア、シミュレーション環境を備えた自律型レスキュー競技のためのRoboCup標準プラットフォーム
llm.tldr_ja: 災害対応シナリオにおける自律型レスキューロボットの研究を促進するため、Unitree A2-Wを共通プラットフォームに採用した新しいRoboCup競技「SPARC」の概要、データセット、シミュレーション環境を公開した。
llm.problem: 自律型レスキューロボット用AIの研究において、カスタムハードウェア開発の敷居が高いこと。
llm.method: Unitree A2-Wを共通標準プラットフォームとし、オープンソースのナビゲーション用ソフトウェアや初期データセット、シミュレーション環境を提供。
llm.result: 研究の参入障壁を下げ、共通ハードウェアプラットフォーム上での再現可能な研究と協調的開発を促進する基盤を構築した。
keywords_ja: 標準プラットフォーム

2611.15429.title: IncR-3DSGG: Incremental Posed RGB Image Based 3D Scene Graph Generation via Privileged Depth Supervision
2611.15429.abstract: Scene graphs provide a compact, structured representation of environments by capturing objects and their spatial or semantic relationships in a form suitable for embodied agents. Existing 3D scene graph generation methods often rely on depth sensing at inference, either to associate object instances across views via point cloud overlap or to compute inter-object relations from geometric cues, limiting deployment to platforms with depth sensors. We propose IncR-3DSGG, which builds 3D scene graphs incrementally from posed\footnote{RGB images with camera extrinsics estimated by an off-the-shelf visual SLAM system.} RGB images, eliminating the use of depth sensors at inference. Our method leverages a Parametric Relation Predictor (PRP) that learns to estimate pairwise distances and relative angles between objects from 2D visual features and 2D geometric cues, using 3D geometric supervision available only during training. These learned pairwise measurements are fused across views through Pose Graph Optimization (PGO)~\cite{grisetti2010tutorial} to recover metrically grounded 3D object positions and build a globally consistent 3D scene graph incrementally. On the real-world 3RScan~\cite{wald2019rio} dataset, our method attains $52.2$ mean object recall and $30.8$ mean predicate recall under the 3DSSG~\cite{wald2020learning} evaluation protocol, against $27.0$ and $17.6$ for MonoSSG~\cite{wu2023incremental}, while using no depth or reconstructed geometry at inference. This shows that relations and metrically grounded 3D object representations can be predicted from posed RGB images alone.

llm.title_ja: IncR-3DSGG：特権的深度教師信号に基づく姿勢付きRGB画像からのインクリメンタル3Dシーングラフ生成
llm.tldr_ja: 推論時に深度センサーを使用せず、姿勢付きRGB画像のみからグローバルに一貫した3Dシーングラフをインクリメンタルに構築する手法「IncR-3DSGG」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の3Dシーングラフ生成手法が推論時の深度センシングに依存しており、適用プラットフォームが制限されること。
llm.method: 2Dビジュアル・幾何学的特徴から物体の相対関係を予測するPRPモデルを用い、ポーズグラフ最適化により複数視点の測定値を統合する。
llm.result: 3RScanデータセットにおいて、推論時に深度情報を用いずに既存のインクリメンタル手法を大きく上回るオブジェクトおよび述語の平均リコールを達成した。

2611.15389.title: A physics-constrained deep reinforcement learning method for autonomous mission planning of Titan deep space probes
2611.15389.abstract: Titan is a compelling target for future deep space exploration, while its extreme Earth-Titan distance and complex environment make continuous ground-in-the-loop planning impractical. Existing planning methods, primarily developed for Earth-observation scenarios, have limited generalizability to uncertain deep space conditions and adaptability to time-varying mission states. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physics-constrained maskable proximal policy optimization (PCM-PPO) method for Titan autonomous mission planning. A Titan-specific discrete-time Markov decision process is established to characterize mission feasibility and resource constraints. A system dynamics and geometric model is incorporated to enhance physical representation, including central gravity, J2 perturbation, third-body attraction, and downlink occultation. To accommodate opportunity targets under a bounded action dimension, PCM-PPO organizes predefined and opportunity targets through a fixed-capacity target pool and represents the mission state with a target-wise state matrix and a global state vector. A physics-constrained action mask constructs an admissible decision domain from current mission states, guiding policy learning toward physically executable decisions and avoiding infeasible exploration. An integrated training strategy facilitates policy optimization under coupled constraints. Comparative, ablation, and uncertainty experiments validate the effectiveness of PCM-PPO. PCM-PPO provides a feasible and interpretable scheme for autonomous mission planning of Titan deep space probes.

llm.title_ja: タイタン深宇宙探査機の自律ミッション計画に向けた物理制約付き深層強化学習手法
llm.tldr_ja: 不確実な深宇宙環境や変動するミッション状態に適応するため、物理制約とマスク付きPPOを組み合わせたタイタン探査機向けの自律ミッション計画手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 地球とタイタン間の極端な通信遅延と複雑な環境により、従来の地球観測用計画手法が汎用性や適応性を欠くこと。
llm.method: タイタン特有のMDPを構築し、システムダイナミクスを組み込んだ物理制約付きマスク可能近傍政策最適化（PCM-PPO）を提案。
llm.result: 比較実験、アブレーション実験、不確実性実験により、タイタン深宇宙探査機の自律ミッション計画における有効性と解釈可能性を実証した。

2611.15386.title: Actuation and Control of Passive Tendon-Driven Soft Extensions Through Rigid Manipulator Motion
2611.15386.abstract: Industrial manipulators offer reach and precision but can damage nearby structures in confined spaces. Soft robots provide compliant contact but typically have limited reach. Rigid-soft systems combine their advantages, although they often require dedicated actuation and control hardware. We propose actuating a passive tendon-driven soft extension through manipulator joint motion. As the robot moves, the exterior spans of tendons anchored to upstream links change, altering tendon tension and deforming the extension. Inspection through narrow apertures, for example, constrains the motion of the end effector (EE). We develop a controller that regulates the soft tip while preserving such EE constraints. A differential model separates rigid transport from soft deformation, combining analytic arm and tendon kinematics with a locally identified span-to-deformation map. We also derive a local upper bound on the number of independent deformation directions transmitted by the tendons under the EE constraint, and conditions for the exponential convergence of the tip error. A quadratic program with control barrier functions imposes obstacle clearance, fulcrum limits, and model-validity conditions. Simulations and real experiments show tip and shape regulation under free, position-constrained, and fulcrum-constrained EE motion.
2611.15386.comment: 16 pages, 12 figures. Soon to be submitted to the IEEE Transactions on Robotics. Code: https://github.com/nachocz/passive_soft_extension_control. Interactive pages and video: https://ignaciocuiral.com/passive_soft_extension_control/

llm.title_ja: 剛体マニピュレータの動きを通じた受動腱駆動型ソフトエクステンションの駆動と制御
llm.tldr_ja: 閉じた狭い空間での安全な作業のため、マニピュレータの関節運動を利用して受動的な腱駆動ソフトエクステンションを駆動・制御する新しいコントローラーを開発した。
llm.problem: 産業用マニピュレータは到達性と精度に優れるが狭所で構造物を損傷しやすく、ソフトロボットは到達性が限られること。
llm.method: 剛体の輸送運動とソフトな変形を分離する差動モデルを構築し、制御バリア関数付き二次計画法を用いて障害物回避や制約を課す。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機実験により、自由状態および位置・支点制約下での先端と形状の制御を実証した。

2611.15381.title: Low-Cost Mobile Bimanual Manipulation for Long-Horizon Toilet Cleaning
2611.15381.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising capabilities for robot manipulation, but their performance on accessible mobile bimanual platforms remains underexplored. We present a low-cost and reproducible mobile bimanual platform integrating two LeRobot SO-101 manipulators with a TurtleBot 4 and a LeRobot-ROS 2 software stack. Using long-horizon toilet cleaning as a case study, we collect 250 real-world demonstrations and evaluate $π_0$, $π_{0.5}$, SmolVLA, and GR00T under the same embodiment and task conditions. We further evaluate variants using SARM-derived task-progress signals and short-term MEM observation history. Among the evaluated models, $π_0$ performs best, achieving 60% strict and 70% relaxed autonomous success, increasing to 90% with limited human intervention. In contrast, the evaluated progress- and memory-augmented variants do not improve their corresponding baselines. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of long-horizon mobile bimanual manipulation on accessible hardware while highlighting remaining challenges in reliable VLA deployment. Project website: https://so101-turtlebot4.github.io/mobile-bimanual-cleaning/

llm.title_ja: 長時間にわたるトイレ掃除のための低コストモバイル両腕マニピュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: LeRobotマニピュレータとTurtleBot 4を統合した低コストなモバイル両腕マニピュレーションプラットフォームを構築し、長時間にわたるトイレ掃除タスクを通じて複数のVLAモデルの性能を評価した。
llm.problem: アクセスしやすいモバイル両腕プラットフォームにおけるVLAモデルの性能が十分に検証されていないこと。
llm.method: 250件の実世界デモンストレーションを収集し、π0、π0.5、SmolVLA、GR00TなどのVLAモデルを同じ条件下で評価。
llm.result: π0が最も優れた性能を示し、厳密な自律成功率60%、限定的な人間介入により90%に達することを実証した。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレーション

2611.15368.title: Bind-WAM: Binding-Uncertainty-Guided Selective Future Imagination in World Action Models
2611.15368.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) can improve robot learning by jointly predicting future visual states and actions, but generating a visual future at every replanning step is expensive and sometimes unnecessary. This raises a critical question: when should a robot policy imagine the future? In this paper, we propose Bind-WAM, a binding-uncertainty-guided WAM for selective future imagination. Bind-WAM introduces language-object binding uncertainty, selectively invoking joint future-action generation when the current observation does not support stable task-relevant action generation. An offline labeling pipeline uses complete demonstrations and action context to identify task-relevant objects and detect reference mismatch, invisibility, and identity drift. The resulting pseudo-labels supervise a lightweight router that predicts binding uncertainty from the current observation and language instruction. At inference, a shared WAM policy invokes selective future imagination according to the predicted uncertainty and its change between consecutive replanning steps. Simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate that Bind-WAM can establish binding uncertainty as a strong, interpretable signal for selective future imagination.

llm.title_ja: Bind-WAM：世界行動モデルにおける結合不確実性誘導型選択的将来想像
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットが安定した行動生成を行えない場合にのみ将来の視覚状態と行動を予測する、言語-物体結合不確実性に基づいた選択的将来想像モデル「Bind-WAM」を提案した。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデルにおいて毎リプランステップで視覚的将来を生成することはコストが高く、常に必要とは限らないこと。
llm.method: タスク関連オブジェクトの結合不確実性を予測する軽量ルーターを導入し、予測された不確実性に応じて将来の想像を選択的に呼び出す。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機実験により、結合不確実性が選択的将来想像のための強力で解釈可能な信号として機能することを示した。

2611.15360.title: CARE-Drive: Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories
2611.15360.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models bring multimodal understanding and world knowledge to end-to-end autonomous driving. To further improve the quality of predicted trajectories, existing studies introduce candidate refinement, residual denoising, and token correction. However, these methods typically focus on unified refinement of the entire trajectory, paying limited attention to the distinct physical quantities and their interactions. We further investigate physical specialization and coordination in trajectory refinement, centering on position and heading for simpler and more intuitive correction modeling. To this end, we propose CARE-Drive (Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories), which decomposes trajectory refinement into waypoint residual correction and position-conditioned heading generation. Through imitation learning and a future-token auxiliary task, the backbone provides predictive representations and a base trajectory. The position expert predicts bounded metric waypoint residuals, while the heading expert reconstructs vehicle orientation from adjacent angular increments conditioned on the corrected path. With the backbone frozen, the two experts are optimized alternately through supervised initialization and reinforcement fine-tuning. This design simplifies refinement through clear physical specialization while preserving conditional coupling during prediction and optimization. On NAVSIM v1, CARE-Drive achieves 88.8 PDMS, improving by 2.4 points over the unrefined base trajectories generated by the same backbone. Ablation studies further support the effectiveness of specialized experts and staged training.

llm.title_ja: CARE-Drive：自車軌道のための結合型交互洗練
llm.tldr_ja: 自動運転のエンドツーエンド軌道予測品質を向上させるため、位置の残差修正と方位の生成を交互に最適化する結合型交互洗練フレームワーク「CARE-Drive」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の軌道洗練手法が軌道全体の一括洗練に注力し、異なる物理量やその相互作用への配慮が不足していること。
llm.method: 位置専門家によるウェイポイント残差補正と、方位専門家による車両向きの再構築を、模倣学習と強化学習を用いて交互に最適化する。
llm.result: NAVSIM v1において88.8 PDMSを達成し、未洗練のベースラインから2.4ポイント向上させた。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.15339.title: Interactive Perception of Granular Materials via Robotic Scooping and Force-Torque Sensing
2611.15339.abstract: Granular materials exhibit complex and highly variable interaction dynamics, making their reliable manipulation challenging without knowledge of their physical properties. We present an interactive perception framework that infers granular material properties directly from force-torque measurements acquired during scooping. The proposed Latent Filter++ combines a bio-inspired frequency-temporal filter-bank representation with a causal latent dynamical model, allowing the representation to evolve as interaction observations become available while avoiding hand-crafted signal preprocessing. The learned latent representation captures physically meaningful variation in granular materials and supports estimation of properties including grain size and bulk density. Evaluated on 26 diverse granular materials, the approach generalizes to materials excluded from training and enables few-shot adaptation of property-specific mappings using a small number of additional interaction samples. Finally, we demonstrate the relevance of the inferred properties to downstream manipulation by examining their correlation with the maximum acceleration the materials can withstand without spilling from the spoon during transport.

llm.title_ja: ロボットによるすくい上げと力覚センシングを通じた粒状体のインタラクティブ知覚
llm.tldr_ja: すくい上げ動作中の力覚・トルク測定値から粒状体の物理特性を直接推論するインタラクティブ知覚フレームワーク「Latent Filter++」を提案した。
llm.problem: 粒状体は複雑で変動しやすい相互作用ダイナミクスを持つため、物理特性の知識なしには信頼性の高い操作が困難であること。
llm.method: 生体模倣型周波数時間フィルターバンク表現と因果的潜在動的モデルを組み合わせたLatent Filter++を開発。
llm.result: 26種類の多様な粒状体に対する評価により、未知の材料への汎化や少量のサンプルを用いた数ショット適応が可能であることを示した。
keywords_ja: インタラクティブ知覚

2611.15317.title: BiPOP: Partial-Order Planning for Long-Horizon Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
2611.15317.abstract: Bimanual robotic manipulation is versatile, yet its central challenge lies not only in executing dexterous motion with each hand, but also in coordinating the two arms for long-horizon manipulation under coupled spatial and temporal constraints. Prior work has largely focused on endowing robots with human-level manipulation skills, paying less attention to the structure of bimanual behaviour itself: many practical tasks are a coordinated composition of reusable unimanual skills and a small set of synchronous bimanual skills. This makes high-level spatio-temporal coordination, rather than skill acquisition alone, a key bottleneck for efficient bimanual execution. We propose BiPOP, a framework that couples Large Language Models (LLMs) with Temporal Partial-Order Planning for long-horizon bimanual manipulation. At its core is an explicit spatio-temporal model that partitions the workspace by arm reachability and captures inter-arm dependencies, arm assignment, synchronization requirements, and opportunities for safe concurrent execution. Building on this model, an LLM translates natural-language instructions into a formal PDDL specification, while a temporal planner enforces the constraints and schedules actions, yielding plans that are logically consistent at the symbolic level and efficient through parallel execution. On simulated long-horizon tasks of varying complexity, BiPOP outperforms open-loop planning with strong reasoning models and closed-loop ReAct-style planning in success rate, planning time, and plan efficiency, and the full pipeline runs end to end on the real bimanual robot NICOL. A failure analysis further shows that LLM-only planners mainly violate spatial and temporal coordination constraints, which motivates delegating these constraints to a symbolic planner. Code: https://github.com/Kchu/BiPOP

llm.title_ja: BiPOP：長時間両腕ロボットマニピュレーションのための部分順序計画
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）と時間的部分順序計画を結合し、空間的・時間的制約の下で効率的な両腕の協調動作を実行するフレームワーク「BiPOP」を提案した。
llm.problem: 両腕マニピュレーションにおいて、単なる器用な動作だけでなく、結合された制約下での長時間にわたる高レベルの空間的・時間的協調がボトルネックとなっていること。
llm.method: ワークスペースを腕の可動域で分割する空間的・時間的モデルを構築し、LLMで自然言語指示をPDDL仕様に翻訳して時間的プランナーでスケジュールする。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび両腕ロボットNICOLを用いた実機実験において、成功率、計画時間、効率の面で既存のLLM単体やReAct型計画手法を上回った。

2611.15296.title: APG-Planner: Learning Vision-Based High-Speed Trajectory Planning via Analytic Policy Gradient
2611.15296.abstract: Vision-based high-speed navigation requires a trajectory planner that can reactively generate smooth, collision-free trajectories from onboard visual observations. Deep reinforcement learning offers a promising approach to vision-based trajectory planning, as it enables the optimization of sequential decision-making policies in complex environments. However, model-free policy gradient methods rely on sample-based policy gradient estimation, which yields noisy gradient estimates and inefficient training. To this end, we propose a framework for learning trajectory planning policies using the analytic policy gradient (APG) method and use it to train APG-Planner, a vision-based high-speed trajectory planner. The proposed framework leverages differential flatness to analytically reconstruct vehicle states from planned trajectories, thereby enabling differentiable trajectory-level state transitions without requiring an explicit low-level dynamics model. By iteratively performing trajectory planning and differentiable state transitions, we construct a differentiable episode rollout and analytically compute policy gradients from episode-level losses, improving both training efficiency and policy performance. After approximately 30 minutes of training on a single GPU, APG-Planner demonstrates comparable or superior performance to existing baseline methods in simulation and achieves speeds of up to 11\,m/s in real-world flight experiments. We further validate the proposed framework on a skid-steer ground robot, demonstrating its applicability to differentially flat robotic systems beyond quadrotors.

llm.title_ja: APG-Planner：解析的ポリシー勾配によるビジョンベース高速軌道計画の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 微分平坦性を利用して状態遷移を微分可能にし、解析的ポリシー勾配（APG）によって高速なビジョンベース軌道計画ポリシーを学習するフレームワーク「APG-Planner」を提案した。
llm.problem: モデルフリーのポリシー勾配法は、サンプルベースの勾配推定に依存するためノイズが多く非効率であること。
llm.method: 微分平坦性を用いて計画軌道から車両状態を解析的に再構築し、エピソード全体にわたる損失から微分可能にポリシー勾配を計算する。
llm.result: シミュレーションで約30分の学習後、実機の飛行実験において最大11 m/sの速度を達成し、地上ロボットへの適用も実証した。

2611.15280.title: Autonomous Trail Racing with a Bicycle Robot
2611.15280.abstract: Navigating off-road trails on a mountain bike requires diverse locomotion skills, including aerial maneuvers, cornering, and slip recovery, paired with sophisticated perception for scene understanding. Translating these capabilities to autonomous, two-wheeled robots remains a formidable challenge. We show that autonomous, high-speed trail navigation can be achieved through a single idea: encoding the trail as a semantic layer of the terrain. In simulation, this layer embeds the navigation task into the training environment; during deployment, it is reconstructed onboard from camera and LiDAR data. First, we introduce a unified learning framework that treats local navigation and locomotion as a joint optimization problem, bypassing the twist or pose command interface of classical control hierarchies. With fixed reward weights, the same framework produces both trail racing and agile parkour, shaped only through terrain semantics and episode length. Second, our perception pipeline combines a frozen vision foundation model with a lightweight dual-head decoder that predicts per-pixel terrain semantics and confidence scores, which are fused with LiDAR range measurements into an egocentric semantic elevation map at 30 Hz onboard an NVIDIA AGX Orin. We validate our framework on the Ultra Mobility Vehicle (UMV), a bicycle robot that autonomously raced across all sections of a kilometer-long, unstructured mountain bike trail at speeds exceeding 5 m/s and averaging 3.26 m/s. In simulation, our policy fails up to an order of magnitude less often than hierarchical baselines while driving faster.
2611.15280.comment: 35 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables (incl. appendix with supplementary figures and tables). Submitted to The International Journal of Robotics Research. Project page: https://pages.rai-inst.com/autonomous-trail-racing/. Code: https://github.com/rai-opensource/sem_map

llm.title_ja: 自転車ロボットによる自律型トレイルレース
llm.tldr_ja: トレイルを地形のセマンティックレイヤーとして符号化し、局所ナビゲーションと運動制御を統合最適化することで、自転車ロボットによる高速な野外トレイル走行を実現した。
llm.problem: マウンテンバイクによる未舗装トレイルの自律航行には、多様な運動スキルと高度な知覚の融合が求められるが困難であること。
llm.method: ビジョン基盤モデルと軽量デコーダによるセマンティック標高マップの構築と、地形セマンティクスに基づいた統合最適化フレームワークの開発。
llm.result: 自転車ロボット（UMV）を用いて、全長1kmを超える構造化されていないマウンテンバイクのトレイルを平均3.26 m/s（最高5 m/s超）で自律走行することに成功した。
keywords_ja: 不整地ナビゲーション
セマンティックマップ

2611.15277.title: DroneDiffusion: Uncertainty-Guided Diffusion Path Planner for UAV Navigation
2611.15277.abstract: We present DroneDiffusion, a perception-aware diffusion planner for local 3-D UAV trajectory generation that explicitly models and avoids failure zones caused by lens flare, overexposure, and reflective surfaces. A vision-language perceptual safety estimator produces a pixel-aligned reliability map that highlights regions of degraded sensing. A denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) is conditioned on this map together with the onboard RGB image, goal point, and initial velocity to generate egocentric 3-D trajectories. To enforce obstacle avoidance at inference time without retraining, we apply training-free CHOMP guidance over a 3-D Euclidean signed distance field. The model is trained entirely in simulation and deployed zero-shot on a real drone. Reliability conditioning raises the mean perceptual reliability along generated trajectories to 0.71, compared with 0.63 for a geometric baseline, while guidance halves the collision rate of the learned prior from 14.7% to 7.8%. Perceptual safety conditioning and geometric guidance are therefore complementary: treating sensor reliability as a first-class signal reduces incursions into unreliable regions while maintaining competitive navigation performance.

llm.title_ja: DroneDiffusion：UAVナビゲーションのための不確実性誘導型拡散パスプランナー
llm.tldr_ja: レンズフレアや過露出などのセンシング劣化領域を明示的にモデル化して回避する、知覚認識型拡散パスプランナー「DroneDiffusion」を提案した。
llm.problem: 環境要因によるセンシングの劣化（フレアや反射など）がUAVのナビゲーションにおける失敗ゾーンを引き起こすこと。
llm.method: ビジョン言語知覚安全性推定器から得られる信頼性マップを条件として、拡散モデルによる3D軌道生成を行い、訓練不要のCHOMPガイダンスを適用する。
llm.result: シミュレーション訓練のみで実機ドローンにゼロショット展開し、知覚信頼性を高めつつ幾何学的ベースラインと比較して衝突率を半減させた。

2611.15217.title: Are We Ready for Snow-tonomous Driving? Challenges Toward Robust Automated Driving in Extreme Weather
2611.15217.abstract: Automated driving has gained remarkable momentum over the past decade, with both industry and academia investing substantial resources in developing perception and control solutions to advance vehicle autonomy. However, these efforts have largely focused on clear-weather scenarios, leaving harsh conditions, such as snow, rain, and fog, comparatively understudied. As a result, inclement weather remains one of the most significant hurdles for autonomous vehicles, often leading to substantial performance degradation in downstream perception and control tasks. In this paper, we present insights from the EU-funded Horizon Europe project ROADVIEW, which aims to develop robust, weather-aware perception and control modules for connected and automated vehicles operating under severe conditions, including snow, rain, and fog. Drawing on four years of large-scale development and real-world demonstrations across multiple vehicle platforms in different locations, we identify ten key challenges that hinder the development of weather-resilient autonomy, including data scarcity, domain shifts, limitations in multimodal perception, control robustness, and validation gaps, among others. We summarize these challenges and lessons learned toward enabling reliable snow-autonomous driving, highlighting critical directions for future research and standardization.

llm.title_ja: 雪上の自動運転の準備はできているか？極限気象下における堅牢な自動運転に向けた課題
llm.tldr_ja: 欧州のHorizon Europeプロジェクト「ROADVIEW」の4年にわたる知見に基づき、雪、雨、霧などの悪天候下で自動運転車を運用する際の10の主要な課題と将来の方向性を総括した。
llm.problem: 自動運転の開発が主に晴天時に焦点を当てており、雪や雨などの過酷な気象条件が知覚や制御に大きな性能低下をもたらすこと。
llm.method: 複数の車両プラットフォームを用いた大規模な実世界デモンストレーションとプロジェクト全体の知見の分析。
llm.result: データ不足やドメインシフト、マルチモーダル知覚の限界など、雪上自動運転の実現に向けた10の主要課題を特定し整理した。

2611.15216.title: Where is My Mug? Training-Free Framework for Personalized Image Segmentation
2611.15216.abstract: \textbf{Personalized Image Segmentation (PIS)} aims to segment the specific object in a target image that matches a user-provided reference. Unlike category-based segmentation or few-shot segmentation, PIS must discriminate between multiple visually similar instances, a requirement central to deployed applications such as augmented reality, personalized content editing, robotics manipulation, inventory tracking, and fine-grained visual retrieval. We show that the strong numbers reported by existing PIS methods are largely an artifact of single-instance benchmarks: when evaluated on realistic scenes with several same-category look-alikes, prior point-prompt methods collapse, because the correct instance is frequently never surfaced as a prompt. We trace this to a recall bottleneck rather than a mask-quality one, and address it with a training-free, modular system. The pipeline first generates high-recall object proposals using an off-the-shelf class-agnostic detector, then matches each proposal to the reference using foundation-model features (e.g., BLIP-2), and finally refines the selected box with SAM. For robust matching we propose \textbf{top-$K$ Sinkhorn}, a patch-level distance that scores each candidate only on its most confidently matched patches; trimming the Sinkhorn dual potentials recovers the robustness of partial optimal transport at more than $100\times$ lower cost, keeping it inside the per-proposal candidate loop. To evaluate this regime, we introduce \textbf{\datasetname}, a realistic multi-instance benchmark. Across \datasetname, PerSeg, PerMIS, and DAVIS, our system surpasses PerSAM, $\mathrm{P}^2\mathrm{SAM}$, and PDM by up to $\sim\!48$ mIoU while matching their runtime and using fewer parameters, establishing a strong, deployable training-free baseline for real-world personalized segmentation.

llm.title_ja: 私のマグカップはどこ？パーソナライズされた画像セグメンテーションのための訓練不要フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 参照画像に一致する特定の物体を複雑なシーンから正確に切り出す、訓練不要でモジュール化されたパーソナライズ画像セグメンテーションシステムを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のパーソナライズ画像セグメンテーション手法は単一インスタンスのベンチマークに依存しており、類似する複数インスタンスが存在する現実的なシーンでは破綻すること。
llm.method: クラス非依存の検出器による高リコールな物体候補の生成、基盤モデル特徴量を用いた参照画像とのマッチング、およびtop-K Sinkhornを用いた部分最適輸送の効率的な計算。
llm.result: 新しく導入した現実的なマルチインスタンスベンチマークや既存データセットにおいて、従来の最先端手法を大幅に上回るmIoUを達成した。
keywords_ja: 画像セグメンテーション

2611.15215.title: AFTER: A World Model with Adaptive Fast--Slow Timescales for Error-Driven Retention
2611.15215.abstract: In robotics and embodied AI, a core challenge for world models is adapting to sudden, persistent, yet initially unknown changes in robot dynamics during interaction. For instance, when a robotic arm grasps an object with an unknown payload, the robot dynamics change suddenly. If the world model fails to adapt, its prediction errors accumulate over the open-loop rollout and ultimately mislead the robot's actions. Existing world models, however, struggle to simultaneously satisfy three critical requirements for dynamics adaptation: responsiveness, reacting promptly to sudden changes to curb prediction error accumulation; stability, distinguishing persistent changes from transient disturbances to prevent incorrect updates; and persistence, retaining the adapted dynamics without new observations so that later predictions do not revert to the old dynamics. Inspired by predictive coding in the human brain with multi-timescale adaptation, we propose AFTER-WM, a world model with Adaptive Fast-slow Timescales for Error-driven Retention, whose prediction errors drive a fast correction that fades and a slow correction that persists, while dynamically adjusting the combination weights of pre-trained experts without altering them, to overcome the trade-offs among responsiveness, stability and persistence. On five simulated robot datasets and real UAV data, AFTER-WM has a lower multi-step mean error than all ten compared models and the highest mean return in a joint-failure control task. In simulation, its multistep mean error is 16%-34% below the strongest compared model's and is also the lowest 1-4 steps after a change and under transient disturbances alone, and its step-40 error is the lowest as well, reflecting responsiveness, stability and persistence. All code (method, baselines, experiments) and datasets will be released online.

llm.title_ja: AFTER：誤差駆動型保持のための適応的速い・遅い時間スケールを持つ世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットダイナミクスの急激な変化に適応するため、予測誤差によって駆動される速い修正と遅い修正を組み合わせた適応型時間スケールを持つ世界モデル「AFTER-WM」を提案した。
llm.problem: ロボットアームが未知のペイロードを持つ物体を把持した際などにダイナミクスが急変し、世界モデルが適応しないと予測誤差が蓄積して制御を誤ること。
llm.method: 予測誤差が減衰する速い修正と持続する遅い修正を駆動させ、事前学習済み専門家の結合重みを動的に調整するマルチ時間スケール適応モデルの構築。
llm.result: 5つのシミュレーションロボットデータセットおよび実機UAVデータにおいて、既存の10モデルと比較して低い多ステップ平均誤差と優れたタスク報酬を達成した。

2611.15135.title: ARTS: An Open-Source, Reproducible Three-Arm Platform for Autonomy Research in Minimally Invasive Surgery
2611.15135.abstract: Research on surgical autonomy needs open platforms that any laboratory can build, yet the most widely shared platform depends on donated clinical hardware, and open alternatives on industrial arms each lack part of the surgical chain. We present the Autonomous Robotic Translational System (ARTS), an open-source three-arm platform for autonomy research in minimally invasive surgery, built entirely from purchasable parts for about USD 137,000. Two UR5e arms hold wristed da Vinci X/Xi instruments, a UR5 arm holds a stereo endoscope with two FLIR cameras, the surgeon console provides haptic handles, footswitches and a stereo viewer, and a hardware stop independent of the software lets a supervisor freeze all three arms in place. The ROS 2 software pins every dependency, installs from the same scripts on bare metal or in containers, and records stereo images with hardware-measured timing. On the real arms, ARTS commands each arm at its controller's full rate (e.g., 500 Hz on the UR5e), the two cameras expose within 12 microseconds of each other, hand motion reaches the arm in 58 ms, and the endoscope image reaches the monitor in 68 ms. The ISO 9283 pose repeatability is 0.14-0.25 mm, comparable to a da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK) Classic arm on the same protocol, and an optical tracker measured a mean remote-center-of-motion error of 0.34-0.37 mm. Three expert and three novice operators performed the Fundamentals of Laparoscopic Surgery (FLS) peg transfer through a laparoscopic trainer box, and one of the experts sutured on a suture pad. The hardware designs, firmware and software are available at https://github.com/MRE-Lab-UMD/arts.
2611.15135.comment: Submitted to the 2027 International Symposium on Medical Robotics (ISMR). † Equal contribution

llm.title_ja: ARTS：低侵襲手術の自律性研究のためのオープンソースで再現可能な3アームプラットフォーム
llm.tldr_ja: 市販部品のみで約137,000米ドルで構築可能な、低侵襲手術の自律性研究に向けたオープンソースの3アームロボットプラットフォーム「ARTS」を開発した。
llm.problem: 手術の自律性に関する研究において、広く共有されているプラットフォームは寄贈された臨床ハードウェアに依存するか、オープンな代替品の一部が欠けていること。
llm.method: 2つのUR5eアームでダ・ヴィンチX/Xi用インストゥルメントを保持し、1つのUR5アームでステレオ内視鏡を保持するハードウェア構成と、ROS 2ベースのソフトウェアスタックの構築。
llm.result: 実機アームでの高速コマンド応答、カメラの同期、およびダ・ヴィンチ研究キットと同等のポーズ再現性とリモート中心運動誤差の達成を実証した。

2611.15117.title: PolyMorphWBC: Whole-Body Control from End-Effector Trajectories for Quadrupedal Mobile Manipulation across Arm Morphologies with Extended Reach
2611.15117.abstract: Quadrupedal mobile manipulators can extend their manipulation workspace by coordinating the mounted arm with the mobile base. At the task level, short-horizon end-effector (EE) trajectories provide an interface for specifying the desired manipulation motion without prescribing how it should be realized by the arm and base. However, executing such trajectories remains challenging because the controller must determine when and how the base should move, and this decision depends on the mounted-arm morphology. We therefore present PolyMorphWBC, a hierarchical controller that takes an EE trajectory as the sole task-level motion command and generates coordinated arm--base motions across four families of 6-DoF mounted arms, with extended-reach trajectories beyond the initial fixed-base reach. Within PolyMorphWBC, a trajectory-conditioned coordinator determines the base motion from previewed EE targets, while arm-specific Inverse Kinematics (IK) tracks the current target, and a frozen locomotion backend executes the resulting motion. Cross-arm reuse is enabled by a Unified Robot Description Format (URDF)-derived morphology conditioning, together with online residual-wrench feedback. We train PolyMorphWBC on procedurally generated arms and structured trajectories within and beyond fixed-base reach. In IsaacLab, it achieves 93.95% completion with 2.30cm position error and 4.81° orientation error on held-out trajectories and arm morphologies. In MuJoCo evaluation against UMI-on-Legs, PolyMorphWBC reduces EE position error by 69--72% and orientation error by 91--97% across four within- and extended-reach trajectories. On a physical Go2--ARX5 system, we demonstrate language-conditioned extended-reach pick-and-place using EE trajectories from pi_0 without vision-language-action (VLA)-generated base commands.

llm.title_ja: PolyMorphWBC：拡張リーチを持つアーム形態にまたがる四脚移動マニピュレーションのためのエンドエフェクタ軌道からの全身制御
llm.tldr_ja: 四脚移動マニピュレータが多様なアーム形態でエンドエフェクタ軌道から協調的な全身動作を生成する階層型コントローラPolyMorphWBCを提案し、シミュレーションおよび実機で有効性を実証した。
llm.problem: アーム形態に依存してベースの移動タイミングや方法を決定する必要があり、エンドエフェクタ軌道の実行が困難であること。
llm.method: プレビューされた目標位置からベース動作を決定する調整器、アーム固有のIK、および固定された移動バックエンドを組み合わせた階層型コントローラを構築した。
llm.result: IsaacLabでは93.95%の完了率を達成し、MuJoCo評価および実機Go2-ARX5システムでの言語条件付きピック＆プレースで優れた追従性能を示した。
keywords_ja: 四脚移動マニピュレータ

2611.15112.title: Elastra: A Simulation Framework for Elastic Bodies
2611.15112.abstract: When robots interact with elastic surfaces such as mattresses and trampolines, changes in loading cause the surfaces to deform and rebound, altering subsequent contact locations and forces. We present Elastra, a simulation framework for modeling this interaction and supporting the training and evaluation of robot control policies. Elastra represents each surface using elements that move only vertically, with elastic connections and damping to model deformation and recovery. Contact forces drive surface motion, and the updated surface geometry is used to compute subsequent contact forces. We systematically validate our simulations against an independent implementation and a real mattress load curve. We further use Elastra to train the Unitree G1 humanoid to stand up on mattresses and trampolines. Using the pretrained HoST policy and ProtoMotions motion tracker as original controllers, we train residual policies through reinforcement learning to add corrections to their joint targets. Adding these residual policies increases the success rate with HoST from 44.1\% to 72.5\%, and from 55\% to 89\% on the trampoline. With ProtoMotions, the success rate increases from 19.0\% to 45.0\% for initial poses not encountered during training. The code and video are available on https://github.com/yichg/elastra.

llm.title_ja: Elastra：弾性体向けシミュレーションフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: マットレスやトランポリンなどの弾性表面とロボットの相互作用をモデル化し制御ポリシーの訓練・評価を支援するシミュレーションフレームワークElastraを提案し、ヒューマノイドの立ち上がり動作の成功率を向上させた。
llm.problem: ロボットが弾性表面と相互作用する際、荷重変化による表面の変形と反発が接触位置や力を変化させ、制御が困難になること。
llm.method: 垂直方向のみに動く要素、弾性接続、減衰を用いて表面を表現し、接触力から表面の動きを計算するシミュレーションフレームワークを構築し、強化学習による残差ポリシーを訓練した。
llm.result: Unitree G1ヒューマノイドにおいて、HoSTポリシーの成功率をマットレス上で44.1%から72.5%、トランポリン上で55%から89%に向上させた。

2611.15101.title: CFGComposer: Compositional Audio-Text-to-Motion Generation via Copula Score Correction
2611.15101.abstract: Generating whole-body gestures that are simultaneously rhythmically synchronized with speech audio and semantically aligned with text descriptions is a fundamental challenge in embodied AI and social robotics. We tackle this Audio-Text-to-Motion (AT2M) problem by composing two independently-trained diffusion models at inference time and refine bias in joint inference by modeling the copula score $s_I$. A rigorous theoretical analysis reveals that naive epsilon blending corresponds to a Product-of-Experts formulation that omits the copula score $s_I$: the cross-modal interaction between audio and text that neither marginal model can capture. We propose CFGComposer: a jointly-trained AT2M diffusion model that estimates $s_I$ via a CFG analogy and injects it as an $ε$-space correction. Experiments on BEAT demonstrate best-in-class semantic fidelity (SRGR $0.9916$, FID $27.18$) with GT-level beat alignment (BA $0.1826$ vs. GT $0.1743$), and 76-83% win rate in blind pairwise human evaluation against all prior methods. Physical deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid confirms direct sim-to-real transfer.

llm.title_ja: CFGComposer：コピュラスコア補正による構成的音声・テキストからのモーション生成
llm.tldr_ja: 音声とテキストから全身ジェスチャーを生成するため、独立に訓練された拡散モデルを推論時に結合しコピュラスコア補正を行うCFGComposerを提案し、優れたセマンティック忠実度とビート同期を実現した。
llm.problem: 音声のリスムとテキスト記述に同時に同調する全身ジェスチャー生成において、周辺モデルでは捉えられないクロスモーダルな相互作用をモデル化する必要があること。
llm.method: CFGの類推を用いてコピュラスコアを推定し、それをε空間の補正として注入する、共同訓練されたAT2M拡散モデルを提案した。
llm.result: BEATデータセットにおいて最高水準のセマンティック忠実度と実測値レベルのビート同期を実現し、Unitree G1ヒューマノイドでの実機転移を確認した。

2611.15093.title: Decide Before You Move: Diffusion-Generated Search Reference for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Object Navigation in Semi-Static Environments
2611.15093.abstract: Open-world navigation requires a robot to locate a user-specified target in an indoor scene under open-vocabulary queries. Realistic indoor environments are semi-static: walls and furniture largely persist while smaller objects move, relocate, or vanish between visits. Prior-map systems answer queries from object poses recorded at reconstruction time, which expire as soon as objects move, whereas online methods re-derive where to look from current observations every few steps, often through expensive calls to a vision--language model. Assuming that walls and large furniture do not move, we keep their map to plan paths, but use a target--furniture co-occurrence prior to decide where to search. We present PreNav, an ObjectNav framework on semi-static environments. Rather than invoking a vision-language model at each step, PreNav generates a single global search reference before the robot moves: an LLM converts target--furniture co-occurrence into a spatial prior, a conditional diffusion model turns that prior and the persistent structure into an ordered centerline with a band around it, and the robot approaches the target once it is detected online. Experiments on a Gibson ObjectNav benchmark show that PreNav outperforms a strong online baseline under matched structural priors, using a generator trained only on room-level ScanNet++ scenes and applied to floor-level Gibson without fine-tuning. Real-world experiments under object relocation and open-vocabulary queries further validate the approach.

llm.title_ja: 動く前に決める：半静的環境におけるゼロショットオープンボキャブラリー物体ナビゲーションのための拡散生成型探索リファレンス
llm.tldr_ja: 半静的環境でVLMを毎ステップ呼び出すことなく、事前に大域的な探索リファレンスを生成して効率的なオープンボキャブラリー物体ナビゲーションを実現するPreNavを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の事前マップは物体移動により陳腐化し、オンライン手法はVLMの頻繁な呼び出しによりコストが高くなること。
llm.method: LLMによる空間事前分布の変換と、条件付き拡散モデルによる永続的構造に基づいた順序付き中心線の生成を組み合わせたPreNavフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: Gibsonベンチマークにおいて強力なオンラインベースラインを上回り、現実世界の物体再配置やオープンボキャブラリークエリの実験で有効性を実証した。
keywords_ja: オープンボキャブラリー

2611.15082.title: Prediction or Persistence? What Future-Prediction Scores Miss About World Models
2611.15082.abstract: Pretrained video world models are compared and chosen as components for robot learning largely by future-prediction scores. On its own, such a score cannot be read as evidence of prediction, because it mixes encoder quality, the near future's resemblance to the recent past, and the predictor's own contribution. We separate the three with a matched control. On 27,000 future-retrieval trials from household egocentric video, a model must pick the true continuation of a clip among eleven candidates from the same video (chance 0.091), ranked zero-shot by its own training criterion. Each model is paired with a persistence control, an identical copy whose predictor is never invoked, so the paired difference isolates the predictor. Score and contribution dissociate within the native-video V-JEPA family alone: the predictor adds +0.291 top-1 for V-JEPA 2.1 but +0.03 to +0.04 for V-JEPA 2 on the identical trials. Across five models the contribution ranges from +0.291 to negative, and it is negative only for the two action-conditioned models, which we evaluate outside their training regime. Persistence alone recovers the encoder ordering expected from pretraining, a sign that the probe tracks real signal. We suggest reporting each future-prediction score together with its persistence baseline. The gap between them, not the score, is what makes the number interpretable: a necessary check costing one forward pass. Establishing downstream usefulness is a separate matter, for a planning or control evaluation.
2611.15082.comment: Accepted at the CoRL 2026 Workshop "Do Robots Need World Models?"

llm.title_ja: 予測か永続性か？将来予測スコアが世界モデルについて見落としていること
llm.tldr_ja: 将来予測スコア単体ではモデルの予測性能を正しく評価できないことを示し、予測器を含まない永続性コントロールとの差分を評価することで真の予測能力を分離・評価できると提案した。
llm.problem: 事前学習済みビデオ世界モデルの評価において、将来予測スコアがエンコーダ品質や過去の近接性を混同していること。
llm.method: 予測器を起動しない同一のコピーである「永続性コントロール」をペアにし、家庭内映像を用いた将来回収トライアルでスコアの差分を比較した。
llm.result: スコアと予測器の寄与度はモデル間で大きく乖離し、特に動作条件付きモデルでは寄与度が負になるなど、差分を評価することで初めて解釈可能な結果が得られることを示した。

2611.15078.title: CrowdMAPS: Crowdsourcing Multiple Actions per State for Real-World Imitation Learning
2611.15078.abstract: Real-world robot imitation learning is often limited by the cost of collecting physical demonstrations, which typically yield only one action label per visited state. We present CrowdMAPS, a web-based crowdsourcing paradigm for augmenting real-robot datasets with Multiple Actions per State (MAPS). After or during standard robot data collection, CrowdMAPS distributes visited robot states to remote annotators through a web-based 3D interface, where they specify alternative valid actions without requiring access to physical robot hardware. This expands robot datasets along a complementary "width" dimension--by increasing the number of actions per visited state--rather than only by collecting more trajectories. We evaluate CrowdMAPS using keyframe-centric goal-pose annotations supplied by non-expert annotators and train imitation policies on the resulting MAPS data. Across five real-world manipulation tasks, increasing MAPS width from one to ten actions per state improves sample efficiency and increases average success rates by 35.6 percentage points for keypose policies and 33.0 percentage points for trajectory policies. These results show that software-mediated human annotations can augment physical robot data to afford denser supervision, establishing CrowdMAPS as a scalable digital layer for real-robot data collection.

llm.title_ja: CrowdMAPS：実世界模倣学習のための1状態あたり複数アクションのクラウドソーシング
llm.tldr_ja: 実ロボットのデータセットに1状態あたりの複数の有効なアクションをウェブベースの3Dインターフェースで追加するクラウドソーシング手法CrowdMAPSを提案し、サンプル効率と成功率を向上させた。
llm.problem: 実世界のロボット模倣学習は、物理的なデモ収集コストが高く、1訪問状態あたり1つのアクションラベルしか得られないことに制限されていること。
llm.method: ウェブベースの3Dインターフェースを介して遠隔アノテーターにロボットの状態を渡し、ハードウェアなしで代替の有効なアクションを指定させるCrowdMAPSパラダイムを構築した。
llm.result: 5つの実世界マニピュレーションタスクにおいて、MAPSの幅を1から10に増やすことでサンプル効率が向上し、平均成功率が大幅に向上した。

2611.15066.title: MiniPose: Miniature-Based Real Data Collection for 6D Pose Estimation of Large Industrial Pipe Segments
2611.15066.abstract: 6-DOF pose estimation of large and heavy industrial objects, such as large piping systems in shipyards and structural components in petrochemical plants, remains relatively underexplored in robotic perception. Repeatedly repositioning large objects is physically and spatially demanding, making it difficult to acquire real training data with sufficient pose diversity. Synthetic data offer a scalable alternative, but faithfully reproducing real RGB-D observations, particularly the structured measurement errors of real depth sensors, remains difficult. We propose MiniPose, a practical pipeline for miniature-based real RGB-D data collection that addresses both the data-acquisition burden and the sim-to-real gap. We fabricate a scaled-down replica and capture RGB-D data of it in diverse poses using a real RGB-D camera. RGB images are used directly, while depth maps are converted to a geometrically consistent representation of the full-scale object via a simple inverse scaling transformation. This allows training to incorporate real appearance and sensor measurement characteristics that are difficult to reproduce using synthetic data alone. To examine whether the benefit depends on a particular network, we evaluate two RGB-D pose estimators with different formulations, PVN3D and RDPN6D. Mixing at most 1,000 miniature images per pipe type, less than 10\% of the training data, with 10,000 synthetic images improves the mean ADD-S AUC across pipe types over synthetic-only training for both estimators. A comparison with training on full-scale real data further suggests that miniature data can serve as a proxy where full-scale collection is difficult, reducing the data-collection burden for large industrial objects.
2611.15066.comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)

llm.title_ja: MiniPose：大型工業用パイプセグメントの6D姿勢推定のためのミニチュアベース実データ収集
llm.tldr_ja: 大型工業用オブジェクトの6D姿勢推定におけるデータ収集の負担とSim-to-Realギャップを解消するため、縮小レプリカを用いて幾何学的に一貫したRGB-Dデータを収集するMiniPoseパイプラインを提案した。
llm.problem: 大型オブジェクトの繰り返し配置は物理的・空間的に困難であり、十分な姿勢多様性を持つ実訓練データの取得が難しいこと。
llm.method: 縮小レプリカのRGB-Dデータをカメラで撮影し、逆スケーリング変換によってフルスケールの幾何学的一貫性を持つ表現に変換して訓練に用いた。
llm.result: 合成データのみの訓練に比べて、10%未満のミニチュア画像を混ぜることで複数のパイプタイプの平均ADD-S AUCが向上した。

2611.15048.title: Does Your World Model Know Actions Have Consequences?
2611.15048.abstract: Embodied world models (WMs) are implicit learning systems that predict the next future latent state directly from observations and actions. Unique from other end-to-end learning systems, the dynamics predictor of WMs can simulate the environment's response to alternative actions without physical deployment nor pre-specifying states of the dynamical system. Current metrics focus on the quality of model outputs, e.g., clarity of reconstructions or task success, but fail to assess the fidelity of modeling consequences of counterfactual actions. Inspecting the forced response to action perturbations through sensitivity analysis is one way to audit how well WMs can predict the consequences of counterfactual actions. Deploying WMs on hardware will require new evaluation frameworks to analyze the tradeoffs between state error and accurate sensitivity prediction.
2611.15048.comment: Presented at "Do Robots Need World Models?" Workshop at Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) 2026

llm.title_ja: あなたの世界モデルはアクションに結果が伴うことを知っていますか？
llm.tldr_ja: 具身体世界モデルが反実仮想アクションの結果を予測する忠実度を評価するため、感度分析を通じた新しい評価フレームワークの必要性を論じた。
llm.problem: 現在の指標は再構成の明瞭さやタスク成功率などのモデル出力品質に焦点を当てており、反実仮想アクションの結果をモデル化する忠実度を評価できていないこと。
llm.method: アクション外乱に対する強制応答を感度分析により検査することで、世界モデルの予測性能を監査する手法について論じた。
llm.result: ハードウェアへの展開において、状態誤差と正確な感度予測のトレードオフを分析する新しい評価フレームワークが必要であることを示した。

2611.15020.title: Genie Sim Benchmark: Real-to-Sim Fidelity and Evaluation
2611.15020.abstract: We evaluate Genie Sim Benchmark through paired real-simulation tasks and complementary system-identification studies. Across 22 robot-task pairs spanning 16 task names, task-specific pi0.5 policies fine-tuned on real-robot data achieve a descriptive Score correlation of 0.9686, MAE 0.0405, RMSE 0.0520, with simulation-real differences from -0.110 to +0.080. G2 crsB experiments assess long-horizon closed-loop position and joint-side torque agreement, while five representative object cases examine identification and cross-engine contact transfer. A separate 32.6503 s teleoperation trajectory, excluded from mechanical identification and servo-gain search, evaluates external position targets through simulated motion-controller command shaping and a calibrated position servo. Across both arms, per-joint position RMSE spans 0.00614-0.03522 rad and current-derived torque RMSE spans 0.73545-4.00099 N m. Native PhysX adaptations recover three recorded interaction tasks, with case-dependent alignment gains. These results support task-specific simulation evaluation through joint assessment of task outcomes and physical-response consistency.

llm.title_ja: Genie Sim Benchmark：Real-to-Simの忠実度と評価
llm.tldr_ja: ペアとなる現実・シミュレーションタスクとシステム同定スタディを通じてGenie Sim Benchmarkを評価し、タスク特化型ポリシーの優れた実世界との相関を確認した。
llm.problem: シミュレーション環境と実世界の間の忠実度を客観的かつ包括的に評価する必要があること。
llm.method: 実ロボットデータで微調整されたタスク特化型pi0.5ポリシーを用いて、スコア相関、位置・トルクの合意度、および接触転移を評価した。
llm.result: 22のロボット・タスクペアにおいて記述スコア相関0.9686を達成し、シミュレーションと現実の差が小さく、物理応答の一貫性を示した。
keywords_ja: シミュレーション評価

2611.15011.title: Fast Inference-Time Policy Refinement via Action-Affine World Models
2611.15011.abstract: Imitation policies can perform complex manipulation, yet small execution errors can accumulate and cause failure. Refinement can correct these errors, but existing approaches often require additional on-policy learning or costly online planning. Our key insight is that a pretrained policy already supplies a useful nominal behavior: refinement can focus on predicting how small action corrections change its outcome. We therefore learn this local response in a form that is cheap to optimize. Our \textit{action-affine world model} (A\textsuperscript{2}WM) learns local action sensitivities offline from action-perturbed policy rollouts. Given interaction history and a policy proposal, it predicts task-relevant geometry as a nominal trajectory plus a linear response to corrections. It predicts the full planning horizon directly, avoiding the propagation of intermediate errors through recursive model evaluations. Quadratic penalties on predicted task errors and linear correction constraints then yield a cheap convex quadratic program (QP). Online refinement requires one model evaluation and one QP solve, while both policy and model weights remain frozen. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, our framework achieves the highest success rate among evaluated baselines, adding only 3.8 ms of mean refinement overhead per control step, excluding base-policy sampling.

llm.title_ja: アクションアフィン世界モデルによる高速な推論時ポリシー洗練
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みポリシーの局所的なアクション感度をオフラインで学習し、高速な二次計画法により推論時に実行誤差を効率的に補正するA^2WMフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 模倣ポリシーの複雑なマニピュレーション実行時に小さな誤差が蓄積して失敗を引き起こすこと。
llm.method: アクション外乱を与えたポリシーのロールアウトから局所アクション感度をオフラインで学習するアクションアフィン世界モデル（A^2WM）を構築し、凸二次計画法（QP）でオンライン洗練を行う。
llm.result: 4つのシミュレーションタスクで最高水準の成功率を達成し、制御ステップあたりわずか3.8msの追加オーバーヘッドで高速な洗練を実現した。

2611.14985.title: ILA: A Transferable Interface-Level Adapter for Compliant Humanoid Motion Tracking
2611.14985.abstract: Humanoid motion tracking is fundamental to reproducing human motions on humanoid robots and serves as an important tool for teleoperation and motion data collection. However, directly tracking reference motions can be unsafe in constrained environments or during physical human--robot interaction, motivating the need for compliant motion tracking. We present ILA, an Interface-Level Adapter for compliant humanoid motion tracking without dedicated interaction sensors. ILA adapts motion references from the robot's observation history, allowing the robot to respond to physical guidance while preserving the capabilities of a pretrained motion tracker. As an interface-level module, ILA can be directly plugged into different pretrained motion trackers without retraining either the adapter or the tracking policies. ILA is trained entirely in simulation to predict reference corrections induced by physical interaction. We evaluate ILA with three humanoid motion trackers and achieve a 63.6--75.4% reduction in guidance-target error compared with their original policies. Matched simulation studies and hardware experiments further show that ILA improves responsiveness to human guidance while preserving nominal motion-tracking performance. These results demonstrate compliant guidance as a reusable, sensor-free extension to pretrained humanoid motion trackers.

llm.title_ja: ILA：コンプライアントなヒューマノイドモーション追従のための転移可能なインターフェースレベルアダプター
llm.tldr_ja: 専用の相互作用センサなしで、ロボットの観測履歴から参照モーションを適応させ物理的ガイダンスに応答可能にするインターフェースレベルアダプターILAを提案した。
llm.problem: 制約された環境や物理的な人とロボットの協調において、参照モーションを直接追従することは安全ではない場合があること。
llm.method: 物理的インタラクションによって引き起こされる参照補正を予測するようにシミュレーションで完全に訓練された、既存のモーション追従器にプラグイン可能なアダプターを構築した。
llm.result: 3つのヒューマノイドモーション追従器において、元のポリシーと比較してガイダンス目標誤差を63.6〜75.4%削減し、応答性を向上させた。
keywords_ja: コンプライアンス制御

2611.14981.title: From a Single RGB Image to Robot Execution: Metric Scene Alignment and Contact-Guided Retargeting
2611.14981.abstract: Extending humanoid interaction generation to new environments remains limited by the need for prebuilt 3D scene assets. Reconstructing scenes directly from single RGB images offers a way to overcome this limitation, but introduces a key challenge in maintaining geometric consistency throughout motion generation and transfer. Visually plausible human motions may be misaligned with the reconstructed scene, while retargeting can introduce additional support errors due to differences between human and robot embodiments. We present a unified pipeline that transforms a single RGB image into a humanoid motion reference. It reconstructs scene geometry from the input image, generates a human interaction conditioned on the reconstructed scene, and retargets the motion to a humanoid robot. To maintain geometric consistency throughout this process, we incorporate two complementary refinement stages before and after embodiment transfer. Before retargeting, Joint Metric Interaction Refinement (JMIR) refines human motion alignment with the registered metric scene while preserving the generated interaction structure. Following retargeting, Contact Guided Residual Retargeting (CGRR) corrects robot specific support errors to restore the intended support relationships. Together, these stages produce motion references that are consistent with the reconstructed scene and can be followed by multiple pretrained humanoid trackers without scene specific policy fine tuning. Compared with GRAIL, our method reduces refinement time from 480 s to 87 s, yielding a speedup of 5.5 times. The complete pipeline achieves a success rate of 89% in simulation and 70% across 50 physical trials on the Unitree G1, demonstrating its effectiveness in generating executable humanoid motion references from single RGB images.

llm.title_ja: 単一RGB画像からロボット実行まで：メトリックシーンアライメントと接触誘導リターゲティング
llm.tldr_ja: 単一のRGB画像から幾何学的に一貫したシーンを再構成し、人間とロボットの身体性の違いによる誤差を補正して実行可能なヒューマノイドモーション参照を生成する統一パイプラインを提案した。
llm.problem: 事前構築された3Dシーンアセットの必要性や、再構成シーンと人間の動きの不整合、リターゲティング時のサポートエラーがヒューマノイドの環境適応を制限していること。
llm.method: シーンアライメントを洗練するJoint Metric Interaction Refinement (JMIR) と、ロボット特有のサポートエラーを修正するContact Guided Residual Retargeting (CGRR) を組み合わせたパイプラインを構築した。
llm.result: 洗練時間を大幅に短縮し、シミュレーションで89%、Unitree G1を用いた50回の実機試行で70%の成功率を達成した。

2611.14969.title: Scaling VLA Serving Under Robotic Execution Constraints
2611.14969.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for general-purpose robotic manipulation. In our production setting, hundreds of VLA-powered robots are already operating in real-world environments, creating an immediate need for efficient fleet serving. We present XInfer, a production-deployed VLA serving system designed to reduce the inference infrastructure cost of large-scale robotic deployments. XInfer jointly coordinates heterogeneous VLA computation with the evolving response requirements of robotic execution. By exploiting computational parallelism while managing interference, XInfer improves GPU efficiency while protecting time-critical robotic feedback. We evaluate XInfer across three VLA models using production-derived workloads, achieving 1.26-3.75 times the effective robot capacity (ERC) of state-of-the-art systems under physical-execution constraints. Our implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/X-Square-Robot/xinfer.

llm.title_ja: ロボット実行制約下におけるVLAサービングのスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模なロボットフリートの推論インフラストラクチャコストを削減しつつ時間的制約のあるフィードバックを保護する、本番運用向けVLAサービングシステムXInferを提案した。
llm.problem: 数百台のVLA駆動型ロボットが実環境で稼働する中で、効率的なフリートサービングが即座に必要とされていること。
llm.method: 異種VLA計算とロボット実行の応答要件を共同で調整し、計算の並列性を活用しながら干渉を管理するXInferシステムを構築した。
llm.result: 3つのVLAモデルを用いた実運用ワークロードにおいて、物理実行制約下で最先端システムのエフェクティブ・ロボット容量（ERC）の1.26〜3.75倍を達成した。

2611.14958.title: Adapting Monocular Depth Estimation in Novel Scenes through Disparity Refinement and Robot Ego-Motion
2611.14958.abstract: The geometric understanding of a scene is a crucial component for safe and efficient robotic operations in novel and unstructured environments. The recent emergence of foundation models for Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE) has provided an opportunity to enrich robotic perception capabilities with dense long-range depth predictions, replacing expensive onboard hardware (e.g., LiDARs and stereo cameras). However, these offline models are primarily trained on affine-invariant depth representations, and their generalization to novel scenes remains unclear. In this work we present EM-ViT, a monocular depth estimation model that learns to adapt online relative depth inputs from a foundation model prior to the metric scale with observations collected during robotic operations. Motivated by the stereo camera parameterization, our method decomposes depth prediction via dense disparity refinement to recover the scene's relative structure and an effective baseline scalar prediction to determine the missing metric scale. The learning process leverages sparse LiDAR points and, optionally, the robot's Ego-Motion (EM) to rapidly train a lightweight Vision Transformer (ViT), while an internal gradient matching loss preserves the fine-grained semantic structure of the input disparity in real-time. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method on publicly available sequences, such as KITTI, and show that our online learning pipeline can adapt to novel scenes faster and with higher accuracy than existing MDE foundation models. The code and supplementary materials will be publicly available at https://emvit-mde.github.io.

llm.title_ja: 視差洗練とロボットの自己運動による新規シーンでの単眼深度推定の適応
llm.tldr_ja: 高価なLiDARやステレオカメラを置き換えるため、スパースなLiDAR点とロボットの自己運動を活用して単眼深度推定（MDE）の基盤モデルをオンラインでメトリック尺度に適応させるEM-ViTを提案した。
llm.problem: 単眼深度推定のオフライン基盤モデルはアフィン不変な表現で訓練されており、新規シーンへの汎化が不明確であること。
llm.method: 高密度な視差洗練により相対構造を復元し、有効なベースラインスカラー予測によりメトリック尺度を決定する、軽量Vision Transformerを用いたオンライン学習パイプラインを構築した。
llm.result: KITTIなどの公開シーケンスにおいて、既存のMDE基盤モデルよりも高速かつ高精度に新規シーンへ適応できることを示した。

2611.14955.title: The Posterior-Prior Epistemic Gap: When World Model Imagination Fails to Carry Task-Relevant Signals
2611.14955.abstract: Model-based planners that roll out imagined futures assume the transition model faithfully propagates task-relevant signals---a property rarely measured directly. In a single-seed case study of a Recurrent State Space Model world model with active-inference planning in the CARLA driving simulator, we identify a \textbf{posterior-prior gap}---posterior (observation-filtered) states retain obstacle information that imagined rollout states progressively lose: a supervised obstacle probe achieves AUC 0.85 on posterior states, but the same probe applied to imagined prior states shows monotonic decay (AUC 0.85$\rightarrow$0.71 over 15 steps; logit separation drops 57\%). Because the probe is identical, the decay isolates the transition model---not the representation---as the information bottleneck. Obstacle avoidance drops to 0\% without privileged runtime coordinates, and the planner's own ensemble-based epistemic term does not flag the loss---ensemble disagreement yields AUC 0.52 as an obstacle classifier (chance level), making the failure an unflagged imagination failure---an unknown unknown at planning time. As a secondary contribution, we show that \textbf{task-conditioned weighting of Effective Free Energy components} over the same world model yields lane keeping ($81.2 \pm 1.8$\% route completion) and obstacle avoidance (28/28 avoided, \emph{using privileged coordinates}) in the CARLA simulator, with runtime weight modulation enabling post-evasion centering.

llm.title_ja: 事後・事前認識ギャップ：世界モデルの想像がタスク関連シグナルを運ぶのに失敗するとき
llm.tldr_ja: CARLA自動運転シミュレータを用いた事例研究により、リカレント状態空間モデルにおいて事後状態と想像された事前状態の間で障害物情報が失われる「事後・事前ギャップ」が存在することを特定した。
llm.problem: モデルベースプランナーが想定する移行モデルがタスク関連シグナルを忠実に伝搬するという仮定が、実際には十分に測定されていないこと。
llm.method: 観測フィルタリングされた事後状態と想像された展開状態に同一のプローブを適用し、情報の損失を障害物情報のAUC変化として測定した。
llm.result: 事後状態では高い認識性能を示す一方で、事前状態では情報が単調に減衰し、プランナーの不確実性指標もそれを検知できない未知の失敗を引き起こすことを示した。
keywords_ja: モデルベースプランニング

2611.14953.title: RSLiveBench-UAV: A Continually Evolving Vision-Language Benchmark for Aerial Spatial Intelligence
2611.14953.abstract: Aerial spatial intelligence (ASI) requires models to understand objects and spatial relationships across changing viewpoints and scales. Evaluating these abilities as models evolve calls for fresh physical observations, yet producing new aerial spatial questions requires repeatedly establishing entity identities, geometric references, and cross-view correspondences. We introduce \textbf{RSLiveBench-UAV}, a continually evolving vision-language benchmark driven by recurring acquisition of real UAV imagery. Its update protocol admits images captured after the preceding release and delays answer disclosure. An entity-centered production workflow uses geometry-assisted association to link repeated observations of physical vehicles, reuse human-verified attributes, and combine them with view-specific annotations and spatial references for traceable question generation. All tasks use deterministic scoring without model judges. We evaluate 30 general-purpose, remote-sensing, and embodied models on 35,491 question records from ten scenes, covering 17 tasks across 2D perception, 3D perception, cross-view perception, and reasoning. All 18 tested embodied models outperform the three selected remote-sensing comparators in Overall, although the strongest embodied model scores 43.29 versus 59.88 for GPT-6-Astra. Fine-grained vehicle recognition remains challenging, and performance varies across heights and camera pitches. Retrospective scene-group comparisons and rolling-window replay characterize score-pattern consistency under scene renewal. RSLiveBench-UAV connects fresh physical observations, entity-centered answer production, and systematic model evaluation to support continual assessment of ASI. Benchmark will release at https://rslivebench.space

llm.title_ja: RSLiveBench-UAV：空中空間知能のための継続的に進化するビジョン言語ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 変化する視点やスケールにわたる空中空間知能モデルを評価するため、実際のUAV画像の定期的な取得と幾何学的アソシエーションに基づく継続的進化型ベンチマークRSLiveBench-UAVを提案した。
llm.problem: 空中空間知能モデルの進化を評価するための、新鮮な物理的観測や新たな空間的質問を作成するための体系的な枠組みが必要であること。
llm.method: 追加画像を取り込む更新プロトコルと、幾何学支援アソシエーションを用いてエンティティをリンクし決定論的スコアリングを行うエンティティ中心の生産ワークフローを構築した。
llm.result: 30のモデルを評価し、すべてのテスト済み具身体モデルがリモートセンシング比較モデルを上回った一方で、微粒子の車両認識など依然として大きな課題があることを示した。

2611.14942.title: Emergent Vision-Shaped Thinking in Text-Only Reasoning through Multimodal Training
2611.14942.abstract: Does multimodal training shape how a language model thinks, even when the input is text only? We test this with targeted causal ablations across 10 multimodal configurations from 6 model families, with matched text-only backbones and cross-family transfer controls. We contrast spatial-imagery tasks that invite mental scene construction with symbol-manipulation tasks solvable by symbolic rules alone. We identify a vision-language axis in hidden-state space and ablate its projection at inference. In Chameleon-7B, this ablation drops accuracy on BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) navigate by 27.6 pp while leaving boolean expressions intact (+5.6 pp), a 33.2 pp double dissociation. The effect is direction-specific and layer-localized, extends to mental-simulation tasks such as mental rotation, paper folding, and perspective taking, and is not explained by task difficulty, reasoning depth, or sequential update load. Together, these results reveal emergent vision-shaped thinking (EVT): text-only reasoning that causally recruits representations introduced or strengthened by vision-language training, without assuming an image-like internal format. The measured effect is spatially concentrated at 7-8B and broadens to non-spatial visual attribute binding in the tested 32B configuration. In dual-path unified models (BAGEL, Janus-Pro), the causal handle localizes to the generation pathway as a compact one-dimensional carrier. The understanding pathway also encodes spatial information in a higher-rank, probe-decodable form, but is not the causal handle. To separate decodability from causal use, we analyze concentration, alignment, and semantic location. These diagnostics explain why behavior, probing, and intervention can diverge. Multimodal training thus reshapes the geometry of text-only reasoning, not just how visual input is processed.

llm.title_ja: マルチモーダル訓練を通じたテキストのみの推論における創発的視覚的思考
llm.tldr_ja: マルチモーダル訓練がテキスト入力のみの場合でも言語モデルの思考方法に影響を与えることを因果的アブレーションにより実証し、視覚的思考の創発を確認した。
llm.problem: マルチモーダル訓練が画像入力なしのテキストのみの推論にどのように影響するか、その内部メカニズムが十分に解明されていないこと。
llm.method: 6つのモデルファミリーの10のマルチモーダル構成にわたる標的を絞った因果的アブレーションを用いて、隠れ空間におけるビジョン言語軸の投影を推論時にアブレーションした。
llm.result: 特定のモデルにおいて空間ナビゲーションタスクの精度が大幅に低下する一方、論理式などは維持されるという二重解離を確認し、マルチモーダル訓練がテキスト推論の幾何学を再形成することを示した。
keywords_ja: 因果的アブレーション

2611.14941.title: Reality Perception Gap: Are AI-Manipulated Video Detectors Ready for the Real World?
2611.14941.abstract: AI-manipulated video detectors are typically evaluated on clean, curated datasets. In deployment, however, videos have usually passed through repost compression on social-media platforms and sometimes were captured by imperfect hardware. To measure detection under these conditions, we introduce Reality Perception Gap (RPG), a benchmark of 10,000 videos from frontier generators and partially synthetic edits, processed with cross-platform repost compression and paired with real footage that carries camera-side optical artifacts. RPG also includes socially fragile content, such as crime and wartime footage, where fabricated videos can cause severe social harm. Across 18 detectors, none catches more than 15% of fakes at a 1% false-positive rate. A positive control and a re-encoding sweep separate two sources of failure: generator and content shift degrades detectors before any compression, and repost compression erases the low-level traces that the artifact-based detectors relies on. Existing detectors therefore struggle when deployment conditions strip away the generation artifacts they rely on. These complementary failures suggest that robust detection requires training under deployment conditions and combining low-level, temporal, and semantic evidence, where passive detection may have reached its limits.

llm.title_ja: 現実知覚ギャップ：AI改ざんビデオ検出器は現実世界の準備ができているか？
llm.tldr_ja: ソーシャルメディアの再エンコード圧縮や不完全なハードウェアによる光学アーティファクトの下で、既存のAI改ざんビデオ検出器が大幅に性能低下することを10,000本の動画からなるベンチマークRPGで明らかにした。
llm.problem: AI改ざんビデオ検出器がクリーンなデータセットで評価されている一方、デプロイ時には再圧縮や撮影時のアーティファクトの影響を受けること。
llm.method: 最先端の生成器や部分的に合成された編集物、クロスプラットフォームの再圧縮処理を組み込んだ10,000本のビデオベンチマークRPGを構築し、18の検出器を評価した。
llm.result: どの検出器も1%の誤陽率で15%以上のフェイクを検出できず、生成アーティファクトに依存した受動的検出の限界を示した。
keywords_ja: ディープフェイク検出
圧縮アーティファクト

2611.14918.title: DIVAL: Diffeomorphic Vector-Field Alignment for Nonholonomic Motion Planning
2611.14918.abstract: Conventional vector-field-based motion planners for nonholonomic robots consist of two steps: first designing a nominal vector field and then controlling the robot to follow it to approach the target. However, a nonholonomic robot cannot follow the vector field instantaneously and may collide with obstacles, due to the inevitable mismatch between the robot's initial heading and the vector field's direction. This paper proposes a diffeomorphic vector-field alignment (DIVAL) method, which aligns the vector field's direction with the robot's initial heading so the robot can follow the vector field from the start. Specifically, the nominal vector field is locally reshaped by applying a diffeomorphic deformation to the workspace, such that the reshaped vector field has the same direction as the robot's heading at the initial position and coincides with the nominal vector field outside the deformed region. Since DIVAL eliminates the initial heading mismatch, the nonholonomic robot can maintain heading alignment with the reshaped vector field throughout the motion. This heading alignment further ensures that the robot preserves the nominal vector field's properties, including obstacle avoidance, convergence to the target, and smooth control signals. Numerical simulations provide vector-field-tracking baselines where the nominal vector fields are reshaped with DIVAL. Compared to the original baselines, the proposed method achieves collision-free convergence in all trials and avoids control discontinuities. Hardware experiments on a ground vehicle further demonstrate collision-free convergence across different targets and initial conditions under real-world disturbances.

llm.title_ja: DIVAL：非ホロノミックモーション計画のための微分同相ベクトル場アライメント
llm.tldr_ja: 非ホロノミックロボットの初期見出しとベクトル場の方向の不一致による衝突や制御不連続を解消するため、ワークスペースの局所的変形によりベクトル場を整列させるDIVAL手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 非ホロノミックロボットは初期見出しとベクトル場の不一致により即座に追従できず、障害物に衝突する可能性があること。
llm.method: ワークスペースに微分同相変形を適用して公称ベクトル場を局所的に再形し、初期位置でのロボットの見出しと同じ方向に揃えるDIVAL手法を構築した。
llm.result: 数値シミュレーションにおいてすべての試行で衝突のない収束を達成し、地上車両を用いた実機実験でも実世界の不確実性下で有効性を示した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング
非ホロノミックロボット

2611.14897.title: Social Engineering Attack Detection in Corporate Communications
2611.14897.abstract: Social Engineering attacks continue to pose a significant risk to the corporate world with a growing level of sophistication. It is difficult to distinguish between authentic and phishing communication via email, chat, and phone. They pose a risk of exposing trade secrets and confidential communications and can create a chain of attack from lower-level employees up to executives. Therefore, we study this growing threat using real-world datasets to build baseline machine-learning models. Our TF-IDF models classify emails as phishing or safe, achieving accuracy above 90%. We build on this by exploring whether psychological manipulation and persuasion indicators can be measured to play a significant role in detecting phishing. Instead of relying solely on surface-level lexical features, we derive interpretable lexicon-based indicators of urgency, trust, greed, and other persuasion cues from the combined email dataset. By evaluating these manipulation-oriented features on their own, we measure how much signal they carry (ROC-AUC of 0.74 on a held-out test split) and test whether they transfer to held-out email sources.

llm.title_ja: 企業通信におけるソーシャルエンジニアリング攻撃の検出
llm.tldr_ja: メール、チャット、電話における巧妙なフィッシング攻撃を検出するため、TF-IDFモデルに加えて緊急性や信頼などの心理的・説得的指標を組み込んだ機械学習ベースラインを構築した。
llm.problem: 企業においてソーシャルエンジニアリング攻撃が高度化しており、本物の通信とフィッシングの区別が困難であること。
llm.method: 実世界データセットを用いてメールを分類するTF-IDFモデルを構築するとともに、解釈可能な語彙ベースの緊急性、信頼、貪欲などの説得的指標を導出して評価した。
llm.result: TF-IDFモデルで90%以上の精度を達成し、心理的指標単体でもROC-AUC 0.74の信号を捉えられることを示した。
keywords_ja: ソーシャルエンジニアリング

2611.14895.title: HeadIO: Body-Frame Heading Decomposition for Neural Inertial Odometry on Head-Mounted Devices
2611.14895.abstract: Inertial odometry (IO) using only Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) enables camera-free head tracking in head-mounted devices such as VR headsets, AR glasses, and earbuds. Prior IO methods operate in a gravity-aligned world frame, which is not yaw-equivariant. Yaw augmentation improves robustness but does not guarantee equivariance; learned equivariant layers achieve it, but EqNIO's full pipeline costs nearly 3$\times$ the FLOPs of ours.
