While raw body-frame IMU inputs are inherently yaw-invariant, head tilt redistributes both gravity and motion signals across device axes, making the representation tilt-variant. We propose HeadIO, which combines a body-frame heading decomposition with a bidirectional Mamba backbone for head-mounted inertial odometry. Our decomposition achieves tilt invariance by separating gravity-aligned and horizontal components using only the tilt component of device orientation. We evaluate on four head-mounted datasets and find that HeadIO improves RTE-5s by 8.1% (0.260 m $\to$ 0.239 m) over world-frame methods with learned equivariant layers on Nymeria, the largest benchmark dataset, at nearly 3$\times$ lower FLOPs and 8$\times$ fewer parameters. HeadIO achieves state-of-the-art performance on our primary metric, RTE-5s, on all Aria-glasses datasets, which natively provide body-frame semantics for our decomposition method. We further evaluate the IMU-only deployment scenario on Nymeria, where HeadIO remains state-of-the-art. We show that our method relies mainly on tilt accuracy, which can be obtained from the gravity signal; for yaw, a single-coefficient gyroscope correction removes 11.6% of the yaw error and improves RTE-5s by 2.5%, and sparse external yaw corrections (for example, one every 30 s) can improve RTE-5s by 12.0%. Our decomposition is lightweight, composes with any backbone, and is suitable for real-time deployment on head-mounted devices.

llm.title_ja: HeadIO: ヘッドマウントデバイス上のニューラル慣性オドメトリに向けたボディフレーム方位分解手法
llm.tldr_ja: HeadIOは、ボディフレームの方位分解と双方向Mambaバックボーンを組み合わせ、低演算量かつ高精度なヘッドマウント型慣性オドメトリを実現する。
llm.problem: 従来手法は重力基準の世界座標系を前提とし、方位等変性の欠如や高い演算コストという課題があった。
llm.method: デバイスの傾き情報のみを用いて重力方向と水平成分を分離するボディフレーム方位分解と双方向Mambaを採用する。
llm.result: 最大のベンチマークデータセットNymeriaにおいて、世界座標系手法と比較して演算量を約3分の1、パラメータ数を約8分の1に抑えつつRTE-5sを8.1%改善した。
keywords_ja: ヘッドマウントディスプレイ

2611.14880.title: FOE-Dreamer: Deployment-Efficient Learning of Cyber Defense Policies in Operational Networks
2611.14880.abstract: Autonomous cyber defense is widely studied with deep reinforcement learning, but most work trains policies inside simulators because learning requires many trial-and-error interactions. Simulator-based training carries a fidelity gap: trained policies face authentication delays, partial action failures, service dependencies, and user traffic patterns that the simulator did not represent, and degrade on transfer. Training directly in the network being defended removes the gap but makes every interaction slow and costly, so sample efficiency becomes the binding constraint. Model-based reinforcement learning has reduced sample requirements on games and physical robots by orders of magnitude by planning inside a learned world model, but it has not been applied to defenders trained in operational networks. We present FOE-Dreamer (Factored Opponent-Enhanced Dreamer), a model-based reinforcement learning framework that trains a defender online and directly in a network on cloud infrastructure, without a simulator stage. FOE-Dreamer separates three sources of variation in the latent state: a controllable component driven by defender actions, an exogenous component driven by benign user activity, and an opponent embedding inferred from defender-observable signals alone. Separating the components reduces the variance in policy gradients during planning in imagination. Against two scripted attacker profiles with user activity emulated by the GHOSTS framework on an 8-host OpenStack testbed, FOE-Dreamer trains within a 3-day budget on a single GPU and achieves about 2$\times$ better episode loss than Rainbow and IQN baselines under matched compute. Both the factoring and the opponent model contribute to the gain, and the learned latents are consistent with the intended separation.
2611.14880.comment: 14 pages, 5 figures. To appear in the proceedings of the Annual Computer Security Applications Conference (ACSAC)

llm.title_ja: FOE-Dreamer: 運用ネットワークにおけるサイバー防御方策のデプロイ効率的な学習
llm.tldr_ja: FOE-Dreamerは、シミュレータを介さずクラウド上のネットワークで直接防御エージェントをオンライン学習する、モデルベース強化学習フレームワークである。
llm.problem: シミュレータベースの学習は現実とのギャップ（適応遅延や部分的な行動失敗など）があり、実ネットワークでの直接学習はサンプル効率が致命的な制約となる。
llm.method: 潜在状態における制御可能成分、外因性成分、相手の埋め込みを分離するモデルベース強化学習により、想像上の計画における方策勾配の分散を低減する。
llm.result: 単一GPUの3日間の予算内で訓練でき、同等の計算リソース下でRainbowおよびIQNベースラインと比較して約2倍のエピソード損失改善を達成した。
keywords_ja: サイバーセキュリティ
モデルベース強化学習

2611.14856.title: Honest Fusion Evaluation for Cross-Domain Deepfake Detection: Leakage Audits and Tail Robustness
2611.14856.abstract: Cross-domain video deepfake detection increasingly uses frozen foundation-model experts, combined by calibrated score averaging, a per-video router picking one expert, or a learned head over concatenated features. Expressive routing and feature fusion are often reported to beat plain averaging. Across a 22-dataset frozen-expert testbed, we find those gains are largely evaluation artifacts. A corner theorem locates the gap routing aims to close: because AUC depends only on score ordering, the best any score-space router can do is an oracle reading the test label to pick each video's expert, a ceiling no realisable, label-blind router reaches. The theorem does not order real routers against a calibrated global average; the case against routing is empirical, and no router we test beats that average. Feature fusion reads raw features, falls outside the theorem, and is audited empirically. Reported gains trace to leakage: holding out one dataset leaks siblings sharing identities and reals (over-crediting routing), while holding out one manipulation keeps that dataset's reals in training (over-crediting feature fusion). A $2\times 2$ over fold and evaluation granularity pins the $+2.6$pp feature-fusion "win" to the fold alone: 12/12 significant under leaky folds vs. 0/12 under honest family-held-out folds, where both gains vanish. Fusion still pays off in the tail of hard videos and families: as experts are added, videos every expert misclassifies drop from 15.2% to 2.3%, and global calibrated fusion (InvB) beats the best single expert on worst-family AUC, selective risk (AURC), and low-false-positive recall, stably across protocols. Practitioners should calibrate and combine globally, hold out whole dataset families, and measure tail performance. For score-space routing under ranking metrics, honest evaluation and expert diversity matter more than combiner complexity.
2611.14856.comment: Accepted at WACV 2027. 19 pages including supplementary material; 6 figures, 10 tables. Code: https://github.com/lukegcollins/WACV27-HFEFCDD

llm.title_ja: クロスドメインディープフェイク検出のための誠実な融合評価：リーク監査とテール頑健性
llm.tldr_ja: クロスドメインのディープフェイク検出におけるルーティングや特徴融合の性能向上の多くは評価時のデータリークに起因しており、厳格な評価を行うと利得が消失することを解明した。
llm.problem: クロスドメイン動画ディープフェイク検出において、複雑なルーティングや特徴融合手法による性能向上が報告されているが、その評価の妥当性が不明確である。
llm.method: 22のデータセットからなる凍結エキスパートテストベッドを用いて、コーナ定理による理論的分析と、厳格なフォールド分割に基づく実証的監査を実施する。
llm.result: 報告されていた特徴融合の優位性はデータリークによるものであり、家族単位で分割した誠実な評価プロトコルでは利得が消失することを示した。
keywords_ja: ディープフェイク検出

2611.14853.title: Can I join you? Extended Social Force Based Model with Predictive Control and Barrier Functions for Humanoid Group Repositioning Amidst Obstacles
2611.14853.abstract: As social and service robots increasingly share interaction spaces in public, they may form groups while coordinating tasks or interacting with humans. Initial group formation alone is insufficient in dynamic settings, because it can be disrupted when a person or another agent joins, leaves, or passes through the group. Although group dynamics and repositioning have been widely studied in swarm robotics and virtual-agent settings, little attention has been given to socially appropriate repositioning behaviors in groups of humanoid robots. Existing social-force-based approaches provide a useful foundation for group behavior, but they have limited obstacle handling, and can produce unsafe behavior as environmental complexity increases. We propose a novel framework that modulates traditional Social Force, guided by Model Predictive Control (MPC) to plan ahead, bounded by Control Barrier Functions (CBF) to increase safety for robot groups repositioning behaviors. This approach aims to produce safer and socially aware group repositioning behaviors under various group formation disturbance. We evaluate the method in simulation through an ablation study and an online user study. The results show that our proposed method can produce smoother and safer repositioning behaviors in complex environments while preserving social appropriateness.

llm.title_ja: 仲間に入れてもらえる？障害物の中でのヒューマノイド群の再配置に向けた予測制御とバリア関数を伴う拡張社会力モデル
llm.tldr_ja: ヒューマノイドロボットの群れが動的な環境や障害物の中で社会的配慮を持ちつつ円滑に再配置を行うため、モデル予測制御と制御バリア関数で社会力モデルを拡張したフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 動的環境において人間や他のエージェントの出入りによってロボット群の隊形が乱れやすく、従来の社会力モデルでは障害物回避や安全性の保証が不十分である。
llm.method: 伝統的な社会力モデルを、先読みのためのモデル予測制御（MPC）と安全性保証のための制御バリア関数（CBF）で変調した統合フレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: シミュレーションの統合評価およびオンラインのユーザー実験により、社会的適切性を維持しながら、複雑な環境でよりスムーズで安全な再配置行動を実現できることを示した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2611.14840.title: SPIRE: Task-agnostic embodied continual learning through autonomous situation inference and causal motor-primitive reuse
2611.14840.abstract: Embodied continual learning requires controllers to infer changing situations, retain prior behavior and reuse motor skills without task labels or known boundaries. The challenge is deciding when to recover earlier behavior and which skills can support new learning. We introduce Situation-guided Primitive Integration for Recurrent Embodiment (SPIRE), a recurrent-spiking system that infers latent contexts from action-outcome evidence and learns context-specific motor actors online. Mature actors become protected sources that combine with a target-context residual to drive recurrent-spiking motor populations. Across coordinate, three-joint and hidden-force control, SPIRE maintained control, autonomously inferred situations, retained prior behavior and accelerated acquisition of an unseen source composition, reducing mean interactions to criterion by approximately 40% relative to matched fresh controllers. Rewinding compatible source actors impaired early acquisition in every matched intervention, demonstrating causal reuse. Against seven recurrent continual-learning and modular-control comparators, SPIRE achieved 2.4 times the mean prior-learning advantage of the strongest eligible task-free alternative selected for each paired stream. These results demonstrate autonomous recovery and causal reuse of motor skills for new learning in continuous embodied control.

llm.title_ja: SPIRE: 自律的な状況推論と因果的運動プリミティブの再利用を通じたタスク非依存な身体性継続学習
llm.tldr_ja: SPIREは、行動と結果の証拠から潜在文脈を自帰還型スパイクシステムで推論し、タスクラベルなしで過去の行動を保持しながら運動スキルを因果的に再利用する継続学習フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 身体性継続学習では、タスクラベルや境界なしに状況変化を推論し、過去の行動を保持しつつどのスキルを新しい学習に再利用すべきか決定することが困難である。
llm.method: 行動結果のエビデンスから潜在文脈を推論し、文脈特異的な運動アクターをオンラインで学習・保護して再利用する再帰型スパイクシステムを提案する。
llm.result: 複数の制御課題において制御を維持し、過去の行動を保持しながら未知のソース構成の獲得を加速させ、同等の未調整コントローラに比べて基準までの相互作用回数を約40%削減した。
keywords_ja: スパイクニューラルネット

2611.14834.title: Learning Low-Latency Action Verification for Frozen Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.14834.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have made significant progress in general-purpose robotic manipulation. However, sampled action sequences can be ineffective, while evaluating alternatives with computationally expensive verifiers adds latency at each policy query. In this work, we propose HDH, a lightweight framework that uses hindsight from a frozen VLA's own deployments to improve action verification. The framework has three stages. First, we deploy the policy and collect its autonomous rollouts. We then train a compact action verifier to assign each action chunk a predicted task-success score. Finally, the frozen VLA generates action candidates, and the verifier selects the candidate with the highest score for execution. Across four LIBERO-10 tasks, HDH achieves an average success rate of 82.3\% and on three real-world manipulation tasks, HDH improves average success over the baseline policy by 22.6\%.

llm.title_ja: 凍結されたビジョン・言語・行動モデルに向けた低遅延行動検証の学習
llm.tldr_ja: HDHは、凍結されたVLAモデル自身の実行履歴を活用して軽量な行動検証器を訓練し、ポリシークエリごとの遅延を抑えつつ高精度な行動選択を実現するフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 汎用マニプレーションにおいてVLAモデルがサンプリングする行動配列は効果的でない場合があり、高価な検証器の利用は各ポリシークエリで遅延を増大させる。
llm.method: 自律ロールアウトから得た事後情報を用いて、行動チャンクに成功スコアを割り当てるコンパクトな行動検証器を訓練し、VLAの候補から最高スコアのものを選択して実行する。
llm.result: LIBERO-10の4タスクで平均82.3%の成功率を達成し、3つの実世界のマニプレーションタスクにおいてベースラインポリシーを平均22.6%上回る成功率の向上を実現した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2611.14769.title: Leaderboard Hacking: Preference-Based Model Evaluations are Vulnerable to Manipulation
2611.14769.abstract: Arena-style rankings of language models are a widely used evaluation framework in online leaderboards, research papers, and model evaluation in production. These rankings aim to realistically assess model performance using pairwise comparisons of anonymous models on user prompts, aggregating votes via the Bradley-Terry model to produce the final ranking. However, we find that these leaderboards are highly vulnerable to several manipulation strategies that unscrupulous providers could use to boost a model's rank: strategic voting (individual votes that boost a model's rank, including votes on irrelevant models), strategic prompting (choosing prompts that favor a model), and strategic nomination (boosting the rank of a model by inserting irrelevant models). We demonstrate these effects on public leaderboard data, analyze the circumstances that cause these vulnerabilities, and describe approaches to safeguard against each attack. Notably, these issues hold for any preference-based evaluation using the Bradley-Terry model that allows open prompting, voting, or model submission. These manipulations boost the rank of nearly every tested model; each attack can boost a model by up to 15-20 places in a ranking and, combined, they can boost a model by up to 45 places.

llm.title_ja: リーダーボードハッキング：選好ベースのモデル評価は操作に対して脆弱である
llm.tldr_ja: オンラインリーダーボードなどで広く使われるブラジ・テリーモデルに基づくペア比較評価は、戦略的投票やプロンプト選択などの複数の操作手法に対して極めて脆弱であることを実証した。
llm.problem: アリーナスタイルのモデルランキングはモデル性能の現実的な評価を目指しているが、悪意あるプロバイダがランキングを不当に引き上げる操作に対して脆弱かどうか検証する必要がある。
llm.method: 公開リーダーボードデータを用いて、戦略的投票、戦略的プロンプト、戦略的指名という3つの操作戦略の効果を実証し、その脆弱性の原因を分析する。
llm.result: 各攻撃によりテストされたほぼすべてのモデルの順位を15〜20位、組み合わせることで最大45位まで不当に引き上げられることを示した。

2611.14762.title: Open-Source Transtibial Prosthetic Bypass Preserving Joint Alignment: Gait Learning and Kinematic Evaluation
2611.14762.abstract: Prosthetic bypasses allow able-bodied individuals to walk with a prosthesis, enabling safe early-stage testing of new prosthetic devices before clinical trials. However, existing transtibial bypasses impose constraints, such as a contralateral shoe lift or a lateral offset of the prosthesis, and their effects on gait remain poorly documented. We present an open-source transtibial prosthetic bypass that preserves part of the sagittal knee mobility without these constraints. Six able-bodied participants familiarized themselves with the bypass for approximately 10~min, then walked on a treadmill with and without it, and joint kinematics were recorded with motion capture and then extracted with OpenSim. All participants were able to walk without handrail support, although single stance remained shorter on the bypass side (27% vs. 45% of the gait cycle). Bypass-side ankle kinematics were consistent with those reported for transtibial prosthesis users, whereas peak knee flexion during swing decreased from 61° to 36° (p<0.001) and hip range of the sound leg increased from 35° to 51° (p<0.01). Although gait with the bypass does not fully replicate that of prosthesis users, it yielded consistent gait patterns after only 10~min of learning. This bypass therefore provides a useful tool for the lower-limb prosthetics research community, facilitating preliminary experiments with able-bodied participants.

llm.title_ja: 関節アライメントを維持するオープンソース下腿義足バイパス：歩行学習と運動学的評価
llm.tldr_ja: 関節アライメントを維持しつつ下腿モビリティの一部を保持するオープンソースの下腿義足バイパスを開発し、健常者参加者による短い学習期間での歩行パターンを評価した。
llm.problem: 既存の下腿義足バイパスは靴の厚底化や外側オフセットなどの制約を課し、歩行への影響についての十分な文書化がなされていない。
llm.method: 膝の矢状面モビリティを部分的に維持するオープンソースのバイパスを設計し、健常者6名が約10分間慣れた後にトレッドミル歩行を行い、モーションキャプチャで運動データを記録した。
llm.result: 義足歩行者で見られるアキレス腱側の運動特性とおおむね一致し、わずか10分の学習で一貫した歩行パターンが得られることを実証した。
keywords_ja: オープンソースハードウェア

2611.14729.title: SunLightBots: Turning sunlight into self-sustained, high-power motion in soft robots
2611.14729.abstract: Soft robots built from active materials can directly convert environmental stimuli into motion, offering a route to energy autonomy and embodied control. However, environmental energy is generally harvested at low power, whereas rapid, mechanically demanding actions require high mechanical output power. Reconciling this mismatch while sustaining self-regulated cyclic actuation is challenging, particularly at the subgram scale, where limited payload capacity constrains the integration of conventional power and control hardware. Here, we present SunLightBots, a class of subgram, sunlight-powered, untethered soft robots that achieve autonomous locomotion under continuous illumination near 1 Sun (100 mW/cm2). Their operation is enabled by a self-resetting snapping (SRS) mechanism that integrates liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) with snap-through instability to accumulate solar energy supplied at low power, release it as rapid, high-power motion, and reset through photothermal-mechanical feedback. Through coordinated optimization of the LCE actuation temperature, photothermal conversion, actuation stress, and structural energy barrier, the system operates near 1 Sun and achieves a peak mass-specific mechanical power of 89 W/kg. At this irradiance, the optimized LCE generates an actuation stress of 0.1 MPa at approximately 60 deg C. SunLightBots demonstrate sustained swimming, crawling, and repeated impulsive jumping. Under 1.5 Suns, the swimmer advances more than three body lengths per cycle. This work provides a materials-mechanics route toward autonomous soft robots powered entirely by the environment.

llm.title_ja: SunLightBots：太陽光をソフトロボットの自己持続的で高出力な運動へと変換する
llm.tldr_ja: SunLightBotsは、液晶エラストマーと自励リセットスナップ機構を統合し、低電力の太陽光を蓄えて高出力な動的運動や駆動を自律的に生み出すサブグラム級のソフトロボットである。
llm.problem: 環境エネルギーの収集は一般に低電力である一方、高速で機械的に負荷の高い動作には高出力が必要であり、特にサブグラム規模での両立が困難である。
llm.method: 液晶エラストマー（LCE）とスナップスルー不安定性を統合した自励リセットスナップ（SRS）機構により、太陽光エネルギーを蓄えて高速な高出力運動として放出する。
llm.result: 連続照明のもとで自律的な遊泳、這行、繰り返し跳躍を実現し、1.5サンの光量では1サイクルあたり体長の3倍以上前進する優れた機動性を達成した。

2611.14685.title: Terrain-Aware Thompson Sampling for Multi-Drone Search and Rescue
2611.14685.abstract: In this work, we propose a decentralized terrain-aware multi-drone Thompson Sampling algorithm tailored for search and rescue (SAR) applications. A probability distribution of locating a lost person is informed by terrain data, using established SAR models (displacement ring, elevation, watershed, dispersion angle, and track offset) derived from historical SAR case data on lost person behavior. Exploration is conducted by a team of drones using Thompson Sampling, where candidate actions are selected by drawing samples from this probability distribution, represented by a per-cell Gaussian posterior whose mean and variance are updated through Bayesian inference. This approach balances exploration of uncertain regions with exploitation of high-probability areas to locate a lost person. Observation uncertainty is incorporated through fractional forest coverage, which measures the percentage of an observation occluded by tree coverage and accounts for reduced detection performance in densely vegetated areas. Simulations using real SAR case data (YOSAR) evaluate the proposed method against a coverage planner and a probabilistic active search method in search regions of 1.5 and 3.8 square kilometers, with 5, 10, 15, and 20 agents flying at 50 km/hr. We demonstrate that our method achieves a success rate of approximately 87% within 60 to 247 seconds in the 1.5 square kilometer region, and success rates of approximately 75% to 91% within 161 to 466 seconds in the 3.8 square kilometer region, across different agent configurations.
2611.14685.comment: Accepted to the 18th International Symposium on Distributed Autonomous Robotic Systems (DARS 2026)

llm.title_ja: 地形を考慮した複数ドローンによる捜索救助のためのトンプソンサンプリング
llm.tldr_ja: 迷失者の過去の行動モデルと地形データを反映した確率分布に基づき、複数ドローンがトンプソンサンプリングにより効率的に探索を行う分散型アルゴリズムを提案する。
llm.problem: 捜索救助活動において、迷失者の発見確率分布や森林被覆による観測不確実性を考慮しつつ、複数のドローンが効率的に未探索領域の探索と高確率領域の活用を両立する必要がある。
llm.method: 過去の捜索救助事例に基づく地形モデルとガウス事後分布を用いたベイズ推論によるトンプソンサンプリングを組み合わせた分散型アルゴリズムを構築する。
llm.result: 1.5平方キロメートルの領域で約87%、3.8平方キロメートルの領域で75%〜91%の成功率を数分以内で達成できることをシミュレーションで実証した。
keywords_ja: トンプソンサンプリング

2611.14488.title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
2611.14488.abstract: Memory-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) policies are meant to remember what happened. Many of them, however, fill memory by time: they sample frames uniformly across the episode and stamp each frame with its time step. Because time passes even when nothing happens, such a memory may not tell waiting from working. We show that it does not. On the counting tasks of RoboMME, we make the robot briefly pause or fidget its wrist. Such a null event changes nothing the task depends on, yet a released memory VLA counts the interval as work done and stops early. We call this failure phantom progress. It cuts success from 47 to 16 of 50 on one task and from 44 to 10 on the other. When the same frames are withheld from memory, success returns, so the cause lies in memory rather than in the interruption itself. We trace the failure to a temporal shortcut: because demonstrations proceed at a steady pace, elapsed time predicts progress. Indeed, rescaling the time stamps alone makes the policy stop early when the clock runs fast and repeat when it runs slow. Surprisingly, removing the time encoding does not cure the failure, because the frames of a null event still occupy slots of the time-sampled memory. Across RoboMME's released designs, vulnerability follows how memory is indexed. Of the fixes the diagnosis suggests, training with injected pauses does not remove the failure and impairs counting, whereas indexing memory by events recovers half or more of the loss without retraining. A memory meant to remember what happened should count events rather than clock ticks.
2611.14488.hf_summary_en: Memory in vision-language-action policies can mistake pauses for progress because it is indexed by time, causing early stopping, while event-based indexing mitigates this without retraining.

llm.title_ja: あなたのロボットの記憶はただの時計か？記憶拡張VLAポリシーにおける時間的ショートカット
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚・言語・行動（VLA）ポリシーの記憶は時間でインデックス付けされているため、一時停止を進捗と誤認して早期停止を引き起こすが、イベントベースのインデックス付けにより再学習なしでこれが緩和される。
llm.problem: 時間ベースの記憶インデックスを持つVLAポリシーが、停止やためらいを進捗と誤認し早期停止を起こすこと
llm.method: 記憶のインデックス付けを時間ではなくイベントベースに変更し、中断や無駄なイベントの影響を排除する
llm.result: イベントベースのインデックス付けにより、再学習なしでファントムプログレスによる性能低下の半分以上を回復した
keywords_ja: 時間的ショートカット
ファントムプログレス

2611.14488.tldr_en: It is shown that a memory meant to remember what happened should count events rather than clock ticks, and it is traced to a temporal shortcut: because demonstrations proceed at a steady pace, elapsed time predicts progress.

2611.14470.title: TanCRAFT: Context-Reasoned Anticipatory Feedback for Assembly Tasks
2611.14470.abstract: Preventing human error in physical assembly tasks requires assistance systems that can intervene before mistakes are made. This is especially challenging in settings where users are free to choose the construction order and correctness depends on the evolving assembly rather than a fixed next step. We present TanCRAFT, a four-stage real-time predictive assistance system that tracks the scene state, reasons about the current partial assembly, forecasts the near-future motion of manipulated pieces, and intervenes when the predicted placement is incompatible with the target. We instantiate our framework and confirm its effectiveness in a controlled tangram assembly task through offline benchmarks and a within-subject user study. Our findings show that the predictive feedback significantly reduces mistakes relative to unguided and reactive sessions, while yielding the lowest mean perceived workload and shortest mean completion time. Overall, these results demonstrate the value of predictive feedback for error prevention and provide a step toward cost-aware assistance for automation and human-robot workcells.
2611.14470.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

llm.title_ja: TanCRAFT：組み立てタスクのための文脈推論型先読みフィードバック
llm.tldr_ja: TanCRAFTは、シーン状態の追跡、組み立て状態の推論、把持部品の未来の動きの予測、目標との不一致時の介入を行う4段階のリアルタイム予測支援システムであり、タスクのミスを大幅に削減する。
llm.problem: 物理的な組み立て作業において、固定された手順ではなく変化する組み立て状態に依存する場合に人間のミスを事前に防ぐことの難しさ
llm.method: シーン状態の追跡、部分的な組み立ての推論、操作部品の近未来の動きの予測、目標不適合時の介入を行う4段階のリアルタイム予測支援システムを構築する
llm.result: 予測的フィードバックにより、未誘導および受動的なセッションと比較してミスが大幅に減少し、知覚される作業負荷の平均が最も低く、完了時間が最も短くなった

2611.14470.tldr_en: TanCRAFT is presented, a four-stage real-time predictive assistance system that tracks the scene state, reasons about the current partial assembly, forecasts the near-future motion of manipulated pieces, and intervenes when the predicted placement is incompatible with the target.

2611.14440.title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model
2611.14440.abstract: Understanding 4D scenes is a core challenge in visual intelligence, requiring models to jointly capture scene geometry, appearance, and dynamics from partial observations. However, existing approaches are subdivided into feedforward models for direct geometric prediction, and generative models for visual synthesis. We introduce UGG, a unified framework for 4D scene understanding that jointly models RGB video and geometric representations such as depth and camera pose. By assigning different noise levels across modalities and time, UGG formulates visual generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion within a single generative model. This flexible formulation enables the model to learn from diverse, heterogeneous datasets with different subsets of geometric and visual annotations. Furthermore, our generative formulation enables inference-time search over multiple plausible scene hypotheses, using geometric evidence extracted from observed RGB frames to improve geometric prediction without ground truth geometry. We demonstrate UGG's effectiveness over non-unified baselines across camera-controlled video generation, depth estimation, and camera pose prediction, including in challenging sparse observation settings. Code and visualizations are available at https://ugg-model.github.io/
2611.14440.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 31 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. Project page: https://ugg-model.github.io/

llm.title_ja: UGG：統合生成ジオメトリモデル
llm.tldr_ja: UGGは、RGBビデオと深度やカメラポーズなどの幾何学的表現を同時にモデル化する4次元シーン理解のための統合フレームワークであり、条件付き補完として視覚生成と幾何学的予測を定式化する。
llm.problem: 既存の4Dシーン理解アプローチが、直接的な幾何学予測のためのフィードフォワードモデルと視覚合成のための生成モデルに分断されていること
llm.method: モダリティと時間にわたって異なるノイズレベルを割り当て、視覚生成と幾何学予測を単一の生成モデル内での条件付き補完として定式化する
llm.result: スパースな観測設定を含む、カメラ制御されたビデオ生成、深度推定、カメラポーズ予測において、非統合型のベースラインを上回る有効性を示した

2611.14440.tldr_en: UGG, a unified framework for 4D scene understanding that jointly models RGB video and geometric representations such as depth and camera pose, is introduced by assigning different noise levels across modalities and time, formulates visual generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion within a single generative model.

2611.14436.title: Metric-Aligned Group Relative Policy Optimization for Explainable Deepfake Detection
2611.14436.abstract: Deepfake detectors are commonly evaluated on real/fake classification alone, but real-world applications require explanations of the visual evidence behind each prediction. Joint vision-language models struggle with authenticity assessment, producing "real" narratives for manipulated images. To address this, we propose a decoupled predict-then-explain pipeline as our submission to the ACM Multimedia 2026 Explainable Deepfake Detection Challenge, with methods trained and evaluated on the XPlainVerse benchmark. A vision-foundation-model ensemble first classifies the image, then a Qwen3-VL-8B model generates a decision-conditioned explanation of the visual evidence. For fake images, a second Qwen3-VL-8B compresses that text into a short non-expert summary without using the image. We further apply metric-aligned Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to optimize both explainers against the challenge criteria. Under matched conditions, GRPO raises complex BERTScore-F1 from 0.686 to 0.712 and also improves grounding (entity and evidence F1); our submission ranked first on complex BERTScore-F1 and seventh overall.

llm.title_ja: 説明可能なディープフェイク検出のためのメトリック整合型グループ相対ポリシー最適化
llm.tldr_ja: 予測してから説明するパイプラインを提案し、メトリック整合型GRPOを適用して両方の説明器を最適化することで、複雑なBERTScore-F1を向上させた。
llm.problem: 現実世界のアプリケーションで必要とされる視覚的証拠の裏付けとなる説明を、従来のディープフェイク検出器や統合型視覚言語モデルが十分に提供できないこと
llm.method: 予測してから説明する decoupled なパイプラインを採用し、ビジョン基盤モデルのアンサンブルとQwen3-VL-8Bを用いてメトリック整合型のGroup Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)で最適化する
llm.result: GRPOの適用により、複雑なBERTScore-F1が0.686から0.712に向上し、グランドリングも改善されてチャレンジで1位を獲得した
keywords_ja: ディープフェイク検出

2611.14436.tldr_en: A decoupled predict-then-explain pipeline is proposed as a submission to the ACM Multimedia 2026 Explainable Deepfake Detection Challenge, with methods trained and evaluated on the XPlainVerse benchmark.

2611.14432.title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
2611.14432.abstract: We describe our solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge: 100 long-horizon household tasks in the OmniGibson simulator. We placed 9th on the final leaderboard, the only independent team in the top 10. The core of the solution is a single vision-language-action (VLA) model, one checkpoint for all 100 tasks, built on our 1st-place 2025 solution, which is based on $π_{0.5}$. On the 50 tasks shared with 2025, its Q rises from 0.260 to 0.371; across all 100 tasks it scores 0.392. Our main conclusion from 2025 was that the model was undertrained, so most of the 2026 work went into training the model for longer, optimizing some training parameters, making each training step slightly faster and reducing the gradient noise: a migration from 50 to 100 tasks (semantic stages built from the demonstrations' skill annotations, task and stage embeddings of new tasks warm-started from similar old ones, and a 21-dimensional action space matching the teleoperation controls); variance-reduced multi-sample flow matching with a simple noise-vs-compute model that picks the number of action-expert samples per observation without ablations; and a 200k-step training run, about one pass over the 211M frames of the demonstrations. A cloud evaluation infrastructure keeps a shared record with provenance, episode diagnostics and restorable simulator states, and runs six simulators on one GPU together faster than real time. On top of the learned policy, 14 tasks are routed to a GPT-6 Astra coding agent that controls the robot through observation and motion tools, starting every episode from a frozen copy of its own practice session on training instances. Across these 14 tasks, Astra's mean Q is 0.639, against 0.108 for the learned policy. The public submission included only part of the Astra results and scored 0.446 Q with 27.3% full-task success.

llm.title_ja: 100の家庭用タスクのための1つのポリシー：2026年BEHAVIORチャレンジに向けた我々の解決策
llm.tldr_ja: OmniGibsonシミュレータにおける100の長期的な家庭用タスクを単一のVLAモデルチェックポイントで解き、最終リーダーボードで9位（トップ10中の唯一の独立チーム）を達成した。
llm.problem: シミュレータ上での多様で長期的な多数の家庭用タスクを、単一のロボットポリシーで効率的に学習・実行することの難しさ
llm.method: π0.5に基づくVLAモデルをベースに、学習時間の延長、勾配ノイズの削減、タスク・ステージ埋め込みのウォームスタート、分散低減マルチサンプルフローマッチングを適用する
llm.result: 全100タスクで0.392のスコアを記録し、特定タスクではGPT-6 Astraコーディングエージェントの併用により平均Q値0.639を達成した
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.14432.tldr_en: The core of the solution is a single vision-language-action (VLA) model, one checkpoint for all 100 tasks, built on the 1st-place 2025 solution, which is based on $\pi_{0.5}$.

2611.14420.title: OnlyAct: Extracting Action Representations from Foundation Models for World Models
2611.14420.abstract: Video world models promise general-purpose interactive simulators, but their training is limited by action supervision: action labels are scarce, fragmented across incompatible specifications, and do not scale with the unlabeled video pretraining corpus. A common workaround jointly trains an action encoder to compress consecutive frames into a latent action and a decoder to reconstruct the next frame from the previous frame and that latent, forcing the latent to capture only new information. This has two limitations: learning the action space from scratch can limit generalization to unseen domains, and the bottleneck trades expressiveness for separation, with tighter settings losing nuance and looser ones risking scene leakage under domain shifts. We argue for a different starting point: rather than learning actions from scratch, we start from a pretrained foundation model (V-JEPA 2), whose embeddings of a frame pair already carry substantial action information after large-scale, diverse video pretraining. The remaining challenge is to extract the action while discarding the scene. We propose a label-free contrastive adaptation framework that pulls together frame pairs sharing the same motion under a different scene and pushes apart pairs from the same scene with different motion, reshaping the geometry of the pretrained space without imposing a reconstruction bottleneck. We introduce a unified evaluation protocol along three axes (action expressiveness, scene invariance, and action-conditioned video generation quality) across robot manipulation, camera navigation, game, and driving benchmarks, most of which are unseen during adaptation. Compared with annotation-free latent-action methods, our representations are substantially more expressive while matching their scene invariance, and they yield world models that transfer demonstrated actions to new scenes more faithfully.

llm.title_ja: OnlyAct：ワールドモデル向け基盤モデルからの行動表現の抽出
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みのV-JEPA 2の埋め込みを利用し、再構築のボトルネックなしにシーンから行動を分離するラベルなし対照適応フレームワークを提案し、表現力を高めた。
llm.problem: ビデオワールドモデルの学習が、希少で断片化された行動アノテーションや、一から行動空間を学習する際のスケーラビリティの限界に直面していること
llm.method: 事前学習済み基盤モデル（V-JEPA 2）を起点とし、同じシーンで異なる動きのペアを遠ざけ、異なるシーンで同じ動きのペアを近づけるラベルフリー対照適応フレームワークを用いる
llm.result: アノテーション不要の潜在行動手法と同等のシーン不変性を維持しつつ、表現力に優れた行動表現を実現した

2611.14420.tldr_en: A label-free contrastive adaptation framework that pulls together frame pairs sharing the same motion under a different scene and pushes apart pairs from the same scene with different motion, reshaping the geometry of the pretrained space without imposing a reconstruction bottleneck is proposed.

2611.14414.title: SIGMO: Sigmoid Gated Interaction-Aware Motion Planning
2611.14414.abstract: Despite the widespread adoption of autonomous vehicle technologies, reliable navigation within cluttered environments remains arduous due to the necessity of interaction-aware strategies; example scenarios include: narrow passages with multiple agents, lane changing in dense traffic, and crossing unsignalized intersections. These scenarios often require highly proactive strategies, simultaneously demanding interpretability and quick adaptability, which challenge end-to-end and data-driven methods. An effective strategy requires: scalability to multiple agents, adaptability to changes in other agents' behavior, and harmony with surrounding traffic without freezing or becoming overly conservative. To meet these requirements, we present SIGMO, a sigmoid-gated interaction-aware motion planner, with two main contributions. First, we formulate polynomial sigmoid functions that analytically estimate yield scores of surrounding agents using physics-grounded interaction features that capture driving intuitions. Second, we integrate the polynomial sigmoid functions into a receding-horizon planner, which facilitates interaction-aware planning with arbitrary trajectory predictions. We validate SIGMO in interaction-intensive simulations and hardware experiments. The results show that SIGMO balances proactive and defensive behavior while remaining computationally lightweight, serving as a strong baseline in a mobility stack. The simulation and hardware experiment videos are available here: https://sites.google.com/view/sigmoid-polygate.

llm.title_ja: SIGMO：シグモイドゲート付きインタラクション認識型モーションプランニング
llm.tldr_ja: SIGMOは、物理学に基づく相互作用特徴を用いて周囲のエージェントの譲歩スコアを解析的に推定するシグモイド関数をリカレンディングホライズン・プランナーに統合し、複雑な環境での信頼性の高いナビゲーションを実現する。
llm.problem: 混雑した環境において、複数のエージェントとのインタラクションを考慮しながら、解釈可能性と迅速な適応性を持つ自律走行のモーションプランニングを行うことの難しさ
llm.method: 物理ベースの相互作用特徴を捉える多項式シグモイド関数を定式化し、それをリカレンディングホライズン・プランナーに統合する
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機実験において、過度に保守的にならずに積極的行動と防御的行動のバランスを保ち、軽量な処理で強力なベースラインとして機能することを示した
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング
インタラクション認識

2611.14414.tldr_en: SIGMO is presented, a sigmoid-gated interaction-aware motion planner that integrates polynomial sigmoid functions into a receding-horizon planner, which facilitates interaction-aware planning with arbitrary trajectory predictions.

2611.14373.title: Gaussian Process-Augmented Model Predictive Contouring Control for 6-DoF Trajectory Tracking with a Holonomic AUV
2611.14373.abstract: Small, holonomic Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) enable close-range inspection of underwater structures from arbitrary viewpoints, requiring accurate position and attitude tracking under state and input constraints. Model Predictive Contouring Control (MPCC) naturally handles these requirements, but relies on an accurate dynamics model, which is difficult to obtain underwater. In this paper, we present a nonlinear MPCC in all six Degrees of Freedom (DoF) for a holonomic AUV and alleviate the inaccuracies in the dynamics by augmenting the nominal model employed with residual dynamics learned via Gaussian Process (GP) regression. The learned residual is embedded in the optimal control problem through a zero-order robust optimization scheme, which keeps the controller real-time capable at 25 Hz. A simulation ablation shows that residual selection is essential when designing the controller, and simulation and in-water experiments with the Multimodality, Observing, Low-cost, Agile (MOLA) AUV validate the resulting controllers against a nominal MPCC and a field proven Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller.

llm.title_ja: ガウス過程で拡張されたモデル予測コンター制御による全方向型AUVの6自由度軌道追従
llm.tldr_ja: 全方向型水中航走体（AUV）の6自由度軌道追従において、モデルの不確実性をガウス過程（GP）回帰による残差学習で補う非線形MPCCを提案し、リアルタイム制御を実現した。
llm.problem: 水中での全方向型AUVの正確な位置・姿勢追従において、正確なダイナミクスモデルの取得が困難であること
llm.method: 非線形モデル予測コンター制御（MPCC）の公称モデルに、ガウス過程（GP）回帰で学習した残差ダイナミクスをゼロ次頑健最適化スキームで組み込む
llm.result: 25Hzでのリアルタイム制御を維持しつつ、シミュレーションおよび実機水中実験において公称MPCCや従来PIDコントローラーに対する有効性を実証した

2611.14365.title: From Video Frames to Robot Meta-Frames: A Unified Latent Interface for World Action Models
2611.14365.abstract: Pretrained video diffusion models (VDMs) offer a powerful foundation for World Action Models (WAMs), which jointly predict robot actions and future observations. Building such models requires injecting low-dimensional robot signals (e.g. proprioception, actions, and values) into a latent space shaped by natural videos, and a key design choice is the interface through which these signals enter: existing schemes treat it as a formatting detail, spending a separate latent frame on each signal or bolting on dedicated encoders and decoders. We argue that signal injection is instead a distribution-alignment problem: how well a representation matches the prior of the pretrained VDMs during denoising. Using the relative reconstruction error of a frozen VDM denoiser as a probe, we find that conventional spatial encodings sit far off this prior, whereas frequency-domain packing yields latents that the denoiser corrects far less. Motivated by this diagnostic result, we propose MetaWAM, which folds all robot signals into a single unified meta-frame: each signal is assigned to a disjoint frequency-domain channel band and lifted to the spatial latent by an inverse DCT, yielding a decodable interface aligned with the pretrained VDM prior without any added module or architectural change. A fixed band layout together with slot-aware routing lets the same meta-frame support policy, world-model, and value prediction over a shared set of robot variables. On RoboCasa, MetaWAM reaches 68.9% success while collapsing the per-signal frames into one and cutting inference latency by 39%, and attains 85.0% success on three real-world Franka tasks. Code and models are available at https://github.com/showlab/MetaWAM

llm.title_ja: ビデオフレームからロボットメタフレームへ：ワールドアクションモデルのための統合された潜在空間インターフェース
llm.tldr_ja: MetaWAMは、すべてのロボット信号を周波数領域のチャンネルバンドに分割して単一のメタフレームに統合し、追加のモジュールなしで事前学習済みビデオ拡散モデルの事前分布に整合させる。
llm.problem: ワールドアクションモデルにおいて、低次元のロボット信号を自然動画の潜在空間に組み込む際のアプローチが断片的であり、事前分布との不整合が生じること
llm.method: すべてのロボット信号を逆離散コサイン変換（DCT）により周波数領域のチャンネルバンドに割り当て、単一のメタフレームとして空間潜在空間に畳み込む
llm.result: ロボット信号ごとのフレームを1つに集約して推論レイテンシを39%削減しつつ、RoboCasaで68.9%の成功率を達成し、実機のFrankaタスクで85.0%の成功率を収めた
keywords_ja: ワールドアクションモデル

2611.14365.tldr_en: MetaWAM is proposed, which folds all robot signals into a single unified meta-frame, yielding a decodable interface aligned with the pretrained VDM prior without any added module or architectural change.

2611.14286.title: ForeseeDrive: Future-Token Conditioning for Anticipatory Generative Driving
2611.14286.abstract: Generative driving planners can represent diverse ego futures, but a downstream scorer can choose only among sampled candidates; it cannot recover an absent maneuver. We present ForeseeDrive, which turns future scene evolution into a deployable interface for shaping candidate generation. Rather than reconstructing dense future states or scoring a fixed menu, ForeseeDrive derives query-indexed tokens from logged actor motion, occupancy evolution, route interactions, and TTC margins, and predicts the same token space from present context at deployment. The tokens condition trajectory geometry before candidates materialize. A zero-token-gated residual path and candidate-preservation loss limit unnecessary drift, while a TTC-margin guard targets brittle safe-to-unsafe boundary crossings. Under their respective benchmark protocols, ForeseeDrive reaches 89.2 PDMS on NAVSIM navtest, 0.41\,m average L2 and 0.05\% collision rate on nuScenes validation, and a 76.50 driving score on Bench2Drive. Controlled DiffusionDrive/NAVSIM diagnostics show an exact zero-token no-op, a small aligned-over-shuffled selected-PDM advantage under preservation, mixed oracle-best quality, and localized TTC-boundary failures. Together, the benchmark results and bounded mechanism tests support future-conditioned generation as a practical interface for anticipation. Code is included in the supplementary materials.
2611.14286.comment: 15 pages (8 pages main text + appendix), 3 figures, 7 tables

llm.title_ja: ForeseeDrive：先読み生成駆動のための将来トークン条件付け
llm.tldr_ja: ForeseeDriveは、過去の行動やオキュパシーの進化からクエリインデックス付きトークンを導出し、将来のシーン展開を候補生成のインターフェースとして条件付けることで、安全かつ多様な自律走行プランニングを実現する。
llm.problem: 生成型運転プランナーにおいて、下流のスコアラーはサンプリングされた候補の中から選ぶことしかできず、欠落した機動を回復できないこと
llm.method: ログに記録されたアクターの動きやオキュパシーの進化等からクエリインデックス付きトークンを導出し、現在コンテキストから予測して軌道形状を条件付ける
llm.result: NAVSIM navtestで89.2 PDMSを達成し、nuScenes検証で平均L2誤差0.41m、衝突率0.05%、Bench2Driveで76.50の運転スコアを記録した
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2611.14286.tldr_en: ForeseeDrive is presented, which turns future scene evolution into a deployable interface for shaping candidate generation, and the benchmark results and bounded mechanism tests support future-conditioned generation as a practical interface for anticipation.

2611.14274.title: From Prediction to Action: Learning Physical Context for Deformable Linear Object Manipulation
2611.14274.abstract: A representation that accurately predicts a deformable object's response is not necessarily the one most useful for choosing manipulation actions. We study this distinction between predictive utility and decision utility in planar single-grasp shape control of Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs). As a common decision backbone, we introduce Geometry-Pointer-Flow (GPF), a geometry-grounded policy that separates grasp-location selection from grasp-conditioned motion generation. Its geometry-only variant reduces one-step executed shape error by 32.8% relative to a DLO-specific diffusion policy, while using 18.7 times fewer parameters and achieving approximately 193 times faster inference. On this backbone, we compare physical context represented by ground-truth parameters, estimated parameters, and learned interaction-history representations, for both forward prediction and executed control. For prediction, ground-truth physical parameters reduce next-shape error by 15.8% over geometry alone, and estimated parameters are slightly more predictive than interaction history. This ordering does not carry over to control: estimated parameters provide no detectable one-step control gain, whereas history-conditioned GPF reduces executed error by 9.9% relative to geometry-only GPF across 470 paired simulation trials. In closed loop, interaction history improves strict-threshold attainment in simulation and yields the strongest zero-shot performance on hardware. All policies are trained exclusively in simulation and transferred to the physical robot without real-world training or fine-tuning. These results show that physical context should be evaluated by the decisions it supports rather than by predictive accuracy alone. Code will be released upon acceptance.

llm.title_ja: 予測から行動へ：変形可能線形物体マニピュレーションのための物理コンテキストの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 変形可能線形物体（DLO）の形状制御において、予測精度だけでなく決定有用性に基づいて物理コンテキストを評価するGeometry-Pointer-Flow（GPF）ポリシーを提案する。
llm.problem: 変形可能なオブジェクトの応答を正確に予測する表現が、必ずしもマニピュレーション行動の選択に最も役立つとは限らないこと
llm.method: 把持位置の選択と把持条件付きモーション生成を分離した幾何学ベースのポリシー「Geometry-Pointer-Flow (GPF)」を導入し、インタラクション履歴の有無を比較する
llm.result: 履歴条件付きGPFは、シミュレーションでの把持誤差を9.9%削減し、シミュレーションのみで訓練したポリシーを実ロボットにゼロショットで適用して優れた性能を達成した

2611.14274.tldr_en: Results show that physical context should be evaluated by the decisions it supports rather than by predictive accuracy alone in planar single-grasp shape control of Deformable Linear Objects.

2611.14257.title: Elastic-WAM: Adaptive Spatiotemporal Imagination for Efficient Robot Control
2611.14257.abstract: World-Action Models improve robot control by predicting future visual dynamics, but iterative video denoising incurs substantial inference overhead. Recent approaches reduce this cost through partial future denoising, yet typically rely on fixed refinement budgets. Our empirical observations reveal that preferred refinement depths vary across tasks and states, while different future regions exhibit varying relevance to action generation. Motivated by these findings, we propose Elastic-WAM, which adaptively allocates world refinement computation across temporal denoising time and spatial future space. A unified spatiotemporal refinement demand field governs when to stop world refinement, how far to advance each denoising step, and which regions to refresh. We parameterize this field with a shared temporal basis and spatial amplitudes, and learn it through a three-stage action-grounded supervised procedure. At inference, the learned field guides recurrent sparse world refinement to improve task success while reducing inference overhead. Evaluations across diverse simulation benchmarks and real-world long-horizon manipulation demonstrate state-of-the-art control performance with reduced inference latency.

llm.title_ja: Elastic-WAM：効率的なロボット制御のための適応型時空間イマジネーション
llm.tldr_ja: Elastic-WAMは、時空間の洗練度を動的に調整するフィールドを用いてワールドモデルの計算量を適応的に配分し、推論のオーバーヘッドを削減しつつ優れたタスク成功率を実現する。
llm.problem: ワールドアクションモデルにおける反復的なビデオノイズ除去が、大きな推論オーバーヘッドを伴うこと
llm.method: ワールド洗練の停止タイミング、ノイズ除去のステップ数、リフレッシュすべき領域を制御する、時空間洗練需要フィールドを導入・学習する
llm.result: 多様なシミュレーションベンチマークおよび実世界の長期マニピュレーションにおいて、推論レイテンシを削減しつつ最先端の制御性能を示した
keywords_ja: ワールドアクションモデル
時空間イマジネーション

2611.14257.tldr_en: Evaluations across diverse simulation benchmarks and real-world long-horizon manipulation demonstrate state-of-the-art control performance with reduced inference latency in Elastic-WAM, which adaptively allocates world refinement computation across temporal denoising time and spatial future space.

2611.14256.title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
2611.14256.abstract: Recent work shows that multimodal agents increasingly self-improve without recurring human annotation. However, each self-improvement mechanism is designed and evaluated within a single scenario, leaving its preconditions unverified under cross-scenario transfer. This survey investigates the structural source of asymmetric mechanism transfer across four scenarios: multimodal reasoning, multimodal generation, GUI and Web navigation, and embodied manipulation. We first formalize the self-evolving multimodal agent by four criteria and a differentia of self-reference, and adopt the three-stage self-evolving loop of experience generation, feedback acquisition, and update consolidation as our analytical framework to position the scenarios along ceilings on rollout count and feedback fidelity. Comparing self-evolving with fixed loops within each scenario separates the limitations that the scenario imposes from those inherent in the self-evolving design. We then recast each mechanism as a trade-off that raises a scarce factor by presupposing a task-structural resource, such as output equivalence or checkable outcomes, and judge it portable, conditional, blocked, or redundant across scenarios. We attribute the asymmetry to divergent combinations of scarce factors and resources across opposite transfer directions, and identify the matched-budget measurements that could overturn these still untested verdicts.

llm.title_ja: クロスシナリオ調査と自己進化型マルチモーダルエージェントの分析
llm.tldr_ja: 自己進化型マルチモーダルエージェントのメカニズムが異なる4つのシナリオ間でどのように転移するかを、報酬やフィードバックの構造的制約に基づいて調査・分析する。
llm.problem: 自己進化メカニズムが単一のシナリオ内でのみ設計・評価されており、クロスシナリオ転移における前提条件が検証されていないこと
llm.method: マルチモーダル推論、生成、GUI/Webナビゲーション、具現型マニピュレーションの4つのシナリオにおいて、自己進化ループの構造と制約をフレームワークに基づいて比較・分析する
llm.result: 希少な要因とタスク構造的資源の組み合わせの差異がメカニズムの非対称な転移を引き起こすことを明らかにし、転移可能性を判定した
keywords_ja: マルチモーダルエージェント

2611.14256.tldr_en: This survey investigates the structural source of asymmetric mechanism transfer across four scenarios: multimodal reasoning, multimodal generation, GUI and Web navigation, and embodied manipulation, and attributes the asymmetry to divergent combinations of scarce factors and resources across opposite transfer directions.

2611.14247.title: Personalized Affective Perception via Continual Learning in Human-Agent Negotiation
2611.14247.abstract: Self-interested intelligent agents that negotiate with humans should interpret nonverbal expressions and adapt their behavior accordingly. However, generic facial-affect models degrade across individuals and contexts, creating a generalization gap. We introduce an affect-adaptive negotiation strategy that incorporates Continual Learning with Imagination for Facial Expression Recognition (CLIFER) to personalize valence-arousal perception in real time. Differential feedback converts changes in valence-arousal direction and intensity into adjustments of the agent's target utility. An asynchronous architecture updates CLIFER in the background during live interaction. In a counterbalanced within-subject study in which 66 participants negotiated with a humanoid robot, the CL-enabled agent achieved significantly higher individual utility and elicited higher participant concession rates than the FaceChannel baseline. The CL condition yielded significantly higher mean arousal estimates, alongside a broader output range. Participant utility and Nash distance did not change significantly between conditions. These outcomes support the practical value of coupling continual affective personalization with differential feedback for real-time negotiation.
2611.14247.comment: 17 pages, 11 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing

llm.title_ja: 人間とエージェントの交渉における継続学習を通したパーソナライズされた感情知覚
llm.tldr_ja: CLIFERを用いた継続学習によりリアルタイムで感情知覚を個人適応させる交渉戦略を提案し、人間との交渉実験でエージェントの効用と相手の譲歩率を高めた。
llm.problem: 人間と交渉する自給自足型エージェントにおいて、汎用の顔面感情モデルが個人や文脈によって劣化し、一般化のギャップが生じること
llm.method: CLIFER（Continual Learning with Imagination for Facial Expression Recognition）を組み込み、感情の価数・覚醒度の変化を利用してエージェントの目標効用をリアルタイムに調整する
llm.result: CL有効化エージェントは、FaceChannelベースラインと比較して、個人の効用を大幅に高め、参加者の譲歩率を向上させた
keywords_ja: 人間エージェント交渉
ヒューマノイドロボット

2611.14247.tldr_en: In a counterbalanced within-subject study in which 66 participants negotiated with a humanoid robot, the CL-enabled agent achieved significantly higher individual utility and elicited higher participant concession rates than the FaceChannel baseline, which support the practical value of coupling continual affective personalization with differential feedback for real-time negotiation.

2611.14186.title: Koopman Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
2611.14186.abstract: We propose a Koopman model-based reinforcement learning (K-MBRL) algorithm for controlling nonlinear robotic systems with unknown dynamics. The K-MBRL learns a control policy by minimizing an approximate policy objective that combines the analytical immediate cost with an estimate of the future cost evaluated at the one-step predicted state. To this end, we develop a stochastic Koopman operator-based learning method to approximate the unknown nonlinear dynamics in a linear representation, while a critic function estimates the remaining future cost. This formulation offers two key advantages. First, the linear Koopman dynamics simplify the model-dependent policy gradient computation to a constant matrix product, enabling computationally efficient policy improvement. Second, one-step model propagation mitigates the accumulation of prediction errors associated with long-horizon rollouts while retaining long-term cost information through the critic. The learned policy enables real-time control through feedforward evaluation without online optimization. We establish policy learning convergence guarantees under standard stochastic approximation assumptions. Simulations on HalfCheetah and quadruped four-legged locomotion tasks demonstrate strong sample efficiency and improved performance compared with classical model-free and model-based reinforcement learning baselines. A pendulum swing-up task is used to assess policy gradient approximation accuracy and conduct ablation studies on the learning mechanism and key hyperparameters. The proposed K-MBRL is further validated on a physical quadruped robot performing a challenging sequence of maneuvers: rising to an upright posture supported by two rounded rear feet, maintaining balance during bipedal walking, and safely returning to the ground, as shown in Fig.1.

llm.title_ja: Koopmanモデルベース強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 未知のダイナミクスを持つ非線形ロボットシステムを制御するために、確率的Koopman作用素学習とクリティック関数を組み合わせたモデルベース強化学習アルゴリズムを提案する。
llm.problem: 未知の非線形ダイナミクスを持つロボットシステムの制御において、モデルベース強化学習の長期ロールアウトによる予測誤差の蓄積や計算の複雑さに対処すること
llm.method: 非線形ダイナミクスを線形表現で近似する確率的Koopman作用素学習法と、将来コストを推定するクリティック関数を組み合わせた方策最適化を行う
llm.result: HalfCheetahや四足歩行タスクにおいて優れたサンプル効率を示し、実機の四足ロボットによる起立・二足歩行などの高度な一連の機動制御に成功した

2611.14186.tldr_en: A stochastic Koopman operator-based learning method to approximate the unknown nonlinear dynamics in a linear representation, while a critic function estimates the remaining future cost is developed, which enables real-time control through feedforward evaluation without online optimization.

2611.14115.title: LEASH: Stay Safe in Agentic Robotics
2611.14115.abstract: Foundation models such as GPT and Claude have shown strong capabilities in spatial understanding and embodied intelligence. These advances make agentic robotics a promising path toward artificial general intelligence in robotics. However, we find that using foundation models to control robots poses serious safety risks, and comprehensive safety evaluation is still lacking. We introduce RoboRisk, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating safety in agentic robotics. Its 92 simulated tasks and 13 physical-robot tasks fall into five categories: Task-level Refusal (T), Plan Repair (P), Execution-time Hazard (E), Injection (I), and Sequential Memory (S). Prior benchmarks cover at most two of these categories, and several evaluate only text outputs. In contrast, RoboRisk covers all five and executes every task in closed loop. We evaluate six state-of-the-art foundation models on RoboRisk: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, and Grok 4.7. These models generally show high harm rates. We also evaluate two robot-specific APIs: the Dream API and PokeBot's RoboAPI. We further propose the Lease-Enforced Agentic Safety Harness (LEASH), which offers essential safety infrastructure for agentic robotics and can be integrated into nearly any agentic architecture. LEASH leverages a decision model (Jev or OpenAI's Decisions API) to implement task, action, and commit gates, which review the task, each action, and each irreversible operation in their visual context. The planner and all three gates share a common safety policy. Experiments on RoboRisk in simulation and on physical robots show that LEASH effectively reduces harm across all six foundation models. It largely preserves their task completion performance and adds little time and token overhead.

llm.title_ja: LEASH：エージェント型ロボットにおける安全性維持
llm.tldr_ja: 基盤モデルを用いたロボット制御の重大な安全リスクを評価するための包括的ベンチマーク「RoboRisk」と、タスク・行動・コミットメントの各ゲートで安全性を担保する「LEASH」ハーネスを提案する。
llm.problem: GPTやClaudeなどの基盤モデルをロボット制御に用いる際に深刻な安全リスクが存在し、包括的な安全性評価や対策が不足していること
llm.method: 5つのカテゴリを網羅する全閉ループベンチマーク「RoboRisk」を構築し、視覚文脈に基づいてタスク・行動・不可逆的操作を監視する安全ハーネス「LEASH」を導入する
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実ロボットの実験において、LEASHがタスク完了性能を維持しつつ、6つの基礎モデルすべてでハーム率を効果的に削減できることを示した
keywords_ja: エージェントロボット

2611.14115.tldr_en: This work introduces RoboRisk, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating safety in agentic robotics, and proposes the Lease-Enforced Agentic Safety Harness (LEASH), which offers essential safety infrastructure for agentic robotics and can be integrated into nearly any agentic architecture.

2611.14111.title: Model-Free Runtime Measurement of Task-Relevant Information
2611.14111.abstract: Autonomous systems increasingly monitor physical kinematics, environmental states and task completion outcomes. While existing work provides methods to plan information seeking actions and interpret acquired observations, current approaches do not monitor whether the live process of information gathering is functioning properly. Consequently, such systems can remain operationally active without resolving outstanding mission requirements. To address this limitation, we introduce Acquisition-State Telemetry (AST), a model free architecture that evaluates ongoing information acquisition from observable evidence relative to declared task requirements. Specifically, a domain interface maps raw observations into task resolution coordinates and normalized comparative representations, which are processed by a fixed causal monitor. This monitor emits two continuous real time signals that quantify (i) prospective progress across unresolved requirements and (ii) informational friction generated when recurrent evidence yields negligible informational gain. We evaluated a single, unadjusted monitor configuration across eight diverse domains including search and rescue dialogue, spatial grid exploration, hierarchical capability acquisition, continuous robotic manipulation, and probabilistic intent estimation. We show that across these domains the friction channel distinguished unproductive stagnation from purposeful exploration prior to task completion, while remaining muted during post completion activity. Furthermore, in closed loop reinforcement learning experiments under early termination constraints, we demonstrate that penalizing informational friction allowed agents to sustain high mission success, whereas unpenalized policies and baselines with matched operational costs failed to complete required tasks.
2611.14111.comment: 17 pages, 5 figures, 2 extended data tables, appendix included. Code available

llm.title_ja: タスク関連情報のモデルフリー実行時測定
llm.tldr_ja: AST（Acquisition-State Telemetry）というモデルフリーのアーキテクチャにより、生データの観測からタスクの進捗と情報的摩擦をリアルタイムに評価し、非生産的な停滞を識別する。
llm.problem: 自律システムにおいて、情報収集のプロセスが適切に機能しているかを監視する仕組みがなく、未解決のミッション要件を解決できないまま動作し続ける可能性があること
llm.method: 生観測をタスク解決座標にマッピングし、未解決要件に対する「見込み進捗」と「情報的摩擦」の2つの連続シグナルを発信する因果モニター（AST）を導入する
llm.result: 検索対話やマニピュレーションを含む8つの多様なドメインにおいて、情報的摩擦チャネルが非生産的な停滞を正確に識別し、強化学習エージェントが高ミッション成功率を維持するのに寄与した

2611.14111.tldr_en: Acquisition-State Telemetry (AST) is introduced, a model free architecture that evaluates ongoing information acquisition from observable evidence relative to declared task requirements, and it is demonstrated that penalizing informational friction allowed agents to sustain high mission success, whereas unpenalized policies and baselines with matched operational costs failed to complete required tasks.

2611.14093.title: BODYinTRANSIT-Lab: A Multimodal Dataset for Investigating Sensory-Driven Transformations in Body Perception and Affective Experiences
2611.14093.abstract: Multimodal datasets that combine synchronised behavioural and physiological signals with subjective affective and body perception measures are still rare. This limits both the understanding of embodied experience and the development of computational models that infer subjective states from sensor data. We introduce BODYinTRANSIT-Lab, a multimodal dataset that addresses this gap by capturing affective, perceptual, and behavioural responses to the Footsteps Illusion. In this closed-loop paradigm, participants perform walking tasks while receiving real-time manipulated auditory feedback of their own footsteps intended to alter perceived body weight. The dataset comprises synchronised recordings from 101 participants recruited through systematic stratification by eating-disorder symptomatology and physical activity level. BODYinTRANSIT-Lab combines full-body kinematics with electromyography, electrocardiography, respiration, and electrodermal activity. Its annotations capture both immediate and post-trial experience, including within-trial perceived-weight ratings, post-trial assessments of body feelings and affective experience, 3D avatar body visualisations, and quantitative body maps. Psychological, behavioural, demographic, and social measures provide further information about factors that may influence individual responses. We provide a deep learning benchmark that uses walking kinematics to classify relative affective valence and perceived weight within subjects. On within-session, segment-level splits, the baseline model achieved mean balanced accuracies of 45.9% for affective valence and 44.5% for perceived weight. The BODYinTRANSIT-Lab dataset provides an experimentally controlled resource for cognitive neuroscience and affective computing research, with potential applications in affect-aware interactive systems, health and well-being technologies, and creative embodied experiences.
2611.14093.comment: 18 Pages, 6 Figures, 7 Tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing

llm.title_ja: BODYinTRANSIT-Lab：身体知覚と感情体験における感覚駆動型変容を調査するためのマルチモーダルデータセット
llm.tldr_ja: 足音の錯覚を用いた閉ループパラダイムを通じて、感情、知覚、行動の反応を捉え、生体信号や主観的評価を統合したマルチモーダルデータセット「BODYinTRANSIT-Lab」を構築した。
llm.problem: 同期された行動・生理学的信号と主観的な感情・身体知覚の測定値を組み合わせたマルチモーダルデータセットが不足しており、具現化された経験の理解や計算モデルの開発が制限されていること
llm.method: 歩行タスク中に自身の足音の聴覚フィードバックをリアルタイムに変更して体重知覚を変化させる閉ループパラダイムを用い、101名からマルチモーダルデータを収集する
llm.result: 歩行運動学を用いて感情価と知覚体重を分類する深層学習ベンチマークを構築し、認知神経科学や感情コンピューティング向けのリソースを提供した
keywords_ja: マルチモーダルデータセット

2611.14093.tldr_en: The BODYinTRANSIT-Lab dataset provides an experimentally controlled resource for cognitive neuroscience and affective computing research, with potential applications in affect-aware interactive systems, health and well-being technologies, and creative embodied experiences.

2611.14092.title: DexSeed: Expanding Human Hand-Object Interactions into Robot Demonstrations for Dexterous Policy Learning
2611.14092.abstract: We study how to generate diverse, physically executable robot demonstrations for dexterous vision-language-action (VLA) learning. Existing demonstration-generation methods typically rely on costly teleoperated examples. Meanwhile, human hand--object datasets provide a reusable source, but existing transfer methods mainly reproduce given interactions. Turning these interactions into VLA training data further requires coverage of different objects and manipulation locations, together with executable arm and finger actions, and visual observations. To achieve this, we present DexSeed, a framework for low-cost generation of dexterous robot data from human hand--object interactions. Our key idea is to expand human sequences while preserving their grasps and realizing the resulting motions under arm-tracking dynamics in physics simulation. Specifically, we organize source sequences by grasp mode with shared language descriptions. InteractionMesh-based retargeting and arm trajectory augmentation adapt these sequences to the robot hand, different object geometries, and pick-and-place locations while preserving local hand--object relationships. An RL finger-control policy produces executable rollouts, while the arm tracks precomputed trajectories. Rendered observations and recorded actions from successful rollouts are paired with grasp descriptions to fine-tune a VLA. Experiments show improved contact fidelity in retargeting and more reliable whole-arm execution than the evaluated baselines. Simulation evaluation and real-world deployment further demonstrate that a VLA fine-tuned solely on the generated demonstrations can execute language-specified grasps. Project page: https://robbyant-research.github.io/DexSeed/.

llm.title_ja: DexSeed：器用なポリシー学習のためのロボットデモへの人間と物体のインタラクションの拡張
llm.tldr_ja: DexSeedは、人間の手と物体のインタラクションデータを活用して物理的に実行可能な器用なロボットデモンストレーションを低コストで生成し、VLAのファインチューニングを行うフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 器用な視覚・言語・行動（VLA）学習のための多様で実行可能なロボットデモンストレーションの生成に、高価な遠隔操作例が必要とされること
llm.method: 人間の把持モードと言語記述に基づき、InteractionMeshベースのリターゲットとアーム軌道拡張を行って物理シミュレーション上でロボットの動きとして実現し、強化学習による指制御ポリシーでロールアウトを生成する
llm.result: リターゲットにおける接触精度の向上と、生成されたデモのみでファインチューニングされたVLAが言語指定された把持を実行できることを実証した
keywords_ja: 器用なマニピュレーション

2611.14092.tldr_en: Simulation evaluation and real-world deployment further demonstrate that a VLA fine-tuned solely on the generated demonstrations can execute language-specified grasps, and improve contact fidelity in retargeting and more reliable whole-arm execution than the evaluated baselines.

2611.14066.title: Generalizing Causal Decision-Making: Markov Equivalence, Transportability and Counterfactuals
2611.14066.abstract: Structural causal bandits use causal knowledge to guide exploration when reward mechanisms are unknown. This paper extends the approach to partially known causal structure, information from other environments, and realizable counterfactual actions. First, we develop graphical criteria for minimal intervention sets under Markov equivalence and characterize possibly-optimal minimal intervention sets for maximal ancestral graphs. A search algorithm finds sets that are possibly optimal in at least one graph represented by a partial ancestral graph. Second, we derive target reward bounds from source distributions through partial transportability, accounting for non-manipulable variables. Dominance relations provide further bounds for action pruning and restricted exploration, with a regret guarantee under valid prior bounds. Third, we formulate counterfactual structural causal bandits over actions supported by specified experimental capabilities. Graphical characterizations of minimality and possible optimality yield algorithms that remove equivalent or dominated choices while preserving an optimal action. Experiments with specified structural causal models examine how these reductions and transferred bounds affect learning. Together, these results clarify how causal knowledge and experimental capabilities determine which actions merit exploration and guide learning within the retained action space.

llm.title_ja: 因果的意思決定の一般化：マルコフ同値、移植性、反実仮想
llm.tldr_ja: 因果関係の知識、環境間の情報、反実仮想行動を統合し、マルコフ同値性や部分的な移植性に基づいて探索すべき行動を特定する因果的構造バンディットの拡張理論を提案する。
llm.problem: 報酬メカニズムが未知の場合に、因果関係の知識を活用して探索を導出する構造的因果バンディットが、部分的に既知の因果構造や他の環境からの情報に対応していないこと
llm.method: マルコフ同値性に基づく最小介入セットのグラフィカル基準の導出、部分的な移植性を介した報酬境界の推定、反実仮想構造的因果バンディットの定式化を行う
llm.result: 同値な選択肢や劣る選択肢を除去しつつ最適行動を維持するアルゴリズムを構築し、因果知識が探索をどのように導くかを明らかにした

2611.14062.title: A human-in-the-loop Control Paradigm for Construction Robotics: From VR-Guided Teleoperation to Semi-Autonomous Dual-Arm Operation
2611.14062.abstract: Construction tasks in hazardous and unstructured environments require both human adaptability and robotic precision, yet existing approaches often treat teleoperation and autonomy as separate control modes. This paper presents a human-in-the-loop control paradigm that enables structured transitions among VR-guided teleoperation, semi-autonomous shared control, and rule-based autonomous execution for contact-rich dual-arm construction tasks. The proposed system combines immersive VR guidance, a manually defined library of reusable skill primitives, and a shared-autonomy framework with explicit human-robot role allocation and command-priority rules. This integration allows operators to retain supervisory and corrective authority while delegating repetitive and precision-critical actions to the robot. The paradigm is validated on a dual-arm platform through representative facade-installation tasks. Results show that autonomous execution provides the best performance under well-calibrated nominal conditions, whereas semi-autonomous control improves resilience when environmental disturbances exceed the predefined autonomous pipeline's correction capability. Semi-autonomous control also substantially reduces subjective operator workload compared with full teleoperation. These findings demonstrate that effective construction-robot control should adapt human involvement to task and environmental uncertainty, using autonomy for repeatable operations and shared control for disturbance recovery.

llm.title_ja: 建設ロボットのためのヒューマン・イン・ザ・ループ制御パラダイム：VR誘導型遠隔操作から半自律型双腕操作へ
llm.tldr_ja: VR誘導遠隔操作、半自律型共有制御、ルールベース自律実行の間で構造的な切り替えを可能にする建設ロボット向けヒューマン・イン・ザ・ループ制御パラダイムを提案する。
llm.problem: 建設作業では人間の適応力とロボットの精密性が求められるが、従来の遠隔操作と自律制御は分離されたモードとして扱われている。
llm.method: VR誘導、再利用可能なスキルプリミティブ、明確な役割分担を持つ共有自律フレームワークを統合した制御パラダイムを提案する。
llm.result: 自律実行は校正された条件下で最高性能を示し、半自律制御は外乱に対する頑健性を高めつつオペレータの作業負荷を大幅に軽減する。
keywords_ja: 双腕マニピュレーション
ヒューマン・イン・ザ・ループ

2611.14062.tldr_en: Results show that autonomous execution provides the best performance under well-calibrated nominal conditions, whereas semi-autonomous control improves resilience when environmental disturbances exceed the predefined autonomous pipeline's correction capability.

2611.14049.title: RedirectMimic: Local Motion Content Redaction for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
2611.14049.abstract: Humanoid motion interfaces should accommodate application-specific movement constraints while retaining useful reference behavior. Local content redaction requires a controller to replace selected movements even when it continues to receive the original reference. Removing the tracking incentive for those movements leaves their replacement unspecified. We introduce RedirectMimic, which separates the reference observed by the actor from the target used to train its execution. A rule-generated edited reference guides tracking rewards during proximal policy optimization, while the deployed observation and action interfaces remain unchanged. We evaluate pose- and speed-defined arm editing in Unitree G1 simulation using a tracker pretrained on 7,509 motion clips. On the overhead-arm task, RedirectMimic reduces core-window content occurrence to 2.7%, compared with 58.9% for reward zeroing and 32.8% for anti-tracking. It achieves 94.2% core-window joint success, combining content suppression, fall-free execution, and local retention. On the speed-defined task, fast outward arm movements occurred at similarly low rates under all three local editing methods. Across both tasks, RedirectMimic achieved the lowest replacement error among these methods and tracked unedited motions with accuracy comparable to that of the pretrained controller. Project page: https://xiaopeng-whu.github.io/RedirectMimic/.

llm.title_ja: RedirectMimic：ヒューマノイド全身制御のための局所的モーション内容修正
llm.tldr_ja: アクターが観察する参照情報と実行学習用ターゲットを分離することで、元の参照を受け取りつつ特定の動きを置き換えるRedirectMimicを提案する。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドのモーションインターフェースにおいて、有用な参照行動を維持しながらアプリケーション固有の移動制約に対応することが困難である。
llm.method: Proximal Policy Optimizationの訓練時にルール生成の編集済み参照でトラッキング報酬をガイドし、観測および行動インターフェースは変更しない。
llm.result: Unitree G1のシミュレーションにおいて、コアウィンドウのコンテンツ発生率を大幅に削減しつつ、高い関節成功率と転倒のない実行を実現した。
keywords_ja: モーションキャプチャ

2611.14049.tldr_en: RedirectMimic is introduced, which separates the reference observed by the actor from the target used to train its execution, which achieves the lowest replacement error among these methods and tracked unedited motions with accuracy comparable to that of the pretrained controller.

2611.14048.title: LaST0.5: A Generalist World Action Model with Interaction-Centric Latent Reasoning
2611.14048.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have recently emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation, endowing policies with strong capabilities for modeling temporal and physical dynamics. Existing WAMs, encompassing both video-first action prediction and joint video-action modeling, directly transfer global physical representations from world models to action generation. However, global scene representations may underemphasize local robot-object interactions, creating a mismatch between representations optimized for world evolution and those required for manipulation. To bridge this gap, we propose LaST0.5, a novel WAM that introduces an interaction-centric physical representation between world modeling and action generation. Specifically, LaST0.5 learns a compact interaction-centric latent space under the supervision of visual interaction cues between the robot and the environment. This reasoning space is instantiated as a latent expert that bridges the world expert and the action expert within a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture. Furthermore, LaST0.5 performs adaptive world-to-action transfer by jointly predicting future representations and progress values, using progress consistency to adjust action execution and trigger future resampling. Finally, we pretrain LaST0.5 on a large-scale robotic data corpus comprising over 14k hours of data, establishing interaction-centric physical reasoning as a scalable and effective paradigm. LaST0.5 achieves 99.5% on LIBERO, surpasses the previous state of the art on ten evaluated RLBench tasks, and demonstrates robust long-horizon execution and precise dexterous manipulation in real-world experiments.

llm.title_ja: LaST0.5：インタラクション中心の潜在推論を備えたジェネラリスト世界・行動モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 世界モデルと行動生成の間にインタラクション中心の物理的表現を導入し、スケーラブルで効果的なマニピュレーションを実現するLaST0.5を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の世界・行動モデルの大域的なシーン表現では局所的なロボットと物体の相互作用が軽視され、マニピュレーションに必要な表現と乖離が生じる。
llm.method: 視覚的インタラクションの手がかりの監督下でコンパクトなインタラクション中心の潜在空間を学習し、Mixture-of-Transformersアーキテクチャに統合する。
llm.result: LIBEROで99.5%を達成し、10個のRLBenchタスクで従来技術を凌駕するとともに、実世界でロングホライズン実行と精密な器用な操作を示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.14048.tldr_en: This work proposes LaST0.5, a novel WAM that introduces an interaction-centric physical representation between world modeling and action generation, and pretrain LaST0.5 on a large-scale robotic data corpus comprising over 14k hours of data, establishing interaction-centric physical reasoning as a scalable and effective paradigm.

2611.14025.title: HiPFuse: Real-Time LiDAR Semantic Segmentation for Robotic Perception on Edge Devices
2611.14025.abstract: Real-time robotic perception requires accurate LiDAR semantics under limited resources. Bird's-eye-view (BEV) aggregation is efficient but can mix differently labeled surfaces in columns. We present HiPFuse, a point-BEV fusion framework that exchanges point and height-partitioned BEV features across horizontal scales, combining point-wise detail with 2D spatial context from one LiDAR scan. Fixed height assignments preserve separate vertical aggregation groups, with auxiliary supervision of initial BEV features using targets from the same 3D cells. A dual-scale BEV context module adds broader context from a coarser grid. On SemanticKITTI and MCD, HiPFuse achieves 63.7% and 62.5% mIoU at 14.2 and 22.4 FPS on Jetson AGX Orin, respectively, exceeding the 10 Hz scan rate. Separate training and evaluation show indoor applicability. Replacing only the baseline semantic front end with HiPFuse in fixed robotic systems reduces odometry absolute trajectory error RMSE by 10.6% on average across two outdoor sequences and increases accepted-loop recall by 8.7 percentage points on SemanticKITTI. Qualitative semantic maps show more continuous road labeling. Our code is available at https://github.com/haiyang2022/HiPFuse.

llm.title_ja: HiPFuse：エッジデバイス上のロボット知覚に向けたリアルタイムLiDARセマンティックセグメンテーション
llm.tldr_ja: 水平方向のスケール間でポイントと高さ分割BEV特徴を交換し、細部と2D空間コンテキストを組み合わせるHiPFuseフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: リアルタイムのロボット知覚では、限られたリソースの下で正確なLiDARセマンティクスを実現することが求められるが、BEV集約は異なるラベルの表面を混同させやすい。
llm.method: ポイントと高さ分割されたBEV特徴を水平スケール間で交換するポイント-BEV融合フレームワークを構築し、二重スケールBEVコンテキストモジュールを追加する。
llm.result: SemanticKITTIおよびMCDにおいてJetson AGX Orin上で高速かつ高精度なmIoUを達成し、オドメトリの絶対軌道誤差を削減した。
keywords_ja: セマンティックセグメンテーション

2611.14025.tldr_en: HiPFuse is presented, a point-BEV fusion framework that exchanges point and height-partitioned BEV features across horizontal scales, combining point-wise detail with 2D spatial context from one LiDAR scan.

2611.13992.title: Pulse or Provenance? What rPPG-Based Deepfake Detectors Learn
2611.13992.abstract: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) has been proposed as a physiological cue for deepfake detection, based on the premise that synthesized faces lack a genuine cardiac signal. We examine what rPPG-style detectors learn on Celeb-DF++ (22 forgery methods) and FaceForensics++ (FF++), using one identically sampled window per real and fake video. On talking-face forgeries, simple chrominance traces reach an AUC of 0.998, exceeding a dedicated rPPG extractor (0.87). Controlled experiments indicate that this signal is not physiological in origin. On fully synthesized forgeries, it is equally discriminative when extracted from background regions or from full frames without face detection, and it is concentrated above the 0.7 to 4 Hz heart-rate band. It is largely removed by shuffling frame order but persists after normalizing resolution, frame rate and encoding, and an independent reimplementation reproduces these findings. Removing high-frequency content makes most synthesized videos appear real, adding it makes real videos appear fake, and injecting a synthetic pulse has little effect. In controlled self-reenactment experiments with two generators, animating a face from a single frame introduces the same high-frequency signal, whereas reconstructing each frame from its own source does not. Face-based chrominance detectors trained on Celeb-DF++ classify over 99% of real FF++ videos as fake, indicating that they largely encode video source rather than manipulation, and a CLIP-based detector exhibits the same behavior. A frozen CLIP backbone matches or exceeds fusions of CLIP with rPPG and frequency features. Finally, we show that the official Celeb-DF and Celeb-DF++ splits share identities and source-video content between training and test, and that custom protocols reusing test videos and identities in training inflate weaker detectors by up to 0.30 AUC.
