llm.title_ja: 脈波か出自か？rPPGベースのディープフェイク検出器が学習しているもの
llm.tldr_ja: rPPGスタイル検出器が何を見ているかを検証し、クロミナンス痕跡が生理的信号ではなく主にビデオの出自や高周波信号をエンコードしていることを示す。
llm.problem: 合成顔には本物の心拍信号がないという前提のもと、遠隔光電容積脈波（rPPG）が生理学的手がかりとしてディープフェイク検出に提案されてきたが、その学習内容の詳細は不明である。
llm.method: Celeb-DF++やFaceForensics++等のデータセットを用いて、実・偽ビデオの同一サンプリングウィンドウに対する検出器の挙動を制御実験で分析する。
llm.result: 検出器の信号は生理学的由来ではなく、背景領域や顔検出なしのフルフレームでも同様に識別可能であり、主にビデオの出自を符号化していることを明らかにした。
keywords_ja: ディープフェイク検出

2611.13992.tldr_en: It is shown that the official Celeb-DF and Celeb-DF++ splits share identities and source-video content between training and test, and that custom protocols reusing test videos and identities in training inflate weaker detectors by up to 0.30 AUC.

2611.13983.title: Optimization-Based Path Planning for Industrial Manipulators: Experimental Validation in Additive Manufacturing
2611.13983.abstract: Robotic additive manufacturing requires joint paths that reconcile robot feasibility with process-specific geometry. We develop an offline optimization-based path planner that combines joint-path regularity and self-collision penalties with process costs and constraints, so that a new process enters through its own reference, residuals, and tolerances. Full-path and boundary-coupled chunked optimization handle references of different lengths. Iterative Weight Tuning (IWT) determines the cost weights from the gaps between Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and their targets. In carbon-fiber winding and robotic 3D printing, the planned paths meet the geometric tolerances and all KPI targets, and both paths are executed on a UR10e, without extrusion for printing, with joint-level tracking recorded during execution.
2611.13983.comment: Submitted for the review in ECC 2027

llm.title_ja: 産業用マニピュレータのための最適化ベースの経路計画：付加製造における実験的検証
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットの実行可能性とプロセス固有の形状を両立させる、関節経路の規則性と自己衝突ペナルティを組み合わせたオフラインの最適化ベース経路プランナーを開発する。
llm.problem: ロボットによる付加製造では、ロボットの運動学的制約とプロセス固有の幾何学的要件を両立する関節経路を計画する必要がある。
llm.method: コストウェートを自動決定する反復ウエート調整（IWT）と、様々な長さの参照を処理するフルパスおよび境界結合型チャンク最適化を組み合わせる。
llm.result: 炭素繊維巻線やロボット3Dプリントにおいて、計画された経路が幾何学的公差とすべてのKPIターゲットを満たし、UR10eでの実機実行に成功した。
keywords_ja: 産業用マニピュレータ

2611.13971.title: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery
2611.13971.abstract: Intraoperative scene perception in ophthalmic microsurgery is limited by instrument occlusion: when a tool enters the high-magnification field, it conceals tissue from both the surgeon and the perception components of robot-assisted systems that process the video. Generative inpainting can remove the occluder but replaces the missing image content with synthesis, which is unsuitable when visual provenance matters. Many video inpainters also depend on future frames and cannot operate online. We present TransGHOST, a causal reference-guided reconstruction pipeline whose non-generative safe mode operates in real time. Every restored value is obtained by resampling a recorded frame using geometric transforms fitted only to visible regions. The system provides per-pixel confidence and provenance and marks unsupported pixels as abstentions. We evaluate TransGHOST on a new veterinary clinical corpus of canine cataract surgery with pixel-level instrument and anatomy labels. Only the occluded region is scored, and each scoring target is verified to differ from the reference supplied to the system. Safe mode reaches 31.89 dB masked PSNR and 0.915 masked SSIM at 51.7 ms median and 85.5 ms 95th-percentile latency. On a pre-declared held-out cohort using instrument cutouts excluded from segmentation training, it reaches 29.83 dB masked PSNR, while matched-mask evaluation on validation shows a 3.45 dB advantage over LaMa. Region-aware reference selection improves masked PSNR by 3.60 dB over recency when candidate references can themselves be occluded. Reference-age analysis further defines the operating interval for the brief, repeated occlusions targeted by TransGHOST.

llm.title_ja: TransGHOST：眼科マイクロサージェリーにおける手術器具による遮蔽領域のリアルタイム・合成フリー再構成
llm.tldr_ja: 可視領域にのみ適合させた幾何学的変換を用いて記録されたフレームをリサンプリングし、非生成型の安全なモードでリアルタイム再構成を行うTransGHOSTを提案する。
llm.problem: 眼科マイクロサージェリーにおいて、手術器具の侵入による遮蔽により、外科医やロボット支援システムの知覚コンポーネントから組織が隠されてしまう。
llm.method: 因果関係に基づく参照誘導型再構成パイプラインを構築し、すべての復元値を可視領域から得られた幾何学的変換によるリサンプリングで取得する。
llm.result: 犬の白内障手術の臨床データセットを用いた評価において、非生成型セーフモードが高いPSNRとSSIMを維持しつつリアルタイムレイテンシを達成した。
keywords_ja: マイクロサージェリー

2611.13971.tldr_en: TransGHOST, a causal reference-guided reconstruction pipeline whose non-generative safe mode operates in real time, is presented and evaluated on a new veterinary clinical corpus of canine cataract surgery with pixel-level instrument and anatomy labels.

2611.13938.title: Dual-Core Tensor Wheel Decomposition with Structure-Cached Acceleration for Tensor Recovery
2611.13938.abstract: Tensor wheel decomposition captures complex correlations in high-dimensional data through interactions between outer-ring factors and a high-order central core. However, updating these components requires the explicit construction and manipulation of large-scale matrices, which limits computational efficiency and incurs particularly high computational and memory costs for the central-core update. To address these limitations, we propose dual-core tensor wheel decomposition (DCTW), which factorizes the central core into two lower-order cores linked by a shared latent bond. Each core is coupled to a different group of outer-ring factors. We further propose a structure-cached acceleration strategy that avoids explicit large-scale matrix multi- plications and caches intermediate tensors generated during tensor network contractions for reuse across block updates. This reuse reduces redundant computation and avoids the explicit construction of large matrices. Complexity analysis and experiments show that the strategy based on structural caching accelerates optimization compared with explicit and implicit up- date schemes while limiting the increase in peak memory as the ranks grow. Experiments on color video completion and robust denoising show that DCTW matches or outperforms representative tensor network methods in reconstruction quality, computational efficiency, and scalability.

llm.title_ja: テンソル復元のための構造キャッシュ加速を用いたデュアルコア・テンソルホイール分解
llm.tldr_ja: 中央コアを共有潜在ボンドで結ばれた2つの低次コアに因数分解し、構造キャッシュ加速戦略を用いて大規模行列計算を回避するDCTWを提案する。
llm.problem: テンソルホイール分解では、中央コアの更新時に大規模行列の明示的な構築と操作が必要となり、計算効率とメモリコストが極めて高くなる。
llm.method: 中央コアを2つの低次コアに分割するデュアルコアテンソルホイール分解（DCTW）と、中間テンソルをキャッシュして再利用する構造キャッシュ加速戦略を提案する。
llm.result: カラービデオ補完やロバストなノイズ除去の実験において、DCTWは再構成品質、計算効率、スケーラビリティの面で既存のテンソルネットワーク法と同等以上の性能を示した。
keywords_ja: テンソルネットワーク

2611.13938.tldr_en: Dual-core tensor wheel decomposition (DCTW), which factorizes the central core into two lower-order cores linked by a shared latent bond, and caches intermediate tensors generated during tensor network contractions for reuse across block updates to avoid explicit large-scale matrix multi- plications.

2611.13929.title: ReACT: Reflection-Consistent Modulation and Cross-Load Consistency for Humanoid Velocity Tracking Under Asymmetric Loads
2611.13929.abstract: In recent years, humanoid loco-manipulation has progressed to whole-body grasping, lifting, and transport. A basic requirement underlying these tasks is carrying the object to its destination, which depends on the locomotion controller accurately executing velocity commands from the navigation policy. However, carrying an object in one hand introduces a persistent asymmetric upper-body load that can degrade velocity tracking. Persistent tracking biases can accumulate into position and heading deviations, increasing the risk of collisions and navigation failure. To address this problem, we present ReACT, a framework for accurate velocity tracking under asymmetric upper-body loads. Reflection-consistent disturbance modulation uses the estimated wrench to modulate actor features for load compensation while preserving action correspondence under reflected observations. Cross-load tracking consistency training compares loaded and unloaded conditions under the same velocity commands to promote consistent velocity tracking across loading conditions. Simulation experiments on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot show improved velocity tracking and reduced directional bias under varying asymmetric loads. Real-world experiments demonstrate collision-free goal reaching in all 40 tested navigation trials under unilateral hand loads with a fixed mapless navigation policy.

llm.title_ja: ReACT：非対称負荷下のヒューマン・ノイド速度追従に向けた反射一貫変調とクロスロード一貫性
llm.tldr_ja: 推定されたレンチを用いてアクター特徴を変調し荷重を補償する反射一貫外乱変調とクロスロード一貫性訓練により、非対称荷重下での正確な速度追従を実現するReACTを提案する。
llm.problem: 片手での物体運搬は、持続的な非対称の上半身荷重をもたらし、ナビゲーションポリシーからの速度追従性能を低下させて衝突や失敗のリスクを高める。
llm.method: 反射一貫外乱変調とクロスロード一貫性訓練を組み合わせ、荷重条件間での一貫した速度追従を促進するフレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: Unitree G1ヒューマン・ノイドのシミュレーションおよび実世界実験において、様々な非対称荷重下での速度追従の改善と衝突のない目的地到達を実現した。

2611.13929.tldr_en: ReACT, a framework for accurate velocity tracking under asymmetric upper-body loads, and reflection-consistent disturbance modulation, which uses the estimated wrench to modulate actor features for load compensation while preserving action correspondence under reflected observations are presented.

2611.13903.title: Persistent Metric-Semantic Maritime Scene Memory from Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs
2611.13903.abstract: Three-dimensional scene graphs (3DSGs) can provide robots with persistent metric-semantic representations for spatial reasoning, but the existing methods have primarily been developed for indoor and terrestrial environments. In this paper we investigate how a representative outdoor open-vocabulary method transfers to maritime environments and which adaptations are needed. Our experiments show that zero-shot representative outdoor 3DSG descriptions agree with our labeled ground truth for a majority of geometry-supported objects on our data, but the resulting map exhibits considerable physical-entity fragmentation, and its terrestrial higher-level assumptions don't capture maritime spatial organization needs. We therefore keep the underlying mapping method and post-process its accumulated evidence. We show a metric-semantic consolidation method followed by geometry-grounded multi-view vision-language model (VLM) reasoning that reconciles remaining fragments into physical entities and groups entities through observations into local places. In parallel, we construct maritime macro regions using map priors and onboard water and structure observations, and associate them with the local places. The resulting representation reduces physical-entity fragmentation beyond both the baseline and our geometry-semantic consolidation component alone, supports correspondence of fixed local places across repeated maritime traversals, and improves contextual retrieval on our reviewed queries over tested baselines. These results show how an outdoor open-vocabulary map can be adapted into persistent maritime scene memory with our methods for object/place identity and spatial abstractions.

llm.title_ja: オープンボキャブラリー3Dシーングラフによる持続的メトリック・セマンティック海洋シーンメモリ
llm.tldr_ja: 屋外用オープンボキャブラリー3Dシーングラフのマッピング手法を海洋環境に適応させ、メトリック・セマンティック統合とVLM推論により断片化を解消する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 3Dシーングラフはロボットに空間推論のための表現を提供するが、既存手法は主に屋内や陸上環境向けに開発されており、海洋環境の空間組織化のニーズを満たさない。
llm.method: 既存のマッピング手法を維持しつつ蓄積されたエビデンスを後処理し、メトリック・セマンティック統合と幾何学的に裏付けられたマルチビューVLM推論を行う。
llm.result: 海洋環境における物理的エンティティの断片化を大幅に軽減し、繰り返し海洋を航行する際の固定された局所的場所の対応付けとコンテキスト検索を改善した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語モデル
オープンボキャブラリー
セマンティックマッピング

2611.13903.tldr_en: The results show how an outdoor open-vocabulary map can be adapted into persistent maritime scene memory with the methods for object/place identity and spatial abstractions.

2611.13863.title: Learn-To-Propagate: Distributionally Robust Motion Planning for Nonlinear Uncertain Systems
2611.13863.abstract: Motion planning for stochastic systems aims to find a sequence of control inputs that drives a system to a goal set while avoiding unsafe states with high probability. Existing approaches, however, are either restricted to linear dynamics with perfect knowledge of the underlying distributions or lack formal correctness guarantees. To address these limitations, we propose \emph{Learn-To-Propagate Distributionally-Robust Forest (L2P-DR-Forest)}, a distributionally-robust sampling-based planning algorithm for \emph{nonlinear} stochastic systems with \emph{unknown} initial state and process noise distributions. Our approach leverages recent advances in optimal transport to learn ambiguity sets that contain the true system distributions with high confidence. We develop an efficient method for propagating these sets through the system dynamics and for verifying their safety. We then integrate these techniques into a novel sampling-based planning algorithm to grow a forest of search trees in the system's state space while accounting for and mitigating the growth of ambiguity-sets radii. We prove that the algorithm is correct, i.e., every returned plan satisfies the specifications with the prescribed confidence, and, under some feasibility and distributional assumptions, is probabilistically complete. Evaluations on several robotic benchmarks demonstrate that our algorithm significantly outperforms existing methods while providing formal guarantees with high confidence.

llm.title_ja: Learn-To-Propagate：非線形不確実システムのための分布頑健なモーションプランニング
llm.tldr_ja: 最適輸送を活用して曖昧集合を学習し、非線形確率システムのダイナミクスに沿って安全性を検証しながら探索木を成長させるサンプリングベースのプランニングアルゴリズムを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の確率システムのモーションプランニングは線形ダイナミクスに限定されているか、基礎となる分布の完全な知識を仮定するか、形式的な正確性の保証が欠けている。
llm.method: 最適輸送を用いた曖昧集合の学習、システムダイナミクスを通じた集合の伝播・安全性検証、およびサンプリングベースの計画アルゴリズムを統合する。

keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2611.13863.tldr_en: This work develops an efficient method for propagating ambiguity sets that contain the true system distributions with high confidence through the system dynamics and integrates these techniques into a novel sampling-based planning algorithm to grow a forest of search trees in the system's state space.

2611.13850.title: Taxonomy-Agnostic Neurosymbolic Grounding of Robot Kinematics
2611.13850.abstract: While symbolic reasoning for task allocation requires grounding a robot's physical capabilities, standard Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) files provide only low-level kinematics without the formal semantic context needed for reasoning. We present URDF2Ontology, an automated, taxonomy-agnostic neurosymbolic framework that transforms raw URDF files into populated, grounded OWL ontologies. It leverages a Large Language Model (LLM) for targeted semantic reasoning, coupled with an iterative sequential graph-purging mechanism to prevent context window saturation. To process complex kinematic structures, it employs a morphology-aware dual-track architecture featuring a bottom-up Tree Track for branching assemblies and a top-down Chain Track for serial limbs. Guided by neurosymbolic guardrails, the framework extracts functional sub-graphs and asserts populated ontologies aligned with arbitrary user-provided taxonomies. Empirical evaluation across a diverse fleet of heterogeneous robots demonstrates strong schema alignment, valid structural extraction, and a significant reduction in manual domain authoring overhead.
2611.13850.journal_ref: 4th AAAI Fall Symposium on Unifying Representations for Robot Application Development, Nov 2026, Arlington, VA, United States. pp.895-903

llm.title_ja: ロボット運動学のタクソノミー非依存型ニューロシンボリック・グラウンディング
llm.tldr_ja: LLMによるターゲットを絞った意味推論と反復的なグラフパージ機構を組み合わせ、URDFファイルから構造化されたOWLオントロジーを自動生成するURDF2Ontologyを提案する。
llm.problem: タスク割当のための記号推論にはロボットの物理的能力のグラウンディングが必要だが、標準的なURDFファイルは低レベルの運動学しか提供せず、正式な意味的文脈が欠けている。
llm.method: 形態学を考慮したデュアルトラックアーキテクチャ（Tree TrackとChain Track）とLLMを活用し、機能的サブグラフを抽出して任意のタクソノミーに沿ったオントロジーをアサートする。
llm.result: 多様な異種ロボットのフリート全体での実証評価により、強力なスキーマ整合性と有効な構造抽出が示され、手動のドメインオーサリングオーバーヘッドが大幅に削減された。
keywords_ja: ニューロシンボリックAI

2611.13850.tldr_en: URDF2Ontology, an automated, taxonomy-agnostic neurosymbolic framework that transforms raw URDF files into populated, grounded OWL ontologies, leverages a Large Language Model for targeted semantic reasoning, coupled with an iterative sequential graph-purging mechanism to prevent context window saturation.
2611.13850.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series

2611.13840.title: Oscillatory Processing Units as a computing substrate for biomimetic intelligence
2611.13840.abstract: Biological intelligence emerges from neural activity that connects sensation, memory and action. Synaptic plasticity, neuronal assemblies and oscillations provide principles for biomimetic computing, but translating them into reusable operations requires a defined computational unit. We introduce Oscillatory Processing Units (OPUs), groups of synthetic neurons sharing a rhythm. Their directed interactions transform incoming activity and prior receiving state into an Oscillatory Occupancy Space (OOS), which becomes available to subsequent computation. We show that source--receiver conditions and oscillatory organization shape these transformations, including their geometry, persistence and historical accessibility. An Atlas of measured relationships supports prospective composition with predicted response classes. Configured circuits perform logical and numerical operations, express associative recall and generate closed-loop decisions with fixed synaptic weights. OPUs and OOS establish a computing substrate for biomimetic intelligence in which experience remains part of the state through which new input becomes action.
2611.13840.comment: 39 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables. Supplementary Information included. Ancillary files: Supplementary Video 1 and source data

llm.title_ja: 生体模倣インテリジェンスのための計算基盤としての振動処理ユニット
llm.tldr_ja: リズムを共有する合成ニューロンのグループである振動処理ユニット（OPU）を導入し、入力活動と事前状態を振動占有空間（OOS）に変換して計算を行う。
llm.problem: 生体の神経活動に基づく計算原理を生体模倣コンピューティングに翻訳するためには、再利用可能な定義された計算単位が必要である。
llm.method: 同期リズムを持つ合成ニューロンのグループ（OPU）を定義し、ソース・レシーバー条件と振動組織を通じた変換や幾何学的特性、連想想起の表現を構築する。
llm.result: 構成された回路が固定シナプス荷重で論理・数値演算を実行し、連想想起を表現し、閉ループ決定を生成できることを示した。
keywords_ja: 生体模倣インテリジェンス
ニューラルネットワーク

2611.13840.tldr_en: This work introduces Oscillatory Processing Units (OPUs), groups of synthetic neurons sharing a rhythm that transform incoming activity and prior receiving state into an Oscillatory Occupancy Space (OOS), which becomes available to subsequent computation.

2611.13819.title: Game-Enhanced Embodied Learning with Event and Foresight Pretraining
2611.13819.abstract: Human gameplay supplies paired observations, actions, and visual consequences that can supplement robot-policy training. We study event-and-foresight pretraining for InternVLA-A1.5, combining recorded keyboard/mouse event prediction with history-conditioned visual supervision through a frozen video model. Coverage-preserving anchor selection constructs one-second targets, and an attention mask prevents teacher-forced future actions from entering foresight queries. The selected corpus contains 394 recordings across 20 games, with 223.36 hours of recorded timestamp span and 2,072,084 training anchors. After 12,400 game-pretraining updates, we compare the resulting initialization with the public base under the same suite-specific robot fine-tuning protocol. Across four LIBERO suites, aggregate success increases from 1,718/2,000 (85.90%) to 1,811/2,000 (90.55%), a gain of 4.65 percentage points. Suite gains are 9.2, 6.8, 0.2, and 2.4 points on Spatial, Object, Goal, and Long. The 40-task breakdown shows 24 improvements, 10 declines, and six ties. These results support the practical value of the complete game-pretraining stage in this evaluated setting, while revealing heterogeneous task outcomes. The comparison includes additional optimization and does not isolate the effects of game data, the two objectives, or training variability.

llm.title_ja: イベントおよびフォーサイト事前学習を用いたゲーム強化型体現学習
llm.tldr_ja: ゲームプレイの記録からイベント予測と履歴条件付き視覚的教師あり学習を組み合わせたイベント・フォーサイト事前学習を行い、ロボットポリシーの初期化を改善する。
llm.problem: 人間のゲームプレイはロボットのポリシー訓練を補完できるが、ペアになった観察、行動、視覚的結果を効率的にロボット学習に統合する方法の検討が必要である。
llm.method: InternVLA-A1.5に対し、記録されたキーボード・マウスイベント予測と凍結ビデオモデルを通じた履歴条件付き視覚監督を組み合わせた事前学習を実施する。
llm.result: 4つのLIBEROスイートにおける評価において、ゲーム事前学習の導入により集約成功率が大幅に向上した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2611.13819.tldr_en: The results support the practical value of the complete game-pretraining stage in this evaluated setting, while revealing heterogeneous task outcomes.

2611.13818.title: WAM is capable in BEHAVIOR-1K: the 2nd-place solution to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
2611.13818.abstract: This work presents the 2nd-place solution (Team IF1001) to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge, which evaluates mobile manipulation across 100 household tasks. Our method is built on a powerful world action model (WAM), Cosmos 3. We improve Cosmos 3 by using richer visual history, task-progress conditioning, and task-group and skill-specific LoRA adapters. During inference, we apply a separate progress estimator to supply task-progress context, and use task- and progress-conditioned routing to select a task-group or skill-specific policy, complemented by action-candidate aggregation, rolling inpainting, and task-specific temporal and gripper control. To meet the minimum inference requirement of 1 FPS, we use neither recursive self-improvement (RSI) nor agentic harness methods and rely on no closed-source models; during official private-test evaluation, our system handled concurrent requests across 100 evaluation ports with limited hardware resources, sustaining an average end-to-end inference rate above 2 FPS per port. Our method achieves a mean Q-score of 0.613 and a full-task success rate of 40.9%, averaged over 3 self-evaluation rounds across all 100 tasks. On the official private test set, with 20 instances per task, our system achieves a mean Q-score of 0.615 and a full-task success rate of 41.2%.
2611.13818.comment: 27 pages, 8 figures, 11 tables. Technical report for Team IF1001's 2nd-place solution to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge at CoRL 2026. Challenge website: https://behavior.stanford.edu/challenge/index.html
2611.13818.tldr_en: This work presents the 2nd-place solution to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge, which evaluates mobile manipulation across 100 household tasks, built on a powerful world action model, Cosmos 3, and improves Cosmos 3 by using richer visual history, task-progress conditioning, and task-group and skill-specific LoRA adapters.

2611.13810.title: Camera equalisation of an 11.5x drop in environmental illuminance: four imitation-learning policies on an SO-101 arm
2611.13810.abstract: Real-robot benchmarks of learned visuomotor policies often record room illuminance as the lighting condition. We show that, on a typical low-cost rig, room light and image light can be almost unrelated. Four imitation-learning policies (ACT, SmolVLA, Diffusion Policy and pi0.5) were trained on the same 50 demonstrations of a pick-and-place task on an SO-101 arm. Each was run for ten rollouts at about 520 lux and again at about 45 lux, an 11.5x reduction. Success was 20/40 in normal light and 19/40 in low light: a change of -2.5 percentage points (95% CI -23 to +19), with no evidence that the policies differed in sensitivity (interaction p = 0.86). The recorded video shows why: mean image brightness was only 3% lower in low light on the front camera and 19% lower on the wrist camera. Both cameras were set to automatic exposure and white balance, which most likely absorbed the difference; exposure was not locked in this experiment. An accidental repeat of one 10-rollout block reproduced its success count (7/10) but matched the first block at only 6 of 10 placements, consistent with chance. We conclude that lux alone does not describe what a policy sees. Camera settings, and image statistics compared with the training recordings, are the quantities to report and control. Data and code are public.
2611.13810.comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, 8 tables. Data and code: https://huggingface.co/datasets/fysical/so101-lighting-autoexposure

llm.title_ja: 環境照度の11.5倍低下のカメラ等化：SO-101アームにおける4つの模倣学習ポリシーの検証
llm.tldr_ja: 環境照度が11.5倍低下する状況下でも、自動露出とホワイトバランスを備えたカメラにより画像明るさの変化が最小限に抑えられ、模倣学習ポリシーの成功率が維持されることを示す。
llm.problem: 実ロボットの視覚運動ポリシーのベンチマークにおいて、室内の照度とカメラが見る画像光の関係が必ずしも直感的ではなく、照度低下に対する頑健性の検証が必要である。
llm.method: SO-101アームを用いたピック＆プレイス課題において、4つの模倣学習ポリシー（ACT、SmolVLA、Diffusion Policy、pi0.5）を通常光と低照度でそれぞれ評価する。
llm.result: 照度が11.5倍低下しても成功率はほとんど変化せず、照度そのものよりもカメラの設定や画像統計量こそがポリシーの性能に影響する重要な因子であることを結論づけた。
keywords_ja: ビジョン運動ポリシー
オープンソースロボット

2611.13790.title: RiSE-Drive: Risk-Sensitive Long-Horizon Candidate Evaluation for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
2611.13790.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving systems increasingly rely on generating multiple trajectory candidates and selecting one for execution. In this setting, a central challenge is no longer only candidate generation, but how to evaluate candidates according to their long-horizon consequences under uncertainty. Existing methods still mainly use deterministic point scores, heuristic subscores, or single-outcome evaluations, which makes it difficult to capture delayed failures, tail risk, and ranking instability under plausible future perturbations. We present RiSE-Drive, a framework for risk-sensitive long-horizon candidate evaluation in end-to-end autonomous driving. RiSE-Drive first performs candidate-conditioned latent future rollout, then estimates long-horizon outcome distributions instead of single scalar scores, and finally ranks candidates using a tail-risk-aware and perturbation-robust decision criterion. This reformulates candidate scoring from deterministic oracle-style evaluation into distributional outcome assessment with explicit risk control. As a result, the evaluator is encouraged to prefer candidates that are not only strong under nominal conditions, but also reliable under long-horizon rollout and safety-critical deviations. Experiments on the NAVSIM-v1 and NAVSIM-v2 benchmarks, as well as the closed-loop HUGSIM benchmark, show that RiSE-Drive achieves state-of-the-art performance and significantly improves the robustness of candidate selection.
2611.13790.comment: 11 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables, including supplementary material. Published in ACM Multimedia 2026 (MM '26)
2611.13790.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM '26), 15482-15491 (2026)

llm.title_ja: RiSE-Drive：エンド物事自動運転のためのリスク感応型ロングホライズン候補評価
llm.tldr_ja: 候補条件付きの潜在的将来ロールアウトを行い、単一のスカラー値ではなく長期的結果分布を推定してテイルリスクを考慮した決定基準でランキングを行うRiSE-Driveを提案する。
llm.problem: エンドツーエンド自動運転において、不確実性下での長期的結果に基づいて複数の軌道候補を評価し選択することが困難である。
llm.method: 候補条件付きの将来ロールアウト、確率的結果分布の推定、およびテイルリスクを考慮したパーチュベーション頑健な決定基準を用いた候補評価フレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: NAVSIMおよびHUGSIMベンチマークにおいて、最先端の性能を達成し、候補選択の頑健性を大幅に向上させた。
keywords_ja: エンドツーエンド学習
シミュレーション評価

2611.13790.tldr_en: RiSE-Drive is presented, a risk-sensitive long-horizon candidate evaluator that preserves the upstream perception and proposal-generation pipeline and ranks trajectories using a criterion combining the distributional location, lower-tail Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), and cross-branch instability.
2611.13790.venue: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia

2611.13779.title: Softness is something you also need! Why compliance helps control: information metrics of a passive walker with compliant ankle
2611.13779.abstract: A great gap in adaptivity, flexibility, and dexterity still exists between intelligent robots, whether they are made of rigid or (partially) compliant components, and their naturally evolved animal and vegetal counterparts. One reason could be of `paradigm' nature. On the one hand, most robots (both rigid and soft) are still designed by following a `Cartesian' approach, with top-down control and a clear mind-body separation. Designing artificial agents on the basis of the principles that we observe in biology is not an easy task. The principles of organization of animals and plants rely on morphological computation and emergence of fit behaviors from loosely coupled networks of embodied agents. Modeling and control require radically new approaches. In this paper we briefly recall and explain some seminal mathematical results linking information metrics and dynamics of the agents, already published years ago; we integrate them with some recent methods developed by us and by the community, we highlight some brief remarks about their relevance and we hint to our current and near future work towards finding concrete and efficient ways for the modeling and control of completely or partially compliant artificial agents and for a better understanding of physical intelligence in nature. We present a technical note summarizing phase-space volume calculations for inverted-pendulum and passive-dynamic walking models, following our proposed framework. Starting from the McGeer compass gait, we introduce knee-ankle compliance, foot-rocker effects, and a Ruina-style compass gait with distributed leg inertia. Standard heel-strike maps are derived and used in the estimation of viable phase-space volumes $W(γ)$, based on a state-dependent Monte-Carlo and Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces methods. We show how the methods based on RKHS allow deeper and more subtle analysis.
2611.13779.comment: main: 11 pages, 6 figures; supplemental: 7 pages, 1 figure

llm.title_ja: 柔らかさも必要だ！コンプライアンスが制御を助ける理由：柔軟な足首を持つ受動歩行者の情報指標
llm.tldr_ja: 形態計算と受動的力学に基づく生物学的原則に着目し、逆さ振り子や受動歩行モデルにおける位相空間体積の計算を通じて、柔軟な人工エージェントのモデリングと制御に関する理論的考察を行う。
llm.problem: 従来のロボット工学はトップダウン制御と心身分離のアプローチに従っており、自然界の動物や植物に見られる適応性や器用さと大きな隔たりがある。
llm.method: McGeerのコンパス歩行を出発点として、膝・足首のコンプライアンスや足ロッカー効果を導入し、状態依存のモンテカルロ法とRKHSを用いて位相空間体積を推定する。
llm.result: 柔軟性やコンプライアンスが物理的知性の理解や効率的な受動歩行モデルの制御において果たす重要性を情報指標の観点から整理した。

2611.13779.tldr_en: A technical note summarizing phase-space volume calculations for inverted-pendulum and passive-dynamic walking models, following the proposed framework, and how the methods based on RKHS allow deeper and more subtle analysis is presented.

2611.13769.title: From Depth to Safe Depth: Uncertainty-Aware Monocular Perception for Mobile Robot Navigation
2611.13769.abstract: Monocular depth foundation models make it tempting to replace depth sensors on mobile robots with a single RGB camera. We show that, used off the shelf, this is unsafe: in a simulated indoor navigation benchmark, a standard Nav2 stack driven by Depth Anything V2 (metric) collides in 63\% of 120 episodes, because the model systematically over-estimates the distance to nearby obstacles. We propose a lightweight plug-in module that turns predicted depth into \emph{safe depth}. A 0.58\,M-parameter head on top of the \emph{frozen} depth model predicts, per pixel, a log-depth correction $μ$ and an uncertainty $σ$, trained with a $β$-weighted Gaussian negative log-likelihood. The navigation stack consumes the one-sided bound $\hat d_{\text{safe}}=d\,e^{μ-kσ}$, where $k$ is set by conformal calibration on a held-out world, and uncertainty also decides which pixels may be treated as floor. The correction halves the depth error (AbsRel $0.262\rightarrow0.134$) and reduces near-range over-estimation from 59.8\% to 12.0\%. In navigation, safe depth raises the success rate from 37\% to 70\% and lowers collisions from 63\% to 3\%, close to the 2\% of ground-truth depth. A constant safety margin calibrated to the same pixel coverage reaches only 30\% success because it freezes the robot; uncertainty-aware safety wins 52 of 56 discordant paired episodes against it. Gains hold on glass, texture-less walls and dark regions.

llm.title_ja: 深度から安全な深度へ：移動ロボットナビゲーションのための不確実性を考慮した単眼知覚
llm.tldr_ja: 単眼深度推定モデルの予測値に補正と不確実性を付加して安全な深度を出力する軽量なプラグインモジュールを提案し、ナビゲーション時の衝突を激減させる。
llm.problem: 単眼深度基礎モデルをそのままモバイルロボットの深度センサの代わりに用いると、近傍の障害物の距離を過大評価して頻繁に衝突を引き起こす。
llm.method: 凍結された深度モデルの上に、対数深度補正と不確実性を画素単位で予測する軽量ヘッドを結合し、共形キャリブレーションを用いた安全な深度を計算する。
llm.result: シミュレーションの室内ナビゲーションベンチマークにおいて、深度誤差を半減させ、衝突率を63%から3%へと大幅に低下させた。

2611.13769.tldr_en: This work proposes a lightweight plug-in module that turns predicted depth into safe depth, and shows that this is unsafe: in a simulated indoor navigation benchmark, a standard Nav2 stack driven by Depth Anything V2 (metric) collides in 63\% of 120 episodes, because the model systematically over-estimates the distance to nearby obstacles.

2611.13766.title: FAME-QP: A GPU-Accelerated Quadratic-Programming Solver for Real-Time Model Predictive Control
2611.13766.abstract: We present FAME-QP, a GPU-accelerated solver for dense quadratic programs arising in linear model predictive control. FAME-QP combines constraint-dependent operator representations with fused single- and two-kernel iterations replayed through CUDA graphs, automatically selecting the execution configuration through device calibration and problem-specific timing. It probes a cached operator bank to select the initial penalty and updates operators lazily when problem matrices change. Numerical benchmarks and simulated humanoid and quadrotor control experiments demonstrate reduced latency relative to competing GPU solvers while maintaining solution accuracy and control performance.

llm.title_ja: FAME-QP：リアルタイムモデル予測制御のためのGPUアクセラレーション型二次計画法ソルバー
llm.tldr_ja: 制約依存の演算子表現とCUDAグラフによる融合カーネル反復を組み合わせた、線形モデル予測制御向けのGPU加速型二次計画法ソルバーFAME-QPを提案する。
llm.problem: 線形モデル予測制御において生じる高密度の二次計画問題をリアルタイムで高速に解くことが求められている。
llm.method: キャッシュされた演算子バンクを利用して初期ペナルティを選択し、問題行列が変化した際に演算子を遅延更新するGPU加速ソルバーを構築する。
llm.result: 数値ベンチマークやヒューマン・ノイドおよびクアドロトールの制御シミュレーション実験において、解の精度と制御性能を維持しつつ競合GPUソルバーと比較してレイテンシを削減した。

2611.13766.tldr_en: FAME-QP combines constraint-dependent operator representations with fused single- and two-kernel iterations replayed through CUDA graphs, automatically selecting the execution configuration through device calibration and problem-specific timing to reduce latency relative to competing GPU solvers.

2611.13732.title: CIALLO: Learning Shared Intent Representations for Cross-Embodiment Manipulation
2611.13732.abstract: Robot demonstrations contain reusable manipulation knowledge, but transferring this knowledge across embodiments requires representations that bridge differences in control interfaces. Action reconstruction alone does not ensure that similar behaviors across robots share a representation. To address this gap, we introduce CIALLO, an action codec that aligns actions, visual changes, and observation-grounded language in a shared space of short-horizon behavioral intent. An embodiment-conditioned decoder maps this intent back to robot-specific actions, allowing a shared representation to support different control interfaces. After pretraining on eight embodiments, CIALLO adapts to a new robot from one recording of at most 10 seconds by updating only its embodiment embeddings. The calibrated codec then remains frozen while a policy learns to predict intent from observations and instructions. We instantiate this policy with Qwen3.5-4B to form Qwen-CIALLO, whose backbone requires no large-scale robot-action pretraining before policy finetuning. With 20 demonstrations per task, Qwen-CIALLO achieves 76.7\% average success across real SO-101 and single-arm Piper robots, compared with 70.0\% for fully finetuned $π_0$. In simulation, we additionally finetune the action decoder, achieving 97.3\% success on LIBERO and 52.7\% on RoboTwin 2.0. The LIBERO policy also achieves 80.8\% on LIBERO-Plus without further finetuning. Together, these results support a shared action codec as a transferable control interface that separates embodiment calibration from task learning.

llm.title_ja: CIALLO：クロスエンボディメントマニピュレーションのための共有意図表現の学習
llm.tldr_ja: クロスエンボディメントマニピュレーション向けに、動作・視覚変化・言語を共有の意図空間に整列させる行動コーデックCIALLOを提案し、少量のデモで多様なロボットに適応させる。
llm.problem: 異なる制御インターフェースを持つロボット間でのマニピュレーション知識の転移が困難であること。
llm.method: 行動・視覚変化・言語を短い地平の行動意図の共有空間に整列させる行動コーデックCIALLOの提案。
llm.result: 実機のSO-101およびPiperロボットで平均76.7%の成功率を達成し、シミュレーションでも高い性能を示した。
keywords_ja: クロスエンボディメント

2611.13732.tldr_en: Qwen-CIALLO, an action codec that aligns actions, visual changes, and observation-grounded language in a shared space of short-horizon behavioral intent, supports a shared action codec as a transferable control interface that separates embodiment calibration from task learning.

2611.13696.title: On Private Knowledge Retrieval and Private Inference for secure multi-agent systems
2611.13696.abstract: Multi-agent systems provide a convenient framework for the massive deployment of agents based on Large Language Models (LLMs). It provides a sound framework where agents can interact with existing software to perform actions in an autonomous way. Agentic AI is the new term to denote these AI-based autonomous systems. In real multi-agent systems, agents need to deal with malicious agents some of which can exploit security vulnerabilities to do harm. A memory poisoning attack is an example of exploiting a vulnerability to modify agents knowledge and, thus, affect its behavior. In an agent, there are different types of memory systems (semantic, episodic, and short-term) which have their own characteristics and for which different memory poisoning attacks may be developed. In this paper we focus on semantic memory, we discuss its attack, and mitigation strategies. We introduce private knowledge retrieval and private inference. We propose a signature system in the knowledge base to prevent from undesired manipulation. This should avoid memory poisoning attacks by introducing security by design in the construction of the semantic memory. In our architecture, an agent contains a local Prolog-like inference system (i.e., using Horn clauses to represent knowledge) which accesses an external knowledge base to get the required knowledge. This externally signed knowledge base is accessed privately. We provide different implementations in Python using different privacy levels including k-anonymity and information-theoretical privacy (IT-PIR).

llm.title_ja: セキュアなマルチエージェントシステムのためのプライベート知識検索とプライベート推論について
llm.tldr_ja: マルチエージェントシステムにおけるメモリ汚染攻撃を防ぐため、外部署名付き知識ベースへのプライベートなアクセスと論理推論を組み合わせたアーキテクチャを提案する。
llm.problem: マルチエージェントシステムにおいて悪意あるエージェントがメモリ汚染攻撃により知識を改ざんし行動に影響を与えること。
llm.method: 署名付きの外部知識ベースへのプライベートなアクセスと、ローカルのProlog様推論システムを組み合わせる。
llm.result: k匿名性や情報理論的プライバシーを含む異なるプライバシーレベルを持つPython実装を提供した。

2611.13696.tldr_en: This paper focuses on semantic memory, discusses its attack, and mitigation strategies, and proposes a signature system in the knowledge base to prevent from undesired manipulation and introduces private knowledge retrieval and private inference.

2611.13690.title: Joint-State Inference for Autonomous Excavators Using Cab-View Vision-Control Fusion
2611.13690.abstract: Reliable state feedback of excavator front-end mechanisms is essential for autonomous excavation, yet retrofitting existing machines with dedicated joint sensors, external cameras, or visual markers can increase deployment and maintenance burdens. This paper proposes a closed-loop autonomous excavation framework for continuous inference of excavator joint states using onboard visual observations and control-related temporal information. The framework encodes structural cues from the current cab-view image, models short-term motion trends from historical joystick commands, and introduces a rolling state buffer for the bucket joint to preserve temporal continuity under severe occlusion. Mechanical joint-range constraints are incorporated into the learning objective to suppress infeasible estimates. The current cab-view image and inferred states are supplied to an Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT)-based control policy for online action generation. Experiments in an AGX Dynamics for Unity simulation environment under diverse operating conditions evaluate joint-state inference and end-to-end task execution. Across 20 autonomous excavation trials, the framework achieved a 95% task-completion rate, with an average joint-state-inference-and-control latency of 10.11 ms per step. The bucket-joint inference achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.965 degrees. These results demonstrate a sensor-light and computationally efficient joint-state-inference approach that can support closed-loop autonomous excavation with reduced dependence on additional sensing infrastructure.

llm.title_ja: キャブビュー視覚・制御フュージョンを用いた自律型油圧ショベルの関節状態推定
llm.tldr_ja: 車載カメラの視覚情報とジョイスティックの時系列制御情報を組み合わせ、追加センサなしで油圧ショベルの関節状態を連続推定するクローズドループ制御フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の油圧ショベルへの専用関節センサや外部カメラの追加が導入・保守の負担を増大させること。
llm.method: キャブビュー画像からの視覚的手がかりと過去のジョイスティック操作の時系列情報を用いた関節状態推定。
llm.result: シミュレーションでの20回の試行で95%のタスク完了率を達成し、バケット関節の平均絶対誤差は0.965度であった。
keywords_ja: 視覚制御フュージョン

2611.13690.tldr_en: A sensor-light and computationally efficient joint-state-inference approach that can support closed-loop autonomous excavation with reduced dependence on additional sensing infrastructure is demonstrated.

2611.13685.title: Ego Guidance: Enhancing Robot Policy Learning with Action-Free Human Egocentric Videos
2611.13685.abstract: In this paper, we investigate how human egocentric videos can benefit robot policy learning without action supervision. Building on a pretrained VLM, we propose Shared Prediction on Action and Representation (SPAR), an MoT architecture in which future visual state prediction can provide independent and complementary learning signals alongside action prediction. We find that representations learned from egocentric videos improve downstream performance on out-of-distribution robot tasks, with further gains as video data scales. We also study the effects of objective choices and data curation, providing insights into how to leverage action-free videos for scalable robot learning.

llm.title_ja: Ego Guidance：行動なしの人間一人称視点動画によるロボットポリシー学習の強化
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みVLMを基に、将来の視覚状態予測を学習信号として活用することで、行動ラベルなしの人一人称視点動画からロボットポリシーの性能を向上させる手法SPARを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットポリシーの学習において、行動監視のない膨大な人間の一人称視点動画を効果的に活用することが難しいこと。
llm.method: 将来の視覚状態予測を独立かつ補完的な学習信号として利用するMoTアーキテクチャSPARの提案。
llm.result: 一人称視点動画から学習した表現が、OOD（分布外）のロボットタスクにおける下流性能を向上させることを示した。

2611.13685.tldr_en: It is found that representations learned from egocentric videos improve downstream performance on out-of-distribution robot tasks, with further gains as video data scales.

2611.13669.title: A computational framework for understanding embodied plans
2611.13669.abstract: Reasoning about people's plans and goals based on their actions is fundamental to human social interaction and essential for cooperative, embodied artificial intelligence. Formalizing this capacity in naturalistic, embodied settings has been a longstanding challenge. Here, we present GenEA, a novel agent representation capable of reasoning over multi-step, long-horizon embodied plans. At the heart of GenEA lies a multilevel state-space that couples the coarse biomechanics of an articulated body and its interactions with nearby objects by extending the task-and-motion planning framework from robotics with simulation-based intuitive physics. By embedding this state-space in a generative model, GenEA yields a joint probability distribution over goals and embodied plans. Across several experiments spanning the qualitatively distinct domains of object manipulation and navigation, featuring diverse tasks and multiple behavioral measures, we show that GenEA, through simple transformations of this joint distribution, recapitulates how humans reason about embodied plans. Crucially, GenEA consistently outperforms strong alternative models, including plausible heuristics, standard task-and-motion planning, and a state-of-the-art vision-language model. GenEA thereby offers a new perspective on the architecture of human reasoning and social cognition, suggesting that embodied artificial intelligence systems seeking to seamlessly interact with humans should adopt GenEA-like generative models of action planning.

llm.title_ja: 体現された計画を理解するための計算フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット工学のタスク・モーション計画をシミュレーションベースの直感的物理学で拡張したマルチレベル状態空間を持つ生成モデルGenEAにより、人間の体現された計画の推論を再現する。
llm.problem: 自然主義的かつ体現された設定における人間の計画や目的の推論の定式化が長年の課題であったこと。
llm.method: 粗い生体力学と物体間インタラクションを結合したマルチレベル状態空間を生成モデルに埋め込んだGenEAの提案。
llm.result: 物体操作やナビゲーションの多様なドメインにおいて、既存の強力な代替モデルを一貫して上回る性能を示した。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション
タスク・モーション計画

2611.13669.tldr_en: GenEA, a novel agent representation capable of reasoning over multi-step, long-horizon embodied plans, is presented, suggesting that embodied artificial intelligence systems seeking to seamlessly interact with humans should adopt GenEA-like generative models of action planning.

2611.13662.title: NIF-VIO: Visual--Inertial Odometry Across Inertial and Non-Inertial Reference Frames
2611.13662.abstract: Conventional visual--inertial odometry (VIO) assumes that observations from cameras and an inertial measurement unit (IMU) are jointly consistent in an inertial reference frame. However, this assumption breaks down under non-inertial conditions. Inside accelerating or rotating carriers, visual observations of the interior reflect carrier-relative motion, while IMU measurements contain additional carrier-induced components, which can compromise conventional fusion. We therefore present NIF-VIO for localization relative to the local environment across inertial and non-inertial reference frames. It adapts visual--inertial fusion based on measurement consistency. As inertial conditions change, early constraint isolation is combined with local reoptimization to limit error propagation before inconsistency confirmation and repair the affected local geometry. Under non-inertial conditions, a compact model with temporally shared parameters is introduced to account for carrier motion while preserving inertial information that complements visual constraints. Experiments on public benchmarks and a self-collected dataset demonstrate that NIF-VIO achieves competitive performance under inertial conditions and improved localization accuracy and availability under non-inertial conditions.

llm.title_ja: NIF-VIO：慣性および非慣性基準フレームを跨ぐビジュアル・慣性オドメトリ
llm.tldr_ja: 測定の一貫性に基づいてビジュアル・慣性融合を適応させ、慣性基準フレームと非慣性基準フレームの両方で局所環境に対する高精度な位置推定を実現するNIF-VIOを提案する。
llm.problem: 従来のVIOが前提とする慣性基準フレームの仮定が、加速や回転を行う非慣性条件下では破綻すること。
llm.method: 測定の一貫性に基づく適応的なビジュアル・慣性融合と、キャリア運動を考慮した時系列パラメータ共有モデルの導入。
llm.result: 公開ベンチマークおよび独自収集データセットにおいて、慣性条件で競争力のある性能を示し、非慣性条件で精度と可用性を向上させた。
keywords_ja: ビジュアル慣性オドメトリ

2611.13662.tldr_en: NIF-VIO is presented for localization relative to the local environment across inertial and non-inertial reference frames and achieves competitive performance under inertial conditions and improved localization accuracy and availability under non-inertial conditions.

2611.13646.title: MouldIt: Data Efficiency of Multi-Task Temporal Representation Learning in Injection Moulding
2611.13646.abstract: Smart industrial solutions that can address multiple tasks require models that understand the underlying processes. We examine representation learning for modeling the injection moulding process as an example of such solutions. We consider its data efficiency and multi-modal benefit compared to classical machine learning alternatives. To this end, we synthesize a process-informed dataset based on a real reference cycle of an Erlanger Träger part. We then introduce MouldIt, a temporal convolution and attention based variational autoencoder that reconstructs in-mould signals, while classifying parts as acceptable or as one of our synthetic failure modes. We evaluate MouldIt on two tasks, known-class classification and unknown-class detection, across nine dataset sizes in single-modal and multi-modal settings. We compare it with an accept-all baseline and the classical methods k-nearest neighbors, logistic regression, random forests, and principal component analysis, which we adapt to support both tasks. MouldIt outperforms classical methods across both tasks from 4000 cycles in the single-modal setting and from 2000 cycles in the multi-modal setting. It achieves part sorting losses of 6.0 $\pm$ 0.7% and 1.0 $\pm$ 0.3% in the single-modal and multi-modal settings respectively, ranking first across all baselines and a combination of principal component analysis and random forests.

llm.title_ja: MouldIt：射出成形におけるマルチタスク時系列表現学習のデータ効率
llm.tldr_ja: 射出成形プロセスをモデル化するための時系列畳み込みと注意機構に基づく変分オートエンコーダMouldItを提案し、従来の機械学習手法よりも少ないデータで高精度な分類・検出を実現する。
llm.problem: 多様な産業タスクに対応するスマートソリューションにおいて、プロセスを理解するモデルのデータ効率とマルチモーダルな利点が十分に活用されていないこと。
llm.method: 成形内信号を再構成しつつ部品の良否を分類する、時系列畳み込みと注意機構を用いた変分オートエンコーダMouldItの提案。
llm.result: 単一モーダルで4000サイクル、マルチモーダルで2000サイクルから従来手法を上回り、優れた不良品ソート損失を達成した。
keywords_ja: 変分オートエンコーダ

2611.13646.tldr_en: This work introduces MouldIt, a temporal convolution and attention based variational autoencoder that reconstructs in-mould signals, while classifying parts as acceptable or as one of the authors' synthetic failure modes, and considers its data efficiency and multi-modal benefit compared to classical machine learning alternatives.

2611.13634.title: An IoT Based Approach for Platform Independent Positioning Service
2611.13634.abstract: KAIST Indoor Localization System (KAILOS) was introduced in 2014 and became one of the world-first complete indoor positioning solutions. It is mainly based on the WiFi signal to estimate location and provide positioning service via mobile application that has many restrictions by the Operating System. This study proposes an extended architecture of KAILOS to make use of the IoT device for removing the barriers of the mobile-app-based approach and conveniently providing indoor positioning service. Design of the IoT device that contains hardware and software is also presented. Via this study, we prove that the IoT-based approach is promising and can be a crucial feature to widen applications of indoor localization services.

llm.title_ja: プラットフォーム非依存測位サービスのためのIoTベースアプローチ
llm.tldr_ja: モバイルアプリベースの制限を克服し、屋内測位サービスを容易に提供するためにIoTデバイスを活用したKAILOSの拡張アーキテクチャを提案する。
llm.problem: モバイルアプリケーションベースの屋内測位システムがOSによる多くの制限を受けること。
llm.method: ハードウェアとソフトウェアを含むIoTデバイスの設計によるKAILOSの拡張アーキテクチャの構築。
llm.result: IoTベースのアプローチが有望であり、屋内測位サービスの応用範囲を広げるために重要であることを実証した。
keywords_ja: プラットフォーム非依存

2611.13634.tldr_en: This study proposes an extended architecture of KAILOS to make use of the IoT device for removing the barriers of the mobile-app-based approach and conveniently providing indoor positioning service.
2611.13634.venue: International Conference on Indoor Positioning and Indoor Navigation

2611.13626.title: FlashMotion: Ultra-Fast Long-Term 3D Motion Generation
2611.13626.abstract: 3D human motion generation plays a crucial role in game development, extended reality (XR), digital humans, and embodied simulation. Beyond motion generation, practical pipelines include rigging, retargeting, and rendering, making ultra-fast long-term 3D motion generation without compromising quality valuable for real-time interactive applications. Despite promising progress, high-quality long-horizon motion generation under tight inference budgets remains challenging, owing to 2 coupled bottlenecks: (1) generative strategies that require many sampling steps for high-quality 3D motion generation and (2) model architectures with substantial per-step computational and memory costs for long sequences. We present FlashMotion, a co-designed framework for high-quality long-horizon 3D motion generation under a strict inference budget, covering text-to-motion, music-to-dance, and speech-to-gesture tasks. To enhance trajectory-level efficiency, we introduce a 3D motion-space MeanFlow formulation with kinematic and dynamic consistency constraints for few-step generation, together with an Adaptive Soft masking mechanism for temporally coherent motion editing. To improve per-step efficiency, we design a lightweight non-autoregressive BiMamba architecture with condition-guided state selection and AdaIN-based condition fusion mechanism, enhancing cross-modal alignment and generalization to longer motion sequences. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FlashMotion achieves overall state-of-the-art performance in both quality and efficiency across text-to-motion, speech-to-gesture, and music-to-dance generation. Code is available at FlashMotion (https://github.com/Sun-Happy-YKX/FlashMotion).

llm.title_ja: FlashMotion：超高速・長期3Dモーション生成
llm.tldr_ja: 厳格な推論予算の下で高品質な長期3Dモーションを生成するため、MeanFlow定式化と軽量な非自己回帰BiMambaアーキテクチャを共同設計したFlashMotionを提案する。
llm.problem: 多くのサンプリングステップを要する生成戦略と、長いシーケンスに対する高い計算・メモリコストが長期3Dモーション生成の障壁となっていること。
llm.method: 3Dモーション空間のMeanFlow定式化と、条件付き状態選択を持つ軽量な非自己回帰BiMambaアーキテクチャの共同設計。
llm.result: テキストからのモーション生成、音楽からのダンス生成、音声からのジェスチャー生成のすべてにおいて、品質と効率の両方で最先端の性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: テキストからモーション

2611.13626.tldr_en: FlashMotion is presented, a co-designed framework for high-quality long-horizon 3D motion generation under a strict inference budget, covering text-to-motion, music-to-dance, and speech-to-gesture tasks, and a lightweight non-autoregressive BiMamba architecture with condition-guided state selection and AdaIN-based condition fusion mechanism, enhancing cross-modal alignment and generalization to longer motion sequences.

2611.13621.title: PUMA: Probability-Constrained Sequential Interaction for Forensic Localization
2611.13621.abstract: Image manipulation localization must jointly exploit semantic structure and noise-sensitive forensic evidence. However, the effects of spatial correspondence, matching quality, and interaction order are often conflated. Existing semantic-forensic fusion methods provide complementary representations, but do not explicitly preserve quality-mismatch information during spatial correspondence or adaptively select the order in which information is propagated across branches. We propose PUMA (Probability-constrained Unbalanced Matching and Aggregation), which combines spatially constrained unbalanced optimal transport with position-wise convex selection between two sequential operators through a shared positional interface. Before normalization, PUMA retains signed transport-mass residuals, constructs row-stochastic cross-branch and within-noise-branch operators, and updates noise features through a gated residual path. PUMA achieves strong localization results on four test sets, with scores on COVERAGE and NIST16 exceeding the published results of the representative methods listed in our comparison. The experiments support the utility of local matching states and adaptive sequential interaction for cross-source localization and several post-processing conditions.

llm.title_ja: PUMA：フォレンジック位置推定のための確率制約付き逐次インタラクション
llm.tldr_ja: 画像操作の位置を特定するため、空間制約付きの不均衡最適輸送と位置ごとの凸選択を組み合わせたPUMAフレームワークを提案し、クロスソースでの優れた測位結果を実現する。
llm.problem: 既存のセマンティック・フォレンジック融合手法が、空間対応における品質の不一致情報を保持せず、情報の伝播順序を適応的に選択できないこと。
llm.method: 空間制約付き不均衡最適輸送と、共有位置インターフェースを通じた2つの逐次演算子間の位置ごとの凸選択を組み合わせたPUMAの提案。
llm.result: COVERAGEおよびNIST16を含む4つのテストセットにおいて既存の代表的手法を超える優れた測位結果を達成した。

2611.13621.tldr_en: PUMA (Probability-constrained Unbalanced Matching and Aggregation), which combines spatially constrained unbalanced optimal transport with position-wise convex selection between two sequential operators through a shared positional interface, is proposed.

2611.13610.title: From Egocentric Human Video to Robot Manipulation in the Era of Embodied Intelligence
2611.13610.abstract: Egocentric human video (EHV) records close-range hand-object interaction (HOI) and the temporal structure of everyday activities, offering a potentially scalable source of experience for robot manipulation. Using this experience for robot control requires recovering useful supervision without recorded robot actions and accounting for differences in morphology, viewpoint, and action space. We define Ego2Robot learning as the process of learning or adapting robot manipulation policies from EHV, organized into four learning paradigms: explicit embodiment transfer, explicit action and task supervision, egocentric video representation pretraining, and latent action and dynamics modeling. The four paradigms differ in what they derive from human video: robot-format demonstrations, interpretable supervision, visual representations, or predictive models of actions and dynamics. For each paradigm, we trace what EHV information is extracted, how robot policies use it, and when the additional data is required. Besides, we review the benchmark datasets that cover EHV, robot demonstrations, and synthetic and simulated resources. This paper links EHV data's contribution to the task information preserved and the robot-specific grounding used during training or deployment. Finally, we identify challenges in physical feasibility, agent coordination, in-context adaptation, controlled evaluation, and predictive control.

llm.title_ja: 一人称視点人間動画から体現AI時代のエージェント型ロボットマニピュレーションへ
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット行動の監視データなしで一人称視点人間動画（EHV）をロボットマニピュレーションの学習に活用する4つの学習パラダイム（Ego2Robot学習）を体系的にレビューする。
llm.problem: 一人称視点人間動画をロボット制御に利用する際、ロボット行動の記録がないことや、形態・視点・行動空間の違いを克服する必要があること。
llm.method: 明示的な体現転移、行動・タスク監督、視覚表現事前学習、潜在行動・ダイナミクスモデリングの4つの学習パラダイムへの整理と分析。
llm.result: EHV情報がタスク情報やロボット特有のグラウンディングにどのように寄与するかを明らかにするとともに、主要な課題とベンチマークを整理した。
llm.limitation: 物理的実現可能性やエージェント調整などにおける今後の課題を特定した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.13610.tldr_en: Ego2Robot learning is defined, which links EHV data's contribution to the task information preserved and the robot-specific grounding used during training or deployment and identifies challenges in physical feasibility, agent coordination, in-context adaptation, controlled evaluation, and predictive control.

2611.13596.title: Towards Reliable VLM Judges: State-Conditional Invariance and Presentation-Aware Diagnostics
2611.13596.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for multimodal and embodied tasks, yet aggregate accuracy or consistency alone does not reveal whether a judge changes its verdict for the right reason. We propose State-Conditional Invariance (SCI), a reliability principle requiring a judge to remain stable under semantics-preserving changes in presentation while responding to causal interventions that change the task outcome. We instantiate SCI in GridWM-Judge, a simulator-grounded diagnostic benchmark built from deterministic MiniGrid trajectories with aligned Full, evidence-removal, and counterfactual variants, plus presentation and representation probes. Across five diagnostic tasks, GridWM-Judge tests local perception, action-conditioned transitions, presentation stability, representation exchangeability, and Full-CF causal discrimination. Our diagnostic evaluations reveal heterogeneous failure modes, including sensitivity to evidence presentation and encoding, low activation on successful trajectories, and weak paired counterfactual discrimination. Perception-controlled analyses further indicate that visual grounding and objective recovery are substantial, model-dependent bottlenecks. These results motivate jointly reporting correctness, presentation stability, and causal sensitivity instead of relying on a single score.

llm.title_ja: 信頼性の高いVLMジャッジに向けて：状態条件付き不変性とプレゼンテーション認識型診断
llm.tldr_ja: マルチモーダル・体現タスクの自動評価において、意味を保った提示の変化に対して安定しつつ因果的介入には応答するという信頼性原則「状態条件付き不変性（SCI）」を提案する。
llm.problem: ビジョン言語モデル（VLM）を自動ジャッジとして用いる際、総合的な正解率や一貫性だけでは正しい理由で判定を下しているか分からないこと。
llm.method: 意味保存型の提示変更に対する安定性と因果介入に対する応答性を要求する状態条件付き不変性（SCI）の原則と診断用ベンチマークGridWM-Judgeの構築。
llm.result: 視覚的グラウンディングや目的の復元がモデルに依存する大きなボトルネックであることを明らかにした。

2611.13596.tldr_en: State-Conditional Invariance (SCI) is proposed, a reliability principle requiring a judge to remain stable under semantics-preserving changes in presentation while responding to causal interventions that change the task outcome.

2611.13592.title: Few-Shot Residual Adaptation of Pretrained Latent World Models
2611.13592.abstract: Pretrained latent world models can support visual planning and control, but their predictions may fail when physical dynamics change at deployment. We study whether such models can adapt from only a few interactions without modifying their pretrained weights or identifying the changed physical parameters. We introduce a few-shot residual adaptation approach that learns self-supervised corrections from latent prediction errors. The corrections are applied both inside the latent predictor and directly to its predicted latent state, while the pretrained world model remains frozen. We evaluate the approach in simulation and on a real robot under center-of-mass and friction shifts. These changes reduce the success of the frozen model to near zero. Using three interaction episodes for adaptation, our dual-site approach recovers 90\% success under the center-of-mass shift and 100\% under the modified friction on the real robot. Ablations show that correcting both locations outperforms single-site adaptation. Our diagnostics further suggest that much of the learned correction reduces a general prediction mismatch, while successful control also depends on shift-specific information captured during adaptation.

llm.title_ja: 事前学習済み潜在世界モデルの少数ショット残差適応
llm.tldr_ja: 物理ダイナミクスが変化した環境下で、事前学習済み潜在世界モデルの重みを固定したまま、予測誤差から自己教師ありの残差補正を学習することで数回のインタラクションで適応する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: デプロイ時に物理ダイナミクスが変化すると、事前学習済みの潜在世界モデルによる予測や制御が失敗すること。
llm.method: 潜在予測器内と予測された潜在状態の双方に、潜在予測誤差に基づく自己教師あり残差補正を適用するデュアルサイト適応手法の提案。
llm.result: 重心や摩擦の変化により成功率がほぼゼロになった実機ロボットにおいて、3エピソードの適応で最大100%の成功率を回復した。

2611.13592.tldr_en: A few-shot residual adaptation approach that learns self-supervised corrections from latent prediction errors that outperforms single-site adaptation and suggests that much of the learned correction reduces a general prediction mismatch, while successful control also depends on shift-specific information captured during adaptation.

2611.13552.title: How Post-Training Influences Verbalized Algorithmic Computation in Language Models
2611.13552.abstract: Post-training improves language-model reasoning, but how it changes the use of internal information and verbalized chain of thought (CoT) remains unclear. We study successive SFT, DPO, and RLVR checkpoints of Olmo-3-7B-Instruct on multi-digit addition, using carry values as known intermediate state. Probes recover carry information from internal activations with similar accuracy in SFT and RLVR, although manipulating this information does not reliably control model outputs. In contrast, the usefulness of verbalized reasoning differs: CoTs produced by RLVR yield higher accuracy across receiving checkpoints than those produced by SFT or DPO. We also show that carry-related statements receive higher importance scores after RLVR than matched random controls. DPO shows similar sensitivity to carry-related statements but without comparable accuracy gains. These results suggest that post-training changes the usefulness of written reasoning and sensitivity to its content in meaningful ways, although greater sensitivity does not necessarily coincide with better problem performance.

llm.title_ja: ポストトレーニングが言語モデルにおける言語化されたアルゴリズム計算に与える影響
llm.tldr_ja: 多桁の足し算を用いてOlmo-3-7B-InstructのSFT、DPO、RLVRチェックポイントを分析し、ポストトレーニングが記述された推論の有用性やその内容に対する感度を変化させることを示す。
llm.problem: ポストトレーニングがモデルの内部情報の利用や言語化された思考の連鎖（CoT）をどのように変化させるかが明確ではないこと。
llm.method: SFT、DPO、RLVRの各チェックポイントにおけるキャリー情報をプローブで抽出し、その活性化や記述された推論の正確性を比較分析する。
llm.result: RLVRによって生成されたCoTは他の手法よりも高い正確性をもたらし、キャリー関連の記述に対する重要度スコアが高くなることを示した。

2611.13552.tldr_en: It is suggested that post-training changes the usefulness of written reasoning and sensitivity to its content in meaningful ways, although greater sensitivity does not necessarily coincide with better problem performance.

2611.13528.title: GEMOR-GS: Global Extrinsic-calibration-refined Mapping and Online Relocalization for 3D Gaussian-Splatting SLAM
2611.13528.abstract: Photorealistic and metrically consistent world representations are a primary requirement for LiDAR--inertial--visual SLAM systems that serve robots over continuous operation. 3D Gaussian splatting makes such representations attainable by supplying an explicit, renderable, and queryable scene model. We present GEMOR-GS (Global Extrinsic-calibration-refined Mapping and Online Relocalization for 3D Gaussian-Splatting SLAM) to make the Gaussian map geometrically accurate, globally refined, and re-enterable, providing a better appearance for robot perception and decision-making. To improve the 3DGS map, the LiDAR--camera extrinsic is first estimated offline by direct-method alignment over dedicated calibration segments and reused by all following online and offline processes. Under the calibrated geometry, keyframe poses and Gaussian parameters are refined alternately under a gated differentiable-rendering and LiDAR--projection objective. The final global reconstruction is then rebuilt from the refined keyframe schema with all online constraints lifted. For the robot SLAM lifecycle, the method recovers the pose from the 3DGS map after tracking loss through an XFeat bypass map, RANSAC-PnP coarse localization, and Gaussian RGB-D warp refinement. Experiments on one self-collected and five public sequences quantify each element: the offline reconstruction wins all paired keyframes against the online map by 14.3--19.9 dB, improves PSNR by approximately 9 dB over Gaussian-LIC2, and achieves 86--100% held-out relocalization success tied to extrinsic quality. The results show that GEMOR-GS improves the geometric accuracy, appearance fidelity, and re-enterability of the 3DGS map, serving as a dependable robot world model for SLAM and downstream tasks.

llm.title_ja: GEMOR-GS：3DガウススプラッティングSLAMのための大域的外因校正を伴う高精度マッピングとオンライン再局所化
llm.tldr_ja: 幾何学的に正確で再突入可能な3Dガウススプラッティング地図を構築・利用するため、大域的外因校正と微分可能レンダリングに基づく最適化、およびオンライン再局所化を統合したGEMOR-GSを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットの継続的な運用のためにフォトリアルで指標的に一貫した世界表現が必要であるが、既存の3DガウススプラッティングSLAMでは幾何学的精度や再突入性が不十分であること。
llm.method: オフラインのLiDAR-カメラ外因校正、キーフレームポーズとガウスパラメータの交互最適化、およびXFeatバイパスとRANSAC-PnPを用いた再局所化の統合。
llm.result: オンラインマップに対してPSNRが約9 dB向上し、86〜100%の保持データに対する再局所化成功率を達成した。

2611.13528.tldr_en: The results show that GEMOR-GS improves the geometric accuracy, appearance fidelity, and re-enterability of the 3DGS map, serving as a dependable robot world model for SLAM and downstream tasks.

2611.13517.title: Differentiable Filtering for Inertial Odometry
2611.13517.abstract: Accurate inertial odometry is critical for autonomous systems but suffers from unbounded drift caused by the integration of sensor noise and biases. In approaches such as TLIO, neural pseudo-measurements are trained independently of their downstream filter. This paper introduces Differentiable Filtering for Inertial Odometry (DFIO), a learning framework that embeds the update stages of an error-state Kalman filter directly into a computational graph. Following standalone pre-training, DFIO jointly optimizes the displacement and covariance output heads using posterior-position supervision through differentiable measurement updates. The proposed system is validated on public pedestrian motion datasets featuring both calibrated and uncalibrated inertial measurements. Experimental results on a pedestrian dataset demonstrate that DFIO reduces mean absolute and one-second relative translation errors by 13.2% and 39.6% relative to the TLIO baseline, and by 7.7% and 17.4% relative to its pre-trained counterpart. Furthermore, evaluations on uncalibrated smartphone inertial data indicate that the proposed method effectively mitigates translational drift and maintains trajectory alignment under highly noisy sensor conditions. Source code will be made publicly available.

llm.title_ja: 慣性オドメトリのための微分可能フィルタリング
llm.tldr_ja: 誤差状態カルマンフィルタの更新ステージを計算グラフに直接埋め込む学習フレームワークDFIOを提案し、歩行者モーションデータセットにおいてドリフトを大幅に削減する。
llm.problem: 正確な慣性オドメトリがセンサノイズとバイアスの統合による無制限のドリフトに悩まされていること。
llm.method: 誤差状態カルマンフィルタの更新ステージを計算グラフに埋め込み、事後位置監視を通じて変位と共分散の出力ヘッドを共同最適化するDFIOの提案。
llm.result: TLIOベースラインと比較して平均並進誤差を13.2%削減し、未校正のスマートフォン慣性データでも安定した軌道整合性を維持した。
keywords_ja: 微分可能フィルタリング

2611.13517.tldr_en: Differentiable Filtering for Inertial Odometry (DFIO), a learning framework that embeds the update stages of an error-state Kalman filter directly into a computational graph, is introduced.

2611.13499.title: DeRep: Learning Depth Representations for End-to-End Navigation in Cluttered Environments
2611.13499.abstract: End-to-end navigation in cluttered environments relies on compact visual representations to support collision avoidance and goal-directed motion. Existing methods typically learn these representations jointly with the policy or through observation reconstruction, which does not explicitly specify what information the representation should preserve. Moreover, they are usually evaluated with a single downstream policy learner, although the benefit of a representation may depend on how the policy is learned. It therefore remains unclear how different representation-learning objectives affect downstream navigation performance and robustness. This work proposes DeRep, a navigation-oriented representation-learning method that combines local bird's-eye-view reachability supervision with depth reconstruction. To compare representation objectives under controlled conditions, we pretrain encoders with a common architecture and freeze them during downstream learning. We evaluate the representations using a linear policy probe, flow-matching imitation learning, and reinforcement learning with PPO. DeRep achieves the lowest linear policy probe prediction error and outperforms reconstruction alone across all six tested PPO conditions. In imitation learning, both reachability-based objectives achieve higher mean success rates than reconstruction alone, with similar mean success rates between the reachability-only and joint objectives. These results demonstrate consistent benefits of incorporating reachability supervision into depth representation pretraining across different downstream learning methods and evaluation conditions. We further deploy the PPO policy with the frozen DeRep encoder in Gazebo and on a physical quadrotor without fine-tuning, demonstrating its capability for zero-shot sim-to-sim and sim-to-real transfer.

llm.title_ja: DeRep：複雑な環境におけるエンドツーエンドナビゲーションのための深度表現学習
llm.tldr_ja: 局所的な鳥瞰図（BEV）の到達可能性監視と深度再構成を組み合わせたナビゲーション向け表現学習手法DeRepを提案し、多様な下流の学習手法で優れた性能を示す。
llm.problem: 複雑な環境でのエンドツーエンドナビゲーションにおいて、既存の表現学習が何を保存すべきかを明示せず、下流のポリシー学習方法への依存性が不明確であること。
llm.method: 局所的な鳥瞰図の到達可能性監視と深度再構成を組み合わせたナビゲーション向けエンコーダの事前学習手法DeRepの提案。
llm.result: 線形ポリシープロプで最小の予測誤差を達成し、模倣学習や強化学習の双方において再構成単独の手法を上回る成功率を示した。
keywords_ja: エンドツーエンドナビゲーション

2611.13499.tldr_en: DeRep is proposed, a navigation-oriented representation-learning method that combines local bird's-eye-view reachability supervision with depth reconstruction and achieves the lowest linear policy probe prediction error and outperforms reconstruction alone across all six tested PPO conditions.

2611.13494.title: Route-Time Conflict Maps for Cooperative End-to-End Autonomous Driving
2611.13494.abstract: Existing cooperative end-to-end driving works at Class A (status-sharing) of the SAE J3216 classes of cooperative driving automation (CDA): vehicles exchange what they perceive, not what they intend, so each plans alone when to go, which limits cooperation and leads to deadlock when both vehicles yield or to collisions when both go. We present When2Go, a cooperative end-to-end driving system that learns when to go by sharing intent under CDA Class B or higher. Each vehicle broadcasts its LiDAR detections with forecast motion as instance tokens, together with its plan and intended trajectory. The receiver draws the fused detections, forecasts and partner plans into a route-time conflict map, the occupancy along its route over the planning horizon, on which a planner scores candidate speed profiles. Where two intended trajectories conflict, an order gate, a precedence network distilled from a right-of-way rule, decides who goes first; both vehicles evaluate it on the same messages and so reach the same order. When2Go imitates the rule-based expert of V2Xverse, which sees the simulator's ground truth; stops that When2Go cannot observe within its 2 s planning horizon are relabelled, so that it does not learn to wait without an observable cause. For our runs only, the benchmarks' PID controller steers by When2Go's waypoints instead of the route, and its forced push of long-waiting vehicles is off. With one model, When2Go sets the state of the art on three closed-loop CARLA benchmarks: 97.8 and 90.7 driving score on InterDrive without and with traffic (best published 90.1 and 78.9), 70.0 on the public V2Xverse protocol (best of sixteen rerun methods 59.1) and 88.2 on MDrive (best rerun 85.1), with 95.0% of its vehicles collision-free (87.7%).

llm.title_ja: 協調型エンドツーエンド自動運転のためのルート・時間コンフリクトマップ
llm.tldr_ja: 車両間で意図や予測軌道を共有する協調型自動運転システムWhen2Goを提案し、ルート・時間コンフリクトマップを用いて衝突のない走行順序を決定することで複数のCARLAベンチマークで最高性能を達成する。
llm.problem: 既存の協調型自動運転が知覚情報のみを交換し意図を共有しないため、デッドロックや衝突を引き起こすこと。
llm.method: LiDAR検出と予測軌道、計画をインスタンストークンとしてブロードキャストし、ルート上の占有状態を示すルート・時間コンフリクトマップと優先順位ネットワークを構築するWhen2Goの提案。
llm.result: CARLAの3つの閉ループベンチマークにおいて、InterDriveで最高97.8の駆動スコアを記録するなど、既存の最先端を更新した。

2611.13494.tldr_en: When2Go is presented, a cooperative end-to-end driving system that learns when to go by sharing intent under CDA Class B or higher, and imitates the rule-based expert of V2Xverse, which sees the simulator's ground truth.

2611.13482.title: ExRL: Sample-Efficient Online Adaptation of Long-Chunk Policies via Execution Length Control
2611.13482.abstract: Predicting long action chunks, often spanning dozens of timesteps, has become a key ingredient in increasingly capable robot policies. In this paper, we find that adapting these long-chunk policies with existing reinforcement learning (RL) methods can require many online samples due to the high dimensionality of the action chunks being optimized, making such adaptation impractical in real-world scenarios where interaction data are costly to collect. Our key insight is to shift adaptation from optimizing actions to optimizing how long to execute each predicted action chunk. This keeps the adaptation space low-dimensional while its expressivity grows with the chunk size. We thus introduce Execution at the Right Length (ExRL), a simple approach which augments the base policy with a lightweight adapter that predicts the execution length of each chunk and is trained using off-policy RL algorithms. Across simulation benchmarks and real-world robotic tasks, ExRL enables sample-efficient adaptation of a diverse range of long-chunk policies with minimal task-specific hyperparameter tuning.
2611.13482.hf_summary_en: Execution at the Right Length (ExRL) enables sample-efficient adaptation of long-chunk robot policies by training a lightweight adapter to predict each chunk’s execution length using off-policy reinforcement learning.

llm.title_ja: ExRL：実行長制御による長チャンクポリシーのサンプル効率の高いオンライン適応
llm.tldr_ja: 実行 at the Right Length (ExRL) により、行動チャンクの最適化ではなく実行長を予測する軽量アダプタを強化学習で訓練することで、長チャンクロボットポリシーのサンプル効率の高い適応を実現する。
llm.problem: 長大な行動チャンクを予測するロボットポリシーを強化学習で適応させる際、高次元な行動空間のため多大なオンラインサンプルが必要になること。
llm.method: 行動の最適化ではなく、各チャンクの実行長を予測する軽量アダプタをオフポリシー強化学習で訓練するExRLの提案。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界のロボットタスクにおいて、最小限のハイパーパラメータ調整で多様な長チャンクポリシーのサンプル効率の良い適応を可能にした。

2611.13482.tldr_en: This paper introduces Execution at the Right Length (ExRL), a simple approach which augments the base policy with a lightweight adapter that predicts the execution length of each chunk and is trained using off-policy RL algorithms.

2611.13472.title: Rhythmic-Semantic Co-Speech Gestures for Emotional Dialogue in Robots
2611.13472.abstract: Co-speech gestures can increase engagement and improve speech understanding. Yet, most data-driven robot systems generate either rhythmic beat-like motion or semantically meaningful iconic gestures, but not both. We present an emotion-aware rhythmic-semantic co-speech gesture system that generates iconic and beat behaviors in real time from text and the robot's internal emotional state. We formalize the task of beat-iconic gesture generation using emotion and propose lightweight models that predict iconic timing and intensity, then fill the remaining spans with emotion-conditioned beats at an appropriate intensity level. We train on the BEAT2 dataset and deploy the system on the social robot Haru. In an online user study with 60 participants, our method shows stronger speech-gesture alignment and is preferred over baseline methods.

llm.title_ja: ロボットの感情的対話のためのリズム・意味的協調音声ジェスチャー
llm.tldr_ja: テキストとロボットの内部感情状態から、アイコニック（意味的）およびビート（リズム的）ジェスチャーをリアルタイムで生成する感情認識型のリズム・意味的協調音声ジェスチャーシステムを提案する。
llm.problem: 大半のデータ駆動型ロボットシステムが、リズム的なビート動作か意味のあるアイコニックジェスチャーのどちらか一方しか生成できないこと。
llm.method: 感情を用いてアイコニックジェスチャーのタイミングと強度を予測し、残りのスパンを感情条件付きビートで埋める軽量モデルの構築。
llm.result: BEAT2データセットで訓練し、社会的ロボットHaruに実装した結果、音声とジェスチャーの整流性が向上しユーザーに好まれた。
keywords_ja: 協調音声ジェスチャー
ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2611.13472.tldr_en: This work formalizes the task of beat-iconic gesture generation using emotion and proposes lightweight models that predict iconic timing and intensity, then fill the remaining spans with emotion-conditioned beats at an appropriate intensity level.

2611.13382.title: Discrete Model-Based Diffusion for Combinatorial Optimization in Multi-Robot Task Allocation
2611.13382.abstract: Decision making in multi-agent and multi-robot systems often involves discrete decision variables, leading to NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems that must be solved within seconds for near real-time implementation. Denoising diffusion has emerged as a powerful tool for such problems, but existing approaches face a trade-off: Model-Based Diffusion (MBD) incorporates diffusion in sampling-based optimization (SBO) without training but only over continuous spaces, while existing diffusion-based combinatorial solvers operate over discrete spaces but require offline training. To this end, we propose Discrete Model-Based Diffusion (Discrete MBD), a training-free SBO method that directly optimizes discrete variables by approximating categorical reverse transition distributions through Monte Carlo sampling. We establish a finite-step lower bound on the probability of finding a global minimizer and show that this bound converges to one as the number of denoising steps increases. Extensive experiments on generic integer programs and heterogeneous multi-robot coalition formation and scheduling demonstrate that Discrete MBD outperforms SBO baselines in nearly all settings while achieving solution quality competitive with that of mixed-integer programming and reinforcement learning methods at a fraction of their computational cost.

llm.title_ja: マルチロボットのタスク割り当てにおける組合せ最適化のための離散モデルベース拡散
llm.tldr_ja: モンテカルロサンプリングによりカテゴリカルな逆遷移分布を近似し、オフライン学習なしで離散変数を直接最適化する訓練不要のサンプリングベース最適化手法「Discrete MBD」を提案し、ほぼすべての設定でベースラインを上回る性能を示した。
llm.problem: マルチエージェントシステムの意思決定におけるNP困難な組合せ最適化をリアルタイムに解く必要があるが、既存の拡散モデルは連続値のみを扱うか、離散空間でオフライン学習を要するトレードオフがある。
llm.method: モンテカルロサンプリングを用いてカテゴリカルな逆遷移分布を近似し、離散変数を直接最適化する訓練不要のサンプリングベース最適化手法「Discrete MBD」を提案した。
llm.result: 汎用整数計画法や異種マルチロボットの連合形成・スケジューリングの実験において、ほぼすべての設定でSBOベースラインを上回り、MIPやRL手法に匹敵する解品質を低計算コストで達成した。
keywords_ja: サンプリングベース最適化

2611.13382.tldr_en: Discrete Model-Based Diffusion is proposed, a training-free SBO method that directly optimizes discrete variables by approximating categorical reverse transition distributions through Monte Carlo sampling and establishes a finite-step lower bound on the probability of finding a global minimizer.

2611.13379.title: Fastener-centric acquisition and AND/OR graph representation of state-dependent disassembly knowledge from CAD-derived virtual assemblies
2611.13379.abstract: Design-stage disassemblability assessment requires knowledge of product structure and the operations available in each assembly state, but CAD assemblies do not directly specify state-dependent disassembly operations. This paper proposes a fastener-centric virtual-disassembly framework that acquires such knowledge from CAD-derived virtual assemblies.
