Fasteners jointly releasing the same constraint are grouped into operation-level sets, avoiding enumeration of arbitrary individual-fastener orders. Their removability is evaluated through state-dependent visibility and tool-access checks and torque-driven virtual-removal trials. After fastener removal, graph-based reasoning identifies candidate moving units, whose separation is evaluated by initial-motion screening, path generation, and physics-based validation. The acquired operations, states, dependencies, validated paths, and simulation-derived attributes are organized into a Transformed AND/OR Graph for subsequent planning and design evaluation. Exhaustive verification with a controlled toy assembly found no branching violations for introduced tool-accessibility and precedence conditions. Evaluation with a 54-component OpenManipulator Chain gripper demonstrated state-dependent fastener-removal and part- or subassembly-separation operations. Visibility and tool-accessibility evaluations pruned 51.4% of fastener-set candidate evaluations, while removal of obstructing components enabled previously inaccessible fastener operations. Operation-level grouping and screening thereby limited detailed physical validation to mechanically plausible candidates. The results demonstrate the feasibility of acquiring product-specific disassembly knowledge from CAD-derived virtual assemblies before manufacture, supporting subsequent disassembly reasoning and design-for-disassembly evaluation.

llm.title_ja: CAD由来の仮想アセンブリからの状態依存分解知識のファスナ中心型取得とAND/ORグラフ表現
llm.tldr_ja: CAD由来の仮想アセンブリから状態依存の分解知識を獲得するファスナ中心の仮想分解フレームワークを提案し、可視性や工具アクセスのチェックにより詳細な物理検証を効率化した。
llm.problem: 設計段階の分解性評価では製品構造や状態ごとの分解操作の知識が必要だが、CADアセンブリは状態依存の分解操作を直接指定しない。
llm.method: 同じ制約を解除するファスナを操作レベルのセットにグループ化し、可視性、工具アクセスチェック、トルク駆動の仮想取り外し試行によって取り外しやすさを評価するフレームワークを提案した。
llm.result: 54部品のグリッパー評価において、可視性・工具アクセス評価によりファスナセット候補の評価を51.4%削減し、機械的に妥当な候補に物理検証を限定できた。

2611.13379.tldr_en: The results demonstrate the feasibility of acquiring product-specific disassembly knowledge from CAD-derived virtual assemblies before manufacture, supporting subsequent disassembly reasoning and design-for-disassembly evaluation.

2611.13370.title: AHEADance: Anticipatory Humanoid Dance from Streaming Audio
2611.13370.abstract: A humanoid that dances to streamed music must commit each motion chunk before it has heard the music that chunk accompanies, and must continue from motion it has already committed. We present AHEADance, a robot-native streaming dance generator executed on a humanoid robot by a whole-body tracker. ListenAhead conditions each chunk on heard music and a frozen music model's forecasts of the coming music, aligned to their target times and weighted by reliability. The forecasts carry the timing of upcoming beats almost as well as the actual future; with them, the generator is better synchronized with the music and concentrates more motion energy at its song's beat frequency. Commit Forcing trains continuation from the model's own committed chunks, updating both the latent history and the decoded boundary of the next chunk; it reduces low activity from 83.5% to 10.3%, the level of real dance. Three music evaluators, each validated on real G1 dance, test synchronization, song and style. On a physical Unitree G1, it dances while the music plays and comes to rest when it stops, without a fall. Project page: https://ihcr.github.io/AHEADance

llm.title_ja: AHEADance：ストリーミング音声からの先読み型ヒューマノイドダンス
llm.tldr_ja: 聴取中の音楽と凍結された音楽モデルの予測を条件付けて未来のビートに同期し、自己のコミット済みチャンクから継続を学習するロボットネイティブなストリーミングダンスジェネレータ「AHEADance」を開発し、Unitree G1の実機で転倒せずに踊ることを実証した。
llm.problem: ストリーミング音楽に合わせて踊るヒューマノイドは、伴奏音楽を聴く前に各モーションチャンクを決定し、すでにコミットしたモーションから継続する必要がある。
llm.method: 聴取中の音楽と凍結された音楽モデルの予測を条件付け、コミット済みチャンクからの継続を学習するCommit Forcingを導入したロボットネイティブなストリーミングダンスジェネレータ「AHEADance」を提案した。
llm.result: 実機のUnitree G1において、音楽が流れている間は音楽に合わせて踊り、音楽が止まると転倒せずに静止することを実証し、低活動状態を83.5%から10.3%に削減した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2611.13370.tldr_en: A robot-native streaming dance generator executed on a humanoid robot by a whole-body tracker, ListenAhead, which conditions each chunk on heard music and a frozen music model's forecasts of the coming music, aligned to their target times and weighted by reliability.

2611.13344.title: PneuGen: Task-Driven Agentic Co-Design of Soft Pneumatic Robots
2611.13344.abstract: Task-driven design of soft robots requires the consideration of factors such as geometry, morphology, material properties, and actuation, resulting in a large and complex design space that is challenging to explore. Computational optimisation methods leverage signals from simulation to iteratively improve designs to achieve task objectives. However, these methods typically demand high computational load for both optimisation and simulation. We present PneuGen, an agentic co-design framework for soft robots that leverages Large Language Model (LLM) agents to search over the soft robot design space efficiently. A designer agent proposes design programs from a parametric component library, and a separate critic agent analyses simulation diagnostics and recommends targeted revisions. Fitted module response models provide reusable physical priors relating geometry and pressure to deformation. Design programs are automatically validated and converted into finite-element simulations, enabling iterative evaluation. Across grasping tasks on primitive shapes and challenging objects, as well as shape-matching tasks that require multi-directional planar and 3D deformation, the proposed framework significantly outperforms prior computational optimisation baselines. Ablation experiments also highlight the utility of the critic agent and the module response model in facilitating efficient design. We additionally demonstrate the agent-generated soft robot designs in real-world shape-matching and grasping tasks.

llm.title_ja: PneuGen：タスク駆動型のエージェントによるソフト空気圧ロボットの協調設計
llm.tldr_ja: LLMエージェントを活用してソフトロボットの設計空間を効率的に探索し、有限要素シミュレーションでの反復評価を行うエージェント協調設計フレームワーク「PneuGen」を提案し、実世界の把持・形状一致タスクで優れた性能を示した。
llm.problem: ソフトロボットのタスク駆動型設計は、形状、モジュール、物性、駆動などの膨大で複雑な設計空間を探索する必要があり、計算負荷が高い。
llm.method: LLMエージェントが設計案を提案し、批評エージェントがシミュレーション診断を分析して修正を推奨する協調設計フレームワーク「PneuGen」を提案した。
llm.result: プリミティブ形状や困難な対象の把持、形状一致タスクにおいて既存の最適化ベースラインを大幅に上回り、実世界のタスクでの有効性も実証した。

2611.13344.tldr_en: PneuGen is presented, an agentic co-design framework for soft robots that leverages Large Language Model agents to search over the soft robot design space efficiently and significantly outperforms prior computational optimisation baselines.

2611.13311.title: One Trajectory, Two Requirements: Accuracy and Local Stability in Euler Sampling for Flow Matching Policies
2611.13311.abstract: Flow matching robot policies commonly use a fixed Euler step count selected from offline accuracy sweeps. At inference time, however, each policy input (visual observation, robot state, and language instruction) together with a source-noise draw defines a different ODE trajectory and sequence of local Jacobians. We ask whether a step count that accurately follows the nominal noise-to-action trajectory can still be too coarse for strongly contracting directions around it. An exact two-coordinate system and a controlled augmentation of six trained flow models show that trajectory accuracy and local Euler stability can impose different step requirements even when the original learned transport is unchanged. We then study a frozen $π_{0.5}$-LIBERO checkpoint without modifying its weights or action dynamics. Across 30 policy inputs from 10 LIBERO-10 tasks, the Jacobian exhibits strong contracting directions near the action endpoint, yet no sampled mode violates the Euler non-expansion condition. On five of those inputs, accuracy sweeps require 4--9 Euler steps at 5% terminal error and 87--112 at 1%. These five paired cases are therefore consistent with accuracy-limited rather than stability-limited sampling under this local criterion, while the controlled experiments show why endpoint accuracy alone cannot rule out a separate stability requirement.

llm.title_ja: 1つの軌跡、2つの要件：フローマッチングポリシーのオイラーサンプリングにおける精度と局所安定性
llm.tldr_ja: フローマッチングポリシーのオイラーサンプリングにおいて、軌跡の精度と局所的なオイラー安定性が異なるステップ数を要求する場合があることを、厳密な座標系と学習済みフローモデルの検証により示した。
llm.problem: フローマッチングのロボットポリシーは固定のオイラーステップ数を使用するが、推論時の入力やノイズによって異なるODE軌跡や局所ヤコビアンが定義されるため、精度と安定性の要件が異なる可能性がある。
llm.method: 厳密な2座標系と6つの学習済みフローモデルを用いた拡張により、公称のノイズ対アクション軌跡に追従する精度と、その周囲の強く収縮する方向における局所安定性のステップ要件を分析した。
llm.result: LIBERO-10タスクを用いた検証において、アクション終端付近で強い収縮方向を示すもののオイラー非膨張条件には違反せず、精度制限と安定性制限のサンプリングの違いを明らかにした。

2611.13311.tldr_en: Five paired cases are consistent with accuracy-limited rather than stability-limited sampling under this local criterion, while the controlled experiments show why endpoint accuracy alone cannot rule out a separate stability requirement.

2611.13307.title: Does Haptic Connection to a Healthy Partner Improve Motor Learning in Chronic Stroke? A Pilot Study of Robot-Based Dyadic Training
2611.13307.abstract: Purpose: Robot-based haptic dyads, where two users exchange forces through robots, have been proposed for robot-assisted neurorehabilitation. This intervention could increase motor learning by promoting motor variability, providing an implicit communication channel, and facilitating social interaction. Despite the potential benefits, few studies have investigated robot-based haptic dyads for neurological populations, and none have included a comprehensive clinical assessment. Design/Methodology/Approach: We present a pilot study investigation of individuals with chronic stroke learning a complex tracking task in solo and dyad conditions. Prior to training, participants completed a battery of cognitive, motor, and sensory assessments. We assessed changes in key kinematic outcomes including tracking error, distance traveled, mean absolute power, and sample entropy. We also performed a correlation analysis of clinical scores with baseline tracking errors. Findings: Baseline tracking error was strongly correlated (r > 0.6) with lower cognitive scores and higher motor scores. Only the solo group demonstrated lower tracking error at assessment (Δ = -5.33, 95%CI [-10.25, -0.40], p = 0.027), but this result was tempered by the removal of an outlier participant. Neither group demonstrated clear retention. The dyad group showed significantly elevated performance, effort, and movement complexity during training. Research Limitations/Implications: The selected task was too difficult to reveal learning for either group, which may be related to its high cognitive demand. Sample size and stroke heterogeneity were also limitation. Originality/Value: Dyadic training increased movement complexity and effort, which are associated with better motor learning. Clinical characteristics such as lesion location, cognition, sensation, and chronicity may influence potential benefits of dyadic training.

llm.title_ja: 健康なパートナーとの触覚接続は慢性脳卒中の運動学習を改善するか？：ロボットベースの二者間訓練のパイロット研究
llm.tldr_ja: 慢性脳卒中患者を対象にロボットを介した二者間訓練（ハプティック・ダイアド）の運動学習への影響を調査したパイロット研究において、二者間訓練は訓練中の動作複雑性と労力を高めたが、保持効果は明確でなかった。
llm.problem: ロボットベースのハプティック・ダイアドは運動学習を促進する可能性が提案されているが、神経疾患集団に対する調査や包括的な臨床評価を行った研究はほとんどない。
llm.method: 慢性脳卒中患者が単独および二者間（ダイアド）の条件で複雑な追従タスクを学習するパイロット研究を実施し、運動学的結果や臨床スコアとの相関を分析した。
llm.result: ダイアドグループは訓練中のパフォーマンス、労力、動作複雑性が有意に高かったが、課題の認知負担の高さなどの理由により明確な保持や学習の向上は示されなかった。
llm.limitation: 選択されたタスクの認知負荷が高すぎて両グループの学習を明らかにできず、サンプルサイズと脳卒中の不均一性も限界である。
keywords_ja: 脳卒中リハビリテーション
ハプティックダイアド

2611.13307.tldr_en: A pilot study investigation of individuals with chronic stroke learning a complex tracking task in solo and dyad conditions found that dyadic training increased movement complexity and effort, which are associated with better motor learning.

2611.13292.title: Large Language Model Explainability for Planning Lunar Rover Trajectories under Uncertainty
2611.13292.abstract: Planning planetary rover trajectories under probabilistic uncertainty is a multi-objective optimization problem that science teams currently iteratively solve and verify by hand. This process becomes impractical when timelines and constraints frequently shift throughout the mission planning phase. Sampling-based planners such as Monte Carlo tree search can speed up this process, but their outputs do not preserve traceability to the science objectives that justify each plan, which the science team needs to verify. We propose an interactive assistant based on a large language model (LLM) that can explain planner trajectories using domain vocabulary and re-run the planner under user-specified conditions to compare alternatives. Previous work has used LLMs inside planner decision-making loops, but we explore using them for post-planning explanation, where they are more likely to be trusted since they do not directly influence planner decisions. Our framework pairs a simulator inspired by the NASA Volatiles Investigating Polar Exploration Rover (VIPER) mission with a ReAct queryable interface that calls curated action tools and retrieval functions. We evaluate the assistant on a query bank consisting of plan comparisons, feasibility, and lookup queries. Experiments show that 90.9% of the assistant's responses are faithful to the planner's outputs, a nearly 65% improvement over zero-shot prompting of the same LLM without tool access, demonstrating the potential for trustworthy explainability of uncertainty-aware traverses with an LLM-based system.

llm.title_ja: 不確実性下での月面ローバ軌跡計画のための大規模言語モデルによる説明可能性
llm.tldr_ja: NASAのVIPERミッションに着想を得たシミュレータとReActクエリインターフェースを組み合わせたLLMベースの対話型アシスタントを提案し、不確実性を考慮したプランナーの軌跡をドメイン用語で忠実に説明できることを示した。
llm.problem: 確率的不確実性下での惑星ローバーの軌跡計画は科学チームが手動で検証・解決しており、計画の変更が多いミッションでは実用的ではないが、サンプリングベースのプランナーの出力はトレーサビリティを欠く。
llm.method: NASAのVIPERミッションに着想を得たシミュレータと、ツールを呼び出すReActクエリインターフェースを組み合わせた、プランナーの事後説明を行うLLMベースの対話型アシスタントを提案した。
llm.result: クエリバンクを用いた実験において、アシスタントの応答の90.9%がプランナーの出力に忠実であり、ツールアクセスなしのゼロショットプロンプトに比べて約65%の改善を達成した。

2611.13292.tldr_en: This work proposes an interactive assistant based on a large language model (LLM) that can explain planner trajectories using domain vocabulary and re-run the planner under user-specified conditions to compare alternatives, demonstrating the potential for trustworthy explainability of uncertainty-aware traverses with an LLM-based system.

2611.13271.title: RaMOD: Moving-Object Detection from Raw mmWave Radar Cubes under Ego Motion
2611.13271.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar provides weather-robust sensing and direct Doppler measurements, yet automotive perception pipelines often reduce its output to sparse point clouds or two-dimensional projections, leaving raw range-azimuth-Doppler (RAD) cubes underutilized. Ego motion induces Doppler responses from world-static structures, while Doppler wrapping aliases radial velocities, complicating moving-object detection and velocity estimation. We present RaMOD (Radar-based Moving-Object Detection), a real-time framework for moving-object detection and velocity estimation from raw RAD cubes acquired by a vehicle-mounted single-chip radar. RaMOD explicitly estimates frame-wise ego motion and uses the estimated radar translational velocity to predict the Doppler region of world-static structures and suppress returns within it. It temporally encodes the suppressed cubes into multi-scale features to predict RAD-space boxes with class labels. For each detected object, it predicts radial and forward velocities under raw-Doppler and Doppler-unwrapped hypotheses, together with Doppler-wrapping probabilities. On our BRIDGE-Liv dataset, RaMOD outperforms all compared raw-radar methods across RAD-cube, RA, and RD detection settings, achieving 80.8% cube mAP at IoU 0.30, 15.7 percentage points above the strongest RAD-cube baseline. Velocity MAE is 1.128 m/s, with 99.87% Doppler-wrapping accuracy.

llm.title_ja: RaMOD：自己運動下での生ミリ波レーダキューブからの移動物体検出
llm.tldr_ja: 車載単一チップレーダから得られる生のレンジ・方位・ドップラー（RAD）キューブから、自己運動を推定して静止構造物のドップラー領域を抑制し、移動物体の検出と速度推定を行うリアルタイムフレームワーク「RaMOD」を提案した。
llm.problem: 自動車の知覚パイプラインはミリ波レーダの出力をスパースな点群等に縮小するため生RADキューブが十分に活用されておらず、自己運動やドップラーラッピングが移動物体検出を複雑にしている。
llm.method: フレームごとの自己運動を明示的に推定し、静止構造物のドップラー領域を予測・抑制した上で、マルチスケール特徴にエンコードしてRAD空間のボックスとクラスラベルを予測するリアルタイムフレームワーク「RaMOD」を提案した。
llm.result: BRIDGE-Livデータセットにおいて、すべての比較対象の生レーダ手法を上回り、80.8%のキューブmAP、速度MAE 1.128 m/s、99.87%のドップラーラッピング精度を達成した。

2611.13271.tldr_en: RaMOD (Radar-based Moving-Object Detection), a real-time framework for moving-object detection and velocity estimation from raw RAD cubes acquired by a vehicle-mounted single-chip radar, outperforms all compared raw-radar methods across RAD-cube, RA, and RD detection settings.

2611.13268.title: Force-Closure Condition for Cooperative Multi-robot Pushing of Rectangular Objects
2611.13268.abstract: In cooperative object manipulation, the placement of pushing contacts determines whether force closure can be achieved and agents can generate arbitrary forces and torques on the object correspondingly. This study derives a necessary and sufficient closed-form condition for the planar force closure of a rectangular object, a common object shape in everyday settings, under four frictionless pushing contacts. For a rectangle of length $b$ and width $a$, force closure holds if and only if $(l_1+l_3-b)(l_2+l_4-a)<0$, where $l_1,l_2,l_3,l_4$ are the four edge contact locations. This condition is independent of the object's center of mass and is used to verify contact configurations before contact force allocation. When the condition is not satisfied, the signs of the two factors indicate which opposing contact pair should be adjusted. The condition and adjustment rule are then integrated into a full-pose trajectory-tracking framework as a geometric feasibility layer to demonstrate their use in control. Static wrench feasibility tests validate the proposed condition, while narrow-passage floating-body simulations show that maintaining a force-closure configuration reduces the RMS tracking errors in $x$, $y$, and unwrapped yaw from $12.05$ m, $18.11$ m, and $535.96^\circ$ to $2.24$ m, $2.66$ m, and $2.69^\circ$, respectively.
2611.13268.comment: 7 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables. Published in CAOS 2026
2611.13268.journal_ref: 2026 IEEE Canadian Atlantic Ocean Symposium (CAOS), pp. 165-170, 2026

llm.title_ja: 長方形物体の協調マルチロボット押しにおける力閉包条件
llm.tldr_ja: 4つの摩擦のない押し接点を有する長方形物体について、質量中心に依存しない平面力閉包の必要十分な閉形式条件を導出し、軌跡追従制御の幾何学的実現可能性レイヤーとして統合して追従誤差の大幅な削減を実証した。
llm.problem: 協調物体操作において、押し接点の配置は力閉包が達成できるかを決定し、エージェントが物体に任意の力とトルクを生成できるかを左右する。
llm.method: 長さと幅を持つ長方形物体に対し、4つの摩擦のない接点位置に関する質量中心に依存しない平面力閉包の必要十分条件を数式で導出し、制御フレームワークに幾何学的実現可能性レイヤーとして統合した。
llm.result: 静的レンチの実現可能性テストにより条件を検証し、浮遊体シミュレーションにおいて力閉包構成を維持することで、x、y、ヨー角のRMS追従誤差が劇的に改善されることを示した。

2611.13251.title: Curie's Jarvis: Autonomous Robotic Chemistry Experiments from Printed Protocols
2611.13251.abstract: A person running a bench experiment works from a printed instruction sheet, tells identical containers apart by the labels written on them, and looks at the bench again before each step. Lab automation usually works the other way around: the procedure is written as a script, and containers stand at fixed positions or carry fiducial markers. We present Curie's Jarvis, a system that lets a robot arm carry out a chemistry experiment on a bench set up for people. It reads the steps from a photo of the printed sheet, finds containers on an ordinary bench with no fixed positions or markers, tells identical-looking containers apart by reading their labels in four camera views, locates its target again before every step, and sets how each step is carried out, including its speed, from what is being handled. On a Franka Panda arm, Curie's Jarvis completed 5 of 5 runs of one protocol from a children's chemistry kit and 4 of 5 runs of another, with no human intervention, and in 160 locates on printed and handwritten labels it identified every container correctly. This brings robots a step closer to doing bench chemistry the way people do.
2611.13251.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables. Rumi Loghmani and Bozhang Song contributed equally

llm.title_ja: Curie's Jarvis：印刷されたプロトコルからの自律的なロボット化学実験
llm.tldr_ja: 人間向けにセットアップされた実験台で、ロボットアームが印刷された手順書を読み取り、固定位置やマーカーなしで容器を認識して化学実験を自律的に実行するシステムを提案する。
llm.problem: 従来のラボ自動化はスクリプト記述や固定位置・マーカーを前提としており、人間の実験環境に柔軟に対応できない。
llm.method: 写真からの手順書の読み取り、固定位置やマーカーのない通常の実験台上での容器の検出、ラベルの読み取りによる容器の識別、各ステップ前のターゲットの再特定を行う。
llm.result: Franka Pandaアームを用いて、子供用化学キットのプロトコルで5回中5回、4回中5回の成功を収め、160回のラベル識別すべてで容器を正しく特定した。

2611.13251.tldr_en: Curie's Jarvis is presented, a system that lets a robot arm carry out a chemistry experiment on a bench set up for people, and locates on printed and handwritten labels every container correctly, bringing robots a step closer to doing bench chemistry the way people do.

2611.13229.title: Incorporating World Models in Decision Making for Next Best View Selection in Active Sensing
2611.13229.abstract: Efficient robotic 3D reconstruction requires selecting views that contribute new surface measurements with few physical captures. Pretrained world models can guide this choice, but a predicted surface may not produce valid depth measurements under the operating conditions of the deployed sensor. We present a deployment adaptation methodology for next-best-view selection that learns a sensor-return adapter from limited local calibration data while keeping the pretrained predictor fixed. The adapter estimates measurement dropout over each predicted surface, allowing the selection method to favor views likely to fill gaps in the measured reconstruction. In a real-robot experiment with a structured-light sensor, the adapted method achieves higher measured surface coverage with 60% fewer captures than nominal selection. The adapted method recovers a surface region that the nominal method repeatedly targets but fails to measure. These results suggest that robots can reuse pretrained predictive models while adapting their decisions to local operating conditions in data-scarce environments.
2611.13229.comment: Accepted to CoRL 2026 Workshop "Do Robots Need World Models?"

llm.title_ja: アクティブセンシングにおける次善の視点選択のための意思決定への世界モデルの組み込み
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済み予測器を固定したまま限られた較正データからセンサーの測定ドロップアウトを推定するアダプターを学習し、次善の視点（NBV）選択に適用する手法を提案、実機実験で少ないキャプチャ回数で高い表面カバレッジを達成した。
llm.problem: 効率的なロボット3D再構成には世界モデルが有効だが、予測された表面は展開されたセンサーの動作条件下で有効な深度測定を生まない場合がある。
llm.method: 事前学習済みの予測器を固定しつつ、限られた局所較正データからセンサーの測定ドロップアウトを推定するセンサーリターンアダプターを学習するデプロイ適応手法を提案した。
llm.result: 構造化光センサーを用いた実機実験において、提案手法は通常の選択法と比較して60%少ないキャプチャ数でより高い表面カバレッジを達成し、従来法が測定に失敗した領域も復元した。
keywords_ja: アクティブセンシング

2611.13229.tldr_en: A deployment adaptation methodology for next-best-view selection that learns a sensor-return adapter from limited local calibration data while keeping the pretrained predictor fixed suggests that robots can reuse pretrained predictive models while adapting their decisions to local operating conditions in data-scarce environments.

2611.13227.title: Latent Barrier Steering: Hierarchical Safety for Generative Planning
2611.13227.abstract: We introduce Latent Barrier Steering (LBS), a hierarchical semantic-to-path framework for safe flow-matching-based generative planning. Existing control-barrier-function (CBF) safety filters for diffusion and flow-matching planners act locally on generated samples, either during sampling or after prediction. Such repair is effective for small violations, but can struggle when a new constraint blocks the whole selected behavior mode rather than merely perturbing it locally. LBS decouples behavior selection from path certification through two coordinated interventions: it first steers the generator's behavior latent toward rollouts with larger safety margin, then decodes the steered latent and applies a path-space CBF quadratic program (QP) only for residual violations. We show that latent steering increases the margin available to the path-space corrector, yielding finite-time recovery guarantees and reduced correction burden. Experiments across navigation and robot end-effector planning tasks show that LBS preserves safety while improving goal reaching and reducing correction burden compared with path-level safety filters.

llm.title_ja: 潜在バリアステアリング：生成型計画のための階層的安全性
llm.tldr_ja: フローマッチングベースの生成型計画に向けた、生成器の潜在変数を安全性のマージンが大きい方へ誘導しつつパス空間のCBFで残余の違反を修正する階層型セマンティック・ツー・パスフレームワーク「LBS」を提案した。
llm.problem: 拡散・フローマッチングプランナーに対する既存の制御バリア関数（CBF）安全フィルターは生成サンプルに対して局所的に作用するため、新しい制約が行動モード全体をブロックする場合には対処しにくい。
llm.method: 生成器の行動潜在変数を安全マージンの大きいロールアウトへと誘導し、デコード後にパス空間のCBF二次計画法（QP）を残余違反に対してのみ適用する「Latent Barrier Steering（LBS）」を提案した。
llm.result: ナビゲーションおよびロボットのエンドエフェクタ計画タスクにおいて、LBSは安全性（ゴール到達）を維持しつつ、パスレベルの安全フィルターと比較して修正負担を軽減した。

2611.13227.tldr_en: Latent Barrier Steering is introduced, a hierarchical semantic-to-path framework for safe flow-matching-based generative planning that preserves safety while improving goal reaching and reducing correction burden compared with path-level safety filters.

2611.13204.title: Ground Reaction Force-Aware Model Predictive Control for Underactuated Upright Physical Assistance
2611.13204.abstract: Many rehabilitation robots execute prescribed motions using reactive tracking controllers that do not explicitly incorporate the user's instantaneous human-ground interaction. This paper presents Ground Reaction Force-Aware Model Predictive Control (GRF-MPC), a framework for upright physical assistance. By integrating live GRF and center of pressure (CoP) measurements directly into a human centroidal dynamics model, GRF-MPC formulates a real-time quadratic program (QP) that optimizes assistive forces and moments over a receding horizon. We deployed GRF-MPC on the Robotic Upright Stand Trainer (RobUST) in an underactuated 4-cable configuration and evaluated it against a fully actuated 8-cable Cartesian impedance baseline in nearly 300 trials across six healthy participants. Across tasks spanning impulsive perturbations, lunge trajectories, and voluntary limits of stability, GRF-MPC reduced peak planar center-of-mass (CoM) error by 19.6% during perturbations, lowered trajectory tracking error by 24.1%, required 28.7% less net mechanical work, and permitted a 45.9% greater normalized voluntary excursion area. The underlying QP solves in under 1 ms, comfortably enabling 100 Hz replanning and demonstrating that incorporating live human-ground interaction into predictive control yields stronger, more transparent physical assistance with half the actuators.
2611.13204.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L), October 2026. 8 pages, 5 figures

llm.title_ja: 地面反力を考慮した、駆動不足型起立身体介助のためのモデル予測制御
llm.tldr_ja: ユーザの瞬間的な地面反力（GRF）と圧力中心（CoP）の測定値を人間の重心ダイナミクスモデルに直接統合し、1ms未満で解ける二次計画法（QP）によりアシスト力を最適化する「GRF-MPC」を提案し、実機で優れた追従性と省力を実証した。
llm.problem: リハビリテーションロボットの多くはユーザーの瞬間的な地面相互作用を明示的に組み込んでいない反応型追従コントローラを使用している。
llm.method: ライブのGRFとCoPの測定値を人間の重心ダイナミクスモデルに統合し、レシーディングホライズン上でアシスト力とモーメントを最適化する実時間QPフレームワーク「GRF-MPC」を提案した。
llm.result: ロボティック起立スタンドトレーナー（RobUST）を用いた実機実験において、外乱時の重心誤差を19.6%削減し、追従誤差を24.1%低減、正味の機械的仕事量を28.7%削減した。
keywords_ja: リハビリテーションロボット

2611.13204.tldr_en: Ground Reaction Force-Aware Model Predictive Control (GRF-MPC) is presented, a framework for upright physical assistance that formulates a real-time quadratic program (QP) that optimizes assistive forces and moments over a receding horizon.

2611.13161.title: Cognitive Multi-Agent Search and Rescue: Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Robotics
2611.13161.abstract: Effective search and rescue (SAR) operations require autonomous systems capable of coordinating multiple heterogeneous agents, adapting to dynamic hazards, and aligning with human mission intent. Existing language-guided reinforcement learning (RL) methods primarily focus on single-agent instruction following and lack mechanisms for team-level coordination in complex, partially observable environments. This paper presents a Cognitive Multi-Agent Framework based on Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (LG-HRL) that integrates natural-language understanding, hierarchical policy decomposition, and a shared cognitive workspace to achieve cohesive multi-agent behavior in SAR scenarios. Human instructions are interpreted by a large language model (LLM) and transformed into structured semantic cues that guide high-level strategy selection and role assignment across UAV and UGV agents. A formal Language-Grounded Multi-Agent Hierarchical Decision Process (LG-MAHDP) is introduced to model the interplay between semantic grounding, hierarchical control, and distributed coordination. Comprehensive experiments in a simulated disaster environment show that LG-HRL improves learning speed by 2.3 times, increases coordination coherence by 37%, and enhances subgoal accuracy and hazard avoidance by 46% and 31%, respectively. The system achieves 20-30% higher victim rescue rates, demonstrates emergent role specialization, and adapts immediately to human verbal updates. Ablation studies confirm that both the shared cognitive workspace and language grounding are critical to overall system performance. Overall, this work establishes a new paradigm for language-guided multi-agent SAR robotics, demonstrating that semantic grounding combined with hierarchical reasoning enables safer, more efficient, and more interpretable autonomous rescue operations.

llm.title_ja: 認知型マルチエージェント捜索救助：協調ロボットのための言語接地型階層型強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 自然言語の指示をLLMで解釈して戦略の選択や役割分担を導く、言語接地型階層型強化学習（LG-HRL）に基づく認知型マルチエージェントフレームワークを提案し、シミュレーション災害環境での救助率向上や協調性改善を実証した。
llm.problem: 効果的な捜索救助（SAR）には複数エージェントの協調や動的ハザードへの適応が必要だが、既存の言語誘導型強化学習は単一エージェント中心であり複雑な部分観測環境でのチーム協調を欠く。
llm.method: LLMによって自然言語の指示を構造化された意味的キューに変換し、UAVとUGVのエージェント間で高レベルな戦略選択と役割割り当てを導く「LG-HRL」フレームワークを提案した。
llm.result: シミュレーション災害環境において、学習速度を2.3倍に向上させ、協調 coherenceを37%増加させ、犠牲者の救助率を20〜30%高めることに成功した。

2611.13161.tldr_en: A Cognitive Multi-Agent Framework based on Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (LG-HRL) that integrates natural-language understanding, hierarchical policy decomposition, and a shared cognitive workspace to achieve cohesive multi-agent behavior in SAR scenarios is presented.

2611.13160.title: How Much of Your VLA Is kNN
2611.13160.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models now exceed 95% success on the LIBERO simulation benchmark, yet it remains unclear how much of this performance requires generalization beyond the training demonstrations. In this work, we show that retrieving nearby demonstrations and reusing their action chunks achieves a success rate of 91.7 % on LIBERO without policy training. Under LIBERO-Plus perturbations, retrieval shows the smallest drop of all evaluated policies. Across nine publicly available VLAs, fine-tuning mostly makes the vision-language backbone a better retrieval key, and the actions of the VLAs remain close to the demonstrations. In addition, we introduce Local Action Consistency (LAC), an offline metric that measures whether nearby observations in representation space are also associated with similar future actions. We show that LAC tracks the success rate of retrieval and can guide the training of a retrieval key. Our evaluation and source code are available at https://github.com/sereact/lerobot_knn.
2611.13160.comment: 21 pages, 10 figures, accepted to the CoRL 2026 G2A/TAG workshop

llm.title_ja: VLAのどれくらいがkNNなのか？
llm.tldr_ja: LIBEROベンチマークにおいて、近傍のデモを検索してアクションチャンクを再利用するだけで、ポリシーの学習なしでも91.7%の成功率を達成できることを示し、VLAの微調整の役割を分析した。
llm.problem: ビジョン・言語・アクション（VLA）モデルはシミュレーションベンチマークで高い成功率を示すが、このパフォーマンスのどれくらいが学習デモンストレーションを超えた汎化を必要としているのかは不明である。
llm.method: 近傍のデモンストレーションを検索してアクションチャンクを再利用する手法をLIBERO上でポリシー訓練なしで評価し、9つのVLAにおける微調整の影響やオフライン指標「Local Action Consistency (LAC)」を調査した。
llm.result: 検索ベースの手法単体で91.7%の成功率を達成し、LIBERO-Plusの外乱に対して最も小さい性能低下を示し、微調整が主にビジョン・言語バックボーンを優れた検索キーにしていることを明らかにした。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・アクションモデル
デモンストレーション検索

2611.13160.tldr_en: This work shows that retrieving nearby demonstrations and reusing their action chunks achieves a success rate of 91.7 % on LIBERO without policy training, and introduces Local Action Consistency (LAC), an offline metric that measures whether nearby observations in representation space are also associated with similar future actions.

2611.13142.title: DOBB: Dynamic Oriented Bounding Boxes for Multi-Agent Collision Avoidance under State Uncertainty and Heterogeneous Dynamics
2611.13142.abstract: Learning-based decentralized collision avoidance must remain reliable under state-estimation uncertainty and heterogeneous agent dynamics. Existing methods typically address these factors through training-domain variation or by exposing uncertainty and capability estimates to the policy at runtime. However, both leave the policy to infer how these quantities should alter the physical separation required for safe interaction, which can couple collision-avoidance behavior to relationships learned from the training distribution. We introduce the Dynamic Oriented Bounding Box (DOBB), an online geometric representation that maps the current state estimate, uncertainty, and agent-specific response characteristics into a dynamic, direction-dependent safety margin. We derive geometric features that jointly characterize the relative configuration and severity of interactions between agents' DOBBs, along with a reward function that preserves the physical interpretation of those interactions. Across four evaluation environments, DOBB achieves the lowest mean total failure rate of 2.6%. This performance persists under out-of-distribution shifts in actuation dynamics and state-estimation uncertainty, with collision-based failure remaining at or below 2.3% in every tested condition. We attribute this robustness to the geometric abstraction of the safety margin, which is less coupled to the specific uncertainty and actuation regimes encountered during training.

llm.title_ja: DOBB：状態不確実性と異種ダイナミクス下でのマルチエージェント衝突回避のための動的指向性バウンディングボックス
llm.tldr_ja: 現在の状態推定、不確実性、エージェント特有の応答特性を動的かつ方向依存の安全マージンにマッピングするオンライン幾何学的表現「DOBB」を提案し、異種ダイナミクスや不確実性のもとでも低い失敗率を達成した。
llm.problem: 学習ベースの分散型衝突回避は、状態推定の不確実性や異種エージェントのダイナミクス下でも信頼性を保つ必要があるが、既存手法ではポリシーが安全な物理的分離を推論する必要があり分布シフトに弱い。
llm.method: 状態推定値、不確実性、応答特性を方向依存の動的安全マージンにマッピングするオンライン幾何学的表現「DOBB」と、物理的解釈を保持する報酬関数を導出した。
llm.result: 4つの評価環境において、作動ダイナミクスや不確実性の分布外シフトが存在する状況でも、平均総失敗率が2.6%と最も低い値を示した。

2611.13142.tldr_en: The Dynamic Oriented Bounding Box is introduced, an online geometric representation that maps the current state estimate, uncertainty, and agent-specific response characteristics into a dynamic, direction-dependent safety margin that persists under out-of-distribution shifts in actuation dynamics and state-estimation uncertainty.

2611.13114.title: ASPIRE: An Agentic System-Identification Platform for Iterative Reasoning and Exploration
2611.13114.abstract: System identification requires expert decisions on the identification method, incorporation of prior physical knowledge, and model validation. We propose ASPIRE, a framework for nonlinear system identification in which a large language model agent selects and executes the identification method. ASPIRE constructs closed-form, nonlinear static or dynamic models from measured data, optionally supplemented by a system description, the intended use of the model, and physical requirements expressed formally or in natural language. Each model includes its parameters, an estimation record, an interpretation of its terms, and an error evaluated on test data inaccessible to the agent. Formal physical requirements are verified independently. ASPIRE operates autonomously or interactively, allowing the agent to ask questions and the user to request further analyses and identification rounds. We evaluate ASPIRE on three measured systems: a mobile robot, a rotational system with dry friction, and a laboratory fermenter. Each system is tested with and without a description, in five runs per task. All 30 runs delivered valid models, at a cost of 0.96 to 3.38 US dollars per run. An assessment by the authors found that, for the 30 models recommended by the agent, one per run, the interpretation of the model and the documentation of its structure selection and parameter estimation fully satisfied 132 of 150 assessed items and partly satisfied 18. The most frequent discrepancy, found in nine models, concerned inaccurate or unsupported claims about model structure selection.

llm.title_ja: ASPIRE：反復的な推論と探索のためのエージェント型システム同定プラットフォーム
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模言語モデルエージェントが非線形システム同定の手法を選択・実行し、測定データから閉形式の非線形静的・動的モデルを構築するフレームワーク「ASPIRE」を提案し、3つの実測システムで有効性を検証した。
llm.problem: システム同定には、同定手法の選択、物理的事前知識の統合、モデル検証に関する専門的な判断が必要とされる。
llm.method: LLMエージェントが非線形システム同定手法を選択・実行し、測定データから閉形式の非線形モデルを構築して物理的要件を検証するフレームワーク「ASPIRE」を開発した。
llm.result: 移動ロボット、摩擦付き回転システム、実験室用発酵槽の3つのシステムにおける30回の実行すべてで有効なモデルを構築し、解釈やドキュメント化の品質も高水準を達成した。

2611.13114.tldr_en: ASIRE, a framework for nonlinear system identification in which a large language model agent selects and executes the identification method, constructs closed-form, nonlinear static or dynamic models from measured data, optionally supplemented by a system description, the intended use of the model, and physical requirements expressed formally or in natural language.

2611.13113.title: Building World Models from Intrinsic Motivation
2611.13113.abstract: In the absence of extrinsic rewards or task supervision, human behavior is guided by intrinsic motivation---neural signals that drive curiosity, creativity, play, and other essential facets of intelligence. Intrinsic motivation plays an important developmental role in building robust world models that enable generalization and adaptation. Yet existing studies leave open how a broad range of intrinsic motivations interacts with world-model representation learning to support downstream control. This limits our understanding of which intrinsically collected experiences build reusable models. To address these gaps, we integrate 24 intrinsic objectives, including established methods and explicit variants spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency, into a common model-based reinforcement learning framework. We evaluate the world models they build through zero-shot, few-shot, and multi-task control in locomotion, manipulation, and open-ended gaming environments, using three representation-learning strategies: observation reconstruction, latent prediction, and redundancy reduction. Curiosity-driven exploration with observation reconstruction yields the strongest aggregate family profile, although the best individual pairing depends on the experiment. In compositional vision-based tasks, intrinsic motivation derived from both episodic and lifelong novelty---providing a complementary memory to the world model's generic recurrent state---achieves the best zero-shot transfer and few-shot adaptation. These findings motivate designing intrinsic motivation and representation learning jointly. Our results demonstrate world models as a powerful tool for measuring the quality of intrinsically motivated experience, and positions intrinsic motivation as a key ingredient for building world models autonomously.

llm.title_ja: 内発的動機からの世界モデル構築
llm.tldr_ja: 好奇心やエントロピー、有能感など24の内発的目的に基づく探索を共通のモデルベース強化学習フレームワークに統合し、世界モデルの品質評価と再利用可能なモデル構築における重要性を実証した。
llm.problem: 外部報酬やタスク監督がない場合、人間の行動は内発的動機に導かれるが、多様な内発的動機が世界モデルの表現学習とどのように相互作用するかは十分に解明されていない。
llm.method: 好奇心、エントロピー、有能感等を含む24の内発的動機を共通のモデルベースRLフレームワークに統合し、移動、操作、ゲーム環境で世界モデルのゼロショット・少数例適応性能を評価した。
llm.result: 観測再構成を用いた好奇心駆動の探索が最も強力な集約プロファイルを示し、エピソード・生涯の新規性から得られる内発的動機がゼロショット転移と少数例適応を最も高めることを明らかにした。

2611.13113.tldr_en: In compositional vision-based tasks, intrinsic motivation derived from both episodic and lifelong novelty---providing a complementary memory to the world model's generic recurrent state---achieves the best zero-shot transfer and few-shot adaptation.

2611.12885.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
2611.12885.abstract: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. From a single demonstration, RoboScript learns each task through rehearsal in simulation, freezes the learned knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation that ensures every deployment input is available on a real robot. On all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. The method generalizes across visual distributions, improves through reflection, scales with the foundation model, and transfers to a physical dual-arm robot through cross-embodiment memory adaptation. With a world in the loop, a robot can learn a manipulation task in its context as well as it learns one in its weights. All code is available at https://github.com/ArcheOne-AI/RoboScript

llm.title_ja: エージェント型ロボットマニピュレーションのためのワールド文脈内学習
llm.tldr_ja: 単一のデモンストレーションからシミュレーション内でタスクをリハーサルし、重みを更新せずにフィードバックを文脈に書き込むWorld In-Context Learning（WICL）を提案し、ロボットマニピュレーションの性能を向上させた。
llm.problem: 学習済みポリシーはネットワークの重みにスキルを焼き付けるため、学習元の分布に縛られ、文脈内学習は現在の世界のフィードバックが欠けるという課題があった。
llm.method: フリーズしたモデルにデモンストレーションを与え、シミュレータ等の世界でリハーサルを行い、そのフィードバックを重みではなく文脈に書き込むWICLとモジュール型インフラのRoboScriptを提案する。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0の50タスクすべてにおいて、クリーンおよびランダム化設定の平均成功率83.4%を達成し、最強の学習済み行動ポリシーを20ポイント以上上回った。

2611.12885.tldr_en: World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights, is proposed.

2611.12879.title: Grasping the Future: Joint 3D Hand-Object Forecasting From Internet Videos
2611.12879.abstract: To interact with an object, we need to anticipate both how it will move and how our hands should move with it. Human videos capture these relationships across everyday activities, offering a natural source for learning to predict future interactions. Learning from them requires recovering motion from completed interactions and using it to anticipate what could happen next. We present $\textit{Grasping-the-Future}$, a unified generative model of joint 3D hand-object motion, including wrist motion, finger articulation, and object position and orientation. Through masked spatiotemporal completion and flow matching, we train a single model for several prediction tasks: forecasting future interactions, predicting hand motion given object motion or vice versa, generating both trajectories toward a desired final object pose, and completing partially observed interactions. We explicitly model hand-object relations and incorporate contact constraints to help preserve grasp relationships during motion. To obtain 3D supervision from internet videos, we develop a scalable pipeline that combines pretrained perception models with joint geometric optimization to reconstruct completed interactions. We combine these recovered trajectories with annotated interaction datasets as training data for all tasks. We demonstrate strong performance across all tasks, outperforming released forecasters on datasets with 3D annotations. Moreover, we show geometric and physical plausibility of the predicted trajectories by retargeting them to a robotic embodiment. Videos are available at https://grasping-the-future.github.io.

llm.title_ja: 未来を掴む：インターネット動画からの3Dハンド・オブジェクト関節動作予測
llm.tldr_ja: インターネット動画から人間のインタラクションを再構成・学習し、手首の動きや指の関節、物体の位置姿勢を含む3Dハンド・オブジェクトのモーションを統合的に予測する生成モデルを提案した。
llm.problem: 物体とインタラクションするためには、物体の動きと手の動きの双方を予測する必要があるが、人間動画からの学習には動作の復元と次状態の予測が必要となる。
llm.method: マスクされた時空間補完とフローマッチングを用いて、手首・指・物体姿勢の予測を統合的に行う単一の生成モデルを構築し、接触制約を組み込んだ。
llm.result: 3D注釈付きデータセットで既存の予測モデルを上回る性能を示し、ロボットの形態にリターゲットすることで幾何学的・物理的妥当性を示した。
keywords_ja: ハンド・オブジェクト

2611.12879.tldr_en: A unified generative model of joint 3D hand-object motion, including wrist motion, finger articulation, and object position and orientation is presented, and geometric and physical plausibility of the predicted trajectories are shown by retargeting them to a robotic embodiment.

2611.12870.title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
2611.12870.abstract: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation. However, introducing action learning may impair this alignment. Principled guidance on data and supervision design for maintaining language-video alignment during action learning remains limited. To investigate this, we curate a pool of approximately 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demonstrations. Building on this, we systematically study how language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision, and the joint use of these two forms affect WAM performance. In particular, we examine how language annotation quality affects pretrained language-video capabilities, and how action supervision from UMI and robot demonstrations extends these capabilities to language-video-action modeling. To better scale the model, we further conduct detailed studies on joint training recipe and model architecture. Under a fixed training budget, mixing egocentric videos and UMI demonstrations improves control generalization. Model architecture affects how effectively these experiences are used, while scaling pretraining under the selected configuration brings further gains. The resulting recipe, post-trained on RoboTwin Clean demonstrations only, achieves success rates of 88.10% and 61.56% under Easy (Clean-to-Clean) and Hard (Clean-to-Random) conditions, respectively. Our model achieves 40.00% SR across three real-world tasks, compared with 23.33% for the strongest baseline, indicating better generalization under unseen conditions. We release the curated data, training code, and model weights.

llm.title_ja: クロスモーダルアライメントによるワールド行動モデルのスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 言語・映像・行動の各監督信号を組み合わせた大規模なデータセットと訓練レシピを用いて、ワールド行動モデル（WAM）の制御汎化性能を向上させた。
llm.problem: 行動学習の導入により、ビデオ事前学習で獲得した言語・映像間のアライメントが損なわれる可能性があり、その維持に関する指導原理が限られている。
llm.method: 言語-映像監督信号、言語-映像-行動監督信号の組み合わせやモデルアーキテクチャ、統合訓練レシピを詳細に調査しスケーリングを行った。
llm.result: RoboTwin Cleanデモンストレーションで事後学習を行ったモデルは、Easy条件で88.10%、Hard条件で61.56%の成功率を達成し、実世界3タスクでも優れた汎化性能を示した。
keywords_ja: クロスモーダルアライメント

2611.12870.tldr_en: This work systematically study how language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision, and the joint use of these two forms affect WAM performance, and examines how language annotation quality affects pretrained language-video capabilities.

2611.12824.title: DreamLander: A 6-DOF World Model based Reinforcement Learning Planetary Lander
2611.12824.abstract: Soft powered descent landings are becoming evermore important in the field of space exploration and scientific advancement, because of their ability to deliver mission critical payloads, both highly accurately and safely. The high efficiency restriction on planetary landings due to the severely limited fuel supply results in the need for optimal guidance trajectories and control. Model based reinforcement learning is proving to be an important tool in simplifying the highly complex process of generating optimal guidance trajectories and control. In this work, we present DreamLander, a state of the art model based reinforcement learning algorithm based on DreamerV3, to generate optimal guidance and control for a realistic 6 degree of freedom entry descent landing problem. The model based approach creates a sample efficient and highly generalizable model that can be applied to a variety of scenarios whilst maintaining a high degree of accuracy, landing within 2 meters of the designated landing zone, and with velocity norm less than 0.3 meters per second. DreamLander makes use of state sensor observations, making progress toward End-to-End solutions of the Entry Descent Landing problem.
2611.12824.journal_ref: Nehma, G.M., Quinn, P., Tiwari, M., & Riano-Rios, C. (2026). DreamLander: A 6-DOF World Model Based Reinforcement Learning Planetary Lander. AIAA SCITECH 2026 Forum

llm.title_ja: DreamLander：6自由度世界モデルに基づく強化学習惑星着陸機
llm.tldr_ja: DreamerV3をベースにした最先端のモデルベース強化学習アルゴリズム「DreamLander」を提案し、現実的な6自由度の突入・降下・着陸問題において最適な誘導と制御を生成した。
llm.problem: 宇宙探査において限られた燃料供給による高い効率制限があり、最適な誘導軌道と制御を生成するための複雑なプロセスの簡素化が求められている。
llm.method: 状態センサー観測を利用し、サンプル効率が高く汎用性に優れたモデルベース強化学習アルゴリズム「DreamLander」を構築した。
llm.result: 指定された着陸ゾーンの2メートル以内、かつ速度ノルム0.3m/s未満で着陸し、高い精度と汎用性を示した。
keywords_ja: モデルベース強化学習

badges.venue: Nehma, G.M., Quinn, P., Tiwari, M., & Ri 2026

2611.12824.tldr_en: This work presents DreamLander, a state of the art model based reinforcement learning algorithm based on DreamerV3, to generate optimal guidance and control for a realistic 6 degree of freedom entry descent landing problem.

2611.12818.title: Simulating Vein Compressibility for Ultrasound-Guided Femoral Access: Speed, Accuracy, and Phantom Validation
2611.12818.abstract: In ultrasound-guided femoral access, probe pressure deforms the tissue and changes the vascular anatomy a robot observes. A simulator must reproduce these mechanics fast enough for robotic interaction, yet the computational effort needed for a clinically meaningful signal like vein collapse before artery is unclear. We test the feasibility of a physics-based simulation in NVIDIA's Isaac Sim for Healthcare, with Stable Neo-Hookean tissue solved by Vertex Block Descent on one GPU. A simulation of a low-fidelity cylindrical benchtop phantom with known geometry and mechanical properties, pressed by a robot, predicted its artery within 5 percentage points at every depth. It matched the vein within 3 points through 11 mm of a 25.4 mm press and followed the collapse behavior of the low-fidelity physical phantom. Across element size, time step, and solver iterations, wall clock time per frame scaled linearly with solver work, but accuracy did not improve with more work. The chosen setting reduced solver time per frame by a factor of 976, from 29,700 ms to 30.4 ms, while remaining within 1.03 points of the finest reference setting. The physics solver alone took 30.4 ms per frame, while the full stack, including ultrasound and graphics rendering, took 56.4 ms per frame. Finally, when seeded with realistic literature-based mechanical properties, the digital leg model compressed the vein far more than the artery at every setting, reproducing the expected clinical signal of vein collapse before artery, which is used to distinguish them. In total, these results suggest that the NVIDIA Isaac Sim platform may be suitable for augmenting reinforcement learning training or online simulation for autonomous femoral access with ultrasound.
2611.12818.comment: Submitted to the Journal of Medical Robotics Research (JMRR) for the International Symposium of Medical Robotics 2027 (ISMR 2027) 11 Pages (8 main + 3 references), 4 figures in main body

llm.title_ja: 超音波ガイド下大腿部アクセスのための静脈圧縮性シミュレーション：速度、精度、ファントム検証
llm.tldr_ja: NVIDIA Isaac Simを活用し、実時間でのロボット操作や強化学習に適用可能な、組織変形と血管の潰れ挙動を再現する物理ベースシミュレーションの実現可能性を検証した。
llm.problem: 超音波ガイド下の大腿部アクセスではプローブの圧力が組織を変形させ血管解剖学を変化させるが、動脈より先に静脈が潰れる現象を再現する高速なシミュレーションの計算負荷は不明である。
llm.method: NVIDIA Isaac Sim for Healthcareを用い、安定化Neo-Hookean組織モデルを頂点ブロック降下法で1つのGPU上で解く物理ベースシミュレーションを構築した。
llm.result: ソルバー時間を976分の1に削減（29,700msから30.4ms）しつつ精度を維持し、臨床的なシグナルである「動脈より先の静脈の潰れ」を再現することに成功した。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション

2611.12818.tldr_en: The NVIDIA Isaac Sim platform may be suitable for augmenting reinforcement learning training or online simulation for autonomous femoral access with ultrasound, and when seeded with realistic literature-based mechanical properties, the digital leg model compressed the vein far more than the artery at every setting, reproducing the expected clinical signal of vein collapse before artery.

2611.12806.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
2611.12806.abstract: Tactile sensing is an indispensable modality for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, a capability that hints at the ultimate frontiers of embodied intelligence. However, commercially available tactile sensors are still at a relatively early stage of development, with each type of sensor offering irreplaceable strengths alongside its own drawbacks. A key challenge is thus to free tactile understanding from sensor-specific physics, so that embodied models can effectively leverage heterogeneous tactile data. To this end, we develop LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model characterized by the following properties. (i) Our model yields a unified representation across different tactile sensors (i.e., piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors), and is easily extensible to new sensor types. (ii) The resulting tactile tokens are plug-and-play: they can be seamlessly integrated into policy models across paradigms, from diffusion policy to vision-language-action (VLA) models such as $π_{0.5}$ and LingBot-VLA, consistently enhancing manipulation dexterity. (iii) Extensive experiments, spanning simulation and real-robot deployments across multiple hardware platforms, demonstrate that our tactile representation substantially benefits complex manipulation tasks while maintaining strong computational efficiency. We believe the findings in this work demonstrate the potential of leveraging cross-sensor data to scale tactile learning, and offer encouraging insights for the design of future hardware and embodied models.
2611.12806.hf_summary_en: LingBot-Touch is a tactile foundation model that learns a unified, extensible representation across heterogeneous tactile sensors, yielding plug-and-play tactile tokens that consistently enhance manipulation policies such as diffusion policy and VLA models.

llm.title_ja: 一般器用把持に向けた異種触覚表現の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な触覚センサーから統一された表現を学習し、拡散ポリシーやVLAモデルにプラグインとして統合できる触覚基盤モデル「LingBot-Touch」を提案した。
llm.problem: 商用触覚センサーは初期段階であり、センサー固有の物理特性に縛られるため、異種触覚データを効果的に活用することが課題となっている。
llm.method: 感圧型・磁気型・視覚触覚型などの異なる触覚センサー間で統一表現を生成し、ポリシーモデルにシームレスに統合できる触覚トークンを出力するLingBot-Touchを開発した。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび複数ハードウェアプラットフォームの実機実験において、計算効率を維持しながら複雑なマニピュレーションタスクを大幅に改善した。

2611.12806.tldr_en: The findings in this work demonstrate the potential of leveraging cross-sensor data to scale tactile learning, and offer encouraging insights for the design of future hardware and embodied models.

2611.12804.title: Benchmarking Real-World Robotic Manipulation through Stochastic Challenges
2611.12804.abstract: A challenging bottleneck in manipulation research is reproducibility and comparability of methods in real-world environments. Since manipulation is an interactive task, it cannot be evaluated on a static dataset of observations. Benchmarking in simulation is a common remedy, but cannot cover the whole complexity of real-world tests. This paper proposes a new paradigm of stochastic challenges. Like the well-known YCB objects, it is based on reproducible real-world scenes and therefore allows system-level innovation and comparability between different platforms. Due to their stochastic nature, our challenges however, mimic the rigor and surprise of hidden test sets. To this end, we show how different robots in different labs can be compared based on their success rate over different random task samples, if these samples come from the same distribution. We propose stochastic challenges as a general paradigm for robot benchmarking and implement this paradigm in a novel benchmark for mobile manipulation, on which we compare two robots tested in two different labs.
2611.12804.comment: Accepted at the 10th Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026). 15 pages, 3 figures

llm.title_ja: 確率的チャレンジを通じた実世界ロボットマニピュレーションのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 再現性のある実世界シーンと確率的タスクサンプリングを組み合わせることで、隠しテストセットと同等の厳密さとシステムレベルの比較を可能にする新しいベンチマークパラダイムを提案した。
llm.problem: マニピュレーション研究における再現性と手法間の比較は、インタラクティブなタスクであるため静的データセットでは評価できず、シミュレーションも限界があるというボトルネックが存在する。
llm.method: 再現可能な実世界シーンに基づき、確率的な性質によって隠しテストセットの厳密さを模倣する「確率的チャレンジ」という新しいパラダイムをモバイルマニピュレーションに実装した。
llm.result: 異なる2つのラボの異なるロボット間で、同じ分布からのランダムなタスクサンプルに対する成功率を基に比較できることを示した。

2611.12804.tldr_en: Stochastic challenges are proposed as a general paradigm for robot benchmarking and implemented in a novel benchmark for mobile manipulation, on which two robots tested in two different labs are compared.

2611.12767.title: Certified Zonotopic Reachability Analysis for Trajectory Tracking on Lie Groups
2611.12767.abstract: Autonomous vehicles track planned trajectories close to obstacles. Unknown disturbances make them deviate from these trajectories. With a bound on the tracking error that disturbances can cause, a planned trajectory can be certified as safe before execution. Existing set-based methods bound the tracking error by one invariant ellipsoid for the whole trajectory or by intervals, which are both conservative. For aerial and space vehicles, the tracking error evolves on a matrix Lie group with nonlinear dynamics. However, for group-affine systems, the error dynamics are linear in Lie algebra coordinates when the vehicle receives the inputs of the reference. The control input and the disturbance enter through the inverse right Jacobian, a matrix that depends on the error. We propagate the linear part of the error dynamics with zonotopes and enclose the effect of the inverse right Jacobian on the disturbance in closed form. The resulting tubes are tight and provably contain all reachable tracking errors in continuous time. When some error components have no input, the inverse right Jacobian leaves unmatched nonlinear terms in the closed loop. None of the tested methods certifies such a closed loop. Hybrid coordinates make these terms matched, so that our controller cancels every nonlinear term that does not contain the disturbance. Our tubes give tighter bounds than the ellipsoid method in simulations of a planar aircraft and a fully actuated multirotor and in real flights of a quadrotor, where the tube contains every measured attitude error. Under larger disturbances and the same feedback gain, the ellipsoid method yields no valid ellipsoid, whereas our tubes remain valid.

llm.title_ja: リー群上の軌道追従に対する証明可能なゾノトープ可到達性解析
llm.tldr_ja: 行列リー群上の非線形ダイナミクスに従う航空・宇宙車両の追従誤差をゾノトープを用いて厳密に伝搬させ、外乱が存在する場合でも安全性を保証する可到達性解析手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 未知の外乱により自律車両が計画軌道から逸脱するため、実行前に安全性を証明する必要があるが、既存の集合ベースの手法は保守的であるか、リー群上の非線形誤差ダイナミクスを十分に扱えない。
llm.method: 群アフィン系においてリー代数座標での誤差ダイナミクスを線形化し、逆右ヤコビアンの影響を閉形式で包み込みながらゾノトープで伝搬するコントローラと解析手法を開発した。
llm.result: 平面航空機やマルチローターのシミュレーションおよび実飛行において、従来のエリプソイド法よりもタイトな追従誤差の境界を導出でき、大きな外乱下でも有効性を維持した。

2611.12767.tldr_en: The resulting tubes are tight and provably contain all reachable tracking errors in continuous time and give tighter bounds than the ellipsoid method in simulations of a planar aircraft and a fully actuated multirotor and in real flights of a quadrotor, where the tube contains every measured attitude error.

2611.12754.title: Sliding into Balance: Benefits of a Sliding Payload for Load Distribution and Disturbance Rejection in Dual-UAV Transportation
2611.12754.abstract: This paper analyzes the cooperative transportation of a payload suspended from two drones in which, instead of being attached to two independent ropes, the payload is allowed to slide along a single rope connecting both UAVs. First, a planar nondimensional dynamical model of the sliding motion with viscous friction is presented. Then, considering stationary drones, this configuration is compared with a fixed payload with the same total rope length, both at equilibrium and under disturbances. The analytical results show that the sliding payload equalizes the tension in both rope segments for any relative position of the drones, so that no rope loses tension at equilibrium; it doubles the region reachable by the payload and, except for low friction combined with a large drone separation, it enlarges the set of admissible disturbances. Finally, a dynamic simulation also shows that under realistic gusty wind profiles, the average tension imbalance between the drones is reduced with respect to the fixed-payload solution.

llm.title_ja: バランスへのスライド：デュアルUAV輸送における荷重分散と外乱除去のためのスライド式ペイロードの利点
llm.tldr_ja: 2機のドローン間を接続する単一のロープに沿ってペイロードがスライドする構成を解析し、張力の均等化や到達可能領域の拡大、外乱耐性の向上を証明した。
llm.problem: 2機のドローンによる吊り下げペイロードの協調輸送において、独立した2本のロープに固定する従来方式では張力の不均衡や制御の限界が生じる。
llm.method: 粘性摩擦を伴うスライド運動の平面無次元力学モデルを構築し、静的な平衡状態および外乱下における固定ペイロード構成との比較解析を行った。
llm.result: スライド式ペイロードは任意の相対位置で両ロープの張力を均等化し、可到達領域を倍増させ、突風プロファイル下での張力不均衡を軽減することを示した。

2611.12732.title: $Σ$-LeWM: Learning World Models via S-Information for Robot Control
2611.12732.abstract: World models have increasingly been applied as a model-based control method for robotics tasks such as manipulation and locomotion. While early world model architectures relied on decoders to prevent mode collapse and learn a predictable latent space, recent works on world models, such as Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture or LeWorldModel, increasingly aim to learn embeddings without a grounding decoder, utilising only a latent forward dynamics predictor and a stabilising entropy term. In this paper, we set out to demonstrate that the further introduction of two additional latent losses to LeWorldModel, a backward dynamics predictor and an inverse dynamics action predictor, enforces further structure on the latent embedding, leading to further gains in both performance and planning efficiency. These are critical properties for improving the applicability of such methods to real-time model-based control of real-world robots. We demonstrate these gains on standard world model benchmarks and two simulated robot manipulation tasks.

llm.title_ja: Σ-LeWM：S情報を通じたロボット制御のための世界モデル学習
llm.tldr_ja: LeWorldModelに後方ダイナミクス予測器と逆ダイナミクス行動予測器の2つの潜在損失を導入し、埋め込みの構造化を強化することでロボット制御の性能と計画効率を向上させた。
llm.problem: 近年のグラウンディングデコーダを持たない世界モデルは潜在的な前方ダイナミクス予測器やエントロピー項に依存しているが、実時間モデルベース制御への適用のためには潜在空間のさらなる構造化が必要である。
llm.method: LeWorldModelの枠組みに、後方ダイナミクス予測器と逆ダイナミクス行動予測器の2つの追加の潜在損失を導入して潜在埋め込みを最適化した。
llm.result: 標準的な世界モデルベンチマークおよび2つのシミュレーションロボットマニピュレーションタスクにおいて、性能と計画効率の向上を示した。

2611.12732.tldr_en: This paper demonstrates that the further introduction of two additional latent losses to LeWorldModel, a backward dynamics predictor and an inverse dynamics action predictor, enforces further structure on the latent embedding, leading to further gains in both performance and planning efficiency.

2611.12687.title: reComposer: Editable Planning for Controllable Image Generation
2611.12687.abstract: Prompt-based image generation makes it easy to produce visual assets, but offers little support for engaging with the creative process. Prompting collapses interdependent creative decisions into a monolithic instruction and returns a finished image, leaving control limited to revising the prompt or correcting the model's output. We present reComposer, a process-oriented image-generation interface built around editable planning, which decomposes users' evolving intent into meaningful creative decisions - such as subject, composition, or palette - and collaborates with users to explore underspecified goals and alternatives. reComposer supports conversational and direct manipulation of the plan, moving between concept-level intent and visual-level control. We evaluated reComposer with 8 design and non-design professionals. Compared to prompting, participants felt greater control and ownership while developing visual assets, exploring alternatives, and iterating on details. Our findings suggest how shifting generative AI interaction from specifying outputs to shaping process can support creative thinking alongside asset production.

llm.title_ja: reComposer：制御可能な画像生成のための編集可能なプランニング
llm.tldr_ja: ユーザーの意図を主題や構図などの創造的決定に分解し、対話的・直接的な操作を通じて生成プロセスを共同で形作る編集可能な画像生成インターフェースを提案した。
llm.problem: プロンプトベースの画像生成は、複雑な創造的決定を一括して指示するため生成結果の修正が難しく、制御が限定的である。
llm.method: ユーザーの発展する意図を意味のある創造的決定に分解し、計画の対話的・直接的操作をサポートするプロセス指向の画像生成インターフェース「reComposer」を構築した。
llm.result: デザインの専門家等の評価において、視覚的アセットの開発、代替案の探索、詳細の反復作業において、より高い制御感と主体性が得られることが示された。
keywords_ja: ヒューマン・AIインタラクション
クリエイティブプロセス

2611.12687.tldr_en: ReComposer is a process-oriented image-generation interface built around editable planning, which decomposes users' evolving intent into meaningful creative decisions and collaborates with users to explore underspecified goals and alternatives.

2611.12678.title: Library of Hands: Fix the Hands, Not the World Model
2611.12678.abstract: A world model predicts how a scene changes after an action, and a planner uses it to search for actions that reach a goal. If the camera moves or the controller changes, the same command moves the robot differently: when its commands are turned by 90 degrees, a frozen planner with the LeWM world model that succeeds in 77.5% of episodes succeeds in only 7.8%. Current fixes retrain the model, need training data, or forget a set-up when it returns. We propose Library of Hands (LoH), a training-free method that keeps the world model frozen and corrects only the map from commands to applied actions, which we call the hand. LoH reads the hand through the frozen model, with no extra sensor: it finds the action that best explains the change between two camera images (a reading). It stores every hand it identifies, so a returning set-up is recognised rather than re-learnt. In closed-loop tests, LoH more than doubles success on three simulated tasks, from 28.6% to 62.3%, and loses only 0.6 percentage points when nothing changes. It also works, unchanged, with two other world models and on two of three models pretrained on real robot data, and its gain grows with the quality of its readings.

llm.title_ja: 手のライブラリ：世界モデルではなく手を修正する
llm.tldr_ja: 世界モデルを凍結したまま、カメラ画像の変化からコマンドと実際の行動のマッピング（手）のみを特定して修正・保存する訓練不要の手法「Library of Hands (LoH)」を提案した。
llm.problem: カメラの移動やコントローラの変更によってロボットの挙動が変わると、既存の世界モデルベースの計画は失敗し、再訓練が必要になる。
llm.method: 世界モデルを凍結し、2枚のカメラ画像の変化から最適な行動を読み取ることで、コマンドから適用行動へのマッピング（手）を特定して蓄積する訓練不要の手法LoHを開発した。
llm.result: 3つのシミュレーションタスクにおいて成功率を28.6%から62.3%へと倍増させ、他の複数の世界モデルや事前学習モデルでも同様に機能することを示した。

2611.12678.tldr_en: Library of Hands (LoH), a training-free method that keeps the world model frozen and corrects only the map from commands to applied actions, which is called the hand, is proposed.

2611.12676.title: VLA Adaptation with Real and Simulated Data: A Case Study on Robotic Chess
2611.12676.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are trained as general-purpose foundation models for robot learning, and require fine-tuning for each downstream task and robot. This raises practical questions such as how much data and training updates are needed, how checkpoints should be selected, and whether simulation can be leveraged to alleviate the cost of real data collection. We study these questions on a task that requires both precise manipulation and spatial understanding of the scene. In this task, an SO-101 arm moves a chess king between two squares that are given only by their names, such as e4 and a5. We fine-tune $π_{0.5}$ with various dataset sizes and update budgets, using teleoperated demonstrations as well as simulated demonstrations from a randomized scripted expert that imitates the variability of human demonstrations. In simulation, the success rate scales with both data and updates. Importantly, we find that a short learning-rate cool-down adds up to 31 points and is necessary for comparing checkpoints, and that validation loss and action error are unreliable for model selection. On the real arm, we fine-tune on up to 256 teleoperated demonstrations and evaluate ten policies in 25 trials each. Partial results indicate that pretraining on the simulated demonstrations helps substantially, most clearly when real data is scarce. We also present a negative result, in which training on the policy's own rollouts with filtered behavior cloning, RECAP-style advantage conditioning, corrections from an automatic coach, or residual reinforcement learning did not yield a measurable improvement over plain behavior cloning in our setting. We release the simulator, the expert and the real demonstrations.
2611.12676.comment: CoRL 2026 Workshop "Pretrain to Adapt: What Makes a Pretrained Policy Adaptable?". 8 pages main text, 15 pages total, 15 figures, 4 tables

llm.title_ja: 実世界およびシミュレーションデータを用いたVLA適応：ロボットチェスに関するケーススタディ
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレーションと実世界のデモンストレーションを組み合わせてVLAモデルを微調整し、データ量や訓練更新回数がタスク成功率に与える影響をロボットチェス課題で調査した。
llm.problem: ビジョン・言語・アクション（VLA）モデルを下流タスクやロボットに適応させる際、必要なデータ量や更新回数、チェックポイントの選定、シミュレーションの活用方法に関する実用的な課題がある。
llm.method: ランダム化されたスクリプトエキスパートによるシミュレーションデモンストレーションと、最大256件の実機遠隔操作デモンストレーションを用いて\(\pi_{0.5}\)を微調整し検証した。
llm.result: シミュレーションでの事前学習が実データ不足を大幅に補うこと、学習率のクールダウンが有効である一方、検証ロスや行動誤差はモデル選択の信頼できる指標にならないことを示した。
keywords_ja: ファインチューニング
シミュレーション活用

2611.12676.tldr_en: A negative result is presented, in which training on the policy's own rollouts with filtered behavior cloning, RECAP-style advantage conditioning, corrections from an automatic coach, or residual reinforcement learning did not yield a measurable improvement over plain behavior cloning in this setting.

2611.12654.title: Correctness Boundaries of Typed Plans for Natural-Language Robot Fleet Control
2611.12654.abstract: We examine what plan validation and execution reports establish in natural-language robot fleet control. Commands are traced through typed plans, deterministic corrections, fleet coordination and outcome checks in a three-level Robot Operating System 2 implementation with twenty simulated robots. An offline benchmark of 44 cases checks plan structure and selected command requirements. Across five local configurations without a response schema, 70.0-87.3% of responses pass. All runs in a selected 18-run simulation series meet their pose-based task conditions. This series includes two successful repeats that replaced incomplete runs after a software change. Saved plans and logs document duplicate pickup assignments and goal adjustments within the original task zones. Separate formation traces show a structurally accepted plan with the wrong formation shape and a rejected route, and an arrival report that omitted a requested robot after replanning. Carry completion records pickup and subsequent drop-off zone presence for the same robot. The cases distinguish changes to executable actions from changes to the requirements covered by a completion report. They motivate checking the effective assignments, goals and reported outcome against the original command.

llm.title_ja: 自然言語ロボットフリート制御における型付きプランの正当性の境界
llm.tldr_ja: 20台のシミュレーションロボットを用いた3層のROS 2実装を通じて、自然言語によるロボットフリート制御におけるプランの検証・実行レポートが何を保証するかを調査した。
llm.problem: 自然言語によるロボットフリート制御において、プランの検証や実行レポートがコマンドに対してどの程度正確であるかの境界を検証する必要がある。
llm.method: 型付きプラン、決定論的修正、フリート協調、結果チェックを組み込んだROS 2ベースの3層実装を用い、44ケースのオフラインベンチマークとシミュレーションシリーズで検証した。
llm.result: 70.0〜87.3%の応答が通過し、効果的な割り当てやゴール、報告された結果と元のコマンドとの整合性をチェックすることの重要性を明らかにした。

2611.12654.tldr_en: It is examined what plan validation and execution reports establish in natural-language robot fleet control, and how these motivate checking the effective assignments, goals and reported outcome against the original command.

2611.12643.title: Simulation-aided Reinforcement Learning with Control Variates
2611.12643.abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms often rely on data collected from a target environment, which can be expensive and noisy. Although simulators can generate large amounts of additional data, standard simulation mixing approaches, which directly combine simulated and real experience, can degrade performance due to simulator inaccuracies, especially when they bias the solution away from the optimal policy. We propose a conservative simulation-aided learning method based on control variates, where simulated data is used solely to reduce variance in the learning process rather than directly shaping the learning target. We develop our approach for Policy-Evaluation, which is a fundamental building block of RL algorithms. Then we combine it within the actor-critic framework towards policy improvement, as well as extend it towards offline RL scenarios. Experiments on multiple MuJoCo benchmark tasks demonstrate improvements over standard simulation mixing approaches, highlighting control variates as an effective tool for simulation-aided reinforcement learning.
2611.12643.comment: Accepted as a poster at NeurIPS 2026. 10 pages main text + appendix, 3 figures. Code: https://github.com/OmerHemo/Simulation-Aided-Reinforcement-Learning-with-Control-Variates

llm.title_ja: 制御変量を用いたシミュレーション支援強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレーションデータを学習ターゲットの直接的な形状変更ではなく、学習プロセスの分散削減のみに用いることで、シミュレータの不正確さによる性能低下を防ぐ保守的な学習手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 強化学習においてシミュレータのデータを用いる際、シミュレータの不正確さやバイアスにより、最適なポリシーから外れて性能が低下するという問題がある。
llm.method: ポリシー評価の基本構成要素に対して制御変量を活用したシミュレーション支援学習手法を開発し、アクター・クリティックフレームワークやオフライン強化学習へ拡張した。
llm.result: 複数のMuJoCoベンチマークタスクにおいて、標準的なシミュレーション混合アプローチを上回る性能を示し、制御変量の有効性を実証した。
keywords_ja: シミュレーション支援

2611.12643.tldr_en: This work develops their approach for Policy-Evaluation, which is a fundamental building block of RL algorithms, and combines it within the actor-critic framework towards policy improvement, as well as extend it towards offline RL scenarios.

2611.12568.title: Modeling and Estimation of a Towed Marine System
2611.12568.abstract: This paper addresses the modeling and state estimation of a towed marine system consisting of two autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs), a pair of umbilical cables, towfish, and a trailing loop cable. Inspired by the existing literature, we employ a lumped-mass modeling approach for the cables and towfish, capturing the essential dynamics while maintaining computational tractability. A Lyapunov-based analysis is conducted to verify the stability and convergence properties of the proposed model. Building on this model, we propose two state estimation methods, namely a reduced-order observer and a perfect-measurement extended Kalman filter (PMEKF), using only the measurements from the ASVs' onboard sensors. Numerical simulations and experimental results are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.
2611.12568.comment: preprint submitted to Ocean Engineering, 23 pages (highlights + 22p manuscript), 12 figures

llm.title_ja: 牽引式海洋システムのモデリングと推定
llm.tldr_ja: 2隻の水上艇、ケーブル、トウフィッシュからなる牽引式海洋システムを対象に、集中質量モデルを用いたモデリングと、オンボードセンサーのみを用いた2つの状態推定手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 複数の水上艇とケーブル等で構成される牽引式海洋システムは複雑なダイナミクスを持ち、計算実用性を保ちながら正確な状態推定を行う必要がある。
llm.method: ケーブルとトウフィッシュに対して集中質量モデリングアプローチを採用し、リアプノフ解析で安定性を検証した上で、縮約型オブザーバーと完全測定拡張カルマンフィルター（PMEKF）を開発した。
llm.result: 数値シミュレーションおよび実験結果を通じて、提案したモデリングと状態推定手法の有効性を検証した。
keywords_ja: 拡張カルマンフィルター

2611.12567.title: LawKAN: Group-Law Layers for Composition -- When Imposing a Known Law Pays Off
2611.12567.abstract: Many tasks compose transformations by a known rule: chained rotations in robotics and navigation. Learned models relearn it, compounding error; classical estimators hardcode it and miss hardware deviations. We impose the known structure and learn only the remainder: an exact non-commutative group law sits in the node of a self-contained layer, its edges learn local increments, and a zero-initialized correction psi learns unknown deviations of the law. A pre-training criterion predicts exact representability. On fixed-angle SU(2) composition, a 54-parameter dense edge is the most accurate dense model, at 27x fewer parameters than the strongest fixed-matrix baseline, and lies 0.05 deg above the Bayes floor. On real robot arms, an isolated 306-parameter psi reaches 1.12-1.14 mm versus 1.29-1.33 mm for Gauss-Newton at N >= 60, and the recipe transfers across three vendors and two protocols. The recipe matches classical fits where the data obey the law and loses where the imposed law is not the task's.
2611.12567.comment: 20 pages main text (53 total), 15 figures, 6 tables in main text (31 incl. appendices). Code: https://github.com/occamolab/lawkan

llm.title_ja: LawKAN：合成のための群律レイヤー —— 既知の法則を課すことの利点
llm.tldr_ja: ニューラルネットワークのノードに厳密な非可換群律を埋め込み、既知の法則からの未知の逸脱のみを学習させることで、パラメータ数を削減しつつ高精度な変換を実現した。
llm.problem: ロボット工学やナビゲーションにおけるチェーン状の回転などの変換合成において、学習モデルは誤差を蓄積して再学習し、従来の推定器はハードコーディングされてハードウェアの偏差に対応できない。
llm.method: 自己完結型の層のノードに厳密な非可換群律を配置し、エッジで局所増分を学習させ、ゼロ初期化した補正項により法則の未知の逸脱を学習する「LawKAN」を提案した。
llm.result: SU(2)合成において最良の密集モデルより27分の1のパラメータ数で高精度を達成し、実ロボットアーム実験でも既存手法と同等以上の性能を示した。
keywords_ja: ニューラルネットワーク
