2611.12557.title: WanderBench: Can World Models Explore Dynamic Worlds from Video?
2611.12557.abstract: Video world models conditioned on an input video make it possible to explore real, recorded dynamic scenes, enabling re-shooting of footage, free-viewpoint replay, and real-to-sim environments for embodied agents. Such uses require the generated rollout to stay faithful to the recorded world, yet existing benchmarks start from a single image or a text prompt, and video-conditioned generation is evaluated mainly on perceptual quality and camera following. These evaluations do not directly assess whether exploration preserves subject identity, event progression, and scene consistency upon revisiting a location. We introduce WanderBench, a benchmark for exploring dynamic worlds from video. It comprises 745 single-shot source videos of real and AI-generated content in three difficulty tiers (3-25 s), paired with camera routes given as keyboard actions, and evaluates six dimensions with 24 human-validated sub-metrics. Benchmarking eight models, we find that as clips grow longer, models keep the static scene and visual quality but lose camera control and the source dynamics, and that none keeps revisited places consistent. We further propose WanderLand, a training-free framework that conditions each frame of a frozen model on the same-instant source and, on revisits, on its own earlier static content. WanderLand improves five models on every dimension, by up to 8.3 points in source-dynamics fidelity.

llm.title_ja: WanderBench：ビデオから動的世界を探索できるか？
llm.tldr_ja: 実世界およびAI生成の動的ビデオを用いて、被写体の同一性やシーンの一貫性を保った探索能力を評価するベンチマーク「WanderBench」と、訓練不要のフレームワーク「WanderLand」を提案した。
llm.problem: ビデオ条件付きの生成モデルにおける既存の評価は、知覚品質やカメラ追従に主眼が置かれており、動的シーンの再訪時における一貫性や探索能力が十分に評価されていない。
llm.method: 745本の単一ショットソースビデオとキーボード操作によるカメラ経路を組み合わせたベンチマークWanderBenchを構築し、フリーズしたモデルにソース映像を条件付けるWanderLandを開発した。
llm.result: モデルはクリップが長くなるとカメラ制御やソースダイナミクスを失うことを示し、WanderLandがすべての次元、特にソースダイナミクスの忠実度を最大8.3ポイント改善することを確認した。

2611.12557.tldr_en: This work introduces WanderBench, a benchmark for exploring dynamic worlds from video, and proposes WanderLand, a training-free framework that conditions each frame of a frozen model on the same-instant source and, on revisits, on its own earlier static content.

2611.12526.title: Galilean Robots, Aristotelian Sensors: Joint Spatiotemporal Trajectory Estimation and Extrinsic Calibration
2611.12526.abstract: Multi-sensor state estimation requires accurate spatial and temporal calibration between heterogeneous sensors. Existing spatiotemporal calibration methods typically represent sensor extrinsic parameters as a rigid-body transformation together with a scalar temporal offset, causing the spatial and temporal parameters to enter the estimation problem through separate mechanisms. While the spatial transformation composes directly with the robot pose, accounting for the temporal offset requires evaluating the trajectory at a shifted time, typically through motion compensation, interpolation, or a continuous-time trajectory representation. In this work, we formulate joint trajectory estimation and spatiotemporal calibration using the special Galilean group for the robot trajectory and the Aristotelian subgroup for sensor extrinsics. This representation incorporates the coupling between motion and temporal offset directly through the group structure, avoiding the need for a separately parameterized continuous-time trajectory. We develop twist- and IMU-driven motion priors, accommodate both ideal and non-ideal clocks, and evaluate the framework with camera, position, and range measurements. Simulated and real experiments demonstrate calibration and trajectory-estimation performance comparable to established methods across heterogeneous sensor configurations. Our simplified framework therefore offers a quality-of-life improvement over existing methods without compromising performance.

llm.title_ja: ガリレオ型ロボット、アリストテレス型センサー：関節時空間軌道推定と外部校正
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット軌道にガリレオ群、センサー外部パラメータにアリストテレス部分群を用いた群構造に基づく表現により、連続時間軌道を別途パラメータ化することなく時空間校正と軌道推定を統合した。
llm.problem: マルチセンサーの状態推定における空間・時間的キャリブレーションでは、空間変換と時間的オフセットが別々のメカニズムで処理されるため、連続時間軌道表現や運動補償が必要となる。
llm.method: ガリレオ群とアリストテレス部分群の群構造を用いて運動と時間オフセットの結合を直接組み込んだ、ツイストおよびIMU駆動の運動事前分布に基づく統合推定フレームワークを定式化・開発した。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機実験において、既存手法と同等のキャリブレーションおよび軌道推定性能をより簡素なフレームワークで実現した。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2611.12526.tldr_en: This work formulates joint trajectory estimation and spatiotemporal calibration using the special Galilean group for the robot trajectory and the Aristotelian subgroup for sensor extrinsics to offer a quality-of-life improvement over existing methods without compromising performance.

2611.12508.title: MARS: Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams for Video Forgery Detection
2611.12508.abstract: Generalizing deepfake detection across facial manipulation and fully generated video remains challenging due to forgery traces varying with the manipulation method and scene content. Explicit spatial and temporal feature differences offer a way to capture this variation, but also respond to natural texture and motion, motivating their joint interpretation with appearance features. We investigate whether combining multiscale feature differences with adapted appearance representations improves detection across both forgery categories. We introduce Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams (MARS), a two-path video detector. The residual path applies fixed spatial and temporal difference-of-Gaussians operators to frozen intermediate features and models the resulting differences alongside appearance context across frames. The semantic path adapts the encoder's normalization parameters for frame classification, and a clip-dependent gate combines their predictions. Under a shared protocol across seven datasets, MARS achieves the highest average AUROC of 91.43\%, outperforming seven compared detectors. When trained on facial manipulations alone, MARS achieves 93.99\% AUROC on GenVideo and 75.50\% on DF26, demonstrating transfer to generated videos without generated-video training data. MARS also provides signed patch and frame contributions, whose faithfulness we evaluate through controlled spatial and temporal removal against random controls. MARS is publicly available for research: Project page: https://vectorinstitute.github.io/mars/ Github: https://github.com/VectorInstitute/mars

llm.title_ja: MARS：ビデオ偽造検出のためのマルチスケール外観残差ストリーム
llm.tldr_ja: 固定された空間・時間ガウス差分オペレーターを用いた残差パスと、外観コンテキストを適応的にモデル化するセマンティックパスを組み合わせた2パスのビデオ偽造検出器「MARS」を提案した。
llm.problem: 顔の改変や完全生成されたビデオにわたるディープフェイク検出の汎化は、偽造の痕跡が手法やシーンによって異なるため困難である。
llm.method: 凍結された中間特徴量に対してマルチスケールな特徴差分をモデル化する残差パスと、正規化パラメータを適応させるセマンティックパスをクリップ依存のゲートで統合するMARSを開発した。
llm.result: 7つのデータセットにわたる共通プロトコルにおいて、最高平均AUROC 91.43%を達成し、顔改変のみで学習した場合でも生成ビデオへの高い転移性を示した。
keywords_ja: ディープフェイク検出
コンピュータビジョン

2611.12508.tldr_en: This work introduces Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams (MARS), a two-path video detector that applies fixed spatial and temporal difference-of-Gaussians operators to frozen intermediate features and models the resulting differences alongside appearance context across frames.

2611.12452.title: V3DSAM: Semantic-Geometric Loop Verification and Geometry-Anchored Persistent Instance Mapping for Feed-Forward Dense SLAM
2611.12452.abstract: To address unreliable cross-view association in long-sequence feed-forward dense SLAM, this letter presents V3DSAM, an open-vocabulary semantic dense SLAM system that establishes physical correspondences at both the scene and object levels. The system combines feed-forward geometric estimates from VGGT-SLAM 2.0 with open-vocabulary semantic observations from SAM3. We introduce semantic-geometric dual-scale loop verification, which identifies false loop closures using pixel-level bidirectional reprojection and object-level 3D spatial correspondences, without accessing backbone-internal features. We further propose geometry-anchored persistent instance mapping, which defines physical instances through class-constrained 3D connectivity in an optimized global coordinate system and assigns global IDs without inter-frame identity propagation. The proposed verifier rejects all four false loop candidates in our TUM RGB-D evaluation, while long-sequence ScanNet experiments show improved instance identity consistency. Thus, V3DSAM reduces dependence on internal backbone features and temporal ID propagation for robust long-term cross-view association.
2611.12452.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)

llm.title_ja: V3DSAM: フィードフォワード型密なSLAMのためのセマンティック幾何学的ループ検証と幾何学アンカー型永続インスタンスマッピング
llm.tldr_ja: 長シーケンスのフィードフォワード型密なSLAMにおける信頼性の低いクロスビュー対応を解決するため、シーンおよびオブジェクトレベルで物理的な対応関係を確立するオープン語彙セマンティック密なSLAMシステム「V3DSAM」を提案する。
llm.problem: 長シーケンスのフィードフォワード型密なSLAMにおける信頼性の低いクロスビュー対応
llm.method: VGGT-SLAM 2.0の幾何学的推定とSAM3のオープン語彙セマンティック観測を組み合わせる
llm.result: TUM RGB-Dの評価で4つの偽ループ候補をすべて排除し、ScanNet実験でインスタンスの一貫性を改善した
keywords_ja: セマンティックセグメンテーション

2611.12452.tldr_en: V3DSAM is presented, an open-vocabulary semantic dense SLAM system that establishes physical correspondences at both the scene and object levels that reduces dependence on internal backbone features and temporal ID propagation for robust long-term cross-view association.

2611.12443.title: MoSTE: Mixture of Spatio-Temporal Experts for Deepfake Detection in Videos
2611.12443.abstract: Generalizable deepfake video detection remains challenging because forgery artifacts vary substantially across manipulation types and often combine diverse spatial and temporal inconsistencies. Existing parameter-efficient adaptation methods typically rely on a single shared representation, rendering them prone to manipulation-specific bias and limiting transfer to unseen forgeries. To address this challenge, we propose Mixture Of Spatio-Temporal Experts (MoSTE), an adaptation framework that enables conditional specialization of forensic representations. Instead of forcing one adapter to model all forgery patterns, MoSTE decomposes adaptation into parallel spatial and temporal expert pools and dynamically routes tokens to the most relevant experts through an unsupervised token-level routing mechanism. This allows experts to naturally specialize in complementary forgery cues without requiring explicit manipulation labels or multi-stage training, while effectively transferring representations from CLIP to the video domain. Extensive experiments across cross-dataset and cross-manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that MoSTE sets a new state of the art in average generalization while preserving strong performance across diverse manipulation families. Additional analysis of expert routing and attention behavior reveals the emergence of expert diversity, suggesting that MoSTE learns complementary spatio-temporal forensic features. Code is available at https://github.com/charbelyah/MoSTE
2611.12443.comment: Accepted to IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV) 2027

llm.title_ja: MoSTE: 動画におけるディープフェイク検出のための時空間エキスパート混合モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 単一の共有表現に依存する既存手法の限界を克服するため、フォレンジック表現の条件付き特殊化を可能にする適応フレームワーク「MoSTE」を提案する。
llm.problem: 改ざんタイプによる偽造アーティファクトの多様性と未見の偽造への転移の制限

2611.12409.title: Bridging Task Planning and Execution for Language-Conditioned Bimanual Manipulation
2611.12409.abstract: Robots are increasingly expected to execute natural-language manipulation tasks in real-world environments. This is particularly relevant in household assistance and logistics, where clutter requires reasoning about both task objectives and execution feasibility. This challenge becomes even more pronounced for bimanual humanoid platforms, where coordinating two manipulators introduces additional interaction and kinematic constraints. We present a zero-shot vision-language framework for execution-aware bimanual manipulation that jointly reasons about task objectives and physical feasibility. Planning is grounded in a structured scene representation that combines semantic object relations with execution constraints, enabling the selection of obstacle relocations and execution choices while preserving task semantics. Compatible actions are organised into parallel bimanual stages with explicit pre- and post-conditions. A hierarchical validator evaluates these conditions under perceptual uncertainty and uses stage-level execution history to support local recovery or targeted replanning. Experiments on the CENTAURO hybrid wheeled-legged humanoid robot across nine language-conditioned manipulation scenarios show higher task success than a non-execution-aware baseline. In dedicated failure scenarios, hierarchical validation recovers from execution failures with fewer model queries than always replanning. These results demonstrate the benefits of combining execution reasoning directly into task planning. Videos and additional material are available on the Project Webpage: https://advrhumanoids.github.io/bridging-planning-execution/.
2611.12409.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures. Accepted at the 2026 IEEE-RAS International Conference on Humanoid Robots (Humanoids 2026). Equal contribution by the first two authors

2611.12383.title: PCTac: Mechanochromic Photonic-Crystal Tactile Sensor for Dexterous Manipulation
2611.12383.abstract: Modern visuotactile sensors primarily sense contact by imaging the deformation of a compliant interface. Using techniques such as photometric stereo, they can recover detailed contact geometry, often represented as surface normals or depth. However, force-related information typically still needs to be inferred indirectly through calibration, geometric reconstruction, or learned mappings. Mechanochromic photonic-crystal (PC) materials offer an alternative physical encoding mechanism: contact loading changes their periodic microstructure and spectral response, directly transforming local stress into a spatially resolved structural-color field. Despite this potential, PC materials have rarely been explored as visuotactile sensors for closed-loop robot learning. We present PCTac, an open-source mechanochromic PC fingertip that uses a dense hue field as its tactile observation. Loading characterization demonstrates a repeatable relationship between the applied normal load and the observed hue response. We further integrate this representation directly into a Diffusion Policy and evaluate it on three real-robot manipulation tasks. Across 90 physical rollouts, PCTac Hue achieves 68 successes (75.6\%), compared with 60 (66.7\%) for PCTac RGB, 57 (63.3\%) for Wedge RGB, and 29 (32.2\%) for vision-only. PCTac Hue also achieves the highest observed success rate on each evaluated task, including Perturbed Test-Tube Insertion, where it achieves 16/30 successes versus 13/30 for tactile RGB baselines and 1/30 for vision-only. These results demonstrate the potential of mechanochromic structural color as a compact, load-sensitive tactile representation for robot learning and closed-loop manipulation. Project page: https://bey0ndt1me.github.io/PCTac-page/.

llm.title_ja: PCTac: 器用なマニピュレーションのためのメカノクロミックフォトニック結晶触覚センサー

2611.12382.title: AutoVLA-D: Learn a Trajectory-Geometric Condition from Reasoning for Autonomous Driving VLA
2611.12382.abstract: Autoregressive VLA planning usually predicts continuous trajectories as the final output, but driving instructions often describe actions rather than ego states, which weakens direct conditioning on the final continuous trajectory. We address this gap with TrajCond, which introduces a discrete trajectory-geometric condition for VLA planning. Specifically, we represent TrajCond as a 1D-Brohan differential action trajectory and learn it with a two-stage training framework before final continuous trajectory prediction. With the simultaneous autoregressive generation of discrete and numeric trajectories, we name our method AutoVLA-D (Double). Experiments on NAVSIM navtest, nuScenes, and NeuroNCAP show that discrete trajectories are weaker as direct outputs but more effective as TrajCond, consistently improving final continuous trajectory prediction across closed-loop and open-loop driving benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/ShivaTeam/AutoVLA-D.

llm.method: 1D-Brohan差動行動軌道としてTrajCondを表現し、最終的な連続軌道予測の前に2段階のトレーニングフレームワークで学習する

2611.12378.title: Safety-Constrained Intelligent Control of a 2-DOF Robotic Manipulator Using Control Barrier Functions
2611.12378.abstract: Control barrier function (CBF) filters depend on dynamic models that can be inaccurate when their parameters and external forces are uncertain. This paper investigates a radial basis function (RBF) neural network compensator whose output is shared by a Cartesian tracking controller and a joint-space CBF filter. An auxiliary state driven by the difference between requested and applied torques corrects the learning signal, reducing the direct influence of filter intervention on adaptation. A two-link manipulator is evaluated through constrained regulation, ablations, matched uncertainty and disturbance trials, and operating-range and timing studies. The results demonstrate that the proposed controller improves tracking while maintaining joint, velocity, and torque limits under parameter uncertainty, and that both the shared compensation and the auxiliary correction contribute to this improvement.
2611.12378.comment: Paper submitted to the European Control Conference 2027

llm.title_ja: 制御バリア関数を用いた2自由度ロボットマニピュレータの安全制約付き知能制御

2611.12351.title: UniOMA: Unified Optimal-Transport Multi-Modal Structural Alignment for Robot Perception
2611.12351.abstract: Achieving generalizable and well-aligned multimodal representations remains a core challenge in robot learning. While recent approaches have attempted to align modalities by modeling conditional or higher-order statistical dependencies, they do not explicitly consider the structural coherence across modalities. In this work, we propose a novel multimodal alignment method that augments existing contrastive losses with a geometry-aware Gromov--Wasserstein (GW) distance-based regularization. To this end, we encode intra-modal geometry for each modality and reduce cross-modal structural discrepancies through a dynamically learned GW barycenter, thereby encouraging structural consistency in addition to instance-level contrastive alignment. We apply this optimal-transport-based alignment strategy to robot perception tasks involving underexplored modalities such as force and tactile signals, where modality data often exhibit varying sample densities. Extensive experiments on five robotic benchmarks show that our method improves structural alignment and downstream performance over state-of-the-art multimodal contrastive baselines across a wide range of downstream tasks, including robot and environment state prediction. Moreover, our GW-based regularization can be seamlessly integrated into most InfoNCE-like objectives.

llm.title_ja: UniOMA: ロボット知覚のための統合型最適輸送マルチモーダル構造アライメント

llm.problem: モダリティ間の構造的一貫性を明示的に考慮しない既存のマルチモーダルアライメント手法の限界
llm.method: 動的に学習されるGW重心を通じてモダリティ間の構造的不一致を削減する最適輸送ベースのアライメント戦略
llm.result: 5つのロボットベンチマークにおいて、力や触覚信号を含む多様なタスクで構造的アライメントと下流性能が向上した

2611.12351.tldr_en: This work proposes a novel multimodal alignment method that augments existing contrastive losses with a geometry-aware Gromov--Wasserstein distance-based regularization and improves structural alignment and downstream performance over state-of-the-art multimodal contrastive baselines across a wide range of downstream tasks, including robot and environment state prediction.

2611.12334.title: Rethinking Radar 3D Perception: Representation Learning from Raw Spectra
2611.12334.abstract: Raw radar spectra are widely viewed as too cluttered and noisy for direct representation learning, motivating handcrafted reductions, sparse point clouds, or compact Doppler descriptors in radar perception. We challenge this assumption and argue that the main limitation lies not in the raw representation itself, but in the absence of a learning objective that separates structured signal from noise. Handcrafted reductions partially address this problem but impose rigid assumptions about what constitutes signal, discarding weak yet informative structure while retaining artifacts that fit the reduction model. Once removed, such information cannot be recovered by supervised learning. We propose an alternative: structure is the component of a radar spectrum that remains reconstructable under localized corruption, while noise is the component that does not. This perspective motivates self-supervised masked modeling for dense radar spectra without predefined signal-noise separation. We instantiate it with Leakage-aware Spectral MAE, a masked autoencoder for raw radar cubes using a corruption strategy inspired by cross-bin energy spreading caused by spectral leakage. We also demonstrate the importance of Doppler organization: treating Doppler as a primary spatial dimension in an x-y-D representation, with height encoded as features, substantially outperforms naive channel stacking and enables effective learning from dense 4D spectra. Without handcrafted reductions, our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art radar-based detectors and point-cloud-based self-supervised learning (SSL) counterparts. These results establish raw radar spectra as an effective representation for 3D perception when paired with an appropriate pretraining objective.
2611.12334.comment: 19 pages, 5 figures, 18 tables. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. Miao Zhang and Mohamed Abdelsamad contributed equally

2611.12317.title: Maximizing Detection Probability in UAV Search Missions using Random-Key Optimizers
2611.12317.abstract: This paper focuses on the stochastic and real-time constraints of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) path planning in Search and Rescue (SAR) missions. We introduce a configurable data-driven and intelligent routing architecture that combines a closed-loop probability update with the Random-Key Optimizers (RKO). Our problem is mathematically modeled as a dynamic probabilistic variant of the Open Vehicle Routing Problem (OVRP), enabling the solver to switch adaptively between two objectives, thereby balancing probability maximization and resource minimization. The framework degrades elegantly under noisy priors but not under biased ones: a systematically biased map performs about half as well as flying with no prior at all. Computational tests show that the proposed scheme is scalable and competitive with single-path scenarios in terms of solution performance and serves as a strong decision guide for intelligent planning in SAR operations in unstable environments

llm.title_ja: ランダムキー最適化を用いたUAV探索ミッションにおける発見確率の最大化
llm.tldr_ja: 捜索救助ミッションにおけるUAVの経路計画の確率的・リアルタイム制約に対処するため、閉ループ確率更新とランダムキー最適化を組み合わせたデータ駆動型の知的ルーティングアーキテクチャを提案する。
llm.problem: 捜索救助ミッションにおけるUAVの確率的かつリアルタイムな経路計画の困難さ
llm.method: 動的な確率的変種としての開放型車両ルーティング問題のモデル化と、確率最大化・資源最小化の動的切り替え

2611.12306.title: ExoStack: A Modular and Reconfigurable Software Framework for Wearable Robotics Using ROS 2
2611.12306.abstract: Wearable robots depend on a software chain that links body-worn sensing to gait interpretation, assistance generation, and actuation. Personalization further requires each measured response to remain associated with the assistance parameters that generated it. This paper presents ExoStack, a modular ROS 2 framework for implementing that chain across embedded hubs and a host computer. Its Embedded Sensing and Actuation (ESA) library configures ESP32 boards as microROS sensing and actuation hubs. ExoCore supplies multi-hub synchronization, gait-event detection, profile generation, motion planning, cost evaluation, and human-in-the-loop (HIL) optimization as configuration-instantiated nodes. The PASE desktop application edits configurations, launches the processing stages, and visualizes ROS 2 topics. Hardware drivers and algorithm plugins can be added through defined interfaces without modifying the generic processing nodes. We characterize hub and planner timing on three embedded computers and demonstrate reuse on two pneumatic exosuits.
2611.12306.comment: The source code and accompanying documentation website for ExoStack are publicly available at https://github.com/debadrata/ExoStack and https://debadrata.github.io/ExoStack_documentation/, respectively

2611.12295.title: Be My Eye: Learning to See Beyond a Robot's Own Perspective
2611.12295.abstract: Robots operating in the real world are inherently subject to partial observability, particularly in multi-robot collaboration, where individual observations may be insufficient for effective task execution. A key challenge is leveraging complementary observations from partner robots to support collaborative decision-making. We argue that information sharing should go beyond passively transmitting raw observations or generic visual features. Instead, robots should selectively encode task-relevant information according to task objectives and execution progress. To this end, we propose a task-oriented active context sharing framework that transforms robot observations into compact representations, preserving critical information under constrained communication budgets. The framework adopts a two-stage training paradigm. In the first stage, onboard observations and task instructions are jointly encoded into compact context representations. Task-oriented future prediction and soft task-progress correspondence learning guide this collaboration-agnostic compression, preserving information about task objectives and execution progress. In the second stage, the learned representations are integrated into a pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policy, enabling bidirectional context exchange. Each robot combines complementary partner information with local observations to guide action generation. Action supervision jointly refines the context representations and policy, aligning information sharing with collaborative decision-making. Controlled experiments demonstrate substantial performance gains under constrained communication budgets, while three real-world experiments validate the framework in complex dual-robot tasks. These results highlight a shift from passive visual transmission toward active, task-oriented context sharing that directly supports collaborative decision-making.

llm.title_ja: Be My Eye: ロボット自身の視点を超えた視覚の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 通信制約下で協調的な意思決定を支援するため、ロボットの観測をタスク目的に応じてコンパクトな表現に変換するタスク指向アクティブコンテキスト共有フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: マルチロボット協調における部分観測性と、単なる生観測や汎用ビジュアル特徴の受動的な共有による情報制約

2611.12295.tldr_en: This work proposes a task-oriented active context sharing framework that transforms robot observations into compact representations, preserving critical information under constrained communication budgets and highlights a shift from passive visual transmission toward active, task-oriented context sharing that directly supports collaborative decision-making.

2611.12286.title: VLA-MOPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Task VLA Policy Consolidation
2611.12286.abstract: Physical intelligence requires embodied agents to ground language in observations and execute actions while retaining useful skills. Vision-language-action (VLA) policies offer a shared interface, but task-specific post-training often produces separate specialists. Consolidation is difficult: mixed-task reinforcement learning provides sparse trajectory-level credit, while offline distillation may miss student-visited observations and endpoint distillation does not supervise intermediate action-generation states. We introduce VLA Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation (VLA-MOPD), a protocol for consolidating flow-matching VLA specialists. After acquiring task or suite experts, a shared student collects robot rollouts and queries the instruction-routed frozen teacher at each visited observation and intermediate ordinary differential equation (ODE) state. Detached per-flow-step transition targets supervise valid action chunks through a masked local matching loss; an optional reference-policy term supports retention on other tasks. Starting from one trajectory per LIBERO task, VLA-MOPD raises mean success-once from 75.4% to 98.9%, compared with 98.15% for endpoint action distillation. It improves mean RoboTwin 2.0 success from 73.0% to 89.3%; on a Piper robot, two consolidation rounds improve average success from 70.0% to 90.0%. In a near-matched Spatial-adaptation study, reference matching limits the Object suite decrease to 3.0 points, versus 13.2 without the reference term.

llm.title_ja: VLA-MOPD: マルチタスクVLAポリシー統合のためのオンポリシー蒸留

keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル
ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.12286.tldr_en: This work introduces VLA Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation (VLA-MOPD), a protocol for consolidating flow-matching VLA specialists and describes how an optional reference-policy term supports retention on other tasks.

2611.12261.title: Hierarchical Multi-Channel Tip-Over Prediction via Isolated Temporal Models for Planetary Rover Safety
2611.12261.abstract: Reliable tip-over prevention is critical for planetary rovers operating in unstructured environments where communication delays prevent real-time human intervention. Existing learning-based approaches typically optimize a single prediction objective, limiting their ability to capture both gradual instability evolution and abrupt terrain disturbances. This work presents a hierarchical multi-channel tip-over prediction framework based on isolated temporal learning. A multi-horizon Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) learns progressive instability patterns from inertial measurements, while a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)-based forward dynamics model predicts nominal rover motion and detects unexpected dynamic deviations through prediction residuals. These complementary signals are integrated through decision-level fusion and priority-based arbitration to generate graded safety actions, including early warning and emergency braking. The proposed system is deployed as an Orocos Real-Time Toolkit (RTT)-based safety component within the Rock robotics framework, operating at 100 Hz on a planetary rover software stack. Experiments on Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) samples collected across heterogeneous terrains demonstrate 97.58% event prediction coverage with a 1.82s median lead time, outperforming individual prediction channels. The results validate that isolated temporal models combined through hierarchical decision fusion provide a robust solution for real-time rover safety in uncertain terrain.

llm.title_ja: 惑星ローバの安全性のための孤立した時間モデルによる階層型マルチチャンネル転倒予測
llm.tldr_ja: 構造化されていない環境で動作する惑星ローバの確実な転倒防止のため、マルチホライズンTCNとGRUベースの動力学モデルを統合した階層型マルチチャンネル転倒予測フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 単一の予測最適化目標のみでは、徐々に進行する不安定性と突然の外乱の両方を捉えるのが困難であること
llm.method: TCNによる不安定性パターンの学習とGRUフォワードダイナミクスモデルの予測残差を決定レベルの融合で統合する
llm.result: 異種地形のIMUデータを用いた実験において97.58%のイベント予測カバー率と1.82秒の中央値リードタイムを達成した

2611.12251.title: RAIL: Representation-Aligned Imitation Learning for Student-Compatible Teacher Policies
2611.12251.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) from raw sensory inputs such as images or onboard sensors can be challenging due to high-dimensional observations and sparse rewards. A common strategy is to train a teacher policy with access to privileged state information and then distill it into a student policy that acts from raw inputs alone. However, when the teacher relies on information unavailable to the student, exact imitation may be impossible, creating an irreducible imitation gap. Existing approaches typically mitigate this mismatch through careful reward shaping or additional reinforcement learning on the student policy after the teacher has been trained. Instead, we introduce Representation-Aligned Imitation Learning (RAIL), which addresses the mismatch during teacher training itself. RAIL learns a latent representation shared across teacher and student observations using contrastive learning, and trains the teacher policy directly in this space. Because the teacher policy is constrained to operate on this shared space, it learns behaviors that are reproducible from student observations. This substantially reduces the imitation gap while preserving task performance. Across multiple environments, RAIL outperforms strong baselines without reward modification or post-hoc student fine-tuning, and surpasses direct reinforcement learning from raw observations. The learned representations further enable zero-shot transfer to new tasks through teacher-only training. Project site: https://merajmammadov.com/rail/.

llm.title_ja: RAIL: 生徒互換性のある教師ポリシーのための表現アラインメント型模倣学習
llm.tldr_ja: 特権状態情報に基づく教師ポリシーと生入力に基づく生徒ポリシーの間の模倣ギャップを軽減するため、教師のトレーニング段階自体で表現のアラインメントを行う手法「RAIL」を提案する。
llm.problem: 教師が利用できる情報が生徒に利用できないことに起因する、解消不可能な模倣ギャップ
llm.method: 対比学習を用いて教師と生徒の観測間で共有される潜在表現を学習し、その空間で直接教師ポリシーをトレーニングする
llm.result: 報酬の変更や事後微調整なしで強力なベースラインを上回り、ゼロショットでの新しいタスクへの転移を可能にした

2611.12251.tldr_en: Representation-Aligned Imitation Learning (RAIL), which addresses the mismatch during teacher training itself by learning a latent representation shared across teacher and student observations using contrastive learning, and trains the teacher policy directly in this space.

2611.13039.title: Robo-MLT: Dual-System Robotic Manipulation for Long-Horizon Medical Laboratory Tasks
2611.13039.abstract: Reliable medical laboratory automation requires robots to complete entire workflows in protocol order while handling changes during execution. A robot may execute each motion correctly yet fail the workflow by confusing visually similar stages or stalling after human intervention. We present Robo-MLT, a dual-system framework that couples explicit workflow monitoring with learned action generation. A vision--language planner composes an ordered atomic-skill sequence from the protocol and the initial workspace observation. A multiframe execution monitor detects when the active skill has completed or become infeasible, then advances the workflow or triggers replanning. A skill-conditioned vision--language--action policy generates the manipulation trajectories, and an asynchronous runtime coordinates it with the monitor. We evaluate Robo-MLT against four policy baselines and a VLM-based monitor baseline on blood gas analysis and blood sample tube sorting, with 50 nominal configurations per method and 20 sample-removal configurations. Robo-MLT achieves task success rates of 82\% and 70\%, exceeding $π_{0.5}$ by 30 and 22 percentage points, respectively. After an operator removes the sample being handled, the system revises the remaining plan and continues processing the other samples. These results indicate that, under the evaluated conditions, explicit workflow monitoring makes long-horizon laboratory manipulation more reliable and recoverable.

llm.title_ja: Robo-MLT：長期的な医療検査タスクのためのデュアルシステム・ロボット操作
llm.tldr_ja: 明示的なワークフロー監視と学習済みアクション生成を組み合わせ、医療検査タスクの自動化における実行中の変化や誤認への頑健性を高めたデュアルシステムフレームワーク「Robo-MLT」を提案した。
llm.problem: 医療検査の自動化では、ロボットが視覚的に類似したステージの混同や、人間の介入後に停止することなどにより、ワークフロー全体を完了できない場合がある。
llm.method: ビジョン・言語プランナーによる順序付きアトミック・スキルの構成、マルチフレーム実行モニターによる監視、スキル条件付きVLAポリシーによる軌跡生成を統合したデュアルシステム「Robo-MLT」を提案した。
llm.result: 血液ガス分析や血液サンプル管の分別のタスク成功率において82%と70%を達成し、既存のベースラインを大幅に上回るとともに、サンプルの除去等の介入後もプランを修復して続行可能であることを示した。

2611.13039.tldr_en: Robo-MLT, a dual-system framework that couples explicit workflow monitoring with learned action generation, is presented and results indicate that it makes long-horizon laboratory manipulation more reliable and recoverable.

2611.12226.title: A Game-Theoretic MPC Planner for Cooperative and Adversarial Drone Coordination
2611.12226.abstract: We present and evaluate a game-theoretic model predictive control planner for cooperative goal reaching and adversarial pursuit-evasion with drones. The planner combines 3D prediction, individual objectives, optional shared separation constraints and trajectory-tracking interfaces. A comparison of cooperative game solvers assesses their ability to find feasible trajectories that resolve conflicts. A computational study quantifies how number of drones, prediction horizon and move blocking affect computation time and numerical acceptance. Move blocking holds control inputs constant over groups of prediction steps, reducing the number of independent control variables and lowering computation time. Timing measurements identify the practical limits of real-time planning in the tested configurations. PyBullet simulations demonstrate cooperative goal reaching and pursuit-evasion. A laboratory flight complements the simulations by validating the trajectory-tracking interfaces on physical drones. The planner can serve as a basis for further evaluation and controller development.
2611.12226.comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, submitted to European Control Conference (ECC27)

llm.title_ja: 協調的および敵対的なドローン調整のためのゲーム理論的MPCプランナー
llm.tldr_ja: ドローンの協調的ゴール到達と敵対的追跡回避のために、3D予測、個別の目的関数、トラジェクトリ追跡インターフェースを組み合わせたゲーム理論的モデル予測制御プランナーを提案・評価する。
llm.problem: 複数ドローンの協調的目標到達や敵対的追跡回避におけるリアルタイムな競合解決と計算量の課題
llm.method: 制御入力を固定して独立した制御変数を減らすムーブブロッキングを組み合わせたゲーム理論的MPCプランナーの構築
llm.result: PyBulletシミュレーションと実機フライトにより、協調的ゴール到達と追跡回避における軌道追跡の有効性を検証した

2611.12226.tldr_en: A game-theoretic model predictive control planner for cooperative goal reaching and adversarial pursuit-evasion with drones and a comparison of cooperative game solvers assesses their ability to find feasible trajectories that resolve conflicts is presented.

2611.12205.title: Graph-Based RL for Sequential Rendezvous Planning with Multiple Patrolling USVs
2611.12205.abstract: In patrol missions involving multiple unmanned surface vehicles (USVs), a designated command USV can support fleet management by sequentially rendezvousing with each patrolling USV. These operations require motion-feasible route planning and priority-aware rendezvous sequencing, with the objective of minimizing mission completion time and total tardiness relative to priority-dependent due dates. We propose a framework combining grid-based path planning, surrogate travel-time prediction, and graph-based reinforcement learning. The path planner accounts for ocean currents and approximates turn-rate constraints through multi-stage maneuvers, with path feasibility empirically validated through trajectory-tracking simulations. For rendezvous sequencing, a Feasible Transition Graph (FTG) represents candidate rendezvous events and temporally feasible transitions, enabling a graph neural network to exploit spatiotemporal rendezvous relationships for policy learning. A surrogate predicts travel times from compact current and motion features to avoid repeated path searches during FTG construction and policy training. Evaluation using grid-based path planning shows statistically significant average objective reductions of 10.5%, 3.5%, and 1.5% compared with greedy, MLP-RL, and 2-step lookahead greedy, respectively. The policy achieves these improvements while requiring approximately 1/35 of the latter's computation time. It maintains its advantage over MLP-RL under unseen priority-tier settings, with larger gains as fleet size increases.

llm.title_ja: 複数パトロールUSVの順次ランデブー計画のためのグラフベース強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 複数無人水上艇（USV）のパトロール任務における効率的な艦隊管理のため、グリッドベース経路計画、サロゲート移動時間予測、グラフベース強化学習を組み合わせたフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 複数USVのパトロールにおける、モーションに実行可能な経路計画と優先度を考慮したランデブー順序付けの最適化
llm.method: 候補となるランデブーイベントと遷移を表す実現可能遷移グラフを用い、グラフニューラルネットワークでポリシーを学習する
llm.result: 従来の貪欲法やMLP-RLに比べて計算時間を大幅に削減しつつ、統計的に有意な目的関数の削減を達成した
keywords_ja: グラフニューラルネットワーク

2611.12205.tldr_en: A framework combining grid-based path planning, surrogate travel-time prediction, and graph-based reinforcement learning is proposed, which maintains its advantage over MLP-RL under unseen priority-tier settings, with larger gains as fleet size increases.

2611.12202.title: Co-Creating Neurorehabilitation Technology Alongside Lived Experience Experts: A Participatory Design Workshop
2611.12202.abstract: Involving patients' lived experience (LE) early in neurorehabilitation technology design can improve the relevance and effectiveness of solutions, yet LE experts are often involved only when finished prototypes are tested. We present and evaluate a participatory design (PD) workshop for early LE involvement, examine how LE contributions influence design processes and outcomes, and provide recommendations for similar approaches. We conducted a PD workshop at the 6th International Conference on NeuroRehabilitation. Five people who have had a stroke (LE experts) and 18 workshop attendees (including the LE experts' caregivers) were organized into five groups. Following the Discover, Define, and Develop phases of the Double Diamond model, each group used Journey Maps and Data Collection Notebooks to co-create a solution for an objective specified by an LE expert. Journey Maps were thematically analyzed, and group audio transcripts underwent structured extraction using a large language model. LE input shifted discussions from discipline-based assumptions toward priorities grounded in lived experience, including fear, confidence, sensory discomfort, fatigue, aesthetics, and independence. Narrow objectives, such as opening a blister pack, produced task-specific solutions, whereas broader objectives generated device concepts, including sensory feedback for cycling and a stimulation-equipped cooking splint. Satisfaction was high among attendees and LE experts. All workshop tools and protocols are shared to support adoption. The workshop offers a practical foundation for involving LE experts early in neurorehabilitation technology development. Future iterations should better capture psychological and social dimensions, allow more reflection, and include the full range of relevant stakeholders through sustained transdisciplinary engagement between researchers and the LE community.
2611.12202.comment: Submitted to JMIR Rehabilitation and Assistive Technologies

llm.title_ja: 生活体験の専門家との共同による神経リハビリテーション技術の共創: 参加型デザインワークショップ
llm.tldr_ja: 神経リハビリテーション技術のデザイン初期段階から患者の生活体験を取り入れるため、ダブルダイヤモンドモデルに基づいた参加型デザインワークショップを実施・評価する。
llm.problem: 完成したプロトタイプのテスト段階まで患者の生活体験の専門家が関与しないことによる、ソリューションの関連性と有効性の低下
llm.method: ジャーニーマップやデータ収集ノートを用いて、Discover、Define、Developの各フェーズで生活体験を持つ専門家と介護者・参加者を組織化するワークショップの開催
llm.result: 患者の生活体験に基づいた優先事項（恐怖、快適さ、独立性など）へと議論の焦点を移行させ、参加者全体で高い満足度を記録した
llm.limitation: 心理的・社会的次元の十分な捕捉や振り返りの時間確保に改善の余地がある
keywords_ja: 神経リハビリテーション

2611.12202.tldr_en: A participatory design workshop for early LE involvement is presented, how LE contributions influence design processes and outcomes are examined, and recommendations for similar approaches are provided.

2611.13034.title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement
2611.13034.abstract: Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Useful practice depends on the agent's current capabilities, so the procedure that chooses practice must also be revisable. We present RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models. The curriculum harness uses accumulated capability evidence to propose informative challenges, while the execution harness responds with reusable revisions that expand execution capabilities. Alternating updates hold one side fixed as the other changes, and admitted challenges form fixed snapshots for comparing execution revisions. Starting from a compact set of LIBERO practice conditions, the resulting frozen deployment outperforms the evaluated controllers and agent systems across four LIBERO-family panels. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 74.0% success, exceeding the initial deployment by 15.0 percentage points and direct execution by its VLA controller by 13.5 points. Case studies document changes to evidence-guided practice selection, drawer-skill grounding, and controller intervention.

llm.title_ja: RoboACE：ロボットの自己改善のための敵対的共進化
llm.tldr_ja: 蓄積された能力証拠に基づいて課題を提案するカリキュラムと、実行能力を拡張する実行ハーネスを共同で進化させるフレームワーク「RoboACE」を提案し、LIBEROベンチマークで高い成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: ロボットエージェントは実行フィードバックからスキルや計画を改善できるが、固定された練習ソースでは新しい弱点を見つけて克服し続けることが難しい。
llm.method: 凍結された基礎モデルの周囲で、カリキュラムハーネスと実行ハーネスを交互に更新・共進化させるフレームワーク「RoboACE」を提案した。
llm.result: LIBERO-PROにおいて74.0%の成功率を達成し、初期展開から15.0ポイント、VLAコントローラによる直接実行から13.5ポイント上回る性能を実証した。

2611.13034.tldr_en: This work presents RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models that outperforms the evaluated controllers and agent systems across four LIBERO-family panels.

2611.12177.title: Embodied First Exam
2611.12177.abstract: Early successes on agentic robotics point to a potential paradigm shift toward using coding agents to control robots. Existing robotics benchmarks are built around visuomotor policy learning, leaving it open whether coding agents can reliably control diverse robots under physical-world constraints. We therefore introduce the Embodied First Exam, a unified, comprehensive, and agent-native evaluation framework where coding agents can choose their own control approach: direct control, code to control, or train a policy to control. We hope it serves as a first exam for coding agents before they enter the physical world, with 1,156 tasks in 35 suites on 47 robots, including 9 new suites that go beyond pick-and-place to spatial puzzles, dexterous manipulation, multi-robot interaction, dynamic whole-body control, and sim-to-sim engineering. Each task can be run in up to three evaluation settings. The Standard Setting mimics the real world: the agent receives only sensor observations and, by default, cannot reset the environment. Its Realtime variant keeps the environment running while the agent reasons. The Privileged Setting gives the agent access to the full simulator state and unlimited resets, allowing it to search for an oracle solution for training purposes. Success rates in this setting serve as an approximate upper bound. On the 456 core tasks, the strongest of eight agents, GPT-6 Astra in Codex, achieves a success rate of 34% in the Standard Setting, leaving much room for improvement. To see where agents fail, we label the stage at which failed attempts go wrong and compare failures across agents, settings, and stage categories.

llm.title_ja: Embodied First Exam: 物理的世界におけるコーディングエージェントのための統合評価フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 多様なロボットを物理的制約下でコーディングエージェントが制御できるかを評価するため、エージェントが独自の制御アプローチを選択できる統合・網羅的な評価フレームワーク「Embodied First Exam」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のロボットベンチマークが視覚運動方策学習に偏っており、コーディングエージェントの物理世界での制御能力が未検証であること
llm.method: 35スイート1156タスクからなり、標準・リアルタイム・特権の最大3つの評価設定でコーディングエージェントの制御アプローチを検証する
llm.result: 最強のエージェントでも標準設定での成功率が34%にとどまり、エージェントの性能向上に向けた大きな余地を示した
keywords_ja: コーディングエージェント

2611.12177.tldr_en: The Embodied First Exam is introduced, a unified, comprehensive, and agent-native evaluation framework where coding agents can choose their own control approach: direct control, code to control, or train a policy to control.

2611.12175.title: GeoMind: A Benchmark for Spatial Understanding in Robotic Manipulation
2611.12175.abstract: Robotic manipulation has advanced rapidly in mapping visual observations and language instructions to actions. However, reliable manipulation in open-world environments requires robust spatial understanding: the ability to identify targets in complex layouts (spatial reasoning) and adapt to scenes that continuously evolve through interaction (spatial memory). Yet existing embodied benchmarks fall short in evaluating spatial understanding: they often introduce strong visual cues that bypass spatial reasoning, and focus on static scenes that offer little insight into an agent's capacity for spatial memory. To address this gap, we introduce GeoMind, a systematic benchmark for structured spatial understanding through tabletop manipulation. GeoMind comprises 54 evaluated task variants organized around spatial reasoning and spatial memory. It also incorporates a scalable pipeline that automates the generation and annotation of task instances with verified targets and executable interactions. Extensive evaluations across diverse embodied agents reveal their consistent weaknesses in spatial understanding. Our findings highlight that these agents struggle to track identities after spatial changes and convert relational or geometric constraints into executable actions. We release the GeoMind benchmark at https://github.com/Notfound-JH/GEOMIND-benchmark.git.

llm.title_ja: GeoMind: ロボットマニピュレーションにおける空間理解のためのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: オープンワールド環境での信頼性の高いマニピュレーションに必要な空間推論と空間記憶を体系的に評価するためのテーブルトップマニピュレーション向けベンチマーク「GeoMind」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の具現化ベンチマークにおける、強力な視覚的手がかりによる空間推論のバイパスと静的シーンへの偏り
llm.method: 空間推論と空間記憶の周囲に組織化された54の評価タスクバリアントと、検証済みターゲットやインタラクションの自動生成・注釈パイプラインの構築
llm.result: 多様な具現化エージェントの空間理解における一貫した弱点（空間変化後の同一性追跡や関係制約の実行可能性への変換の困難さ）を明らかにした
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.12175.tldr_en: GeoMind is a systematic benchmark for structured spatial understanding through tabletop manipulation that automates the generation and annotation of task instances with verified targets and executable interactions and releases the GeoMind benchmark, a systematic benchmark for structured spatial understanding through tabletop manipulation.

2611.12162.title: Same Physics, Different Gradients: A State-of-the-Art Report on Differentiable Physics Simulation
2611.12162.abstract: Differentiable simulation propagates derivatives through a physics simulator, turning animation, system identification, control, and computational design into gradient-based optimization. Engines differ in the physics they model and, less visibly, in which mathematical object they differentiate. We separate two questions the literature conflates. The referent is which object the returned derivative belongs to: the finite computation that executed, the converged equation it approximates, or the continuous dynamics. The realization describes the organization of the backward pass: automatically generated differentiation, an equation-level adjoint solve, or a custom adjoint. The referent defines the target against which exactness is assessed; the implementation determines how accurately that target is approximated. Cost depends on the realization together with how the states needed by the backward pass are retained or recovered. Crossing the axes places every method and engine we classify in a cell, separates claims the literature merges, and shows that the apparent trade-off between exactness and memory follows from how methods have been built rather than from a constraint. A second, orthogonal taxonomy covers contact, where the map is non-smooth. We then ask whether a correct gradient helps. Four mechanisms by which useful gradients are lost are cataloged and measured on one testbed, where the advantage of the exact derivative over the equation-level adjoint depends on where the fitting target comes from as much as on the solver budget, and we review the evidence that zeroth-order methods can outperform simulator gradients in the regimes where those mechanisms act. The model classes, systems techniques and applications are surveyed through this lens, and we close with a reporting checklist, a released diagnostic that computes it, and a research agenda.

llm.title_ja: 同じ物理学、異なる勾配: 微分可能物理シミュレーションに関する最新動向レポート
llm.tldr_ja: 微分可能物理シミュレータにおける数学的オブジェクトの微分と逆伝播の整理を通じて、手法およびエンジンの分類、正確性とメモリのトレードオフ、勾配の有効性を検証する。
llm.problem: 文献において、微分対象となる数学的オブジェクト（有限計算、収束方程式、連続ダイナミクス）と逆パスの実現方法が混同されていること
llm.method: シミュレータがモデル化する物理と数学的微分対象・逆パスの組織化に基づく軸による分類、および接触などの非滑らかなマップの分類の導入
llm.result: 正確性とメモリのトレードオフが本質的な制約ではなく構築方法に起因することを示し、モデルクラスやシステム技術を調査した
keywords_ja: 微分可能シミュレーション

2611.12162.tldr_en: The evidence that zeroth-order methods can outperform simulator gradients in the regimes where those mechanisms act is reviewed, and the evidence that zeroth-order methods can outperform simulator gradients in the regimes where those mechanisms act is reviewed.

2611.12149.title: EgoLabel: Zero-Shot Egocentric Auto-Labeling with Cross-Modal Consistency
2611.12149.abstract: Egocentric auto-labeling requires depth, camera pose, object, and human-pose estimates to agree across independently developed models. Differences in units, coordinate conventions, and scale can make individually plausible predictions geometrically inconsistent. We present \textbf{EgoLabel}, a zero-shot pipeline that combines off-the-shelf models without target-domain labeled training and provides explicit cross-modal registration and consistency diagnostics. The pipeline integrates MonST3R for geometry, LocateAnything with GMC-BoT-SORT and SAM~2 for objects, and V-HPOT for hands; FisheyeViT provides a separate whole-body compatibility demonstration. Our main hand evaluation uses H2O sensor depth. Across 20 sequences, per-hand depth anchoring reduces the mean of per-sequence median hand--depth residuals by $23\%$ relative to a single global scale, yielding a pooled median of $84.6\,\mathrm{mm}$ against a $20.5\,\mathrm{mm}$ ground-truth reference. Hand PA-MPJPE is $14.53\pm1.29\,\mathrm{mm}$, whereas absolute MPJPE is $119.1\pm31.3\,\mathrm{mm}$, revealing a substantial gap between aligned and metric accuracy. On three RGB-only sequences, camera ATE is $1.40\pm0.29\,\mathrm{cm}$ after $\mathrm{Sim}(3)$ alignment. We also identify a sliding-window implementation issue that allows sensor-initialized depth to change during optimization. Because hand anchoring and its residual share the same depth map, the residual measures internal consistency rather than independent accuracy. These results characterize both the utility and the current limits of the registration pipeline.

llm.title_ja: EgoLabel: クロスモーダルの一貫性を用いたゼロショット・エゴセントリック自動ラベリング
llm.tldr_ja: 独立に開発されたモデルを統合し、明示的なクロスモーダル登録と一貫性診断を行うゼロショットのエゴセントリック自動ラベリング手法「EgoLabel」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のエゴセントリック自動ラベリングモデル間では、単位・座標系・スケールの違いにより幾何学的な不整合が生じる課題がある。
llm.method: MonST3R、LocateAnything、SAM 2、V-HPOTなどの既存モデルを組み合わせ、明示的なクロスモーダル登録と一貫性診断を行う。
llm.result: 手ごとの深度アンカリングにより、シーケンスごとの中央値手深度残差の平均を単一のグローバルスケールと比較して23%削減した。
llm.limitation: アライメント精度とメトリック精度の間に実質的な乖離があり、センサー初期化深度が最適化中に変化する実装上の問題が確認された。

2611.12149.tldr_en: This work presents EgoLabel, a zero-shot pipeline that combines off-the-shelf models without target-domain labeled training and provides explicit cross-modal registration and consistency diagnostics, and identifies a sliding-window implementation issue that allows sensor-initialized depth to change during optimization.

2611.12139.title: BioMARS 2.0: a robotic biologist for formulating and adapting biological experiments
2611.12139.abstract: Biological experimentation is not reducible to a single optimization problem, but requires decisions at multiple levels of abstraction: translating scientific knowledge into experimental procedures, adapting culture conditions to measured phenotypes and selecting interventions that test biological hypotheses. Automating experimental execution does not, by itself, determine which experiments should be performed next or how they should change in response to biological feedback. Here we introduce BioMARS, a human-in-the-loop multi-agent robotic system that connects knowledge-guided experimental decision-making with robotic execution and biological feedback. At the procedural level, BioMARS generated literature-grounded protocols and traceable action plans, improving expert-reviewed protocol quality scores across four model backends. At the parametric level, BioMARS used image-derived phenotypes from robotic retinal organoid culture to select subsequent experimental conditions, with higher reported scores in later rounds of the three-round experiment. At the intervention level, BioMARS nominated drug-repurposing candidates from biomedical evidence and advanced six candidates to wet-lab testing by researchers. Together, these studies demonstrate feedback-driven robotic biological experimentation within a framework that supports decisions about experimental procedures, culture conditions and biological interventions.

llm.title_ja: BioMARS 2.0：生物学的実験の立案と適応を行うロボット生物学者
llm.tldr_ja: 知識に基づく実験の意思決定、ロボットによる実行、生物学的フィードバックを結合した人間参加型マルチエージェントロボットシステム「BioMARS」を提案する。
llm.problem: 生物学的実験の自動化において、次にどの実験を行うべきか、または生物学的フィードバックに応じてどう変更すべきかを決定することは困難である。
llm.method: 知識に基づく実験計画、ロボットによる網膜オルガノイド培養の画像由来表現型を用いた条件選択、および薬物再目的化候補の選定を統合する。
llm.result: プロトコル品質の向上、培養実験の後期ラウンドにおける高スコア化、および6つの薬物候補の湿式実験への進行を実現した。

2611.12136.title: LHNav: Long-Horizon Humanoid Navigation via Multirate Coordination and Physics-Grounded Action Data
2611.12136.abstract: We study humanoid navigation across multiple destinations under long-horizon language instructions. This task is challenging because robots must maintain progress across successive goals while continuously producing natural, stable whole-body motion through confined spaces. However, task decomposition in existing methods does not by itself ensure progress throughout execution, while waypoint-based navigation does not guarantee natural, route-faithful whole-body motion. Our key idea is to organize navigation into three complementary roles operating at different time scales: a Brain for task reasoning, a Cerebellum for local motion generation, and a Brainstem for whole-body execution. We realize this idea in LHNav, an asynchronous system that uses progress and arrival feedback to coordinate navigation goals, VLA motion-token prediction, and whole-body control. To train the Cerebellum for natural, route-faithful motion, we develop a physics-grounded data engine that improves physical tracking of motion references along collision-aware routes and pairs the resulting demonstrations with rendered visual observations. Together, these designs allow task planning to proceed alongside continuous movement and extend single-goal navigation to successive destinations with natural, route-faithful whole-body motion. In simulation, our navigation VLA outperforms OmniNav and DualVLN in single-goal success and motion smoothness, with fewer collisions and falls. Using a VLA trained only on single-goal demonstrations, LHNav achieves a 75.56% success rate on long-horizon navigation tasks. Deployment on the Unitree G1 further demonstrates single-goal navigation and zero-shot long-horizon task execution in real-world environments, including layouts with repositioned objects. Project website: https://robbyant-research.github.io/LHNav/.

llm.title_ja: LHNav：マルチレート協調と物理ベースの行動データに基づく長期的ヒューマノイドナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: タスク推論を行うBrain、局所動作生成を行うCerebellum、全身実行を行うBrainstemの3つの役割を非同期に協調させる長期的ヒューマノイドナビゲーションシステム「LHNav」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存手法ではタスク分解やウェイポイントベースのナビゲーションだけでは、狭い空間での自然で安定した全身運動や長期的目的の達成を保証できない。
llm.method: 進捗と到着フィードバックを用いて目標・VLAトークン予測・全身制御を協調させる非同期システムと、物理ベースのデータエンジンを開発した。
llm.result: シミュレーションで成功率や動作の滑らかさが向上し、Unitree G1の実機でも単一およびゼロショットの長期的タスク実行に成功した。

2611.12136.tldr_en: The key idea is to organize navigation into three complementary roles operating at different time scales: a Brain for task reasoning, a Cerebellum for local motion generation, and a Brainstem for whole-body execution, which allows task planning to proceed alongside continuous movement and extend single-goal navigation to successive destinations with natural, route-faithful whole-body motion.

2611.12130.title: Compact and Wide-Force-Range Magnetorheological Hand Exoskeleton for Kinesthetic Feedback in Teleoperation
2611.12130.abstract: Hand kinesthetic feedback is crucial for restoring and enhancing human perception of force and displacement in robotic hand teleoperation. Wide perception range of force feedback is vital in rendering objects of different stiffness, especially for high-stiffness rendering. However, existing approaches struggle to achieve wide range of force feedback while maintaining compact and wearable design. This paper presents a hand exoskeleton system employing magnetorheological (MR) brakes to provide a wide range kinesthetic feedback during teleoperation. The MR brake provides a braking torque ranging from 0.01 to 0.918 Nm, while maintaining a compact structure with a total mass of only 39.8 g. The proposed exoskeleton can render fingertip forces up to 21 N while maintaining back-driving force of 1.01 N. Experimental results show that the system allows users to discriminate object stiffness using kinesthetic feedback alone. In a tele-grasping task, when both conditions achieved a 100% success rate, kinesthetic feedback led to a 28.2% reduction in object contact force compared to visual feedback only, enhancing object safety and operator immersion. Questionnaire results further indicate that kinesthetic feedback improves reliability, realism, and user confidence during teleoperation.

llm.title_ja: テレオペレーションにおける運動学的フィードバックのためのコンパクトで広範囲な磁気粘弾性ハンド外骨格
llm.tldr_ja: 磁気粘弾性（MR）ブレーキを用いて、軽量かつコンパクトな構造を維持しながら広範囲な力フィードバックを提供するハンド外骨格システムを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の手法では、コンパクトで装着可能なデザインを維持しながら、高剛性レンダリングに適した広範囲な力フィードバックを実現することが困難である。
llm.method: MRブレーキを採用し、0.01〜0.918 Nmの制動トルクと39.8 gの軽量コンパクトな構造を両立したハンド外骨格を設計・実装した。
llm.result: 最大21 Nの指先力をレンダリング可能であり、把持タスクにおいて接触力を28.2%削減しつつ、把持成功率100%を維持した。

2611.12130.tldr_en: Experimental results show that the hand exoskeleton system employing magnetorheological brakes to provide a wide range kinesthetic feedback during teleoperation improves reliability, realism, and user confidence during teleoperation, and indicates that kinesthetic feedback improves reliability, realism, and user confidence during teleoperation.

2611.12129.title: RAPA: Ray-Aware Physics Augmentation for Robust Camera-LiDAR Calibration
2611.12129.abstract: Camera-LiDAR calibration is essential for reliable perception in robotic and autonomous systems. Most target-based calibration methods rely on checkerboard observations, but accurate checkerboard feature extraction from LiDAR point clouds remains challenging due to measurement sparsity. Existing approaches either require manual annotation of 3D corners or depend on geometric feature extraction methods, both of which can become unreliable when checkerboard features are insufficiently observed. In this paper, we formulate checkerboard localization as a 2D detection problem using cylindrical LiDAR reflectivity images. To overcome the limited availability of labeled training data, we propose ray-aware physics augmentation (RAPA), which generates diverse synthetic samples from a single checkerboard observation. The generated data are used to improve detector robustness and generalization under varying sensing conditions. Across four independently captured indoor and outdoor locations, the proposed synthetic augmentation exceeds the strongest evaluated image-space augmentation baseline by 16.1-43.1 percentage points in mAP@0.5. Compared with training-free target-based methods on 242 observations, RAPA yields the largest number of valid target localizations, with 96.4% of its returned detections yielding valid target poses. These reliable localizations support downstream camera-LiDAR calibration across all four evaluated locations. Overall, RAPA addresses a key bottleneck in target-based calibration by enabling automated LiDAR-side target localization with only a single annotated target observation.

llm.title_ja: RAPA：堅牢なカメラ・LiDARキャリブレーションのためのレイ認識物理ベース拡張
llm.tldr_ja: 単一のチェッカーボード観測から多様な合成サンプルを生成し検出器の頑健性を高めるレイ認識物理ベース拡張（RAPA）を提案する。
llm.problem: LiDAR点群からのチェッカーボード特徴量抽出は計測の疎らさゆえに困難であり、既存手法は手動注釈や複雑な幾何学的特徴抽出に依存している。
llm.method: 円柱状LiDAR反射率画像を用いた2D検出問題としてチェッカーボード位置合わせを定式化し、単一観測から多様なサンプルを生成するRAPAを導入する。
llm.result: 4つの屋内・屋外環境において、既存の画像空間拡張ベースラインをmAP@0.5で16.1〜43.1ポイント上回り、96.4%の有効なターゲット姿勢を返した。
keywords_ja: センサーキャリブレーション

2611.12129.tldr_en: This paper proposes ray-aware physics augmentation (RAPA), which generates diverse synthetic samples from a single checkerboard observation, and addresses a key bottleneck in target-based calibration by enabling automated LiDAR-side target localization with only a single annotated target observation.

2611.12120.title: SCALE: Small-Model-First Concept Abstraction with LLM-Guided Experience Internalization
2611.12120.abstract: Autonomous agents must continually acquire reusable knowledge from experience without relying on costly large language model (LLM) reasoning for every decision. However, existing experience-based approaches often struggle to transform accumulated observations and reasoning into compact knowledge that lightweight models can independently apply. This paper proposes SCALE, a small-model-first framework that integrates selective LLM reasoning, experience-driven concept abstraction, and knowledge internalization. A lightweight model handles routine predictions, while prediction errors and accumulated cross-episode evidence selectively trigger LLM reflection. The LLM analyzes relevant historical experiences, generates positive and negative counterfactual examples, and proposes reusable concept hypotheses. Independently validated concepts are progressively incorporated into hierarchical neural representations, enabling lightweight models to exploit increasingly abstract knowledge. Meanwhile, mastered experiences are excluded from active memory while their original records remain available in a complete archive. Experiments across ten random seeds show that historical recall improves held-out accuracy from 87.11% to 98.28%, hierarchical concept knowledge increases difficult-case accuracy from 55.33% to 66.47%, and abstract archiving reduces active experience records from 6,000 to 1,528.

llm.title_ja: SCALE：LLMガイドによる経験内面化を伴う小型モデル優先の概念抽象化
llm.tldr_ja: 軽量モデルが日常的予測を処理し、エラーや蓄積された証拠に基づいて選択的にLLMの推論・概念抽出を呼び出す「SCALE」フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 自律エージェントは、すべての意思決定に高コストなLLM推論を頼ることなく、経験から再利用可能な知識を継続的に獲得する必要があるが、それは難しい。
llm.method: 予測エラー等で選択的にLLMのリフレクションをトリガーし、反事実的例の生成や再利用可能な概念仮説の提案を経て階層的ニューラル表現に統合する。
llm.result: 履歴の想起により未知データの正解率が87.11%から98.28%に向上し、アクティブな経験レコードが削減された。

2611.12120.tldr_en: SCALE is proposed, a small-model-first framework that integrates selective LLM reasoning, experience-driven concept abstraction, and knowledge internalization that improves held-out accuracy, hierarchical concept knowledge, and abstract archiving.

2611.13030.title: APS-VLA: Action-Guided and Future-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.13030.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies have demonstrated strong generalization in robotic manipulation, yet processing dense visual tokens often incurs high inference latency. Visual token pruning offers a practical way to reduce this cost, but identifying a compact set of tokens that preserves reliable action generation remains challenging. Existing methods largely rely on static or immediate heuristic cues to estimate token importance. We introduce APS-VLA, a framework that learns visual token selection from robot demonstrations while keeping the pretrained VLA backbone frozen. A lightweight Decision Influence Estimator scores tokens conditioned on current visual observations, language instructions, and robot proprioception. Its training combines two complementary signals: action supervision matches both the full-input policy predictions and demonstrated actions, while an auxiliary visual transition objective uses demonstrated actions to predict subsequent visual features from the selected representation. At deployment, the estimator performs a single hard selection and packing step before the policy's native action-generation procedure; the auxiliary predictor is removed. Experiments with OpenVLA-OFT on LIBERO and with $π_{0.5}$ and XR-1 on RoboCasa365 demonstrate inference acceleration with modest changes in task success. Across five real-world tasks on two dual-arm platforms, APS-VLA reduces mean policy inference latency from 137.25 to 93.25 ms, achieving a $1.47\times$ speedup with an average success rate of 61%, compared with 60% for the unpruned baseline. Together, these results support APS-VLA as a modular, plug-in framework for efficient robotic control across VLA architectures, preserving the underlying policy parameters and native action-generation procedure.

llm.title_ja: APS-VLA: 効率的な視覚・言語・行動モデルのための行動誘導型および将来予測型トークンプルーニング
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みのVLAバックボーンを固定したまま、ロボット実演から視覚トークンの選択を学習する効率的なフレームワークAPS-VLAを提案し、タスク成功率を維持しつつ推論を高速化した。
llm.problem: VLAポリシーはロボット操作で高い汎化性能を示すが、密な視覚トークンの処理に高い推論レイテンシが生じる。
llm.method: 軽量な決定影響推測器により、現在の視覚観測・言語指示・固有受容感覚に基づいてトークンをスコア化し選択する。
llm.result: 5つの実世界タスクにおいて、平均推論レイテンシを137.25msから93.25msに短縮し、同等の成功率を維持した。
keywords_ja: トークンプルーニング

2611.13030.tldr_en: APS-VLA is introduced, a framework that learns visual token selection from robot demonstrations while keeping the pretrained VLA backbone frozen, preserving the underlying policy parameters and native action-generation procedure.

2611.12113.title: Motion Belief Action: From a Visual Scene Map to Physical Decisions
2611.12113.abstract: A robot that works among people must judge what it cannot see: whether an object is still where it was last seen, and whether a pull on a door or drawer is worth its risk. Maps that track object change hold nothing about force, maps of physical properties answer a risk question at a fixed risk level, and vision-language-action models keep no explicit estimate of hidden physics. We propose Motion Belief Action (MBA), a decision layer on the scene map. From how often people move an object and how much force it needs, how much load it holds and whether it is blocked, MBA chooses under a force limit to look again, nudge, open, brace or decline, with its risk set by the task's costs. On real activity in 9 kitchens, it predicts whether an object is still in place better than FreMEn and Perpetua, and decides when to look again at lower cost than these and the persistence filter, because about a quarter of placements end in a pick-up within 30 s. On real pulls of doors and drawers in 17 locations, made by a person with a force-sensing gripper, the map's force estimates decide better than a part-type average. Setting the risk from the costs also beats a published risk rule at its fixed level. In simulation, with the force limit at the training parts' median force, MBA raises SmolVLA's and Octo's scores by declining pulls; most declined door pulls would fail, but on drawers more would have opened, and a part-type average gets about half of this gain. In both, a published risk rule set to the risk these costs imply is MBA's rule for a single pull and decides as well in the main settings. A link between opening and holding force, a probing nudge and an action prior for camera tracking do not help in the main settings, and over the real-pull sweep the nudge costs a little.

llm.title_ja: Motion Belief Action：ビジュアルシーンマップから物理的意思決定へ
llm.tldr_ja: オブジェクトの移動頻度や必要な力、負荷、障害物情報に基づき、力制限の下で最適な行動を選択するシーンマップ上の決定レイヤー「MBA」を提案する。
llm.problem: 従来のマップは力に関する情報を保持せず、ビジョン・言語・アクションモデルは隠れた物理特性の明示的な推定を行わない。
llm.method: オブジェクトの移動頻度、必要とされる力、負荷、閉塞状態を入力として、見る・軽く押す・開ける・支える・見送るなどの判断をタスクコストの制限下で行う。
llm.result: 9つのキッチンの実環境において従来手法よりも低コストかつ高精度にオブジェクトの存在を予測し、ドアや引き出しの引き抜き実験でも優れた結果を示した。

2611.12113.tldr_en: Motion Belief Action is proposed, a decision layer on the scene map that chooses under a force limit to look again, nudge, open, brace or decline, with its risk set by the task's costs, beating a published risk rule at its fixed level.

2611.12111.title: GAP: Generalized Adaptation Prior for Dexterous Piano Playing
2611.12111.abstract: Dexterous hands enable versatile manipulation, but policies trained in simulation often degrade on hardware owing to non-idealities, and the high-dimensional action space makes real-world adaptation costly. Piano playing, which requires precise and coordinated multifinger motion, offers a representative testbed. We propose GAP (Generalized Adaptation Prior for Dexterous Piano Playing), a sample-efficient adaptation framework that learns how to adapt, rather than how to act, during simulation pretraining and transfers this adaptation prior to hardware. Between repeated executions, GAP uses feedback to adjust the actions of the next one: a gradient guidance network learns from paired executions how adjusting actions affects playing performance, and its gradients guide these adjustments. In simulation, GAP yields approximately 2.4 times the F1 scores improvement of the existing fast-adaptation baseline for dexterous piano playing under the same interaction budget. The learned prior also generalizes to musical pieces held out from pretraining. On a physical dexterous hand, the same simulation-pretrained prior improves F1 scores by 3.6%-23% across three pieces of varying difficulty after approximately 7 min of adaptation each. These results suggest a practical route to reduce the real-world interaction needed to deploy dexterous hands.

llm.title_ja: GAP：器用なピアノ演奏のための一般化適応事前学習
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレーション事前学習時に「行動の仕方」ではなく「適応の仕方」を学習し、その適応事前学習を実機へ転移するサンプル効率の良いフレームワーク「GAP」を提案する。
llm.problem: シミュレーションで訓練された政策は実機の非理想性のために性能が低下し、高次元な行動空間のせいで実世界での適応に高いコストがかかる。
llm.method: 試行間で勾配ガイダンスネットワークを用いて演奏パフォーマンスの変化から次回の行動調整を学ぶフィードバックベースの適応フレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: シミュレーションでベースラインの約2.4倍のF1スコア向上を達成し、実機の多指ハンドでも約7分の適応後に3.6%〜23%のF1スコア改善を実現した。

2611.12111.tldr_en: GAP (Generalized Adaptation Prior for Dexterous Piano Playing) is proposed, a sample-efficient adaptation framework that learns how to adapt, rather than how to act, during simulation pretraining and transfers this adaptation prior to hardware.

2611.12102.title: SPARK: Simple Post-training for Adapting pRetrained Knowledge to Robot Control
2611.12102.abstract: Large-scale representation learning has produced public foundation models that provide strong general-purpose visual features. However, their pretraining objectives are not designed for robot representation learning, so the resulting embeddings tend to emphasize global semantics rather than the temporally sensitive representations required for robot control. Training robot models from scratch is also undesirable due to the limited scale and high collection cost of robotics data, as well as the substantial computational burden of pre-training. In this paper, we propose SPARK (Simple Post-training for Adapting pRetrained Knowledge), a post-training method that adapts foundation models to robot control. SPARK is built on two principles: temporal abstraction, which encourages the encoder to derive compact features that preserve information essential for understanding temporal changes and action-relevant scene structure, and knowledge preservation, which aligns patch-level representations with those of the original foundation model to retain useful pretrained semantics. These objectives yield compact visual state representations that remain semantically meaningful while preserving useful prior knowledge. Experiments across multiple robotics benchmarks show that SPARK consistently improves success rates and generalization over vanilla foundation models, and further demonstrate that these gains transfer to real-world robot manipulation.

llm.title_ja: SPARK：事前学習済み知識をロボット制御に適応させるためのシンプル事後学習
llm.tldr_ja: 時間的抽象化と知識保存の原則に基づき、汎用視覚基盤モデルの表現をロボット制御用に適応させる事後学習手法「SPARK」を提案する。
llm.problem: 汎用基盤モデルの事前学習目的はロボット制御に最適化されておらず、ロボット固有のデータ不足や計算コストの面からゼロからの訓練も望ましくない。
llm.method: 時間的変化の理解に必要な情報を維持するコンパクトな特徴抽出を促す時間的抽象化と、元のモデルのパッチ表現を整合させる知識保存を組み合わせる。
llm.result: 複数のロボットベンチマークにおいて、バニラな基盤モデルと比較して成功率と汎化性能が一貫して向上し、実機マニピュレーションへの転移も実証された。
keywords_ja: 実機マニピュレーション

2611.12102.tldr_en: SPARK (Simple Post-training for Adapting pRetrained Knowledge), a post-training method that adapts foundation models to robot control, is proposed and built on two principles: temporal abstraction and knowledge preservation.

2611.12099.title: SAM-VTP: Video Memory and Measured Geometry for Continuous Traversability Segmentation
2611.12099.abstract: Traversability prediction is a core component of autonomous navigation, yet most vision-based methods operate frame-wise and produce temporally inconsistent predictions. We present SAM-VTP (Video Traversability Prediction), which fine-tunes SAM2's video memory pathway for dense, prompt-free traversability segmentation, conditioning each frame on a persistent memory of prior observations. Rather than inferring terrain geometry from appearance, we measure it: slope, roughness and height are computed from depth and fused into the image features. We also introduce an offline continuous supervision pipeline that generates dense per-pixel traversability targets in [0,1] from depth-derived geometry and semantic priors, requiring no robot deployment and no per-pixel annotation, capturing conditional feasibility that binary labels cannot represent. On TartanGround, a large-scale synthetic ground-robot dataset, SAM-VTP improves fuzzy Jaccard from 0.908 to 0.924 and binary IoU from 0.854 to 0.886 over SAM-TP, a frame-wise SAM2 baseline, against a seed-to-seed spread below 0.001, and cuts frame-to-frame flicker by 31%. In closed-loop trials at two field sites, driving the same planner and controller, the baseline's dropouts leave the planner without a feasible path 3.3x more often on a paved course and 6.9x on rough ground, while SAM-VTP runs at 21.4 FPS on the Orin Nano the robot carries.

llm.title_ja: SAM-VTP：連続的通行可能性セグメンテーションのためのビデオメモリと計測幾何学
llm.tldr_ja: SAM2のビデオメモリ経路を微調整し、深度から計算した幾何情報を画像特徴に統合して、プロンプト不要で高密度な通行可能性セグメンテーションを行う「SAM-VTP」を提案する。
llm.problem: 多くのビジョンベースの通行可能性予測手法はフレーム単位で動作するため、時間的に不整合な予測結果を生成してしまう。
llm.method: 深度から傾斜・粗さ・高さを計算して画像特徴に融合し、過去の観測の持続的メモリに基づいて各フレームを条件付けするビデオメモリ経路を利用する。
llm.result: シミュレーションデータセットにおいて、ベースラインと比較してファジィJaccardおよび二値IoUを向上させ、フレーム間のチラツキを31%削減した。

2611.12099.tldr_en: An offline continuous supervision pipeline is introduced that generates dense per-pixel traversability targets in [0,1] from depth-derived geometry and semantic priors, requiring no robot deployment and no per-pixel annotation, capturing conditional feasibility that binary labels cannot represent.

2611.12087.title: Compass 1: Towards Open-World and Persistent Embodied Navigation from Monocular RGB Videos
2611.12087.abstract: Embodied navigation requires agents to achieve persistent spatial awareness and long-horizon execution stability in open-world environments. However, existing navigation architectures struggle to sustain both capabilities, remaining effective only over a handful of recent frames. We present Compass 1, the first embodied navigation foundation model to unify language understanding and video generation while enabling memory backtracking through nearly 2mins of visual history. Without altering the underlying architecture, we introduce History Representation, which integrates sparse visual keyframes with an explicit History Representation Map to preserve long-term spatiotemporal context. To effectively leverage this history, we further introduce History Utilization, a structured VQA supervision protocol comprising three categories: task-stage grounding, exploration consistency, and spatiotemporal target retrieval, enabling map-grounded reasoning and stable persistent long-horizon navigation. To fuel this system, we establish a complete annotation pipeline for monocular RGB videos and open-source a massive dataset featuring over 500 hours of high-quality real-world interactions and over 2,000 hours of annotated web videos. Trained mainly on the distribution of 1m height camera, Compass 1 generalizes seamlessly across diverse embodiments and scenarios, ranging from indoor environments to pedestrian-dense streets, spanning wheeled robot at 0.35m, quadruped dog at 0.5m, humanoid at 0.85m, and aerial drone at 1.5m. Compass 1achieves a dominant overall success rate of 79.4% across open-world evaluations, compared to 17.8% for the strongest baseline. It demonstrates exceptional zero-shot execution exceeding 90% on foundational tasks, a 250% boost in exploration, and an unparalleled leap from 0% to 58% in challenging persistent history backtracking.

llm.title_ja: Compass 1：単眼RGB動画からのオープンワールドかつ持続的な身体性ナビゲーションに向けて
