llm.tldr_ja: 言語理解と動画生成を統合し、約2分間の視覚的履歴によるメモリバックトラッキングを可能にする初の身体性ナビゲーション基盤モデル「Compass 1」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のナビゲーションアーキテクチャは、持続的な空間認識と長期的実行安定性の両方を維持できず、数フレーム程度しか有効に機能しない。
llm.method: スパースな視覚キーフレームと明示的な履歴表現マップを統合した履歴表現と、タスク段階の接地などの構造化VQA監督プロトコルを導入する。
llm.result: 多様なロボット形態や環境において圧倒的な全体成功率（79.4%）を達成し、探索性能の大幅な向上を示した。

2611.12072.title: Learning Contextual Motion Constraints for Object Rearrangement Exploration
2611.12072.abstract: The motion of an articulated part in cluttered surroundings is constrained not only by an object's intrinsic joint limits but also by extrinsic obstacles. However, existing approaches primarily consider object articulation properties alone. Here we present Motion Constraint Prediction Network (MoCo-Net), a two-stream neural network that jointly predicts the continuous motion ranges of articulated parts and obstacle heatmaps highlighting potential collision regions from partial-view point cloud observation. By capturing both internal and external motion constraints, MoCo-Net produces more accurate feasible motion range prediction and obstacles recognition, improves generalization for novel objects in new scenes, and enables robots to construct a scene configuration space for efficient exploration of rearrangement actions. Our experiments show that MoCo-Net's two-stream design enhances each other to deliver more accurate predictions, which subsequently form a compact configuration space for a customized planner to efficiently rearrange the scene.

llm.title_ja: オブジェクト再配置探索のためのコンテキストモーション制約の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 部分観測点群から関節可動域と障害物ヒートマップを同時に予測する2ストリームニューラルネットワーク「MoCo-Net」を提案する。
llm.problem: 関節のある部品の動きは、オブジェクト自体の関節限界だけでなく外的な障害物によっても制約されるが、既存手法は関節特性のみを考慮している。
llm.method: 部分ビュー点群の観測から、関節部分の連続的な動作範囲と潜在的な衝突領域を示す障害物ヒートマップを結合予測するMoCo-Netを開発した。
llm.result: 2ストリーム設計により互いの予測精度が高まり、効率的なシーン再配置のためのコンパクトなコンフィギュレーション空間の構築が可能になった。

2611.12072.tldr_en: A two-stream neural network that jointly predicts the continuous motion ranges of articulated parts and obstacle heatmaps highlighting potential collision regions from partial-view point cloud observation, which produces more accurate feasible motion range prediction and obstacles recognition and enables robots to construct a scene configuration space for efficient exploration of rearrangement actions.

2611.12038.title: DPGS-SLAM: Diffusion-Prior and Provenance-Aware Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Dynamic Visual Sensing
2611.12038.abstract: This paper presents DPGS-SLAM (Diffusion-Prior and Provenance-Aware Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM) for dense mapping in environments containing dynamic objects. Dynamic observations can contaminate camera tracking and scene reconstruction in visual SLAM (simultaneous localization and mapping). Although 3DGS (3D Gaussian splatting) enables efficient dense mapping, existing 3DGS-SLAM systems may exhibit instability when dynamic objects violate their underlying static-scene assumption. Excluding dynamic observations can reduce their influence on tracking and mapping, but may leave occluded static backgrounds missing or weakly constrained. Our proposed DPGS-SLAM is a monocular RGB SLAM framework that supports provisional representations of insufficiently observed static backgrounds through asynchronous diffusion-based background completion and provenance-aware Gaussian mapping. Dynamic regions are identified through optical-flow-based motion discovery and temporally consistent mask propagation by SAM2 (segment anything model 2). For selected keyframes, a fine-tuned diffusion inpainting model generates plausible background appearance in occluded regions, while Metric3D v2 predicts metric depth from the completed images to initialize provisional Gaussian primitives. Provenance labels distinguish generated primitives from observation-supported primitives, excluding generated content from camera-pose estimation and observed-map optimization. When previously occluded backgrounds become visible, eligible generated primitives are removed, and observation-supported primitives are independently initialized from real RGB observations and predicted depth. Experimental results demonstrated competitive camera tracking, with average ATE RMSE values of 1.2 cm on TUM RGB-D and 2.7 cm on BONN RGB-D. On StaDy4D, DPGS-SLAM improved average PSNR by 4.60 dB over WildGS-SLAM using only monocular RGB input.

llm.title_ja: DPGS-SLAM：動的ビジュアルセンシングのための拡散事前学習および来歴認識型単眼ガウススプラッティングSLAM
llm.tldr_ja: 非同期の拡散ベース背景補完と来歴認識型ガウス表現を用いて、動的オブジェクトが存在する環境で高精度なマッピングを行う単眼RGB SLAMフレームワーク「DPGS-SLAM」を提案する。
llm.problem: 動的オブジェクトが存在する場合、ビジュアルSLAMにおいてカメラ追跡やシーン再構成が汚染され、静的シーンの仮定が破綻する。
llm.method: オプティカルフローとSAM 2による動的領域の特定、インパインティングによる背景補完、および生成されたプリミティブと観測されたプリミティブを区別する来歴ラベルの導入を行う。
llm.result: TUM RGB-Dなどのデータセットにおいて、平均ATE RMSE 1.2 cmという優れたカメラ追跡性能を実証した。
keywords_ja: ガウススプラッティング

2611.12038.tldr_en: DPGS-SLAM is a monocular RGB SLAM framework that supports provisional representations of insufficiently observed static backgrounds through asynchronous diffusion-based background completion and provenance-aware Gaussian mapping.

2611.12017.title: Grasp-Taxonomy Conditioning as a Mode Switch for Dexterous Grasping of Climbing Holds
2611.12017.abstract: Dexterous grasping in robotics relies on distinct hand configurations depending on object geometry. We introduce BetaGrasp, a 3D diffusion policy that conditions a DP3-style point-cloud policy on a four-class grasp label (crimp, sloper, pinch, and jug), running on a Franka arm with a 16-DoF LEAP hand. We also introduce a climbing-hold benchmark: a spring testbed whose ratchet gives a slip-force reading in newtons. In our analysis the policy's point-cloud encoder did not separate the four holds, so the scan alone gave it little to choose a grasp from. Without the label (a DP3-style baseline), simulated rollouts from the robot's reset pose all end in a jug grasp, whatever the hold (25% correct grasp type, versus 94% for BetaGrasp). The label works as a switch for which grasp the policy performs. On 80 paired hardware trials, BetaGrasp raises average slip force from 9.6 N to 14.3 N, and grasps slipping fully off the hold drop from 44% of trials to 10%.

llm.title_ja: クライミングホールドの器用な把持のためのモードスイッチとしての把持分類条件付け
llm.tldr_ja: 4種類の把持ラベルでDP3スタイルの点群ポリシーを条件付けし、把持タイプを切り替える3D拡散ポリシー「BetaGrasp」を提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットによる器用な把持はオブジェクトの形状に応じたハンドの構成に依存するが、点群のスキャン単体ではホールドに応じた適切な把持選択が難しい。
llm.method: クリンプ、スローパー、ピンチ、ジュグの4分類の把持ラベルを条件とした3D拡散ポリシーを導入し、スリップフォースを測定するベンチマークで評価した。
llm.result: BetaGraspは正しい把持タイプの割合を25%から94%に改善し、平均スリップフォースを14.3 Nに高め、把持の滑りを大幅に削減した。

2611.12017.tldr_en: BetaGrasp is introduced, a 3D diffusion policy that conditions a DP3-style point-cloud policy on a four-class grasp label (crimp, sloper, pinch, and jug), running on a Franka arm with a 16-DoF LEAP hand.

2611.11996.title: OASIS: Optimization-Aware Subgoal Inference with Safety Constraints for Autonomous Mobile Robot Navigation
2611.11996.abstract: Navigation in dynamic environments requires mobile robots to make progress toward their goals while respecting motion limits and avoiding surrounding obstacles. Learned subgoal policies can guide model predictive control beyond its local prediction horizon, but a geometrically suitable subgoal does not necessarily lead to a successfully solved control problem. This paper proposes OASIS, a hierarchical navigation framework that incorporates recent optimization outcomes into reinforcement learning-based subgoal generation. A high-level policy trained using Soft Actor--Critic generates local subgoals, while a nonlinear model predictive controller tracks them subject to motion limits, geometric collision-avoidance constraints, and embedded high-order control barrier function constraints. The outcomes of controller optimizations over each subgoal interval are summarized and provided to the policy at its next decision, without requiring additional optimization calls. The framework is evaluated in five navigation scenarios with static and moving obstacles, including dense interactions and sensing uncertainty. Comparisons with hierarchical and direct-goal control variants show that OASIS achieves the highest aggregate navigation success. Matched comparisons across three training seeds further show a consistent success advantage over the otherwise identical hierarchy without optimization-status input. The selected-policy comparison also shows fewer primary optimization failures with similar mean controller time.

llm.title_ja: OASIS：自律移動ロボットナビゲーションのための安全性制約付き最適化認識型サブゴール推論
llm.tldr_ja: 強化学習ベースのサブゴール生成に最近の最適化結果を組み込んだ階層型ナビゲーションフレームワーク「OASIS」を提案する。
llm.problem: 学習済みサブゴールポリシーはモデル予測制御をガイドできるが、幾何学的に適切なサブゴールが必ずしも制御問題を成功に導くとは限らない。
llm.method: Soft Actor-Criticで訓練された高レベルポリシーがローカルサブゴール生成を行い、非線形モデル予測コントローラーがモーション制限や衝突回避制約を満たしつつ追従する。
llm.result: 動的・静的障害物を含む5つのナビゲーションシナリオにおいて最高の統合ナビゲーション成功率を達成した。

2611.11996.tldr_en: This paper proposes OASIS, a hierarchical navigation framework that incorporates recent optimization outcomes into reinforcement learning-based subgoal generation and shows a consistent success advantage over the otherwise identical hierarchy without optimization-status input.

2611.11981.title: Thermo-VLA: A Thermal-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model with Gated Residual Modulation for Robotic Manipulation
2611.11981.abstract: Recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have begun incorporating thermal sensing, but existing approaches typically treat thermal images as ordinary visual inputs, providing limited support for temperature-aware relational reasoning in manipulation. To address this limitation, we propose Thermo-VLA with a ThermoRes Encoder, which decomposes thermal images into cold and hot attribute representations and injects them into the RGB token through language-conditioned residual modulation, enabling temperature-driven target selection and continuous manipulation. We further construct six real-world robotic tasks on a dual-arm Unitree G1 platform, spanning basic grounding to relational reasoning. Experiments show that Thermo-VLA achieves an average success rate of 0.86 across four thermal-dependent tasks, outperforming a pi_0.5 baseline that directly incorporates RGB-thermal observations by 18 percentage points. Under unseen-object and scene variations, Thermo-VLA maintains an average success rate of 0.78, achieving the best generalisation performance among the compared methods. Beyond thermal sensing, we transfer the same residual modulation mechanism to colour attributes and observe consistent improvements in both simulation and real-robot experiments, indicating its potential to generalise beyond thermal attributes. Project website: https://j-x-chen.github.io/Thermo-VLA-web/

llm.title_ja: Thermo-VLA：ロボットマニピュレーションのためのゲート残差変調を備えたサーマル対応視覚言語アクションモデル
llm.tldr_ja: サーマル画像を冷・温属性に分解し、言語条件付き残差変調を介してRGBトークンに統合する「Thermo-VLA」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のサーマル対応VLAモデルはサーマル画像を通常の視覚入力として扱っており、温度を考慮した推論のサポートが不十分である。
llm.method: ThermoResエンコーダによりサーマル画像を冷熱属性に分解し、言語条件付き残差変調でRGBトークンへ注入することで温度駆動型ターゲット選択を実現する。
llm.result: Unitree G1プラットフォーム上の4つのサーマル依存タスクで平均成功率0.86を達成し、ベースラインを18ポイント上回った。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語アクションモデル
ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.11981.tldr_en: Thermo-VLA with a ThermoRes Encoder is proposed, which decomposes thermal images into cold and hot attribute representations and injects them into the RGB token through language-conditioned residual modulation, enabling temperature-driven target selection and continuous manipulation and indicating its potential to generalise beyond thermal attributes.

2611.11978.title: CSG-Nav: Confidence-Aware Semantic-Geometric Fusion for Robust Exploration and Accurate Zero-Shot Object-Goal Navigation
2611.11978.abstract: Zero-shot object-goal navigation requires autonomous agents to explore unseen environments and locate target objects without task-specific training, posing challenges in perceptual reliability under observation uncertainty and physically grounded goal termination. Although foundation-model-based approaches improve generalization, they remain vulnerable to unreliable long-range perception, hallucination-induced directional bias, and semantically plausible but geometrically incorrect stopping decisions. To address these limitations, we propose CSG-Nav, a zero-shot navigation framework centered on confidence-aware multimodal information fusion. CSG-Nav integrates three complementary fusion mechanisms. First, semantic-source fusion integrates open-vocabulary detection results, detection confidence, scene observations, and relational reasoning to produce more reliable direction-level semantic scores and suppress hallucination-induced directional bias. Second, spatial-confidence fusion weights multi-view semantic evidence using a Gaussian decay function, suppressing unreliable distant observations while accumulating spatially consistent exploration preferences. Third, semantic-geometric decision fusion combines semantic target detection with depth-based 3D localization to support physically grounded stopping decisions. Experiments on HM3Dv1, HM3Dv2, and MP3D demonstrate competitive zero-shot performance, achieving success rates of 58.9%, 71.6%, and 44.3%. Fusion-level ablations and real-world deployments in indoor and outdoor environments further verify the effectiveness and practicality of CSG-Nav for robust navigation under uncertain perception. Code is available at https://xr-ui.github.io/CSGNav.github.io/

llm.title_ja: CSG-Nav：頑健な探索と正確なゼロショット物体目標ナビゲーションのための信頼度認識型意味・幾何学融合
llm.tldr_ja: 信頼度に基づくマルチモーダル情報融合を中心としたゼロショットナビゲーションフレームワーク「CSG-Nav」を提案する。
llm.problem: 基盤モデルベースの手法は汎化性能を向上させるが、信頼性の低い長距離知覚、ハルシネーションによる方向バイアス、誤った停止判断に対して脆弱である。
llm.method: 意味的ソース融合、空間的信頼度融合、意味的・幾何学的決定融合の3つの補完的融合メカニズムを統合する。
llm.result: HM3DおよびMP3Dデータセットのゼロショット評価において、優れた成功率を達成し、実環境での有効性を示した。
keywords_ja: ゼロショットナビゲーション
物体目標ナビゲーション

2611.11978.tldr_en: CSG-Nav is proposed, a zero-shot navigation framework centered on confidence-aware multimodal information fusion that demonstrates competitive zero-shot performance and the effectiveness and practicality of CSG-Nav for robust navigation under uncertain perception.

2611.11947.title: The Relative Value of Demonstration Data: Execution Time Limits and Operator Mixtures in Behavior Cloning
2611.11947.abstract: Robot demonstration datasets combine demonstrations from teleoperators of uneven experience, so collection teams need to know how many demonstrations from one group match those from another. We measure this with a data multiple: the ratio of the numbers of demonstrations two groups need for their policies to reach the same success rate. On robomimic's simulated Square and Can tasks, we train behavior-cloning policies on demonstrations from the two teleoperators robomimic labels Better and the two it labels Worse, varying dataset size and the share of Worse demonstrations. On Square, within robomimic's 25-second time limit, an all-Worse training set needs 1.55 times as many demonstrations as an all-Better set. Most of this difference is late completion: policies trained on Worse demonstrations finish later, as the Worse teleoperators do, and with a 100-second limit the multiple falls to 1.11. On Can, most of the difference remains at 100 seconds. If each Worse demonstration were worth 1/1.55 of a Better one, as in an all-Worse set, a half-Better, half-Worse set on Square would need 1.22 times as many demonstrations as an all-Better set. In fact, it needs 13% more than that, and this excess persists at every time limit from 20 to 200 seconds. The excess remains when training draws demonstrations uniformly instead of in proportion to their length. On Square, within the 25-second limit, switching to these Worse teleoperators is cheaper at equal success only if they earn less than a third of the Better teleoperators' hourly pay, because Worse demonstrations also take longer to record.

llm.title_ja: デモンストレーションデータの相対的価値：行動クローンにおける実行時間制限とオペレーターの混合
llm.tldr_ja: 異なる熟練度のテレオペレーターによるデモンストレーションデータが行動クローンの成功率に与える影響を、データ倍率を用いて測定する。
llm.problem: ロボットのデモンストレーションデータセットには異なる経験を持つオペレーターのデータが混在しており、グループ間でどの程度の量が必要かを知る必要がある。
llm.method: robomimicのシミュレーションタスクを用いて、「Better」と「Worse」とラベル付けされたオペレーターからのデモンストレーションサイズや割合を変化させて行動クローンを訓練する。
llm.result: Worseなデモンストレーションは時間制限内で完了が遅れるため多くの量を必要とし、時間制限の延長やデータ収集コストに応じた経済的影響を明らかにした。
keywords_ja: デモンストレーションデータ

2611.11947.tldr_en: This work measures the ratio of the numbers of demonstrations two groups need for their policies to reach the same success rate with a data multiple: the ratio of the numbers of demonstrations two groups need for their policies to reach the same success rate on robomimic's simulated Square and Can tasks.

2611.11941.title: Flip Anything with Agentic Robotics Self-Learning
2611.11941.abstract: Flipping is a fundamental robotic manipulation skill that requires reorienting a target object in a stable pose on a planar support surface by rotating it 180$^\circ$ about an axis parallel to the support surface -- think of flipping a coin from heads to tails. Although flipping is a common objective in industrial tasks such as parts inspection, mechanical assembly, and tool use, coding a bimanual robot with grippers to flip diverse objects is a significant challenge. In this paper, we show that a coding agent can autonomously develop and refine object-flipping strategies through iterative learning in physics simulations across diverse object geometries. Progressive skill acquisition, from basic handover to toppling and pushing, robust grasping and sensing, and thin-object manipulation with recovery, improves task success from 24.7% to 95.0%. The resulting graph-based code integrates high-level strategy selection with reactive control, enabling multi-stage flipping on physical robots.

llm.title_ja: エージェント型ロボットの自己学習による「何でもフリップ」
llm.tldr_ja: 物理シミュレーションにおける反復学習を通じて、多様なオブジェクト形状に対するフリップ戦略をコーディングエージェントが自律的に開発・洗練する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 把持を備えた二腕ロボットに多様なオブジェクトをフリップさせるためのプログラミングは大きな課題である。
llm.method: ハンドオーバー、トプル、プッシング、把持などの段階的なスキル獲得を行い、高レベルの戦略選択と反応的制御を統合したグラフベースのコードを生成する。
llm.result: タスクの成功率が24.7%から95.0%に向上し、実機ロボットでの多段階フリップを実現した。
keywords_ja: オブジェクトフリップ

2611.11941.tldr_en: It is shown that a coding agent can autonomously develop and refine object-flipping strategies through iterative learning in physics simulations across diverse object geometries, enabling multi-stage flipping on physical robots.

2611.11940.title: Reliability-Adaptive Multimodal Relative Pose Tracking for Underwater Leader-Follower Robots
2611.11940.abstract: Underwater leader-follower formation control requires continuous relative-pose estimation despite degraded sensing conditions and limited onboard computation. This paper presents a reliability-adaptive multimodal perception framework for six-degree-of-freedom relative-pose tracking between two moving underwater robots. The framework integrates complementary visual, acoustic-ranging, and hydrodynamic measurements while accounting for their distinct physical characteristics and time-varying reliability. It adaptively weights modality contributions and models temporal dependencies with linear computational complexity, enabling efficient pose estimation on embedded hardware. Extensive experiments were conducted using a custom-built AUV platform, with 648 pool trials spanning two leader vehicle types, three illumination conditions, and nine trajectory patterns. Evaluation yields an average translational error of 3.8 cm and an average orientation error of 2.4°. On an onboard NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, the fusion network achieves an inference latency of 17.62 ms, providing a 2.69-fold speedup over the evaluated Transformer-based fusion baseline. Closed-loop experiments further demonstrate stable formation maintenance with a moving leader under onboard computational constraints. A multimodal dataset containing measurements from all 648 trials will be made publicly available.

llm.title_ja: 水中リーダー・フォロワーロボットのための信頼度適応型マルチモーダル相対姿勢追跡
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚、音響測距、流体力学的測定の特性や時間変化する信頼度を考慮し、適応的に重み付けして統合する信頼度適応型マルチモーダル知覚フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 水中のリーダー・フォロワー型フォーメーション制御では、劣化したセンシング環境や限られたオンボード計算量の下でも継続的な相対姿勢推定が必要となる。
llm.method: 視覚、音響測距、流体力学的計測の信頼度を適応的に重み付けし、線形計算量で時間的依存性をモデル化する統合ネットワークを構成する。
llm.result: 648回のプール試験において平均平行誤差3.8 cm、平均配向誤差2.4°を達成し、Nvidia Jetson上で高速な推論と安定したフォーメーション維持を実現した。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2611.11934.title: Scale-Consistent Monocular Fisheye Visual Odometry via Spherical Bundle Adjustment-Guided Unsupervised Depth Learning
2611.11934.abstract: The wide field of view of fisheye cameras and the simplicity of a monocular setup make monocular fisheye visual odometry (VO) attractive for robotic localization and mapping. Nevertheless, scale drift remains a major challenge over long trajectories. Unsupervised depth learning can help to mitigate this issue, but the pronounced distortion of fisheye images poses challenges for accurate depth estimation. This article presents S$^2$D-FVO, a monocular fisheye VO framework integrating spherical bundle adjustment (SBA)-guided unsupervised depth learning to improve scale consistency and depth estimation accuracy. Given that pixel reprojection residuals do not uniformly reflect angular deviations between viewing rays and that the first-order linearization of a scalar angular reprojection residual is insensitive to perturbations along one tangent direction, SBA employs tangent-space angular reprojection residuals derived from the spherical logarithmic map. These residuals retain sensitivity along both tangent directions, with their norms equal to the corresponding scalar angular residuals. A median depth-based scale regularization term is further integrated into SBA to constrain the reconstruction scale. Building on these formulations, SBA replaces the pose estimation network during unsupervised depth learning, providing more reliable relative poses for view synthesis. In turn, depth estimates from the well-trained depth estimation network provide scale references for SBA, improving scale consistency while allowing individual 3-D landmark positions to be refined. Extensive experiments conducted on multiple public datasets, as well as two newly collected large-scale datasets, demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms representative existing approaches in both depth and trajectory estimation accuracy and is applicable to different camera models.

llm.title_ja: 球面バンドル調整誘導型の教師なし深度学習を用いたスケール一貫性のある単眼魚眼ビジュアルオドメトリ
llm.tldr_ja: 球面バンドル調整（SBA）誘導型の教師なし深度学習を統合した単眼魚眼VOフレームワークS^2D-FVOを提案し、スケール一貫性と深度推定精度を向上させた。
llm.problem: 単眼魚眼ビジュアルオドメトリにおける長距離軌道でのスケールドリフトと魚眼画像の大幅な歪みによる正確な深度推定の困難さ。
llm.method: 球面対数写像由来の接空間角度再投影残差を用いたSBAを教師なし深度学習の姿勢推定ネットワークの代わりに組み込み、中央値深度ベースのスケール正則化項を統合した。
llm.result: 複数の公開データセットおよび2つの新規大規模データセットでの実験により、提案手法が従来の代表的なアプローチを深度と軌道の精度で凌駕することを示した。
keywords_ja: ビジュアルオドメトリ

2611.11934.tldr_en: A monocular fisheye VO framework integrating spherical bundle adjustment (SBA)-guided unsupervised depth learning to improve scale consistency and depth estimation accuracy, which outperforms representative existing approaches in both depth and trajectory estimation accuracy.

2611.11921.title: An Evaluation of Tabular Foundation Models as Training-Free World Models
2611.11921.abstract: World models are widely considered to be a potential key component of model-based reinforcement learning and robot planning, but typically require task-specific training on substantial interaction data. We investigate whether a pretrained tabular foundation model (TabFM) can serve as a training-free dynamics model for world modeling by framing next-state prediction as in-context regression over transition pairs, and where such a model helps and where it breaks. Across synthetic dynamical systems and robot locomotion benchmarks, TabFM is more accurate than LSTM and MLP models trained from scratch on the same limited transitions in almost all settings, and among regressors fitted to the same data it is the most accurate on locomotion, while a Gaussian process is more accurate on smooth low-dimensional systems. However, models trained on the full dataset remain substantially better on most systems. When rolled out autoregressively over multiple steps, TabFM's accuracy depends strongly on how much context it is given. With a short context, its rollouts quickly degrade to the level of a trivial baseline, whereas with a long context they improve substantially and, on one locomotion task, exceed a trained LSTM. Inference is also about three orders of magnitude slower than an LSTM. Overall, in their current state, we find that training-free priors are useful as predictors when data are scarce and enough context is available, but they are not yet a substitute for trained world models in planning.

llm.title_ja: 訓練不要の世界モデルとしての表形式基盤モデルの評価
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みの表形式基盤モデル（TabFM）が訓練不要の動的システム・ロボット移動の動力学モデルとしてどのように機能するかを検証した。
llm.problem: 世界モデルの構築には通常、大量のインタラクションデータを用いたタスク固有の訓練が必要である点。
llm.method: 遷移ペアに対するコンテキスト内回帰として次状態予測を定式化し、事前学習済みTabFMを訓練不要の動的モデルとして評価した。
llm.result: データが少なで十分なコンテキストがある場合、TabFMは予測子として有用であるが、計画において訓練済み世界モデルの代わりにはまだならないことがわかった。
llm.limitation: 推論速度はLSTMの約3桁遅く、コンテキストが短いと性能が自明なベースラインレベルに劣化する。

2611.11921.tldr_en: Overall, in their current state, it is found that training-free priors are useful as predictors when data are scarce and enough context is available, but they are not yet a substitute for trained world models in planning.

2611.11894.title: Distilling Instructions into Weights: Closed-Form Edits Fix a Robot Policy's Misreading
2611.11894.abstract: Generalist robot policies often fail at one step of a task they can otherwise perform. We ask whether such a failure can be repaired by editing the policy's weights directly, without gradients, training data, or a change to the instruction. Told to put the cube then the banana in the bowl, a zero-shot $π_{0.5}$ vision-language-action policy in RoboLab releases the cube before it reaches the bowl. Replaying 21 of these decisions under rewordings shows that it binds "in the bowl" to the wrong object. Closed-form instruction distillation copies the per-layer effect of an explicit rewording into the language model's MLP weights. On 128 held-out seeds, success rises from 27 to 106 episodes, with 81 fixed and 2 broken ($p=7\times10^{-22}$), while an update of the same size in random directions leaves success unchanged. The edit also lifts two other tasks without detectable harm on the remaining 13, and a variant that stores 0.16% of the parameter count keeps most of its effect. Placed in the action expert or action head instead, the same distillation helps less or not at all. Our released tool reproduced the fix end to end on new held-out seeds, from 8/64 to 36/64. Edits aimed at perception, a missing grasp, contact physics, or the gripper threshold did not help, and of seven blind Claude Opus editors, only the one given the misread instruction produced an edit that passed held-out scoring. These results suggest that weight edits work best when a known-good input already exists to distil. Because reruns with unchanged weights flip about a third of paired outcomes, evaluations should pair seeds, rerun the unedited policy, and confirm gains on held-out seeds.
2611.11894.comment: 23 pages, 7 figures. Project page with videos: https://ali-adeeb.com/weightsmith/ ; code and benchmark: https://github.com/adeeb10abbas/weightsmith

llm.title_ja: 指示の重みへの蒸留：閉形式の編集によるロボットポリシーの誤読の修正
llm.tldr_ja: 勾配や訓練データを使わず、閉形式の指示蒸留を用いてポリシーのMLP重みを直接編集することで、汎用ロボットポリシーの誤読を修正できることを示した。
llm.problem: 汎用ロボットポリシーが、実行可能なタスクの一部において指示の解釈を誤り失敗すること。
llm.method: 明示的な言い換えの層ごとの効果を言語モデルのMLP重みにコピーする閉形式の指示蒸留を用いた。
llm.result: 128個の保持シードにおいて成功率が27から106エピソードへと向上し、他のタスクも損なわずに改善された。
llm.limitation: 知覚、把持の欠落、接触物理、グリッパーの閾値を対象とした編集は効果がなかった。

2611.11894.tldr_en: Results suggest that weight edits work best when a known-good input already exists to distil, and because reruns with unchanged weights flip about a third of paired outcomes, evaluations should pair seeds, rerun the unedited policy, and confirm gains on held-out seeds.

2611.11887.title: How Many Candidates Does a One-Step World Model Need? A Random-Codebook Account of Nearest-of-m Training on Frozen DINO Tokens
2611.11887.abstract: One-step stochastic world models avoid the mode averaging of deterministic feature predictors without the tens of network evaluations per step that diffusion and flow matching require. The simplest such objective is nearest-of-m matching (conditional implicit maximum likelihood estimation, IMLE): draw m candidate futures and pull only the one closest to the observed outcome. Recent work conjectures that a small m suffices for feature-space world models and that a strictly proper energy score should replace the hard minimum. We test both claims with one-step world models on frozen DINOv2/v3 patch tokens, using benchmarks whose futures can be enumerated. Under mode-like uncertainty, nearest-of-m with m=16 covers the enumerated futures better than 50-step flow matching (at about 1/30 of its latency), one-step flow generators and an energy-score generator at matched parameter counts, and its rollouts stay on the token manifold where flow rollouts drift. One quantity governs the choice of m: the nearest-of-m objective is the expected distortion of a random codebook of m draws from the generator. This view yields three predictions, recorded before the corresponding runs: (i) memorization of the realized outcome in contexts that never repeat, whose strength is governed by the codebook's miss distortion I(m) rather than its miss probability, and which an energy-score generator does not escape by raising m; (ii) a flattening of mode probabilities with m, matching a known optimum within 0.01; and (iii) under-dispersion on continuous high-dimensional outcomes, which bounds the method on real robot video. Per-step matching on self-rollouts cuts long-horizon error by a third on a stochastic Push-T variant; an ablation separates its manifold and coverage benefits. Planning success does not improve despite accurate risk estimates, a negative result we report with its diagnosis.
2611.11887.comment: 30 pages (12-page main text, appendices A-H). Code: https://github.com/thddydgnl/nearest-of-m-world-models

llm.title_ja: 1ステップ世界モデルに必要な候補数はいくつ手か：凍結DINOトークンに対するNearest-of-m訓練のランダムコードブック説明
llm.tldr_ja: m=16を用いたnearest-of-m（条件付き暗黙的最尤推定）による1ステップ確率的世界モデルが、多様な不確実性下で50ステップのフローマッチングよりも優れた将来予測と高速性を実現することを示した。
llm.problem: 決定論的特徴量予測のモード平均化や、拡散・フローマッチングが持つステップごとの多大なネットワーク評価の必要性。
llm.method: 凍結されたDINOv2/v3パッチトークン上で、観測結果に最も近い1つの候補のみを引き上げるnearest-of-mマッチングを用いた1ステップ世界モデルを構築した。
llm.result: m=16のnearest-of-mは、50ステップのフローマッチングの約1/30のレイテンシで列挙された未来をよりよくカバーし、軌道がトークン多様体上に留まった。
llm.limitation: 連続的な高次元の出力に対する過小分散が、実ロボット映像への適用を制限する。

2611.11887.tldr_en: Under mode-like uncertainty, nearest-of-m with m=16 covers the enumerated futures better than 50-step flow matching, one-step flow generators and an energy-score generator at matched parameter counts, and its rollouts stay on the token manifold where flow rollouts drift.

2611.11885.title: Design of a hybrid tendon-linkage finger with coupled and adaptive motion
2611.11885.abstract: Dexterous robotic fingers require coordinated joint motion and adaptability to object contact, while independently actuating multiple joints increases the complexity of the transmission mechanism. This paper presents a hybrid tendon--linkage robotic finger with four mechanical degrees of freedom driven by three actuators. The MCP abduction/adduction joint is driven through a bevel gear, while MCP and PIP flexion/extension are driven by separate bidirectional tendon transmissions. The DIP joint is not independently actuated but is coupled to the PIP joint through a four-bar linkage with a torsional spring and mechanical stopper. The tendon routing also introduces mechanical coupling between the MCP and PIP joints. Kinematic analysis was conducted to describe the coupled and adaptive motions, and experiments were performed to evaluate the joint motion characteristics. ArUco-based measurements showed that the coupled motion closely matched the theoretical prediction, whereas the adaptive motion was partially limited by interference between linkage components. The fabricated finger demonstrated different contact postures with cylindrical, cuboid, and irregularly shaped objects, and the mean peak fingertip force was 4.56 N. The proposed mechanism provides both coupled motion and contact-dependent adaptation without requiring an additional actuator for the DIP joint.
2611.11885.comment: This manuscript has been submitted for possible publication

llm.title_ja: 連動動作と適応動作を備えたハイブリッド腱リンク指の設計
llm.tldr_ja: 3つのアクチュエータで駆動する4つの自由度を持つハイブリッド腱リンク式ロボットハンドの指を設計し、連動動作と接触に応じた適応動作の双方を実現した。
llm.problem: 器用なロボット指において、関節の協調動作と物体の接触に対する適応性を求めると、複数の関節を独立駆動させる伝達機構が複雑化する点。
llm.method: 傘歯車によるMCP外転・内転、双方向の腱伝達によるMCP・PIP屈曲・伸展、およびトーションスプリングとメカニカルストッパーを持つ4節リンクによるDIPの連動を組み合わせたハイブリッド機構を開発した。
llm.result: ArUcoベースの測定により、連動動作が理論予測と一致し、円筒や直方体などの様々な形状の物体に対して異なる接触姿勢を示し、平均ピーク指先力が4.56 Nであることが確認された。
llm.limitation: 適応動作はリンク部品間の干渉によって部分的に制限された。

2611.11869.title: Action Representation for Spatial Generalization in Robot World Models
2611.11869.abstract: Spatial generalization in robot world models depends on whether action representations capture the physical relationships that remain valid across changing spatial configurations. Yet different coordinates can describe the same interaction, whereas similar motions can produce different outcomes when local physical conditions change. How these distinctions affect learned prediction remains insufficiently understood. This study evaluates matched action representations defined in world, object, and surface coordinate frames using a controlled robotic peeling benchmark. Global pose and contact relocation experiments reveal a cost associated with limited training data when equivalent interactions receive different spatial descriptions. Removing information about peel thickness creates an irreducible ambiguity because identical predictive inputs can correspond to different material removal outcomes. Coordinates defined relative to the surface improve consequence prediction and counterfactual action selection under accurate local observations, but learned predictors remain vulnerable to uncertainty in the coordinate frame. Joint centering of the surface and tool removes sensitivity to translation of their common origin, whereas incorrect contact geometry and actual execution deviations introduce different failure mechanisms. These results show that effective spatial generalization depends on preserving the relationships between actions and states that determine physical consequences, rather than simply minimizing coordinate variation. This perspective provides a principled basis for designing robot world models that reuse physical knowledge across spatial configurations while retaining the distinctions essential to prediction and planning.

llm.title_ja: ロボット世界モデルにおける空間的汎化のための行動表現
llm.tldr_ja: 空間的汎化には座標変化を最小化することではなく、物理的結果を決定する行動と状態の関係を維持することが重要であることを示した。
llm.problem: 空間配置の変化に応じて有効な物理関係を捉える行動表現の違いが、学習された予測にどのように影響するか十分に理解されていない点。
llm.method: ワールド、オブジェクト、表面の各座標系で定義された一致する行動表現を用いて、制御されたロボットピーリングベンチマークによる評価を行った。
llm.result: 表面に対して定義された座標系は結果の予測と反実仮想的行動選択を改善するが、座標系の不確実性に対して脆弱であることが示された。
llm.limitation: 学習された予測器は座標系の不確実性に依然として脆弱である。

2611.11869.tldr_en: This study evaluates matched action representations defined in world, object, and surface coordinate frames using a controlled robotic peeling benchmark to show that effective spatial generalization depends on preserving the relationships between actions and states that determine physical consequences, rather than simply minimizing coordinate variation.

2611.11868.title: Fade to... Red? Scheduling Coloured Noise Exploration Supports Efficient Robot Learning with Reduced Movement Jerk
2611.11868.abstract: Exploration in deep reinforcement learning (RL) for continuous control is commonly driven by temporally uncorrelated Gaussian (white) action noise, which leads to jerky motions with locally constrained exploration. In contrast, temporally correlated coloured noise, particularly pink noise, has been shown to support more efficient exploration in RL. Motivated by these findings, we inquire whether scheduling changes to the noise colour over the course of training can outperform white noise for continuous control robotics. We perform a systematic study of 49 linear schedules between white and red noise, together with generalised state-dependent exploration (gSDE), on four sparse-reward manipulation tasks with a Fetch arm and a Shadow Dexterous Hand. We find that the noise colour at the end of training does not affect learning efficiency or end performance, whereas fading towards red noise halves the jerk of exploration in every task. Balancing learning efficiency, end performance and smoothness, red noise emerges as the preferred strategy: it learns as efficiently as pink noise with almost 2-fold less movement jerk. We therefore recommend exploration schedulers that fade towards red noise as the default for off-policy robot learning.
2611.11868.comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Accepted at the ACRA 2026 conference. Cite as: "López, F. M., and Cruz, F. (2026). Fade to... Red? Scheduling Coloured Noise Exploration Supports Efficient Robot Learning with Reduced Movement Jerk. In Proceedings of the Australasian Conference on Robotics and Automation (ACRA). Australian Robotics and Automation Association (ARAA)."

llm.title_ja: 赤色へフェード？着色ノイズ探索のスケジューリングによる、動作ジャークを低減した効率的なロボット学習の支援
llm.tldr_ja: 連続制御の深層強化学習において、赤色ノイズに向かって徐々に変化させるノイズ探索スケジュールを導入し、学習効率を維持しながら移動のジャークを半減させた。
llm.problem: 連続制御における深層強化学習の探索は白色ノイズに依存することが多く、ローカルに制約された探索とジャークの多い動作を引き起こす点。
llm.method: 白色ノイズから赤色ノイズへの49種類の線形スケジュールと一般化状態依存探索（gSDE）を、4つのスパース報酬マニピュレーションタスクで体系的に評価した。
llm.result: 赤色ノイズへフェードする戦略は、ピンクノイズと同等の学習効率を維持しつつ、移動ジャークをほぼ2分の1に減少させることを示した。

2611.11868.tldr_en: Red noise emerges as the preferred strategy for exploration in deep reinforcement learning: it learns as efficiently as pink noise with almost 2-fold less movement jerk and is recommended as the default for off-policy robot learning.

2611.11856.title: DeltaForge: A Post-hoc Mixture-of-Experts VLA for Multi-Domain Autonomous Driving
2611.11856.abstract: Fleets of driving vision-language-action (VLA) models are developed one domain at a time: each operator finetunes a shared base model on private data, producing specialized experts that are costly to consolidate into a single model. Weight merging loses accuracy as heterogeneous domains accumulate, and dense mixture-of-experts routing is prohibitively expensive to combine them. We present DeltaForge, to our knowledge the first post-hoc mixture-of-experts VLA for driving, which consolidates N independently finetuned per-domain models into a single multi-domain model from their weights and a small proxy set alone. When different operators finetune the same base model, their weight updates end up sharing a lot of structure. We exploit this by decomposing all the updates together using singular value decomposition (SVD), splitting each one into a shared part (the same across all domains) and a tiny domain-specific part. The router then only needs to work with those tiny domain-specific pieces, not the full expert weights, which is what keeps the approach efficient. Then two cooperating clip-level blind routers, one over the VLM reasoning experts and one over the flow-matching dynamics experts, are trained from soft labels on the proxy dataset. Across six diverse domains spanning urban, off-road, and highway driving on cars, trucks, and all-terrain vehicles (ATVs), DeltaForge approaches the accuracy of the per-domain experts and surpasses every merging, routing, centralized, and federated baseline at close to single-model parameter and compute cost. Adding a new domain requires only projecting its weight update onto the shared basis with no end-to-end retraining needed. The resulting model also generalizes to domain combinations it was never explicitly trained on.

llm.title_ja: DeltaForge：マルチドメイン自動運転のための事後混合専門家VLA
llm.tldr_ja: 特化型ドメインモデルの重みを特異値分解により分解・共有化し、軽量なプロキシデータセットでルーターを訓練することで、複数の独立した専門家モデルを単一のマルチドメインVLAモデルに統合するDeltaForgeを提案した。
llm.problem: 自動運転向けVLAモデルのドメインごとの微調整による特化モデル乱立と、それらを統合する際の手法における重み統合の精度低下や高コストな密な混合専門家（MoE）ルーティング。
llm.method: 複数のドメイン固有モデルの重み更新を特異値分解（SVD）で分解して共通ベースと小さなドメイン固有部分に分け、ソフトラベル付きプロキシデータセットで2つの協調型クリップレベル盲目ルーターを訓練した。
llm.result: 都市、オフロード、高速道路を含む6つの多様なドメインにおいて、ドメイン特化型専門家の精度に迫り、従来のあらゆる統合・ルーティングベースラインを凌駕した。

2611.11856.tldr_en: DeltaForge is presented, to the authors' knowledge the first post-hoc mixture-of-experts VLA for driving, which consolidates N independently finetuned per-domain models into a single multi-domain model from their weights and a small proxy set alone.

2611.11854.title: Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids (DASH): Latency-Agnostic Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models for Humanoid Manipulation
2611.11854.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models pair a vision-language backbone with an action head, but in closed-loop control the backbone sits on the control-critical path: while it computes, the robot keeps moving, so each executed action is conditioned on an increasingly stale observation. A larger backbone therefore directly blocks reactivity, especially in humanoid dexterous manipulation. We present DASH, a Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids that removes this coupling. DASH splits the policy into a slow vision-language model (System 2) and a fast flow-matching action head (System 1) that run as concurrent processes over the LCM communication protocol, so the control rate is set by the action head alone, independent of backbone size. The action head fuses stale semantics from a frozen backbone with fresh vision from its own ResNet encoder, desynchronized training exposes it to the staleness it meets at deployment, and an adaptive temporal aggregator aligns overlapping action chunks under variable inference latency. On an asynchronous RoboTwin benchmark that charges inference latency in simulated time, DASH holds 20 Hz control rate from 0.8B to 8B backbones while the synchronous rate falls from 9.7 to 4.1 Hz, with higher success at every size. On a real humanoid with dexterous hands, DASH achieves clearly higher pick-and-place success than the synchronous pipeline.

llm.title_ja: ヒューノイド用非同期分離システム（DASH）：ヒューノイドマニピュレーションに向けたVLAモデルの遅延非依存型スケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: VLAモデルの視覚言語バックボーンと行動ヘッドを非同期で実行するシステム（DASH）を提案し、バックボーンサイズに依存せず高い制御周波数と把持成功率を実現した。
llm.problem: 閉ループ制御において大規模な視覚言語バックボーンの計算遅延が制御クリップパスをブロックし、ロボットの反応性を低下させる点。
llm.method: ポリシーを低速なVLM（システム2）と高速なフローマッチング行動ヘッド（システム1）に分離し、非同期のプロセスとして通信プロトコル経由で実行することで、行動ヘッド単独で制御レートを維持する。
llm.result: シミュレーション上のRoboTwinベンチマークおよび実機のヒューノイドハンドにおいて、同期型パイプラインと比較して高い制御レート（20 Hz）と優れたピック＆プレース成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ヒューノイドロボット

2611.11854.tldr_en: DASH is presented, a Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids that removes this coupling between vision-language-action backbone and action head, and achieves clearly higher pick-and-place success than the synchronous pipeline.

2611.11842.title: A Benchmark and Layered Evaluation Protocol for Evidence-Grounded Shared Belief Updating in Connected Robotics
2611.11842.abstract: Connected physical systems fuse observations from robots, IoT sensors, and edge-AI modules into a shared account of the world, yet most evaluations score only the final answer or action and cannot tell whether a method attributed the evidence, updated its belief, handled contradictions, and justified its decision. We argue that shared reasoning in Connected Robotics should be evaluated as an evidence-to-belief trajectory, and introduce the Connected Robotics Evidence Graph (CREG) Benchmark to make that trajectory measurable. CREG comprises 350 deterministically generated scenarios across seven regimes (justified revision, belief preservation, relation association, contradiction onset and resolution, stale/delayed evidence, and source reliability), each exposing a normative posterior reference at every evidence prefix, validated by an independent log-odds checker and screened by a blinded expert audit. Nine representation conditions separate relation content from serialization, ordering, and metadata. Evaluating four open-weight instruction models and six transparent fusion baselines yields three findings. First, entity grounding accounts for a substantial part of the weak-model deficit. Second, deleting semantic relations costs 15.3 points of strict belief-state accuracy on relation-dependent scenarios (Holm-corrected p<0.001), but an information-matched structured list outperforms the full graph and shuffling the graph does not hurt: relation content matters where required, while graph serialization confers no consistent advantage. Third, belief accuracy is strongly non-monotonic along the evidence sequence, with mid-trajectory failures that endpoint-only evaluation cannot detect. All scenarios, references, prompts, metrics, and analysis code are released for offline, hardware-free reproduction.
2611.11842.comment: 15 pages (10 main + 5 supplementary), 6 figures, 4 tables; supplement adds 1 figure and 7 tables. Project page: https://creg-bench.github.io

llm.title_ja: 接続されたロボティクスにおける証拠に基づく共有信念更新のためのベンチマークと階層型評価プロトコル
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットやIoTセンサーからの観測に基づく共有推論を評価するための証拠から信念への軌道ベンチマーク（CREG）を提案し、表現条件ごとの性能差を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 接続された物理システムにおいて、従来の評価は最終的な回答や行動のみをスコア化し、証拠の帰属や信念の更新、矛盾の処理を評価できない点。
llm.method: 7つのレジームにわたる350のシナリオからなる接続ロボティクスエビデンスグラフ（CREG）ベンチマークを構築し、オープンウェイトモデルおよび融合ベースラインを評価した。
llm.result: 実体接地がモデルの弱さの主な原因であり、信念の精度は証拠のシーケンスに沿って強く非単調になることを示した。

2611.11842.tldr_en: It is argued that shared reasoning in Connected Robotics should be evaluated as an evidence-to-belief trajectory, and the Connected Robotics Evidence Graph (CREG) Benchmark is introduced to make that trajectory measurable.

2611.11830.title: ROS2MR: Connecting ROS 2 Motion Planning to Mixed-Reality Trajectory Visualization
2611.11830.abstract: Mixed reality (MR) allows users to inspect planned robot motion within their physical surroundings, but displaying trajectories from robotics software requires converting their joint configurations and timing into a format the MR application can play back. This paper presents ROS2MR, an extension of the MR-Robotics LAB platform that converts YAML-serialized ROS 2 joint trajectories, including MoveIt motion plans, into the platform's existing JSON playback format. The converter validates the input, maps arm joints by name, and resamples the trajectory at a nominal rate of 30 Hz, using cubic Hermite interpolation when joint velocities are supplied and linear interpolation otherwise, while binary gripper commands are sampled separately using a zero-order hold. A Python export helper combines sequences of motion plans and gripper states into a single trajectory and checks positional agreement at segment boundaries. The MR application was also adapted for Apple Vision Pro in addition to Meta Quest 3. A technical evaluation showed that the converter preserved the normalized duration and endpoint configurations for dense, sparse, and irregularly timed inputs. With supplied velocities, the position RMSE was approximately 2.91x10^-5 degrees for all sampling patterns; without them, sparse input increased it to 0.85 degrees, and close positional agreement did not guarantee accurate velocity profiles. A pick-and-place sequence retained its open--closed--open gripper order, although off-grid transitions were shifted to the output sampling grid. The resulting file-based pathway enables inspection of ROS-generated trajectories in MR without a live ROS connection.

llm.title_ja: ROS2MR：ROS 2のモーションプランニングと混合現実感軌道ビジュアライゼーションの接続
llm.tldr_ja: ROS 2のジョイント軌道を混合現実（MR）アプリケーションの再生形式に変換するツール「ROS2MR」を提案し、ライブROS接続なしでの軌道検査を可能にした。
llm.problem: 計画されたロボット動作を物理環境内でMRを用いて検査する際、ロボットソフトウェアの軌道形式をMRアプリの再生用に変換する必要がある点。
llm.method: YAMLシリアライズされたROS 2ジョイント軌道をJSON形式に変換し、キュービックエルミート補間や線形補間を用いて30 Hzで再サンプリングするPythonエクスポートヘルパーを開発した。
llm.result: 入力の正規化されたデュレーションとエンドポイント設定を維持し、指定された速度情報により低い位置RMSEを達成して、オープン・クローズのグリッパー順序を保持した。
llm.limitation: 近接する位置の一致が正確な速度プロファイルを保証するわけではなく、オフグリッド遷移が出力グリッドにシフトする。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2611.11830.tldr_en: ROS2MR is presented, an extension of the MR-Robotics LAB platform that converts YAML-serialized ROS 2 joint trajectories, including MoveIt motion plans, into the platform's existing JSON playback format, and enables inspection of ROS-generated trajectories in MR without a live ROS connection.

2611.11815.title: Generalizable Output Feedback Optimal Control via Transformers Without Explicit State Estimation
2611.11815.abstract: Classical optimal control is used to design a separate controller for each plant. This paper asks a different question. Can one learned policy serve a whole family of partially observed, noisy linear systems? We show that one transformer can. The policy is trained to imitate optimal LQG control on a heterogeneous family of Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems with Multiple Inputs and Multiple Outputs (MIMO), whose dimensions, cost matrices, and noise levels all vary. A shared representation with system-wise standardization, zero-padding, masking, and an encoding of the cost and noise covariances lets one set of weights control every member of the family. At run time, a short window of noisy measurements is all the policy needs to produce a control action, with no plant matrices and no state estimator. We characterize the relation between the optimal LQG policy (represented as a dynamic state-space model) and a static transformer acting on a finite window of measurements. We then express the closed-loop excess cost of any causal policy as the energy of its deviation from the optimal action. Finally, we evaluate the approach on 28 simulated systems. The trained policy reaches the optimal cost to within a median gap of $0.4\%$ for seen systems. For unseen systems, a light fine-tuning step brings the median gap to $1.0\%$.

llm.title_ja: 明示的な状態推定なしのTransformerを用いた一般化出力フィードバック最適制御
llm.tldr_ja: 部分観測される多様な線形システムファミリー全体に対して、明示的な状態推定器なしで単一のTransformerポリシーを用いて最適に近い制御を達成した。
llm.problem: 古典的最適制御ではプラントごとに個別コントローラーの設計が必要である点。
llm.method: 多様な入出力を持つLTIシステムのファミリにおける最適LQG制御の模倣学習を通じて、システム間の標準化やゼロパディング、コスト・ノイズ共分散のエンコーディングを導入したTransformerを訓練した。
llm.result: 学習済みポリシーは、既知のシステムに対して中央値で0.4%、未知のシステムに対しても軽量な微調整により1.0%のギャップ内で最適コストを達成した。

2611.11815.tldr_en: The relation between the optimal LQG policy (represented as a dynamic state-space model) and a static transformer acting on a finite window of measurements are characterized and the closed-loop excess cost of any causal policy is expressed as the energy of its deviation from the optimal action.

2611.11809.title: Budget-aware Correspondence-driven View Selection for Real-time 3D Perception of Mobile Robots
2611.11809.abstract: 3D visual perception and scene reconstruction are critical for autonomous robots and intelligent transportation, yet real-world deployments often generate long, redundant image sequences that hinder downstream processing. This report investigates BCVS (budget-aware correspondence-driven view sampling), a pose-free view selection algorithm that offers 22+ FPS on a CPU, enabling online filtering for efficient 3D perception by mobile robots. Unlike existing approaches that rely on full structure-from-motion (SfM) pipelines or camera pose estimation, BCVS employs a purely correspondence-based scoring strategy that prioritizes view novelty while maintaining sufficient overlap for geometric stability. Given a user-specified budget, BCVS iteratively selects the most distinct frames and suppresses near-duplicates, producing compact subsets that preserve connectivity and minimize reconstruction loss. Extensive experiments on benchmark show that BCVS outperforms CPU-friendly baselines at tight budgets and remains competitive as budgets scale. Field trials with large aerial and marine robotics data further validate its practicality and scalability: BCVS reduces redundancy up to 16% while sustaining robust SfM registration and high-quality 3D reconstructions.

llm.title_ja: モバイルロボットのリアルタイム3D知覚に向けた予算考慮型・対応駆動型ビュー選択
llm.tldr_ja: 姿勢推定を必要とせずCPU上で22 FPS以上で動作する、冗長な画像シーケンスを削減する予算考慮型のビュー選択アルゴリズム（BCVS）を提案した。
llm.problem: 自動運転やモバイルロボットのリアルタイム3D知覚において、実世界展開で生成される長くて冗長な画像シーケンスが後続処理を阻害する点。
llm.method: 完全なStructure-from-Motion（SfM）やカメラ姿勢推定に依存せず、幾何学的安定性のためのオーバーラップを維持しながら新規性を優先する、対応ベースのスコアリング戦略を採用した。
llm.result: ベンチマーク実験および大規模な空海ロボットのフィールド試行において、SfM登録と高品質な3D再構築を維持しつつ最大16%の冗長性を削減した。

2611.11809.tldr_en: This report investigates BCVS (budget-aware correspondence-driven view sampling), a pose-free view selection algorithm that offers 22+ FPS on a CPU, enabling online filtering for efficient 3D perception by mobile robots.

2611.11798.title: PAIR: Proprioception-Aligned Image-Ray Representations for Viewpoint-Robust Manipulation
2611.11798.abstract: While imitation learning has made substantial progress toward generalizable robot manipulation through scaling, viewpoint robustness remains a major bottleneck. Visuomotor policies rely heavily on visual inputs, yet images provide an inherently ambiguous signal under viewpoint change: similar scenes may appear markedly different across viewpoints, while distinct states may share certain visual overlaps. A policy must therefore infer not only the task-relevant state, but also how it is visually projected under a particular camera configuration. This entanglement of viewpoint-dependent appearance and task-relevant state can make learning inefficient and limit generalization to unseen viewpoints. Recent work has begun to address this challenge through camera-ray conditioning and representation learning using geometric cues to induce invariance. However, providing camera information as additional context does not by itself ground visual representations in how the task scene is visually projected, while geometric alignment without camera context can introduce spurious correspondences by ignoring viewpoint-dependent projection. We propose PAIR, a contrastive learning framework that aligns joint image-ray representations using robot proprioception. PAIR encourages observations with similar robot states to remain close in representation space across viewpoints, providing a structured grounding signal for learning viewpoint-robust features. PAIR is a highly adaptable framework: it can be used to train Diffusion Policy (DP) or post-train vision-language-action (VLA) models. In simulated and real-world manipulation benchmarks with camera variation, PAIR consistently outperforms the behavior cloning baseline without ray conditioning by 12.7% and 26.7% points, respectively, demonstrating stronger generalization to unseen viewpoints. Project website: PAIRrobot.github.io.

llm.title_ja: PAIR：視点ロバストなマニピュレーションのためのプロプリオセプション整合画像レイ表現
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットの固有受容感覚を用いて視点間での画像レイ表現を整合させる対照学習フレームワークPAIRを提案し、視点変化に対するマニピュレーションのロバスト性を向上させた。
llm.problem: 模倣学習における視点変動に対するロバスト性の欠如と、視点依存の外見とタスク関連状態の絡み合いによる学習効率の低下。
llm.method: ロボットの状態が類似する観測を視点間で表現空間において近づけるよう促す、プロプリオセプションを用いた対照学習フレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界のマニピュレーションベンチマークにおいて、レイ条件付けを行わない行動クローンベースラインをそれぞれ12.7%および26.7%上回る成功率を達成した。

2611.11798.tldr_en: PAIR is a contrastive learning framework that aligns joint image-ray representations using robot proprioception, providing a structured grounding signal for learning viewpoint-robust features and can be used to train Diffusion Policy or post-train vision-language-action models.

2611.11789.title: HolidayFactory 1.0: Simulating, Generating, and Evaluating Industrial Robot Tasks
2611.11789.abstract: Robots are typically evaluated in episodes that begin from a reset, while industrial work consists of repeated jobs whose outcomes affect subsequent operations. Evaluating such work at scale requires simulation of task-critical physical interactions, construction of industrial environments, and measurements of performance as scene state persists. We present HOLIDAYFACTORY 1.0, a framework for simulating, generating, and evaluating industrial robot work. Given a human-specified workplace and task, the framework defines a world pairing a scenario of scene variants and process logic with an evaluation defining a job, metrics, and a rubric. HOLIDAYFACTORY 1.0 comprises three components. HOLIDAY-SIM extends Newton's SDF-based hydroelastic contact with additional constitutive laws and a semi-implicit primal-dual solver, couples stateful actuator dynamics to articulated motion, and derives tactile and joint observations from simulated states. Agentic world construction generates simulation-ready assets and scene variants using geometric and interaction checks, and proposes task-conditioned evaluations for human confirmation and executable checks. 24/7-BENCH introduces seven industrial tasks in which jobs are evaluated without resetting the scene, measuring completed, failed, and unfinished jobs, throughput, latency, and motor energy. Controlled studies characterize the proposed contact, actuator, and tactile models and examine the effectiveness of verification-guided world construction. Experiments on scene and evaluation generation further reveal the limitations of model critics and the difficulty of ensuring that generated evaluations faithfully capture task requirements. We examine job-level evaluations with scripted trajectories (e.g., code-as-policy) but have not yet compared policies over persistent runs.

llm.title_ja: HolidayFactory 1.0：産業用ロボットタスクのシミュレーション、生成、および評価
llm.tldr_ja: 産業用ロボットの作業をシミュレート、生成、評価するための統合フレームワークHOLIDAYFACTORY 1.0を提案した。
llm.problem: ロボットが通常初期状態からのリセットを前提としたエピソードで評価される一方、実際の産業作業は結果が後続の操作に影響を与える継続的なジョブである点。
llm.method: SDFベースのハイドロ弾性接触、状態依存のアクチュエータダイナミクス、エージェントによるワールド構築、およびシーン状態をリセットせずに評価する7つの産業用タスクベンチマーク（24/7-BENCH）を実装した。
llm.result: 接触・アクチュエータ・触覚モデルの特性を評価し、シーンおよび評価生成におけるモデル批判の限界と課題を明らかにした。
llm.limitation: ジョブレベルの評価においてスクリプト化された軌道を用いた検証を行っているが、完全な網羅には至っていない。

2611.11789.tldr_en: 24/7-BENCH introduces seven industrial tasks in which jobs are evaluated without resetting the scene, measuring completed, failed, and unfinished jobs, throughput, latency, and motor energy.

2611.11780.title: Planners Exploit Deterministic Error: Dithered Low-Bit World Models
2611.11780.abstract: Sampling-based planners such as MPPI and CEM query a learned world model thousands of times per control step, so low-bit world models are an obvious way to make model-based control cheaper on a robot. With round-to-nearest activation quantization and no calibration, we find that planning can collapse, by up to 100 points of success, while the world model's latent one-step prediction error stays no larger than that of a stochastic rounding scheme that plans well. At the same bit width, what decides the outcome is not the size of the rounding error but whether it persists across planner iterations and is shared across candidates. Round-to-nearest leaves an error that persists, and an iterating planner drifts toward the candidates that this error favors; in TD-MPC2, holding the same dither fixed within a step or an episode brings the drift back. Dither shared by all candidates and redrawn at every iteration removes most of the damage at the same bit width and without training: at least half of it in all 19 affected Meta-World cells (task $\times$ bit width) of TD-MPC2 (median 95%), in 4 of 5 DINO-WM cells, and in all 8 affected tasks of a 317M-parameter multi-task TD-MPC2. Captured as CUDA graphs on an Ampere GPU, a W8A4 integer TD-MPC2 world model runs its planning rollouts 1.9-3.3$\times$ and the whole planning step 1.3-1.5$\times$ faster than FP32, though not faster than BF16 with pre-converted weights; shared dither adds at most 2.3% latency. In TD-MPC2, block-scaled NVFP4 removes most of the damage and MXFP4 part of it, which ties the failure to coarse grids with a shared scale. Hypotheses, thresholds and analysis code were fixed before the data that test them, and the hypotheses that failed are reported.

llm.title_ja: プランナーは決定論的誤差を利用する：ディザ付き低ビット世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 低ビット世界モデルにおけるプランニングの崩壊の原因が丸め誤差の大きさにではなく誤差の持続性にあり、候補間で共有されるディザを用いることでトレーニングなしで回避できることを示した。
llm.problem: ロボットのモデルベース制御において計算コスト削減のために低ビット世界モデルを用いると、丸め誤差によりプランニングが破綻する点。
llm.method: 丸め・量子化時に、すべての候補で共有されイテレーションごとに再描画されるディザ（確率的丸めのようなランダム性）を導入した。
llm.result: TD-MPC2の19のタスクセルや他のモデルにおいて、トレーニングなしで丸め誤差によるプランニングの破綻を防ぎ、W8A4整数モデルでFP32に対して1.3〜3.3倍の高速化を達成した。

2611.11780.tldr_en: With round-to-nearest activation quantization and no calibration, it is found that planning can collapse, by up to 100 points of success, while the world model's latent one-step prediction error stays no larger than that of a stochastic rounding scheme that plans well.

2611.11755.title: Graph-Sparse Distributed Predictive Control for Multi-Robot Motion Planning vianEdge-Consensus ADMM
2611.11755.abstract: This paper presents a distributed model predictive control (MPC) architecture for collision-avoiding motion planning of planar robots with double-integrator dynamics. To reduce coordination demands, a time-varying predicted conflict graph selects relevant pairwise interactions. The associated collision-avoidance constraints are convexified once per MPC update using warm-start trajectories, yielding a fixed convex quadratic program (QP). The resulting QP is then decomposed using an edge-consensus formulation of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), enabling parallel robot-local optimization and independent closed-form projections onto separating half-spaces. Execution is selectively supervised by a centralized high-order control barrier function (HOCBF) QP when the distributed candidate does not satisfy the direct-execution conditions. Evaluated in C++ simulations involving 8, 16, and 32 robots, the proposed architecture achieves collision-free execution and substantially improves computational scalability while maintaining task-level performance comparable to a centralized complete-graph baseline.

llm.title_ja: グラフ疎分散予測制御を用いたエッジ合意ADMMによるマルチロボットモーションプランニング
llm.tldr_ja: 時間変化する競合グラフとエッジ合意に基づくADMMを用いて、マルチロボットの衝突回避モーションプランニングを効率的かつスケーラブルに分散最適化するアーキテクチャを提案した。
llm.problem: マルチロボットシステムにおける衝突回避モーションプランニングの協調要求と計算スケーラビリティの課題。
llm.method: 予測競合グラフによるペアワイズ相互作用の選択、ウォームスタートを用いた凸二次計画問題（QP）への変換、およびエッジ合意ADMMによる分散最適化を組み合わせた。
llm.result: 8、16、32台のロボットを用いたC++シミュレーションにおいて、集中型完全グラフベースラインと同等のタスクパフォーマンスを維持しながら、衝突のない実行と大幅な計算スケーラビリティの向上を実現した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2611.11755.tldr_en: The proposed architecture achieves collision-free execution and substantially improves computational scalability while maintaining task-level performance comparable to a centralized complete-graph baseline.

2611.11732.title: Particle Filtering with Generative Trajectory Models for State Estimation and Control
2611.11732.abstract: Generative models can support both state estimation and control in robotics. For control, a common approach is to use the model as a policy that directly samples actions conditioned on observation histories. However, models that jointly represent states, actions, and observations can also predict how the robot state and its environment evolve. We investigate whether these predictions can improve state estimation and control through a change in inference procedure, without modifying the pretrained model. To this end, we use particle filtering to maintain competing hypotheses about state histories. A single pretrained diffusion model generates these hypotheses along with their predicted observations and associated action proposals. As new measurements arrive, particles are reweighted according to how well their predicted observations match the measurements. While particle filtering conventionally uses these weights only for state estimation, we also use them to guide action selection, favoring proposals associated with hypotheses that better explain the observations. Simulation experiments in partially observed navigation and vision-based manipulation demonstrate improvements in both state estimation and task performance compared to action generation without filtering, using the same pretrained model and no additional test-time information.

llm.title_ja: 状態推定と制御のための生成軌道モデルを用いた粒子フィルタリング
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みの生成拡散モデルを変更することなく、粒子フィルタリングの重みを状態推定だけでなく行動選択のガイダンスにも活用することで、状態推定とタスク性能を向上させた。
llm.problem: ロボットの制御において生成モデルは状態や環境の進化を予測できるが、推論手順を変更せずに状態推定と制御の両方を改善する手法の検討が不足している点。
llm.method: 事前学習済みの単一拡散モデルによって生成された状態履歴の仮説（粒子）に対し、新しい測定値との一致度に基づいて重み付けを行い、その重みを用いて観測をよりよく説明する行動提案を優先した。
llm.result: 部分観測されたナビゲーションと視覚ベースのマニピュレーションのシミュレーション実験において、フィルタリングなしの行動生成と比較して状態推定とタスク性能の両方が改善された。

2611.11732.tldr_en: This work uses particle filtering to maintain competing hypotheses about state histories in a single pretrained diffusion model, and uses these hypotheses to guide action selection, favoring proposals associated with hypotheses that better explain the observations.

2611.11727.title: State Media at Retrieval Time: A Large-Scale Audit of Russian State-Aligned Sources in AI Chatbot Responses
2611.11727.abstract: The Pravda Network is a Russian state-aligned media aggregator, with over 110 websites and more than 15 million articles published since 2023. Given its prolific and repetitive output, emerging scholarship argues that the Pravda Network was built to influence AI systems. We conduct a large-scale audit of leading AI chatbots to understand: (1) the retrieval rates of Pravda Network articles, (2) the conditions of retrieval, and (3) whether chatbot responses affirm or caveat this content. We build a 10,000 prompt corpus from sampled Pravda Network headlines varied along two dimensions (headline rewording and user skepticism) and query 11 AI chatbots via the web interface (n=104,997 completed responses). Overall, we find susceptibility to Pravda Network retrieval to be infrequent---appearing in 7.3% of responses---and highly platform dependent---with three chatbots responsible for 94% of retrievals (You.com, Claude, and Copilot). Among the frontier models, Claude is an outlier: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Meta AI retrieved no Pravda Network articles, likely indicative of a domain-level filtering policy. All 11 chatbots, however, retrieved other Russian state-aligned media to some degree (median=13.56% of responses). When Pravda Network articles are surfaced, caveat rates vary widely by platform (from 5.3% to 76.2%), with You.com providing the fewest caveats. We also identify the tactic of headline washing: where 9.92% of sampled Pravda Network headlines attribute their reporting to other, often more credible, media outlets, while the articles themselves are republished from Russian state-aligned media. We discuss headline washing's potential to launder state media as independent reporting. With this audit, we provide a systematic analysis of AI chatbots' susceptibility to Russia's latest attempt to manipulate the information environment.

llm.title_ja: 検索時の国家メディア：AIチャットボットの回答におけるロシア国家系情報源の大規模監査
llm.tldr_ja: 1万件のプロンプトを用いて11社のAIチャットボットを監査し、ロシア国家系メディア（プラウダネットワーク）の検索率やプラットフォームごとの差異、および「見出し洗浄」戦術の実態を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 新興の研究においてロシア国家系の情報集約ネットワークがAIシステムに影響を与えるために構築されたと議論されているが、チャットボットでの実際の検索状態や脆弱性が十分に分かっていない点。
llm.method: プラウダネットワークの見出しから構築した1万件のプロンプトを用いて11のAIチャットボットのウェブインターフェースをクエリし、約10万件の完了した応答を分析した。
llm.result: プラウダネットワークの検索は全体としては7.3%と低頻度であったがプラットフォーム依存性が高く、一部のモデルでは他のロシア系メディアも高率で検索されること、また情報源を偽る「見出し洗浄」が存在することが判明した。

2611.11727.tldr_en: A large-scale audit of leading AI chatbots is conducted to understand the retrieval rates of Pravda Network articles, the conditions of retrieval, and whether chatbot responses affirm or caveat this content, and discusses headline washing's potential to launder state media as independent reporting.

2611.11718.title: Accelerated Reinforcement Learning for Soft Robotics: Hours Instead of Years
2611.11718.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) requires large amounts of interaction data or a reliable simulator, both hard to obtain for nonlinear soft robotic hardware. Recent work shows that a time-scale separation inherent to soft robot dynamics justifies their reduction to low-dimensional invariant manifolds, known as adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs). We demonstrate that an aSSM-reduced model, a simple polynomial ordinary differential equation learned purely from pre-collected data, can serve as an RL training environment. On a pneumatically actuated soft arm, we train a trajectory-tracking policy in 3 hours on a six-dimensional aSSM-reduced model and deploy it without fine-tuning, whereas reproducing this policy training extrapolates to 3 years of hardware interaction. Our policy tracks dynamic targets with 40% lower error than otherwise identical policies trained on a 4.8-million-parameter recurrent neural network (RNN) or a 1.7-million-parameter transformer, which take 13 and 100 hours to identify, against 5 minutes for our mathematically justified 6,924-parameter model.

llm.title_ja: ソフトロボティクス向け加速強化学習：数年の代わりに数時間で
llm.tldr_ja: ソフトロボットの時空間分離特性を利用した低次元不変多様体（aSSM）モデルを強化学習の訓練環境として用いることで、数年かかる実機インタラクションをわずか数時間に短縮した。
llm.problem: 強化学習には膨大なインタラクションデータや信頼性の高いシミュレータが必要であるが、非線形なソフトロボットのハードウェアではこれらを取得することが極めて困難である点。
llm.method: 事前収集データから純粋に学習された低次元の多項式常微分方程式であるaSSM縮小モデルを強化学習の訓練環境として利用した。
llm.result: 空気圧駆動ソフトアームにおいて、6次元のaSSM縮小モデル上で3時間で軌道追従ポリシーを訓練して微調整なしで実機にデプロイし、RNNやTransformerベースのポリシーよりも低い誤差と高速な同定を実現した。

2611.11718.tldr_en: This work demonstrates that an aSSM-reduced model, a simple polynomial ordinary differential equation learned purely from pre-collected data, can serve as an RL training environment and tracks dynamic targets with 40% lower error than otherwise identical policies trained on a 4.8-million-parameter recurrent neural network (RNN) or a 1.7-million-parameter transformer.

2611.11709.title: Data-Driven Precision Control of Soft Helicoid Robots
2611.11709.abstract: A purely data-driven method grounded in the theory of adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs) was recently used to model and control nonlinear soft robotic simulators. Here, we extend the methodology to learn aSSM-reduced models from data collected from hardware soft robotic platforms. Specifically, we learn a five dimensional (5D) aSSM-reduced nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) that accurately models the dynamics of a soft-helicoid trunk robot. We then use this ODE in a model predictive control scheme to demonstrate real-time precision control across various challenging closed-loop trajectory-tracking tasks, ranging from 2D to 3D trajectories with static and dynamic constraints. We find that our methodology enhances accuracy and precision across all control tasks compared to available data-driven linear methods and model-free reinforcement learning. While we focus here on a soft-helicoid trunk robot, our methodology relies solely on hardware data and is therefore applicable to a broader class of soft robotic systems.
2611.11709.comment: Submitted to npj Robotics. 44 pages, supplementary information included

llm.title_ja: ソフトヘリコイドロボットのデータ駆動型精密制御
llm.tldr_ja: ハードウェアから収集したデータを用いて断熱スペクトル部分多様体（aSSM）に基づく低次元非線形ODEモデルを学習し、モデル予測制御を用いて実時間での精密な軌道追従制御を実現した。
llm.problem: 非線形なソフトロボットの高精度な実時間モデル化と制御は困難である。
llm.method: ハードウェアデータから5次元のaSSM低次元化非線形ODEを学習し、モデル予測制御に利用した。
llm.result: データ駆動型線形手法やモデルフリー強化学習と比較して、すべての制御タスクで精度と正確性が向上した。
llm.limitation: ソフトヘリコイドトランクロボットに焦点を当てているが、データ駆動型手法であるため他のソフトロボットにも適用可能。

2611.11709.tldr_en: This work learns a five dimensional (5D) aSSM-reduced nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) that accurately models the dynamics of a soft-helicoid trunk robot and uses this ODE in a model predictive control scheme to demonstrate real-time precision control across various challenging closed-loop trajectory-tracking tasks.

2611.11698.title: Compute Regeneration through Re-Productization: Reorganizing Retired Edge AI Silicon into a Delivered Multilingual Service Robot
2611.11698.abstract: Useful edge hardware can lose product support while retaining substantial computation. We treat this as systems design: compute regeneration here means re-productization, retaining the compute module while redesigning the surrounding product organization. Our case is GEdgeBot, a multilingual service robot built around a retired 32 GB Jetson AGX Xavier. A source-grounded inventory shows the box alone supplies inference, while the combined system exposes five on-device AI services, a seven-language speech chain, three sensing domains, and one deterministic seven-byte control boundary. AI and orchestration stay on the Xavier; finite motor-pulse generation on an STM32F407. Audits cover the six-mode control state machine, readiness barriers and sound orientation. Historical single-prototype measurements report 1,782 MB GPU memory with YOLO, Whisper-small, and NLLB-200 resident, a direct-control p99 deviation rising from 0.24 to 49.93 ms under concurrent AI load, and six of six trigger-to-follow demonstrations at 4.35 s mean latency, with conversational voice unavailable. A November campaign restores an isolated inference stack, re-measures AI workloads, and repeats control-frame runs. Driving two execution organisations with the same 6,000 measured 50 ms frame intervals shows the finite-pulse boundary removes host jitter from the pulse train but not the command start phase; its stopping bound is host-enforced, while the MCU 16-bit pulse field is unclamped. A six-check static audit exposes a host--MCU queue mismatch, and a 14-scenario replay executes the audited main() dispatcher across six modes with zero physical device opens and 54 contract-checked frames. Results support an existence claim and a reproducible architectural hypothesis, not fleet-level reliability. The 208 direct-control ratio remains unreplicated; MCU waveform capture and on-site fault injection remain open.

llm.title_ja: 再製品化によるコンピュートの再生：引退したエッジAIシリコンを多言語サービスロボットへ再構築する
llm.tldr_ja: サポートが終了したJetson AGX Xavierを再利用し、音声チェーン、AI推論サービス、決定論的モーター制御境界を備えた多言語サービスロボットを構築した。
llm.problem: 有用なエッジハードウェアが、十分な計算能力を残しながら製品サポートを失うこと。
llm.method: 引退したJetsonとSTM32F407を組み合わせ、AI処理とハードウェア制御境界を分離したシステム設計を行った。
llm.result: 有限パルス境界によりホストのジッタがパルス列から除去されることなどを検証し、再現可能なアーキテクチャ仮説を実証した。
llm.limitation: 艦隊レベルの信頼性は確立しておらず、歴史的な単一プロトタイプの測定に基づいている。

2611.11698.tldr_en: This case is GEdgeBot, a multilingual service robot built around a retired 32 GB Jetson AGX Xavier, and results support an existence claim and a reproducible architectural hypothesis, not fleet-level reliability.

2611.11697.title: SurgTAP-3D: A Large-Scale Cross-Surgery Video Dataset with Contact-Aware 3D Motion Tracking
2611.11697.abstract: Understanding 3D scene dynamics in minimally invasive surgery (MIS) is a fundamental step toward physically intelligent and autonomous surgical systems. However, existing public datasets offer limited scalability and diversity in real-world clinical scenarios. Moreover, annotations typically focus on either tissue or instruments alone, overlooking tool-tissue interactions. This gap limits applications such as augmented reality guidance and autonomous surgery driven by vision-language-action (VLA) models or world models, which demand large-scale, high-quality 3D supervision. In this work, we construct SurgTAP-3D, a large-scale in-vivo pseudo-3D surgical motion tracking dataset and benchmark, comprising 520K frames, 4,549 action clips, and 1.4M 2D/3D point trajectories from diverse robotic and manual procedures under unified action categories. To make annotation scalable, we design a unified framework for surgical 3D point tracking that converts uncalibrated monocular surgical videos into structured 4D annotations through contact-region prompting, active-tool segmentation, dynamic bundle adjustment, and global 4D refinement. This pipeline adapts foundation priors to surgical videos and produces temporally consistent trajectories, pseudo-scale geometry, camera poses, and instrument masks. The dataset captures realistic challenges inherent to surgical environments, including occlusions, smoke, bleeding, and rapid instrument motion. We establish a comprehensive benchmark on SurgPose, SurgT, and STIR, covering both instrument and tissue tracking. We demonstrate instrument displacement estimation, deformable surface reconstruction, and foundation-model fine-tuning. Extensive experiments and analysis demonstrate the effectiveness of our dataset and annotation framework for 3D surgical point tracking, reconstruction, and surgical action understanding. Homepage: https://wrld.github.io/surgtap-3d/
2611.11697.comment: Accepted to IEEE Transactions on Robotics (T-RO)

llm.title_ja: SurgTAP-3D：接触認識型3Dモーション追跡を備えた大規模クロス手術ビデオデータセット
llm.tldr_ja: 接触領域のプロンプトや動的バンドル調整などを用いて、未校正の単眼手術ビデオを構造化された4Dアノテーションに変換する統一フレームワークと大規模データセットを構築した。
llm.problem: 既存の公開手術データセットは拡張性や多様性が限られており、道具と組織の相互作用が見落とされている。
llm.method: 接触領域プロンプト、アクティブツールセグメンテーション、動的バンドル調整を用いた統一3Dポイント追跡パイプラインを設計した。
llm.result: 520Kフレーム、4,549のアクションクリップ、140万の2D/3Dポイント軌跡を含むSurgTAP-3Dを構築し、効果を実証した。
keywords_ja: コンピュータビジョン

2611.11697.tldr_en: This work designs a unified framework for surgical 3D point tracking that converts uncalibrated monocular surgical videos into structured 4D annotations through contact-region prompting, active-tool segmentation, dynamic bundle adjustment, and global 4D refinement, and establishes a comprehensive benchmark on SurgPose, SurgT, and STIR, covering both instrument and tissue tracking.

2611.11690.title: A Physical Testbed for Self-Driving Laboratories: Comparing Bayesian and Agentic Optimization in a Minimal Closed-Loop Color Formulation Task
2611.11690.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) integrate laboratory robotics and automation with AI-driven decision-making to close the design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycle. However, physical testbeds that combine off-the-shelf hardware and AI into a functioning closed-loop workflow remain in early stages of development, and their integration with commercial laboratory automation is comparatively less developed. In this work, we develop a physical testbed that assembles and integrates commercially available laboratory automation instruments and demonstrate continuous, closed-loop, autonomous operation over 24 cumulative hours of unattended experimentation. We validate this platform on a minimal closed-loop discovery task in which the system autonomously formulates aqueous dye mixtures to match a target absorbance spectrum. The system completed six independent campaigns, each consisting of 48 closed-loop iterations over approximately four hours. In every campaign, the system autonomously selected, dispensed, and measured each mixture, with an AI-driven decision-making algorithm determining subsequent formulations without human intervention. Using this testbed, we compared the performance of two AI-driven decision-making algorithms, traditional Bayesian optimization (BO) and an agentic approach, in selecting mixtures under a fixed total-volume constraint. The agentic optimizer matched target absorbance spectra using fewer iterations than BO, with reductions up to 52%, and converged on a solution for one target that BO failed to match within 48 iterations. These results demonstrate a reference physical platform for SDLs that can evaluate both established and emerging AI strategies, including large language model (LLM)-directed optimization, before their deployment in real-world applications where experiments may be costly and time-consuming to prepare.

llm.title_ja: セルフドライビング・ラボラトリー向け物理テストベッド：最小限の閉ループ色彩配合タスクにおけるベイズ最適化とエージェント型最適化の比較
llm.tldr_ja: 市販の実験室自動化機器を統合した物理テストベッドを開発し、24時間の無人連続運転を行い、色彩配合タスクでAI駆動型アルゴリズムを評価した。
llm.problem: 市販ハードウェアとAIを組み合わせた機能的な閉ループワークフローを持つ物理テストベッドの開発は初期段階にある。
llm.method: 市販の実験室自動化機器を統合した物理テストベッドを構築し、ベイズ最適化とエージェント型最適化の性能を比較した。
llm.result: エージェント型オプティマイザーはベイズ最適化よりも少ない反復回数で目標吸光度スペクトルに一致させることができた。
keywords_ja: セルフドライビングラボ
