2611.11690.tldr_en: A physical testbed is developed that assembles and integrates commercially available laboratory automation instruments and demonstrates continuous, closed-loop, autonomous operation over 24 cumulative hours of unattended experimentation, demonstrating a reference physical platform for SDLs that can evaluate both established and emerging AI strategies, including large language model (LLM)-directed optimization.

2611.11688.title: Streaming Failure Forecasting: VLA Failure Monitors That Keep Learning After Deployment
2611.11688.abstract: Failure monitors for vision-language-action (VLA) policies are trained offline and then frozen. After deployment, lighting, objects and cameras drift, and the policy itself is updated or moved to new tasks. On recorded real-robot runs, after a switch of task or policy version, a frozen monitor fit on the old task ranks failures little better than chance. We present Streaming Failure Forecasting (SFF), a monitor that keeps learning from the one label every episode provides: whether it succeeded. SFF keeps the offline monitor's network fixed and refits only its last linear layer after each episode, at 2.18 ms per policy call on a Jetson CPU core. Its alarm threshold moves only after successes, which in simulation kept false alarms near target except when two drifts came at once. With every setting locked before testing, SFF ranks failures better than the same monitor kept frozen on 4 of 5 simulated test suites under unannounced drift, and above resetting on detected drift on every suite. Carried with its locked learner settings to 434 recorded runs of four VLAs on real SO-101 arms, replayed across unannounced switches of task or policy version, it ranks failures better than the frozen monitor for every VLA and, in an exploratory comparison, above a full reset at the true switch. A deployed failure monitor need not stay frozen: refitting its readout from outcomes is cheap and helps after the changes we tested.
2611.11688.comment: 25 pages, 13 figures, 9 tables. A short version was accepted at the Sim2Real2Field and EEAI workshops at CoRL 2026. Project page: https://sff-research.org

llm.title_ja: ストリーミング故障予測：デプロイ後も学習し続けるVLA故障モニター
llm.tldr_ja: エピソードごとの成功・失敗の1つのラベルから最終線形層のみを再学習することで、デプロイ後の環境変化に適応するストリーミング故障予測モニターを提案した。
llm.problem: VLAポリシーの故障モニターはオフラインで学習され固定されるため、環境やタスクのドリフトに対応できない。
llm.method: ネットワークを固定し、エピソードごとに最後の線形層のみを再学習するStreaming Failure Forecasting（SFF）を提案した。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機のSO-101アームを用いた実験において、未通知のドリフト下でも凍結されたモニターより優れた故障ランキング性能を示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.11688.tldr_en: Streaming Failure Forecasting (SFF) is presented, a monitor that keeps learning from the one label every episode provides: whether it succeeded, which in simulation kept false alarms near target except when two drifts came at once.

2611.11674.title: Brain-Aligned Latent Actions: Imposing Premotor Cortex Geometry on a Robot's Action Vocabulary
2611.11674.abstract: Robot policies increasingly act through a small vocabulary of discrete latent actions learned from unlabeled video, yet training leaves open which motion receives which code. We find this choice highly unstable: two independently trained runs of Moto's latent motion tokenizer assign the same robot clips to nearly unrelated codes (adjusted Rand index 0.001), and evaluating one tokenizer in bf16 instead of fp32 reassigns 74% of its tokens. We use this freedom to impose the representational geometry of macaque ventral premotor cortex (PMv), recorded while a monkey drew shapes, on the tokenizer's code assignment, with a straight-through similarity loss trained alongside its reconstruction objective on robot video. In one training run per target, on five shape categories the loss never saw, the PMv-trained tokenizer reaches a representational similarity of 0.52 with PMv, against 0.20-0.26 for released and no-prior tokenizers and 0.42 for the 95th percentile of random kinematic encoders. Kinematic, language, and random targets do not transfer (-0.17 to -0.03). Two results limit the claim: a hand-picked kinematic descriptor, the stroke's initial direction, matches PMv better (0.65), and a label-shuffled PMv control scores 0.41. We specify the downstream manipulation test, on a CALVIN pipeline that reproduces Moto's published results, before running it.
2611.11674.comment: 16 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables. Robot manipulation results (CALVIN) will be added in a later version

llm.title_ja: 脳の整列に基づく潜在アクション：マカクの運動前野の幾何学をロボットのアクション語彙に課す
llm.tldr_ja: マカクザルの腹側運動前野（PMv）の表現幾何学をロボットの潜在モーショントークナイザーに課すことで、コード割当ての不安定性を解消し、脳と整列した表現を獲得した。
llm.problem: ラベルなし動画から学習される離散的な潜在アクションの割当ては不安定であり、初期化や精度によって大きく変化する。
llm.method: マカクのPMvの記録データから得た幾何学を、再構成目的に加えたストレートスルー類似度損失を用いてトークナイザーのコード割当てに課した。
llm.result: PMvで学習されたトークナイザーは、ランダムなエンコーダと比較してPMvとの間で高い表現類似度を達成した。
llm.limitation: 手動で選択した運動記述子の方がPMvによく一致するなど、いくつかの制限が存在する。
keywords_ja: モーショントークナイザー

2611.11674.tldr_en: This work uses the representational geometry of macaque ventral premotor cortex, recorded while a monkey drew shapes, to impose the representational geometry of macaque ventral premotor cortex on the tokenizer's code assignment, with a straight-through similarity loss trained alongside its reconstruction objective on robot video.

2611.11665.title: HINT-VLM: Humanoid Interactive Navigation over Rough Terrain with Embodiment-Grounded Vision-Language Model
2611.11665.abstract: Humanoid robots have achieved significant progress in locomotion and manipulation, enabling traversal over rough terrain and richer interaction with the environment, such as moving obstacles. However, most traditional navigation methods assume non-interactive environments and focus only on traversal. While Navigation Among Movable Obstacles (NAMO) approaches relax this assumption, prior efforts have largely focused on flat environments and reactive interaction, rather than predicting object movability and planning ahead. These limitations become critical in outdoor rough-terrain scenarios, where robots must jointly reason about terrain traversability and object movability. In this work, we address NAMO for humanoid robots in cluttered outdoor rough terrain by proposing a hybrid planning framework that combines semantic priors from a Vision-Language Model (VLM) with embodied robot interaction data through a Gaussian process (GP) residual model. The GP corrects the VLM-derived movability prior to produce embodiment-grounded probabilistic movability estimates, which are then incorporated into hierarchical uncertainty-aware planning. The proposed approach allows humanoids to jointly leverage locomotion and manipulation for efficient and safe navigation, representing the first solution to NAMO in rough terrain through predictive movability reasoning and probabilistic VLM integration.

llm.title_ja: HINT-VLM： embodimentグラウンデッドなビジョン言語モデルを用いた荒地におけるヒューマノイドの対話型ナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: ビジョン言語モデル（VLM）からの意味論的事前知識とガウス過程残差モデルを組み合わせたハイブリッド計画フレームワークにより、荒地での動的障害物回避とナビゲーションを実現した。
llm.problem: 従来のナビゲーション手法は非対話的環境を仮定しており、荒地での地形通行性と物体移動性の同時推論が困難である。
llm.method: VLMの移動性事前知識をガウス過程（GP）残差モデルで補正し、不確実性を考慮した階層的計画に組み込んだ。
llm.result: 予測的移動性推論と確率的VLM統合を用いることで、荒地において移動と操作を統合した効率的で安全なナビゲーションを可能にした。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2611.11665.tldr_en: This work addresses NAMO for humanoid robots in cluttered outdoor rough terrain by proposing a hybrid planning framework that combines semantic priors from a Vision-Language Model with embodied robot interaction data through a Gaussian process (GP) residual model.

2611.11662.title: Enhancing Balance and Posture in Material Handling Tasks with a Wearable Robotic Tail
2611.11662.abstract: Frequent heavy lifting is linked to musculoskeletal strain, with lower back pain affecting up to 40% of manual labourers. Inspired by animals using tails for balance, we developed a wearable robotic tail as a dynamic counterbalance. Ten participants performed an imitated shelf loading/unloading task across three conditions: active tail, passive tail, and no tail. Kinematics, centre of pressure, and muscle activation (gastrocnemius, erector spinae, tibialis anterior, biceps brachii) were measured. Compared with no tail, the active tail achieved >20 mm reduction in centre of pressure peak displacement, 4.3 degree reduction in trunk motion, and >9% and >20% reductions in erector spinae and gastrocnemius activity, respectively. The passive tail produced smaller reductions, suggesting passive counterbalancing helps while active movement augments it further. Biceps brachii activation increased with the active versus passive tail. The ankle kinematics and tibialis anterior activation were unchanged. These findings support wearable robotic tails for improving balance during material handling.

llm.title_ja: 装着型ロボットテールを用いたマテリアルハンドリング作業におけるバランスと姿勢の改善
llm.tldr_ja: 動的カウンターバランスとして機能する装着型ロボットテールを開発し、棚の荷積み・荷下ろし作業中の姿勢や筋肉活動への効果を検証した。
llm.problem: 頻繁な重量物の持ち上げは筋骨格系の負担につながり、多くの労働者が腰痛に悩まされている。
llm.method: 10名の被験者がアクティブテール、パッシブテール、テール無しの3つの条件で荷役作業を行い、運動学や筋活動を計測した。
llm.result: アクティブテールは圧力中心のピーク変位を20mm以上減少させ、体幹の動きや脊柱起立筋・腓腹筋の活動を大幅に削減した。

2611.11662.tldr_en: Findings support wearable robotic tails for improving balance during material handling by suggesting passive counterbalancing helps while active movement augments it further.

2611.11650.title: FlowEval: How Much Adaptation Does an Embodied Foundation Model Need at Deployment?
2611.11650.abstract: Large-scale pretraining is reducing the amount of adaptation required to deploy embodied foundation models, but it is not guaranteed that a pretrained model already provide the level of performance required in every deployment. Practitioners therefore need to understand how well a pretrained model matches a target deployment and how much adaptation data is left to be collected. We study whether a small set of successful target-domain demonstrations can reveal whether and how much target-domain data will be required before any adaptation. We introduce FlowEval, a set of training-free metrics that use the flow-matching objective to probe an embodied foundation model with a set of demonstrations. FlowEval quantifies predictive disagreement on successful target demonstrations to assess how well a pretrained model fits a target deployment. Across four embodied foundation model families: Pi-0.5, MolmoAct2, GR00T, and DreamZero, FlowEval distinguishes seen from unseen deployments across real-world and simulated manipulation. Further, by finetuning Pi-0.5 and GR00T on 17 RoboCasa365 manipulation tasks, we showed that FlowEval correlates with how success rate improves as additional adaptation data is provided. Together, these results suggest that FlowEval can serve as a lightweight, training-free diagnostic of how much model--deployment adaptation may be required.

llm.title_ja: FlowEval：具身基盤モデルはデプロイ時にどれだけの適応を必要とするか？
llm.tldr_ja: フローマッチング目的関数を利用して具身基盤モデルの予測の不一致を測定し、追加の適応データの必要性を推論するトレーニング不要の診断指標FlowEvalを提案した。
llm.problem: 事前学習済み具身基盤モデルがターゲットのデプロイ環境にどの程度適合しているか、どれだけの適応データが必要かを事前に把握する必要がある。
llm.method: 成功したターゲットデモのセットを用いて予測の不一致を定量化する、トレーニング不要の指標「FlowEval」を導入した。
llm.result: 複数の具身基盤モデルファミリーにおいて、FlowEvalが既知の環境と未知の環境を区別し、ファインチューニング時の成功率の向上と相関することを示した。

2611.11650.tldr_en: FlowEval is introduced, a set of training-free metrics that use the flow-matching objective to probe an embodied foundation model with a set of demonstrations that quantifies predictive disagreement on successful target demonstrations to assess how well a pretrained model fits a target deployment.

2611.11648.title: PA-SaR: Perception-Aware Learning, Control, and Coordination for Multi-Robot Search and Rescue
2611.11648.abstract: Autonomous SaR requires robots to explore unknown or partially known environments, avoid hazards, coordinate team activities, and guide discovered victims to safety. Improving individual capabilities of robots does not necessarily improve mission outcomes: safer motion can restrict the exploration behavior, faster discovery can increase the rescue demand, and effective guidance depends on victim responses. We introduce PA-SaR, a mathematical and architectural framework for coordinating heterogeneous local control, learning-based exploration, supervisory task allocation, and adaptive approach-lead victim guidance around mission-level objectives. PA- SaR distinguishes environmental ground-truth, robot-specific perceptions, and simulated victim behavior. This provides a common basis for integrating complementary mechanisms and analyzing their interactions across mission stages. We demonstrate the framework through single- and multi-robot simulation studies incorporating model-predictive and learning-based exploration, perception-based safety shielding, event-driven task allocation, and adaptive victim guidance. The results show trade-offs between collision avoidance and search completion, indicate that supervisory allocation improves search completion beyond information sharing alone, and demonstrate that increased exploration does not necessarily yield more rescues. Adaptive guidance increases rescues relative to continuous leading, without a detected improvement in mean or final victim trust or a reduction in mortality. These findings support evaluating local control, team coordination, and evacuation as related but distinct aspects of autonomous SaR within the considered simulation environments.

llm.title_ja: PA-SaR：マルチロボット捜索救助のための知覚認識型学習、制御、および協調
llm.tldr_ja: 局所制御、学習ベースの探索、タスク割り当て、適応的誘導を統合した数理・アーキテクチャフレームワークPA-SaRを提案し、シミュレーションで評価した。
llm.problem: 自律型捜索救助（SaR）において個々のロボットの機能を向上させるだけではミッション全体の成果向上につながらない。
llm.method: 環境のグランド真値、ロボット個別の知覚、模擬的な被災者の行動を区別し、それらを統合するPA-SaRフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: 衝突回避と探索完了のトレードオフや、監視型割り当てが情報共有単独よりも探索完了を改善することなどをシミュレーションで示した。
llm.limitation: シミュレーション環境での評価に限定されている。

2611.11648.tldr_en: PA-SaR is introduced, a mathematical and architectural framework for coordinating heterogeneous local control, learning-based exploration, supervisory task allocation, and adaptive approach-lead victim guidance around mission-level objectives and supports evaluating local control, team coordination, and evacuation as related but distinct aspects of autonomous SaR within the considered simulation environments.

2611.11646.title: ColNav: Uncertainty-Aware Spacetime Collision Checking with Bounding Volume Hierarchies
2611.11646.abstract: Safe navigation for mobile robots in dynamic and uncertain environments requires planning paths that avoid collisions with other moving targets. Typically this involves forward propagating the robot motion and checking for collisions at sampled points in space and time. Such methods can miss collisions between sampled points and are not robust to uncertainty in the state estimates. We propose ColNav, a robust collision check formulation with geometric volumes. The key aspect of our approach is encoding the uncertainty in the targets' and the ego robot's positions and velocities into spacetime tubes, in two variants that consume bounded-set and Gaussian uncertainty descriptions, respectively. The tubes are organised in bounding volume hierarchies, so that a single tree traversal covers the entire horizon, rather than testing sampled time instants, and returns a robust geometric certificate together with an estimate of the time to collision. Static and dynamic obstacles share the same representation. Our approach reaches the goal with a 100% success rate under prediction model mismatch, where the best baseline reaches 65%, and maintains up to three times the clearance in dense traffic. We also validate real-time operation on a physical robot.

llm.title_ja: ColNav：バウンディングボリューム階層を用いた不確実性を考慮した時空衝突判定
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットや対象の位置・速度の不確実性を時空チューブにエンコードし、バウンディングボリューム階層を用いて効率的かつ頑健に衝突判定を行うColNavを提案した。
llm.problem: 動的で不確実な環境でのモバイルロボットの安全なナビゲーションにおいて、サンプリング点間の衝突見落としや状態推定の不確実性への対応が課題である。
llm.method: 有界集合およびガウス不確実性記述を時空チューブとしてエンコードし、バウンディングボリューム階層（BVH）で整理して単一の木探索で処理する手法を提案した。
llm.result: 予測モデルのミスマッチ下で100%の成功率を達成し、高密度な交通状況でもベースラインの最大3倍のクリアランスを維持した。

2611.11646.tldr_en: ColNav, a robust collision check formulation with geometric volumes, encoding the uncertainty in the targets' and the ego robot's positions and velocities into spacetime tubes, in two variants that consume bounded-set and Gaussian uncertainty descriptions, respectively.

2611.11605.title: ScanDreamer: A Map-Grounded World Model for Quadrotor Navigation
2611.11605.abstract: Quadrotors inspecting buildings and tunnels must navigate unknown clutter with a forward-facing depth camera whose limited field of view constrains scene understanding and collision-avoiding navigation. Recent world-model agents learn navigation through imagined experience (e.g., AirDreamer), but remain data-intensive and often lack explicit geometric memory and awareness of what the camera can observe. We propose ScanDreamer, a map-grounded world model that constructs an online 2D scan-memory map from depth images and vehicle pose. Our world model, actor, and critic are conditioned on this map, which also defines a geodesic progress reward. Moreover, a forward-cone penalty discourages horizontal motion outside the camera's viewing direction. During imagination, ScanDreamer propagates the quadrotor pose over a frozen map and derives progress and wall-contact signals from the mapped geometry. We train ScanDreamer for 0.8 million environment steps (5.5 h on one GPU) and evaluate it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim over 1560 episodes spanning unseen layouts and parameter ranges. Across three seeds (mean $\pm$ SD), ScanDreamer achieves 96.3 $\pm$ 0.3% success with 3.6 $\pm$ 0.3% collision, compared with 59.6 $\pm$ 3.0% success and 28.8 $\pm$ 2.8% collision for AirDreamer at the same online-interaction budget. Removing the forward-cone penalty increases collisions to 9.9 $\pm$ 3.1%. These results show that combining explicit map memory, map-grounded imagination, and perception-aware motion substantially improves navigation performance and data efficiency. The source code is available at https://github.com/WANGSHUAIzzzz/ScanDreamer.
2611.11605.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to AICAP 2027; decision pending

llm.title_ja: ScanDreamer：クアッドローターのナビゲーションに向けたマップグラウンデッド世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 深度画像と車両ポーズからオンラインで2Dスキャンメモリマップを構築し、それに基づいて想像上の経験からナビゲーションを学習するマップグラウンデッド世界モデルを提案した。
llm.problem: 限られた視野を持つ前方深度カメラを使用するクアッドローターが、未知の障害物をナビゲートする際、既存の世界モデルはデータ効率が悪く幾何学的記憶が欠けている。
llm.method: オンラインの2Dスキャンメモリマップを構築し、それに基づく測地学的進行報酬や前方コーンペナルティを組み合わせた世界モデルScanDreamerを提案した。
llm.result: NVIDIA Isaac Simを用いた実験で、ベースラインと比較して大幅に高い成功率と低い衝突率を達成した。

2611.11605.tldr_en: Results show that combining explicit map memory, map-grounded imagination, and perception-aware motion substantially improves navigation performance and data efficiency.

2611.11601.title: Kinora: A Versioned Workflow for Text-to-Motion Generation, Robot Retargeting, and Interactive Validation
2611.11601.abstract: Motion generation tools produce candidate trajectories, but interactive robot authoring also requires recoverable execution, traceable edits, explicit geometry, and model-specific validation. We present Kinora, a system that connects text-to-motion generation, a motion library, local agent tools, robot retargeting, and trajectory refinement through versioned artifacts. The current release uses an independently specified 52-joint authoring rig and procedural skeleton previews, separating the distributed human geometry from externally installed generation models and robot assets. Human-motion edits preserve frames outside a selected interval, while robot edits create immutable candidates whose reports govern acceptance and export. We evaluate server 0.5.1 and Gadget 0.15.2 with 156 core regression test executions, 49 Gadget executions, four CUDA generation/editing cases, a 30-frame G1 retargeting check, and a 3,600-frame synthetic G1 fixture paired with a suspended negative control. All four CUDA cases passed their numerical gates; the turning splice nevertheless retained a 14.3 cm support-foot drift proxy warning. The G1 positive fixture completed bounded simulation replay, whereas the suspended control was quarantined before replay. These results support selected integration and preservation contracts. They do not establish semantic-quality improvements, population-level feasibility, or hardware safety.
2611.11601.comment: 10 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables. Technical report on Kinora server 0.5.1 and Gadget 0.15.2. Code and release artifacts: https://github.com/PoirotJin/kinora

llm.title_ja: Kinora：テキスト・トゥ・モーション生成、ロボットリタイゲッティング、およびインタラクティブ検証のためのバージョン管理ワークフロー
llm.tldr_ja: テキスト・トゥ・モーション生成、ローカルエージェントツール、ロボットリタイゲッティングをバージョン管理されたアーティファクトで接続するシステムKinoraを提案した。
llm.problem: モーション生成ツールは候補軌道を生成するが、インタラクティブなロボットオーサリングには再現可能な実行や追跡可能な編集が必要である。
llm.method: 独立して指定された52関節のオーサリングリグと手続き型スケルトンプレビューを使用し、世代モデルとロボットアセットを分離したシステムを構築した。
llm.result: CUDA生成ケースの数値的ゲート通過や、G1ロボットを用いたシミュレーションリプレイによる統合および保存契約の検証を行った。
llm.limitation: 意味的品質の改善、母集団レベルの実行可能性、またはハードウェアの安全性は確立されていない。
keywords_ja: ロボットオーサリング

2611.11601.tldr_en: Kinora is presented, a system that connects text-to-motion generation, a motion library, local agent tools, robot retargeting, and trajectory refinement through versioned artifacts, and supports selected integration and preservation contracts.

2611.11580.title: Qubit-to-Motion: Traceable Action Provenance in Hybrid QRL for Robotic Bin-Packing Sequencing
2611.11580.abstract: Hybrid quantum reinforcement learning has been explored for robotic decision-making, but evaluations often emphasize task success, return, or convergence, leaving unresolved whether quantum circuit outputs influence constrained actions and remain traceable through robot execution. We present \texttt{Qubit-to-Motion}, an evidence-centered framework for support-constrained sequencing and simulated robotic placement. Four Pauli-$Z$ readouts provide the sole learned input to the actor and critic, while a support mask enforces admissible object selection. Each decision is recorded and linked via step indices and SHA-256 fingerprints to a sealed route, deterministic Cartesian and inverse-kinematics waypoints, prescribed joint motion, and MuJoCo contact replay. A frozen checkpoint is evaluated across five deterministic 30-object scene variants. All 150 placements satisfy support, containment, and settling criteria. A fixed-state zero-readout intervention changes $90.0\pm0.0\%$ of decisions, demonstrating dependence on the joint circuit representation. Mean macro travel is $34.537\pm0.206$~m, inference requires $8.60\pm1.27$~ms per route, and replay achieves $8.764\pm0.220~μ$m mean final position error with 0.356~mm maximum interpenetration. These results establish reproducible decision-to-contact traceability. The implementation is available at \href{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Qubit-to-Motion-Quantum-Reinforcement-Learning-F7DC}{\textcolor{linkpink}{the anonymous repository}}.

llm.title_ja: Qubit-to-Motion：ロボットの箱詰めシーケンスにおけるハイブリッド量子強化学習の追跡可能なアクションプロバンス
llm.tldr_ja: Pauli-Z読み取りを用いたハイブリッド量子強化学習において、決定から接触までの全過程をステップインデックスとSHA-256フィンガープリントで追跡可能にするフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: ハイブリッド量子強化学習の評価はタスク成功率や報酬に偏りが多く、量子回路の出力をロボットの実行全体で追跡可能かどうかが未解決であった。
llm.method: 4つのPauli-Z読み取りをアクターとクリティックの入力とし、サポートマスクで制約を課しつつ、SHA-256で各決定を追跡する仕組みを構築した。
llm.result: 150の配置すべてが基準を満たし、ゼロ読み取り介入実験により量子表現への依存と再現可能な追跡可能性を実証した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.11580.tldr_en: Qubit-to-Motion, an evidence-centered framework for support-constrained sequencing and simulated robotic placement, establishes reproducible decision-to-contact traceability.

2611.11576.title: Continuous modeling of manipulative participation for stance analysis: Online discourse on the 2024 Street Animal Law in Türkiye
2611.11576.abstract: Studies of online political discourse commonly infer public opinion through stance analysis while implicitly assuming that observed user participation is authentic. Meanwhile, studies focusing on detecting manipulative participation are typically modeling it as a binary phenomenon, overlooking the varying degrees to which users may engage in coordinated or inauthentic behavior. This study proposes a continuous modeling approach for manipulative participation and examines its integration with stance analysis. Using online discourse on the 2024 Street Animal Law in Türkiye as a case study, we collected a dataset comprising 7,320,574 tweets from 537,994 users. From this corpus, 301 users were selected through a high-information sampling strategy and manually annotated by domain experts using a 10-criterion rubric that yields user-level continuous manipulative participation scores. Evaluation under a unified user-level cross-validation protocol showed that the proposed framework accurately estimates both manipulative participation and user stance, with gradient boosting methods providing the best manipulative participation estimates and BERTurk achieving the highest stance classification performance. External validation on an independently annotated user set demonstrated good generalization performance. The findings support modeling manipulative participation as a continuous construct rather than a binary label, providing a more informative basis for computational analyses of the relationship between manipulative participation and stance in online political discourse.
2611.11576.comment: Submitted to Journal of Computational Social Science

llm.title_ja: スタンス分析のための操作的参加の継続的モデリング：トルコにおける2024年野良動物法に関するオンラインディスコース
llm.tldr_ja: バイナリの現象として扱われがちな操作的参加を継続的構成概念として捉え、勾配ブースティングとBERTurkを用いてスタンス分析と統合する新しいモデリング手法を提案した。
llm.problem: オンラインの政治的ディスコースのスタンス分析において、ユーザーの参加が本物であると暗黙的に仮定されているか、操作的参加が二値現象としてモデル化されている。
llm.method: 730万件を超えるツイートから収集したデータに対し、専門家による10基準の評価基準を用いた継続的な操作的参加スコアの注釈付けと機械学習モデルの適用を行った。
llm.result: 提案手法により操作的参加の程度とユーザーのスタンスを正確に推定できることを示し、独立した注釈付きデータセットで良好な汎化性能を実証した。
keywords_ja: ソーシャルメディア分析
フェイクニュース検出

2611.11576.tldr_en: Evaluation under a unified user-level cross-validation protocol showed that the proposed framework accurately estimates both manipulative participation and user stance, with gradient boosting methods providing the best manipulative participation estimates and BERTurk achieving the highest stance classification performance.

2611.11555.title: Concurrent Learning-Based Inertial Parameter Estimation and Control of Quadrotors
2611.11555.abstract: In this letter, we consider trajectory tracking control and inertial parameter estimation of a quadrotor UAV whose center of mass (CoM) does not coincide with its geometric center. Onboard payloads like an IMU, a camera, or a battery are not necessarily placed at its geometric center. Moreover, during the flight these sensors might move because of external disturbances and cause a CoM offset. Thus, these events and equipment introduce an offset and cause the inertia matrix to be non-diagonal. We develop an integral concurrent learning (ICL)-based geometric controller that estimates the mass, the CoM offset, and the full inertia matrix online, without an accelerometer or numerical derivatives, and tracks a given trajectory corrected by the offset estimated online. We prove that the estimated parameters converge to their true values under a finite excitation condition. We validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm using a simulation example.
2611.11555.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures. To be submitted to IEEE Control Systems Letters (L-CSS) with the CDC 2027 option

llm.title_ja: 同時学習に基づくクアッドローターの慣性パラメータ推定と制御
llm.tldr_ja: 加速度計や数値微分を用いずに、質量、重心オフセット、および完全な慣性行列をオンラインで推定し、軌道追従制御を行う積分同時学習（ICL）ベースの幾何学的コントローラを開発した。
llm.problem: ペイロードの移動や外乱によりクアッドローターの重心が幾何学的中心からずれ、慣性マトリックスが非対角化するため制御が困難になる。
llm.method: 加速度計を使用せず、オンラインで質量や重心オフセット、慣性行列を推定する積分同時学習（ICL）ベースの幾何学的コントローラを開発した。
llm.result: 有限励起条件の下で推定パラメータが真の値に収束することを証明し、シミュレーション例でアルゴリズムの有効性を検証した。
llm.limitation: シミュレーション例による検証のみ。

2611.11555.tldr_en: An integral concurrent learning (ICL)-based geometric controller is developed that estimates the mass, the CoM offset, and the full inertia matrix online, without an accelerometer or numerical derivatives, and tracks a given trajectory corrected by the offset estimated online.

2611.11554.title: Kimodo-Policy: Learning Kinematic Action Models for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
2611.11554.abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires continuous coordination of high-dimensional whole-body motion to realize task objectives. While vision-language-action models and world action models transfer semantic and visual-dynamics priors to robot control, these priors do not necessarily capture the structure of robot motion. We introduce Kinematic Action Models (KAMs), a paradigm that treats whole-body motion as a direct pretraining target and uses a pretrained motion generator as the primary action-generation backbone. KAMs ground learned temporal and cross-body coordination priors through task conditioning, visual observations, and execution feedback. We present Kimodo-Policy as an initial instantiation, combining a frozen Kimodo text-to-motion backbone with lightweight ControlNet-based visual conditioning. A root-body-hand hierarchy coordinates locomotion and manipulation, while motion-history conditioning and repeated action-chunk prediction bridge motion synthesis and closed-loop control. Following large-scale loco-manipulation pretraining, the policy achieves the highest overall success among compared policies on multi-task HumanoidArena (72.14%), competitive performance on SIMPLE, and 60% mean success across eight real-world tasks, with 678M parameters (92M trainable). Ablations support the contribution of the pretrained motion backbone. Together, these results provide initial evidence for motion generation as a complementary foundation for humanoid action learning.
2611.11554.comment: 23 pages, 14 figures, 4 tables. Project page: https://kimodo-policy.github.io/

llm.title_ja: Kimodo-Policy：ヒューマノイドのロコモーション・マニピュレーションに向けた運動学的アクションモデルの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みのテキスト・トゥ・モーションバックボーンをアクション生成の主軸として利用し、視覚的条件付けと組み合わせることでヒューマノイドの全身運動を制御するKinematic Action Models（KAMs）を提案した。
llm.problem: ビジョン言語モデルや世界行動モデルはセマンティックな事前知識を転送できるが、ロボットの運動構造を必ずしも捉えていない。
llm.method: 凍結されたKimodoテキスト・トゥ・モーションバックボーンとControlNetベースの視覚的条件付けを組み合わせたKimodo-Policyを開発した。
llm.result: HumanoidArenaでの最高平均成功率や実世界タスクでの良好な成績を達成し、事前学習済みモーションバックボーンの有効性を示した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2611.11554.tldr_en: Kinematic Action Models (KAMs), a paradigm that treats whole-body motion as a direct pretraining target and uses a pretrained motion generator as the primary action-generation backbone, is introduced, providing initial evidence for motion generation as a complementary foundation for humanoid action learning.

2611.11529.title: Data Manipulation Attacks Against Machine Learning Integrated Cyber-Physical Systems
2611.11529.abstract: There is a well-established body of work demonstrating that individual machine learning (ML) algorithms can be manipulated or deceived. However, in many real-world systems, multiple ML algorithms are composed to enable automated decision-making, particularly in Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS). Often such systems use a composition of vision, planning, and other ML models to affect their internal state and ultimate take actions in the physical world. While there is a huge literature on the (in)security of ML algorithms, it is not immediately clear how an attacker might leverage their ability to trick individual learners when attacking the composition as a whole. We develop methods for creating an attack policy (a mapping from state to attack) for a data-manipulating attacker affecting a CPS or other state-machine-based AI compositions. We describe our framework, a basic threat model and corresponding methods for computing an optimal attack policy, as well as planned extensions. The goal of this work-in-progress paper is to stimulate conversation and forge new collaborations regarding the security of compositional learning.

llm.title_ja: 機械学習を統合したサイバー物理システムに対するデータ操作攻撃
llm.tldr_ja: サイバー物理システム（CPS）や状態機械ベースのAI構成において、個々の学習器を騙す能力を持つ攻撃者がどのようにシステム全体を攻撃できるかを評価するための攻撃ポリシー計算手法を開発した。
llm.problem: 個々の機械学習アルゴリズムの脆弱性は広く研究されているが、複数のMLモデルが組み合わされたCPS全体に対する攻撃手法は十分に解明されていない。
llm.method: 状態から攻撃へのマッピングを行う攻撃ポリシーを作成するための基本的な脅威モデルと最適な攻撃ポリシーを計算する手法を開発した。
llm.result: コンポーザブルラーニングのセキュリティに関する議論を促進するための枠組みと脅威モデルを提示した（ワークインプログレス）。
llm.limitation: アイデアや枠組みの提案を主目的としたワークインプログレス論文である。
keywords_ja: サイバー物理システム
機械学習セキュリティ

2611.11529.tldr_en: Methods for creating an attack policy for a data-manipulating attacker affecting a CPS or other state-machine-based AI compositions are developed, as well as planned extensions.

2611.11521.title: K-PWM: Control-Oriented Structured Bilinear World Models under Partial Observation
2611.11521.abstract: World models learn internal simulators of environment dynamics for prediction, planning, and control, yet learning them from limited, noisy, and partial observations remains challenging. While much progress has focused on pixel-based observations, many physical systems instead provide vector-valued measurements that reveal only part of the underlying state. We introduce K-PWM, a probabilistic world model for prediction and control under partial observation. K-PWM couples Koopman-bilinear latent dynamics with a nonlinear observation decoder and performs probabilistic latent-state inference through the learned model via extended Kalman filtering and smoothing, without a separately trained inference network. Its bilinear structure enables exact propagation of the maintained Gaussian belief through the latent transition and efficient rollouts for uncertainty-aware model predictive path integral (MPPI) control. For training K-PWM, we present a generalized expectation conditional maximization (GECM) procedure with closed-form updates for the generators, noise covariances, and latent prior, complemented by gradient-based decoder learning. A Koopman-consistent initialization selects the latent dimension from data and initializes the action-dependent dynamics. With limited training data, K-PWM achieves lower long-horizon prediction error than the evaluated baselines on partially observed Gymnasium MuJoCo systems, while substantially reducing training time relative to the strongest prediction baseline. On high-dimensional MuJoCo Menagerie robots, it achieves competitive tracking accuracy with low per-step computation times, demonstrating potential for real-time deployment. These results support structured probabilistic dynamics as a data- and compute-efficient approach to world modeling and control under partial observation.

llm.title_ja: K-PWM：部分観測下における制御指向の構造化双線形世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: Koopman双線形潜在ダイナミクスと非線形観測デコーダを組み合わせ、拡張カルマンフィルタを用いて部分観測下での確率的予測と制御を行う世界モデルK-PWMを提案した。
llm.problem: 部分観測しか得られない制限された環境において、限られたデータとノイズから精度の高い内部シミュレータ（世界モデル）を学習することは困難である。
llm.method: Koopman双線形潜在ダイナミクスを非線形観測デコーダと結合し、拡張カルマンフィルタを用いた確率的潜在状態推論と一般化期待条件最大化（GECM）による学習手法を提案した。
llm.result: 部分観測されたGymnasium MuJoCoシステムにおいて、従来のベースラインよりも長いホライゾンの予測誤差を低減し、学習時間を大幅に短縮した。

2611.11521.tldr_en: K-PWM is introduced, a probabilistic world model for prediction and control under partial observation that achieves lower long-horizon prediction error than the evaluated baselines on partially observed Gymnasium MuJoCo systems, while substantially reducing training time relative to the strongest prediction baseline.

2611.11516.title: Breaking survivorship bias in driving world models
2611.11516.abstract: World models allow autonomous vehicles to imagine the consequences of candidate actions before execution, but their reliability depends on the futures represented in their training data. We identify a survivorship bias in driving world models: because the futures recorded in prevailing driving datasets almost always end safely, existing models often imagine benign outcomes even when a collision is imminent. We introduce a neutral world model (NWM) that learns both routine and safety-critical futures from a mixture of routine driving and real accident videos with a bounding-box-guided objective. The NWM more faithfully anticipates imminent collisions, while maintaining a low false collision rate and competitive generation quality in routine driving. We further use the model as an imagination engine for decision-making. Given multiple ego trajectories, the NWM predicts the future associated with each candidate, and a reward function evaluates these imagined outcomes before selecting an action. On challenging NAVSIM scenarios, this procedure selects the better trajectory more reliably than the baseline world model. Zero-shot experiments with real-world pedestrian dummy crossing data collected using an autonomous research vehicle further demonstrate transfer to unseen sensor observations. These results show that correcting survivorship bias enables world models to more faithfully reason about futures and support safety-critical decision-making in autonomous driving.

llm.title_ja: 自動運転世界モデルにおける生存者バイアスの打破
llm.tldr_ja: 通常の運転動画と実際の事故動画の混合データを用いて、衝突間近の危険な未来と日常的な未来の両方を学習する中立的世界モデル（NWM）を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の運転データセットは安全に終わる未来ばかり記録されているため、自動運転の世界モデルが差し迫った衝突時でも安全な結果を想像してしまう生存者バイアスが存在する。
llm.method: 日常運転と事故動画の混合データからバウンディングボックス誘導目的関数を用いて学習する中立的世界モデル（NWM）を開発した。
llm.result: NAVSIMシナリオにおいて、ベースライン世界モデルよりも信頼性高く優れた軌道を選択でき、実世界の歩行者ダミーデータへのゼロショット転移も実証した。

2611.11516.tldr_en: A neutral world model (NWM) is introduced that learns both routine and safety-critical futures from a mixture of routine driving and real accident videos with a bounding-box-guided objective and is used as an imagination engine for decision-making in autonomous driving.

2611.11509.title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
2611.11509.abstract: Recent studies of embodied agents based on frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) develop harness engineering around the MLLM, such as harnesses with post-trained policies and recursive self-improvement loops. Yet whether these additions exceed the native capability of the MLLM remains unexplored. We introduce SimplEvo to explore how far an MLLM can improve under direct control when it retains its execution experience in self-written text memories. It requires no weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information. The MLLM writes a coordinate-free task memory once from a single demonstration. Under a strict train-test protocol, it then creates a bounded working memory on training episodes only and refines it after each episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery. Both memories stay fixed at test time. On EBench, SimplEvo lifts the success rate (SR) of GPT-6-Astra under direct control from 46.7% to 81.7%, and tops the RoboDojo leaderboard with 69.63% SR and a score of 75.32. Compared with memories that also store past visual frames, SimplEvo reaches a similar SR with text memory alone while using fewer tokens. With its memories fixed, SimplEvo also generalizes to unseen layouts and randomized scene configurations. Moreover, the working memory transfers across models: written by GPT-6-Astra, it can be reused as is by weaker MLLMs and improve their performance without any adaptation of their own.

llm.title_ja: エピソードの振り返りと改善：身体性エージェントのためのシンプルなメモリ進化
llm.tldr_ja: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル（MLLM）の実行経験をテキストメモリとして保持・洗練させることで、重みの更新や事後学習を行わずに直接制御下での性能を大幅に向上させる手法「SimplEvo」を提案する。
llm.problem: フロンティアMLLMを用いた身体性エージェントのハーネス工学において、追加の工夫がMLLM自体のネイティブな能力を超えられるかは未解明であった。
llm.method: 座標系に依存しないタスクメモリをデモから1度だけ書き込み、訓練エピソードのみで作業メモリを構築・洗練させる「SimplEvo」を導入した。
llm.result: EBenchにおいてGPT-6-Astraの成功率を46.7%から81.7%に向上させ、RoboDojoリーダーボードで首位を獲得した。

2611.11509.tldr_en: SimplEvo is introduced to explore how far an MLLM can improve under direct control when it retains its execution experience in self-written text memories and can be reused as is by weaker MLLMs and improve their performance without any adaptation of their own.

2611.11500.title: ForeAct: Geometry-Guided Action Learning from World Representations
2611.11500.abstract: Robotic manipulation requires representations that capture both scene geometry and its evolution during interaction. Existing approaches have largely treated these two aspects separately. World action models capture such dynamics by coupling action prediction with future video generation, but their reliance on iterative diffusion or rectified-flow inference leads to high computational cost, while their representations lack explicit spatial structure. Explicitly modeling scene geometry typically requires auxiliary modules that increase both parameter count and computational cost. Conversely, geometry-centric policies primarily recover observed spatial structure and often lack explicit supervision for anticipating future geometric changes during interaction. To address these limitations, we introduce ForeAct, which repurposes a pretrained video world model as a single-pass representation backbone for low-latency control. ForeAct directly processes the clean latent of the current observation in one forward pass, eliminating future-frame synthesis and iterative denoising while retaining the backbone's pretrained spatiotemporal priors. Rather than introducing a separate geometry backbone, ForeAct uses learnable tokens supervised by next-frame relative depth to shape the shared video representation through bidirectional self-attention. This compact interface turns the spatial knowledge already encoded in the backbone into a future-aware representation for action generation, with little parameter overhead. The lightweight geometry readout is used only during training and removed at deployment, enabling low-latency, geometry-aware control without depth input or an external geometry backbone. Without additional large-scale pretraining, ForeAct achieves 96.6% average success on LIBERO, 63.5% on SimplerEnv-Bridge, and a 74.4% success rate across 90 real-world rollouts.

llm.title_ja: ForeAct: 表現からの幾何学誘導型行動学習
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みの動画世界モデルを単一パスの表現バックボーンとして再利用し、反復的な潜在空間の逆拡散や将来フレームの合成を行わずに低遅延で幾何学を考慮した制御を実現する「ForeAct」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のワールドアクションモデルは計算コストが高く、明示的な空間構造を欠いており、幾何学中心のポリシーは将来の変化に対する指導が不十分であった。
llm.method: 次フレームの相対深度で学習可能なトークンを監督し、双方向自己注意を通じて共有ビデオ表現を形成するForeActを開発した。
llm.result: 追加の大規模事前学習なしで、L...において平均96.6%の成功率を達成した。

2611.11500.tldr_en: ForeAct is introduced, which repurposes a pretrained video world model as a single-pass representation backbone for low-latency control, eliminating future-frame synthesis and iterative denoising while retaining the backbone's pretrained spatiotemporal priors.

2611.11489.title: Beyond Memory Limits: A Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Map Representation for Large-Scale 3D Autonomous Exploration
2611.11489.abstract: Autonomous UAV exploration is increasingly used for large-scale surveying and inspection in inaccessible or disaster-affected environments, where onboard memory and computational resources are often severely constrained. Most existing UAV exploration systems maintain globally queryable geometric map representations for motion planning and exploration decision-making, causing memory consumption and spatial-query costs to increase with the explored area. Robot-centric local mapping bounds dense-map memory and computation but discards global task context needed for long-horizon exploration.We present FLAVOR, a hierarchical spatio-temporal framework that confines dense metric geometry to a robot-centric local map while retaining compact global observation and task context. At the observation level, lightweight LiDAR-keyframe visibility records preserve ray-wise evidence for frontier reasoning. At the task level, unresolved frontiers beyond the local-map extent are retained as compact pending tasks associated with odometry anchors. A sparse topological graph connects these anchors through retained routes for future revisits.Upon returning to a task region, FLAVOR reconstructs the frontier and exploration viewpoint from observations, while the topological route is instantiated and validated against the current local map before execution. Dense-map capacity remains fixed as exploration expands, with exploration-dependent memory growth confined to compact observation and task context.FLAVOR achieves 31.98--41.88% shorter exploration time and a 94--99% smaller map memory footprint than the best baseline that completes all three simulated scenes. In real-world deployments, it reduces this footprint by 92.67% in the forest and 62.42% at the construction site relative to an explicit point-cloud ikd-tree while preserving long-term task continuity under constrained onboard resources.
2611.11489.comment: 16 pages, 12 figures, preprint submitted to Elsevier

llm.title_ja: メモリ制限を超えて：大規模3D自律探索のための階層型時空マップ表現
llm.tldr_ja: 高密度な局所幾何マップをロボット中心に限定しつつ、コンパクトな大域的観測とタスクコンテキストを保持することで、大規模環境の探索におけるメモリ消費と計算コストを劇的に削減する階層型時空フレームワーク「FLAVOR」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のUAV探索システムでは、大域的な幾何マップを維持するため、探索面積の拡大に伴いメモリ消費と空間クエリコストが増加する。
llm.method: LiDARキーフレームの可視性記録による局所マップと、未解決フロンティアをオドメトリアンカーに関連付けるスパーストポロジカルグラフを組み合わせたFLAVORを開発した。
llm.result: シミュレーションで最適なベースラインと比較して探索時間を31.98〜41.88%短縮し、マップのメモリフットプリントを94〜99%削減した。

2611.11489.tldr_en: FLAVOR is presented, a hierarchical spatio-temporal framework that confines dense metric geometry to a robot-centric local map while retaining compact global observation and task context while preserving long-term task continuity under constrained onboard resources.

2611.13000.title: PhysMoE: Fast Spatial Grounding with Single-Token Coordinate Representation in Modality-Decoupled VLMs
2611.13000.abstract: Embodied Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are backbones for robotic planning and manipulation. However, for coordinate prediction in grounding tasks, existing architectures suffer from two distinct bottlenecks: discrete tokenization disrupts spatial continuity with high decoding latency, while standard point regression fails on multi-contact affordances and irregularly shaped targets. To resolve these challenges, we propose PhysMoE, introducing three core contributions: (1) sharing lower layers for multimodal context while routing upper layers to specialized spatial (pixel) and linguistic (text) experts by physical modality, eliminating gradient interference; (2) encoding each coordinate as a single token by reusing the visual encoder's learned positional embeddings, injecting 2D spatial priors to natively align coordinates with visual features and ease training; and (3) differentiable Signed Distance Field (SDF) supervision on pointing, accommodating affordances and irregular geometries without costly mask decoders. Compared to the base model, PhysMoE achieves a 15.7% average gain and an 8.31x throughput speedup across 9 coordinate-based grounding benchmarks (trajectory, affordance, and localization), while preserving multimodal understanding and reasoning across 11 text-based embodied benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: PhysMoE: モダリティ分離型VLMにおける単一トークン座標表現を用いた高速な空間グラウンディング
llm.tldr_ja: 上位層を物理モダリティごとに専門家にルーティングし、2D空間事前分布を注入する単一トークン座標表現とSDF教師信号を用いるPhysMoEを提案し、空間グラウンディングの精度とスループットを大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 既存のVLMは、座標予測において空間連続性を損なう離散トークン化や、マルチコンタクトに対応できない点群回帰のボトルネックを抱えている。
llm.method: 下位層を共有しつつ上位層を空間・言語の専門家にルーティングし、単一トークンでの座標エンコーディングと微分可能なSDF教師信号を導入する。
llm.result: 9つの空間グラウンディングベンチマークで平均15.7%の精度向上と8.31倍のスループット向上を達成した。
keywords_ja: 空間グラウンディング

2611.13000.tldr_en: PhysMoE achieves a 15.7% average gain and an 8.31x throughput speedup across 9 coordinate-based grounding benchmarks (trajectory, affordance, and localization), while preserving multimodal understanding and reasoning across 11 text-based embodied benchmarks.

2611.11464.title: Off-Policy RL with Online Inference Tuning: My Solution to the CoRL 2026 RoboEval Challenge
2611.11464.abstract: The CoRL 2026 RoboEval challenge has eight bimanual tasks, and it ranks a policy not only on whether it succeeds but on how: every stage of the task, done safely, efficiently and with both arms in coordination, scored against human demonstrations. My solution has two parts. The generic part, carried over from my LeHome challenge solution, is off-policy RL on a $π_{0.5}$-based policy that is also its own value function. It is trained with AWR and RECAP on advantages of the exact official score, in a loop where every rollout is at the same time a Thompson-sampling trial of about 20 inference parameters. Out of the box, it took the policy to 0.85 RDS on held-out seeds in two days (and it was still very far from convergence). The competition-specific part adds data that local exploration cannot find: generated demonstrations that reach the full reward, and recovery episodes that start from the policy's own failures. The submitted policy reaches 0.990 RDS on held-out seeds and 0.987 on the official seeds.
2611.11464.comment: Technical report for the RoboEval Challenge at CoRL 2026. Code: https://github.com/IliaLarchenko/RoboEvalSolution ; checkpoint: https://huggingface.co/IliaLarchenko/RoboEvalSolution ; project page: https://ilialarchenko.com/projects/roboeval2026/

llm.title_ja: オンライン推論チューニングを用いたオフポリシー強化学習：CoRL 2026 RoboEvalチャレンジの解決策
llm.tldr_ja: CoRL 2026 RoboEvalチャレンジに向けて、価値関数でもあるπ0.5ベースのポリシーに対して正確な公式スコアの優位性を用いたオフポリシー強化学習と生成デモデータを適用し、高精度な両腕ロボット制御を実現した。
llm.problem: CoRL 2026 RoboEvalチャレンジにおいて、成功だけでなく安全性、効率性、両腕の協調を含めた総合的なタスク達成が求められていた。
llm.method: AWRとRECAPを用いたオフポリシー強化学習、20個の推論パラメータによるトンプソンサンプリング、および失敗からのリカバリエピソードを追加したデータ拡張を行った。
llm.result: 隠しシードにおいて0.990 RDS、公式シードにおいて0.987 RDSを達成した。
keywords_ja: 両腕マニピュレーション

2611.11438.title: When Coding Agents Get Arms: Safety Risks Across the Digital-Physical Boundary
2611.11438.abstract: Advances in spatial understanding have enabled frontier models to power coding agents that control a real robot arm zero-shot and end-to-end, without task-specific demonstrations or retraining. This brings two new safety challenges. First, the extensive knowledge of frontier models lets these agents perform tasks that earlier VLA and WAM paradigms could not, opening the door to new forms of capability misuse. Second, coding agents can access digital resources such as web pages and emails. Threats in these resources, such as indirect prompt injection, can carry over into the physical world when the agent controls a robot. We therefore introduce ArmedAgent, the first systematic benchmark to evaluate both risks for coding agents performing zero-shot robot control. It covers robustness, malicious use, and indirect injection across 36 tasks in 5 scenarios, evaluated in simulation and validated on a physical robot arm. A distinctive portion of the tasks target harmful behaviors that earlier VLA paradigms could not perform. Testing several frontier models, including GPT-6-Astra, under widely used agent frameworks, we find substantial safety risks in current systems.

llm.title_ja: コーディングエージェントが腕を持ったとき：デジタルと物理の境界を越えた安全性のリスク
llm.tldr_ja: フロンティアモデルを搭載したコーディングエージェントが実ロボットアームを直接制御する際の、能力の悪用や間接的なプロンプトインジェクションといった新たな安全上のリスクを体系的に評価するベンチマーク「ArmedAgent」を提案する。
llm.problem: 空間理解の進展によりコーディングエージェントがロボットを直接制御できるようになったが、機能の悪用やデジタル環境からの脅威が物理世界へ波及する危険性があった。
llm.method: 頑健性、悪用、間接的インジェクションをカバーする5つのシナリオ・36のタスクからなる初の体系的ベンチマーク「ArmedAgent」を構築した。
llm.result: GPT-6-Astraを含む複数のフロンティアモデルを用いたテストにより、現在のシステムにおける重大な安全上のリスクが明らかになった。
keywords_ja: コーディングエージェント
プロンプトインジェクション

2611.11438.tldr_en: ArmedAgent is introduced, the first systematic benchmark to evaluate both risks for coding agents performing zero-shot robot control and robustness, malicious use, and indirect injection across 36 tasks in 5 scenarios, evaluated in simulation and validated on a physical robot arm.

2611.11304.title: TransArt3D: From Two States to Articulated 3D Reconstruction with Video Transition Priors
2611.11304.abstract: Reconstructing interactable articulated assets from a few images is key to robotics and simulation, yet highly underconstrained. Existing optimization-based methods fit an articulated asset under a static 3D prior that scores each state independently, so per-state reconstruction errors leak into the estimated moving part and joint as false motion. Video diffusion models capture how objects move between states, but only implicitly in 2D. To this end, we present TransArt3D, an optimization-based framework that reconstructs an articulated 3D asset from two endpoint images by translating this video transition prior into explicit part structure and joint kinematics. It first lifts frames generated between the endpoints with a transition-coupled 3D consensus that applies the static 3D prior jointly across frames, stabilizing unchanging regions and initializing the parts and joint. A rectified-flow kinematic refinement then lets the video prior supervise a 3D motion field over the whole transition, while part assignment and a shared joint constrain the field throughout optimization, keeping per-state errors out of the articulation. Finally, a motion-aware canonical appearance fusion uses the recovered articulation to map both endpoint images onto one canonical surface, texturing regions that only one state reveals. On PartNet-Mobility, TransArt3D outperforms methods given the same two endpoints in geometry and joint accuracy, and surpasses methods given six observed states in articulated-state geometry, joint localization and appearance.

llm.title_ja: TransArt3D：ビデオ遷移事前知識を用いた2状態からの関節型3D再構築
llm.tldr_ja: 2枚の端点画像から、ビデオ拡散モデルの遷移事前知識を明示的なパーツ構造と関節運動学に変換することで、関節型3Dアセットを高精度に再構築する最適化ベースのフレームワーク「TransArt3D」を提案する。
llm.problem: 少数の画像からの関節型アセットの再構築は極めて制約が緩く、従来の静的3D事前知識に基づく手法では状態ごとの誤差が偽の動きとして混入していた。
llm.method: 遷移結合3Dコンセンサスによるフレーム間補間、整流フローによる運動学的洗練、およびモーション認識型正準外観融合を行うTransArt3Dを開発した。
llm.result: PartNet-Mobilityにおいて、同じ2枚の端点画像を入力された従来法よりも優れた幾何学的・関節精度を達成し、6つの状態を観測された従来法をも凌駕した。

2611.11304.tldr_en: TransArt3D is an optimization-based framework that reconstructs an articulated 3D asset from two endpoint images by translating this video transition prior into explicit part structure and joint kinematics, and outperforms methods given the same two endpoints in geometry and joint accuracy.

2611.11296.title: Single-Radar Bilateral 3D Near-Field Imaging for Mobile Robots
2611.11296.abstract: Mobile robots operating in homes need reliable 3D perception of nearby furniture and surrounding structures, yet recovering this information on both sides of the robot's path with a single forward-mounted millimeter-wave radar remains challenging because of near-field wavefront curvature, viewpoint-dependent target visibility, and limited elevation diversity. This paper presents a motion-assisted framework for reconstructing structures on both sides of a robot's trajectory. Our near-field model relates scene reflectivity to stepped-frequency multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) observations across frequencies and robot positions using spherical paths from transmitter (Tx) to scatterer to receiver (Rx). Bilateral Tx combining provides wideband directional weighting, while sliding-aperture back-projection coherently focuses the measurements using near-field propagation distances. Top-K power fusion combines local images with different visibility. The reconstruction provides lateral-forward support for multi-layer height extraction, followed by guarded adaptive height refinement using the original MIMO channels. Experiments in controlled, office/study, and corridor environments produce mean lateral-forward localization errors of 4.65, 5.63, and 5.98 cm, respectively, with peak-to-background ratios (PBRs) exceeding 13 dB. The framework recovers bilateral 3D scattering structure from one forward pass using a single radar, without relying on learned representations of the scene.

llm.title_ja: 移動ロボットのための単一レーダーによる両側3D近傍イメージング
llm.tldr_ja: 移動ロボットの単一の前方搭載ミリ波レーダーを用い、近傍波面曲率や視点依存の視認性の課題を克服して、ロボット軌道の両側にある構造物を再構築するモーション支援型フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 単一の前方搭載ミリ波レーダーを用いてロボットの移動経路の両側の構造物を復元することは、近傍波面の曲率や視野の制約から困難であった。
llm.method: 周波数とロボット位置を繋ぐ近傍野モデルを活用し、双方向Tx結合、スライディングアパチャー逆投影、トップKパワー融合を組み合わせたモーション支援型フレームワークを開発した。
llm.result: オフィスや回廊環境の実験において、平均の左右前方位置誤差が4.65〜5.98cm、PBRが13dBを超える精度で両側3D散乱構造を復元できた。

2611.11296.tldr_en: A motion-assisted framework for reconstructing structures on both sides of a robot's trajectory that recovers bilateral 3D scattering structure from one forward pass using a single radar, without relying on learned representations of the scene.

2611.11286.title: Cable construction effects on the lateral forces and wakes of helically stranded cables under oblique inflow
2611.11286.abstract: Helically stranded cables in aerial towing systems experience oblique inflow, but are often modeled as smooth cylinders, neglecting three-dimensional cross-stream coupling and surface texture. We perform large-eddy simulations and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition for a smooth cylinder and four stranded cables at four inclinations from $22.5^\circ$ to $90^\circ$, all stationary, with $Re \approx 1.0 \times 10^4$. Aerodynamic differences are governed mainly by cross-sectional symmetry and strand-scale groove depth. Force-source decomposition shows that surface pressure contributes 94.9%--98.3% of the mean normal force and dominates the mean lateral force. High-symmetry, quasi-circular envelopes maintain balanced circumferential pressure, whereas deep-grooved, low-symmetry tri-lobed geometries produce asymmetric separation and a persistent lateral pressure imbalance. In the wake, high-symmetry cables sustain spanwise-synchronized Karman shedding at moderate-to-high inclinations, concentrating fluctuation energy in a dominant low-rank mode. Deep grooves disrupt shedding coherence, deflect the recirculation zone laterally, and spread energy across broadband scales. Mean lateral force and lateral-force fluctuations are therefore decoupled: the quasi-circular $(1 \times 19)$ cable has minimal mean lateral force but strong periodic fluctuations, while the deep-grooved $(3 \times 7)$ cable has weak fluctuations but appreciable mean lateral force. These results support construction-dependent cable selection and aerodynamic load modeling.

llm.title_ja: 斜め流入下におけるヘリカルより線の側方力と後流に対するケーブル構造の影響
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模渦シミュレーションとスペクトル固有直交分解を用い、斜め流入を受けるヘリカルより線ケーブルの構造（溝の深さや対称性）が、平均側方力や後流の変動エネルギーに与える影響を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 空中けん引システムにおけるヘリカルより線ケーブルは斜め流入を受けるが、滑らかな円柱としてモデル化されることが多く、3次元の横断方向の結合や表面テクスチャが無視されていた。
llm.method: レイノルズ数約1.0×10^4の条件で、滑らかな円柱と4種類のより線ケーブルを対象に大型渦シミュレーション（LES）とSPOD解析を実施した。
llm.result: 表面圧力が高・低対称性や溝の深さに応じて平均側方力や変動を支配しており、準円形ケーブルと深溝付きケーブルで側方力の性質が異なることを示した。

2611.11242.title: DeepSoMo: Deformable Object Motion Estimation under Proprioceptive Partial Observability via Predictive Latent Dynamics
2611.11242.abstract: Estimating the motion of deformable bodies in soft robotics from proprioceptive sensing is challenging due to partial observability, as internal observations provide only indirect access to global motion, contact, and shape evolution. In such settings, instantaneous observations are insufficient, and accurate estimation requires temporally consistent latent representations. This paper studies deformable motion estimation under proprioceptive partial observability from a latent dynamics perspective. We argue that a key requirement for long-horizon estimation is latent temporal consistency, where latent states remain predictive of future observations. To this end, we present DeepSoMo, a learning-based framework that enforces predictive structure in latent dynamics through a self-supervised latent prediction constraint. We evaluate the approach in a canonical deformable dynamics setting using high-fidelity finite-element simulation as a controlled source of ground truth. Results demonstrate consistent improvements in trajectory estimation, orientation recovery, shape reconstruction, and contact inference over architecture-matched recurrent baselines.

llm.title_ja: DeepSoMo：予測型潜在ダイナミクスを通じた固有受容的部分観測下での変形体運動推定
llm.tldr_ja: 自己教師あり潜在予測制約を利用して潜在ダイナミクスに予測構造を強制することで、内部の固有受容的センシングのみから変形体の運動、接触、形状変化を高精度に推定する学習フレームワーク「DeepSoMo」を提案する。
llm.problem: ソフトロボティクスにおいて固有受容的センシングから変形体の運動を推定する際、内部観測が間接的な情報しか与えない部分観測性が課題となる。
llm.method: 自己教師ありの潜在予測制約により潜在空間の時間的整合性を強制する学習ベースのフレームワーク「DeepSoMo」を構築した。
llm.result: 高精度な有限要素法シミュレーションを用いた評価において、従来のリカレントベースラインと比較して軌道推定、姿勢復元、形状再構築、接触推論が一貫して向上した。

2611.11242.tldr_en: DeepSoMo is presented, a learning-based framework that enforces predictive structure in latent dynamics through a self-supervised latent prediction constraint and demonstrates consistent improvements in trajectory estimation, orientation recovery, shape reconstruction, and contact inference over architecture-matched recurrent baselines.

2611.11239.title: A Layer-wise Study of How Style Rewriting Breaks the Calibration of Zero-Shot LLM Fake-News Detectors
2611.11239.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly asked to judge whether a news article is true, and their stated confidence is often taken at face value. We test what happens to that confidence when an article's writing style, but not its facts, is manipulated, as in recent \emph{style attacks} on fake-news detectors. Tracing how the prediction and its confidence form layer by layer inside the network, we study three model families (LLaMA-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Mistral-7B) on three fake-news benchmarks, and find the same three patterns in every model--dataset pairing. First, on the original articles the models are competent and largely honest judges: they settle on an answer, briefly become overconfident, and then correct their confidence in the final layers. Second, style-rewritten articles break this self-correction: the models become far less accurate, under the strongest attack, worse than random guessing, yet remain just as confident, so they are \emph{confidently wrong} precisely when a warning is most needed. Third, nearly all of the damage comes from rewriting into sensational or emotionally charged styles, while sober, neutral rewrites leave the models' honesty largely intact. The practical implication is that an LLM's confidence about veracity cannot be trusted as a safety signal when an article's style may have been manipulated.

llm.title_ja: ゼロショットLLMフェイクニュース検出器のキャリブレーションをスタイル書き換えが破壊する仕組みの層別分析
llm.tldr_ja: 事実を変えずに文章の文体のみを操作するスタイル攻撃が、3つのモデルファミリーにおいてLLMの真偽判断の自己修正機能をどのように破壊し、モデルが誤った判断に対して過度な確信を持つようになるかを層別に分析した。
llm.problem: ニュースの真偽を判定する大規模言語モデル（LLM）の出力確信度が、文体の書き換えによってどのように変化するかは十分に解明されていなかった。
llm.method: LLaMA-3-8B、Qwen2.5-7B、Mistral-7Bの3つのモデルファミリーを対象に、3つのフェイクニュースベンチマークを用いて層ごとの予測と確信度の変化を追跡調査した。
llm.result: 原著記事では最終層で確信度を正しく修正できる一方で、煽情的なスタイルに書き換えられた記事に対してはモデルが「自信過剰に間違える」状態になることを明らかにした。
keywords_ja: フェイクニュース検出
モデルのキャリブレーション

2611.11239.tldr_en: Large language models' confidence about veracity cannot be trusted as a safety signal when an article's style may have been manipulated, and the practical implication is that an LLM's confidence about veracity cannot be trusted as a safety signal when an article's style may have been manipulated.

2611.12983.title: CAFE: Closed-Loop Autonomous Task Formulation and Execution without Instance-Specific Instructions
2611.12983.abstract: Scene-driven robot autonomy requires selecting tasks from observations as well as executing them. We study scene-driven task formulation and execution under predefined cleaning, safety, and storage/organization categories, without instance-specific goals or action sequences. CAFE maintains online memory of objects, functional zones, and execution states. A rule-guided Trigger-LLM admits formulation from accumulated evidence; Draft, Complete, and Audit propose goals, resolve execution details, and check dependencies. Outcomes update memory for correction and subsequent discovery. Evaluation in 12 AI2-THOR scenes compares three backbones and task-complexity tiers using coverage, constraint, and execution metrics. Tri-LLM records higher GCR scores than the evaluated baselines across three backbones and task-complexity tiers. Controls examine completion, auditing, zones, feedback, triggering, and prompt examples. LimoCobot traces illustrate storage, cleanup, and recovery from a failed grasp. The study examines how shared scene state connects task discovery to execution and outcome-driven revision.

llm.title_ja: CAFE: インスタンス固有の指示なしで動作する閉ループ自律タスク定式化と実行
llm.tldr_ja: インスタンス固有のゴールなしに、観測からタスクの選定と実行を行うオンライン記憶を持つフレームワークCAFEを提案し、AI2-THORシーンでの評価で高いGCRスコアを記録した。
llm.problem: シーン駆動型のロボット自律性において、インスタンス固有の指示なしで観察からタスクを選定し実行することが課題となっている。
llm.method: オンラインメモリを維持し、ルール誘導型のTrigger-LLMと複数のプロセス（Draft, Complete, Audit）でタスクの定式化と実行を行う。
llm.result: 12のAI2-THORシーンにおける評価で、Tri-LLMベースラインと比較してより高いGCRスコアを記録した。

2611.12983.tldr_en: The study examines how shared scene state connects task discovery to execution and outcome-driven revision and examines how shared scene state connects task discovery to execution and outcome-driven revision.

2611.11166.title: DexForesight: Grounding Dexterous Policies with Implicit Spatial Foresight
2611.11166.abstract: Dexterous manipulation requires rich spatial foresight over both the surrounding scene and the robot hand. Existing world-action models often acquire such predictive knowledge through explicit future prediction. We introduce DexForesight, a framework that learns spatial foresight implicitly by injecting dynamics-aware world representations into the latent space of a dexterous policy. During training, DexForesight learns an action-conditioned spatial world model from offline scene depth, kinematic hand geometry, and demonstration trajectories. The world model predicts 3D hand-point motion and visual feature changes, capturing both articulated hand dynamics and scene changes under demonstrated actions, including the motion of fingers occluded from the cameras. We then freeze the world model and align policy queries with its predictive world queries, transferring the learned spatial dynamics into policy latents and using them to condition action generation. At deployment, only the policy is retained, operating on RGB observations, language, and robot state without depth input or explicit future prediction. On 11 DexJoCo simulation tasks, DexForesight improves the overall success rate of the base policy from 49.4% to 60.5%. On three real-robot dexterous manipulation tasks, DexForesight achieves 58.3% success, compared with 50.0% for the strongest baseline.Project page https://dexforesight.github.io/

llm.title_ja: DexForesight：暗黙的な空間的先読みによる器用な操作方策の接地
llm.tldr_ja: オフラインのシーン深度や手の運動学データを基に、アクション条件付きの空間世界モデルを構築して方策の潜在空間に動的な予測表現を注入し、深度入力なしで器用なマニピュレーションを実現する「DexForesight」を提案する。
llm.problem: 器用なマニピュレーションには周囲のシーンとロボットハンドの双方に対する豊かな空間的先読みが必要だが、既存のワールドアクションモデルは明示的な将来予測に依存していた。
llm.method: 手の3D点群の動きや視覚的特徴の変化を予測する世界モデルを学習し、その予測クエリに方策のクエリをアライメントすることで空間ダイナミクスを方策に転移するDexForesightを開発した。
llm.result: 11のDexJoCoシミュレーションタスクでベースラインの成功率を49.4%から60.5%に向上させ、3つの実機器用操作タスクでも58.3%の成功率を達成した。

2611.11166.tldr_en: DexForesight is introduced, a framework that learns spatial foresight implicitly by injecting dynamics-aware world representations into the latent space of a dexterous policy by injecting dynamics-aware world representations into the latent space of a dexterous policy.

2611.11164.title: Tutorial: Vision-Based Formation Control with Differential-Drive Robots
2611.11164.abstract: This tutorial presents a step-by-step introduction to multi-robot formation control using differential- drive robots, an overhead camera, and Python. ArUco markers are used to estimate robot positions and orientations, while desired pairwise displacement vectors define a circular formation. By comparing measured and desired relative positions, the controller computes movement vectors that are converted into differential-drive wheel commands, with basic proximity-sensor-based obstacle avoidance. The tutorial guides readers through hardware and software setup, robot pose estimation, formation geometry, feedback control, system integration, and formation-error evaluation. Motivated by the need to bridge the gap between theoretical understanding and practical implementation in robotics education, we emphasize how mathematical concepts are translated into coordinated behaviors on physical robots. Although the implementation uses a specific robotic platform, the underlying perception and formation-control principles can be adapted to other differential-drive robots and simulation environments. The accompanying open-source GitHub repository provides the Python implementation, setup instructions, and demonstrations to support hands-on learning and further exploration of multi-robot systems.

llm.title_ja: チュートリアル：差動駆動ロボットを用いたビジョンベースのフォーメーション制御
llm.tldr_ja: オーバーヘッドカメラとArUcoマーカーを用いて差動駆動ロボットの相対位置を推定し、分散協調的な円形フォーメーション制御を実践的に学ぶためのステップバイステップのチュートリアルを提供する。
llm.problem: ロボット工学教育において、理論的な理解と物理的な実装の間のギャップを埋める実践的な教材の必要性があった。
llm.method: PythonとArUcoマーカーによる姿勢推定、相対位置の比較に基づくフィードバック制御、および障害物回避を組み合わせたシステムを構築し手順を解説した。
llm.result: 読者が数学的概念を物理ロボット上の協調行動へと翻訳し、多重ロボットシステムの学習を深められるオープンソースのGitHubリポジトリを提供した。
keywords_ja: フォーメーション制御

2611.11164.tldr_en: This tutorial presents a step-by-step introduction to multi-robot formation control using differential- drive robots, an overhead camera, and Python, and emphasizes how mathematical concepts are translated into coordinated behaviors on physical robots.

2611.11148.title: MOSU2: Long-range Navigation System with Multi-modal Scene Understanding
2611.11148.abstract: Robots that travel long distances through public outdoor spaces must do more than avoid obstacles: they must remain on terrain suited to their mobility and decide when to proceed, yield, or detour around pedestrians, cyclists, vehicles, traffic signals, and temporary restrictions. These decisions are difficult because their correctness often depends on how a scene evolves, such as whether an approaching car is slowing or a cyclist will cross the robot's path. Vision-language models (VLMs) can interpret such cues, but they reason over images that lack metric geometry and motion. Supplying this evidence at every step is too slow for real-time navigation, and hand-crafted triggers cannot anticipate the open-ended variety of outdoor situations. We present MOSU2, a long-range navigation system with two-stage trajectory selection, in which first-stage contextual reasoning determines when additional evidence is needed and what to retrieve. Only when an interaction remains unresolved does the first stage trigger the second stage to retrieve geometric and dynamic information and align it with scene context to make navigation decisions. Building on MOSU, MOSU2 follows routes from GPS-based route planning and filters candidate trajectories through multi-modal traversability analysis before selecting a trajectory to move the robot. In real-world experiments spanning stop gestures, construction sites, crosswalks, and roads shared with vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians, MOSU2 raises mean navigation success from 61.8% to 94.2% and condition-detection accuracy from 72.2% to 91.4% over its single-image predecessor, at about 2.2 times its mean decision latency. Project website: https://jinggm.github.io/mosu2/

llm.title_ja: MOSU2：マルチモーダルシーン理解を備えた長距離ナビゲーションシステム
llm.tldr_ja: 第一段階の文脈推論により追加の幾何学的・動的情報の取得要否を判断し、必要な場合のみ第二段階で詳細情報を取得してマルチモーダルな通行可能性解析を行うことで、屋外での長距離ナビゲーション性能を大幅に向上させる「MOSU2」を提案する。
llm.problem: 屋外の公共スペースを長距離移動するロボットにおいて、歩行者や交通信号などの状況変化に対する動的な判断は、単一画像ベースのVLMでは幾何学や運動情報の不足により困難であった。
llm.method: 2段階の軌道選択を採用し、GPSルートに沿ってマルチモーダル通行可能性分析により候補軌道をフィルタリングするMOSU2を開発した。
llm.result: 実世界の実験において、前身システムと比較して平均ナビゲーション成功率を61.8%から94.2%に、条件検出精度を72.2%から91.4%に向上させた。

2611.11148.tldr_en: MOSU2 is presented, a long-range navigation system with two-stage trajectory selection, in which first-stage contextual reasoning determines when additional evidence is needed and what to retrieve, and only when an interaction remains unresolved does the first stage trigger the second stage to retrieve geometric and dynamic information.

2611.11136.title: From Game Generation to Game Playing: Fully Automated Ability Training for Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.11136.abstract: Training vision-language-action (VLA) models to follow gameplay instructions across diverse games is limited by the cost of collecting demonstrations. We introduce a framework that automatically generates game environments and expert demonstrations. An LLM-powered agent uses game-building tools to construct executable environments and tasks targeting specified skills. Programmatic experts then use privileged simulator state to generate aligned instructions, rendered observations, and keyboard and mouse actions. We train our game policy, Script2Play, by post-training a 4B vision-language model with behavior cloning on 150.3 hours of synthetic Minecraft and Roblox gameplay, without human gameplay demonstrations or reinforcement learning. Evaluation on multiple public game benchmarks demonstrates that Script2Play follows gameplay instructions effectively and generalizes across game engines, highlighting the effectiveness of targeted synthetic supervision.

llm.title_ja: ゲーム生成からゲームプレイへ：ビジョン・言語・行動モデルのための完全自動化された能力トレーニング
llm.tldr_ja: LLMベースのエージェントとプログラムによる専門家を利用してゲーム環境と専門家のデモデータを完全自動で生成し、人間のデモンストレーションなしでVLAモデルを事後学習させるフレームワーク「Script2Play」を提案する。
llm.problem: 多様なゲーム環境にわたってゲームプレイの指示に従うVLAモデルの訓練は、デモンストレーション収集のコストによって制限されていた。
llm.method: LLMエージェントによるゲーム・タスクの構築と、シミュレータの特権状態を利用したインストラクション・画像のレンダリング・行動の自動生成を経て、4Bのビジョン言語モデルを模倣学習で事後学習させるScript2Playを開発した。
llm.result: MinecraftやRobloxの合成ゲームプレイ150.3時間のデータを用いた訓練により、ゲームエンジンをまたいで指示に効果的に従うことができることを示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.11136.tldr_en: Evaluation on multiple public game benchmarks demonstrates that Script2Play follows gameplay instructions effectively and generalizes across game engines, highlighting the effectiveness of targeted synthetic supervision.

2611.11131.title: CrossLiDAR: Controllable Multi-Sensor LiDAR Sequence Generation
2611.11131.abstract: High-fidelity LiDAR simulation remains a bottleneck for scalable development and validation of autonomous systems. Existing generators can synthesize realistic scans, but they are typically constrained to a single sensor configuration, offer limited control over structure and geometry, and drift in long-horizon 4D generation. We present CrossLiDAR, a unified transformer-based framework capable of generating controllable and spatio-temporally consistent multi-sensor LiDAR sequences. Our approach leverages a rectified flow objective with a Multi-Modal Diffusion Transformer (MM-DiT) backbone, within a compact latent space of range images. To support multiple LiDAR sensors, an Inter-sensor Module enables interaction across sensors, while a ControlNet-style branch provides structural conditioning (e.g., BEV priors or 3D bounding boxes). For modeling the temporal consistency, CrossLiDAR generates short $N$-frame sequences and extends them autoregressively to improve long-horizon coherence. Our model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving an average improvement of 29.56\% in JSD and 15.36\% in MMD evaluated on nuScenes and the Waymo Dataset. CrossLiDAR bridges the gap to modern autonomous-driving simulation by enabling calibration-consistent multi-sensor LiDAR rollouts over long horizons for controllable, scenario-based testing.

llm.title_ja: CrossLiDAR：制御可能なマルチセンサーLiDARシーケンス生成
llm.tldr_ja: 範囲画像のコンパクトな潜在空間内で整流フロー目的関数とMM-DiTバックボーンを用い、センサー間モジュールと構造的条件付けによって長期間かつ整合性のあるマルチセンサーLiDARシーケンスを生成する「CrossLiDAR」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のLiDAR生成手法は単一のセンサー構成に制限されており、構造や幾何学の制御が限定的で、長期間の4D生成でドリフトが発生するという課題があった。
llm.method: マルチモーダル拡散Transformer（MM-DiT）とセンサー間モジュールを組み合わせ、ControlNetスタイルの構造条件付けと自己回帰的な長期間拡張を行うCrossLiDARを開発した。
llm.result: nuScenesおよびWaymoデータセットにおいて、JSDで平均29.56%、MMDで15.36%の改善を達成し、最先端のベースラインを大きく上回った。

2611.11127.title: From Festival Video to the Stage: A Sim-to-Real Ladder for Long-Horizon Expressive Whole-Body Dance on a Commercial Humanoid
2611.11127.abstract: We present a pipeline for transferring Awa Odori, a traditional Japanese festival dance, from monocular video to a commercial Unitree G1 EDU humanoid. The pipeline combines human mesh recovery, kinematic retargeting, reinforcement learning for motion tracking in simulation, and onboard deployment via ONNX. Training ran on a single RTX 5070 GPU. An eleven-version deployment ladder evaluated on hardware examines three interventions. We detect and repair silent corruption of deployment artifacts, model state-estimator drift during training, and edit the reference motion to support stable execution and a controlled ending. The final policies achieved three consecutive rope-free completions of a 43-second routine, a 46-second performance with automatic handoff, and a continuous 9.7-minute rope-free performance composed from the captured motion. In a live handover, a single remote request let the robot start from and return to the manufacturer's walking controller on stage, with a measured torque-free window of 45-140 ms. We report the training dynamics and hardware outcomes and discuss failure boundaries involving compliant flooring and occlusion in monocular capture.
2611.11127.comment: 19 pages, 12 figures. Four supplementary videos are linked in the manuscript

llm.title_ja: フェスティバルビデオからステージへ：商用ヒューマノイドでの長時間の表現力豊かな全身ダンスのためのシム2リアル梯子
llm.tldr_ja: 単眼ビデオから阿波踊りのモーションを抽出し、人体のメッシュ復元、運動学リターゲット、強化学習によるシミュレーションでの追従を経て商用Unitree G1ヒューマノイドに実装するパイプラインを提案する。
llm.problem: 単眼ビデオからの伝統的なダンスの抽出と、商用ヒューマノイドロボットへの長時間の動的動作のシム2リアル転移には、状態推定のドリフトや物理的制約への対応という課題があった。
llm.method: 11段階のデプロイメント梯子（展開アーティファクトの修復、状態推定ドリフトのモデル化、参照モーションの編集など）を構築し、ONNXを用いてオンボードで実行した。
llm.result: 43秒のルーティンの3回連続のロープなし完了や、自動ハンドオフを含む46秒のパフォーマンス、9.7分間の連続パフォーマンスを達成した。
llm.limitation: 床面の柔軟性や単眼キャプチャにおけるオクルージョンに起因する失敗境界が存在する

2611.11127.tldr_en: A pipeline for transferring Awa Odori, a traditional Japanese festival dance, from monocular video to a commercial Unitree G1 EDU humanoid using human mesh recovery, kinematic retargeting, reinforcement learning for motion tracking in simulation, and onboard deployment via ONNX is presented.

2611.11123.title: HARP-Bench: Benchmarking Robot Manipulation Around Active Humans
2611.11123.abstract: Recent robot manipulation benchmarks have enabled systematic evaluation of general-purpose robot policies across diverse objects, scenes, instructions, and embodiments. However, most existing benchmarks still assume that the robot is the only active agent and that task semantics are determined primarily by the instruction and object state. This assumption overlooks a common source of real-world variation: humans actively sharing the workspace. In such settings, humans may reveal an implicit goal, complete part of the task, temporarily change object availability, or constrain safe robot motion while working nearby. We introduce HARP-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating robot manipulation policies in workspaces shared with active humans. HARP-Bench treats human activity as part of the manipulation problem, rather than as background scene variation. It organizes human-present manipulation into four conditions: Cueing, Contribution, Interruption, and Co-presence. These conditions are instantiated through everyday manipulation tasks, including paired human-present variants for controlled comparison with standard manipulation. HARP-Bench also provides a demonstration-generation pipeline for dynamic human-present settings. We evaluate VLA models, imitation-learning methods, and heuristic policies on HARP-Bench. Human-present variations challenge current policies, and higher task success does not consistently improve safety. Quantitative failure analysis identifies manipulation and recovery as the dominant remaining challenges. Training with HARP-Bench demonstrations improves human-present performance in simulation. A real-world study on one task family shows improved performance under human contribution, but not interruption, providing initial evidence of the data's utility and identifying limits of transfer. Code is available at https://github.com/UMass-Embodied-AGI/harp.

llm.title_ja: HARP-Bench：活動的な人間の周囲におけるロボットマニピュレーションのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 作業スペースを共有する人間を背景の変動ではなくマニピュレーション問題の一部として扱い、キュューイング、貢献、中断、同居の4つの条件でロボット方策を評価するベンチマーク「HARP-Bench」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のマニピュレーションベンチマークの多くはロボットのみが能動的エージェントであると仮定しており、作業スペースを共有するアクティブな人間がもたらす多様性を考慮していなかった。
