llm.method: 日常的なマニピュレーションタスクを用いた4つの条件（キューイング、貢献、中断、同居）を定義し、動的な人間共存環境に対応するデモンストレーション生成パイプラインを備えたHARP-Benchを構築した。
llm.result: VLAモデルや模倣学習手法の評価により、人間がいる状況でのタスクが現在のポリシーにとって大きな挑戦であり、高いタスク成功率が必ずしも安全性の向上に直結しないことを示した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2611.11123.tldr_en: This work introduces HARP-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating robot manipulation policies in workspaces shared with active humans, and organizes human-present manipulation into four conditions: Cueing, Contribution, Interruption, and Co-presence.

2611.11098.title: Efficient VLA Inference via Retrieval-Based Speculation and Hardware Acceleration
2611.11098.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to understand and execute complex instructions, but their autoregressive (AR) action generation introduces significant latency on resource-constrained robotic platforms. Speculative decoding can accelerate AR-based inference by parallelizing action generation and verification; however, existing approaches rely on costly draft models, which are inefficient on edge platforms. In this paper, we propose Zora, a hardware-software co-design framework for accelerating AR-based VLA inference. Specifically, Zora introduces a lightweight retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based draft model that exploits robotic dynamics without additional neural draft models. We further reduce batch verification overhead through a kinematics-guided action-acceptance strategy and a KV-cache-sharing attention mechanism. To address the retrieval overhead introduced by RAG-based drafting, we co-design dedicated hardware support, Zora core, to address the memory irregularity in RAG-based drafting. We evaluate Zora on four VLA models with the LIBERO benchmark. Zora retains comparable accuracy while achieving up to 3.4$\times$ speedup with software-only optimization and up to 7.6$\times$ speedup with hardware support over GPUs.

llm.title_ja: 検索ベースの推測とハードウェアアクセラレーションによる効率的なVLA推論
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットダイナミクスを活用する軽量なRAGベースのドラフトモデルと専用のハードウェアアクセラレーションを組み合わせることで、リソースの限られたロボットプラットフォーム上でVLAモデルの自己回帰推論を高速化する「Zora」を提案する。
llm.problem: ビジョン・言語・行動（VLA）モデルの自己回帰的なアクション生成は、リソースの限られたロボットプラットフォーム上で重大なレイテンシを引き起こす。
llm.method: RAGベースの軽量ドラフトモデル、運動学誘導型のアクション受入戦略、KVキャッシュ共有アテンション機構を導入し、専用ハードウェアコア（Zora core）と協調設計した。
llm.result: LIBEROベンチマークを用いた4つのVLAモデルの評価において、ソフトウェア最適化のみで最大3.4倍、ハードウェア支援により最大7.6倍の高速化を達成しつつ、精度を維持した。
keywords_ja: ハードウェアアクセラレーション

2611.11098.tldr_en: Zora is proposed, a hardware-software co-design framework for accelerating AR-based VLA inference that introduces a lightweight retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based draft model that exploits robotic dynamics without additional neural draft models and reduces batch verification overhead through a kinematics-guided action-acceptance strategy and a KV-cache-sharing attention mechanism.

2611.11090.title: Large-Scale Hierarchical Decision-Making in Robot Control via ADMM
2611.11090.abstract: Sparse hierarchical nonlinear programming (SH-NLP) based on the $\ell_0$-norm provides a powerful framework for integrated, efficient hierarchical decision-making in robot kinematic control, for example in the presence of a large set of possible end-effector candidate locations. While Sequential Sparse Hierarchical Quadratic Programming (S-SHQP) with interior-point method based SHQP sub-problem solvers exploit the hierarchical, sparse structure of such problems, they are less amenable to effective warm-starting between subsequent, coherent control steps. In this work, we formulate an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) to efficiently solve related SHQP sub-problems. We introduce efficient substitutions for auxiliary variables representing $\ell_0$-norm surrogates. The solver efficiently handles separable decision functions by evaluating linear algebra expressions in the appropriate order. Results in large-scale kinematic and dynamic control show reduced computation times of up to 23.5% compared with a structure-exploiting interior-point method in low- to moderate-accuracy regimes. Furthermore, hierarchical decision-making is extended to whole-body dynamic control for humanoid walking, where the need for high-accuracy solutions is highlighted.

llm.title_ja: ADMMを用いたロボット制御における大規模階層型意思決定
llm.tldr_ja: l0ノルムに基づくスパース階層型非線形プログラミングのサブ問題を効率的に解くために、交互方向乗数法（ADMM）を定式化し、大規模な運動学および動的制御において計算時間を大幅に削減した。
llm.problem: 従来の逐次スパース階層二次計画法（S-SHQP）の内点法ソルバーは、連続する制御ステップ間での効果的なウォームスタートがあまり容易ではなかった。
llm.method: l0ノルムの代替変数に対する効率的な置換を導入し、分離可能な決定関数を適切な順序の線形代数式評価で処理するADMMベースのソルバーを開発した。
llm.result: 大規模な運動学・動的制御の実験において、構造を活かした内点法と比較して、低〜中精度レジメで最大23.5%の計算時間削減を実現した。

2611.11090.tldr_en: An Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) is formulated to efficiently solve related SHQP sub-problems and efficient substitutions for auxiliary variables representing $\ell_0$-norm surrogates are introduced.

2611.11089.title: Control-Aware Command Generation for Asynchronous Control and Action Inference with Vision-Based Policies towards Fast Execution
2611.11089.abstract: Vision-based control policies, including vision-language-action models, have enabled robots to perform increasingly complex tasks. However, their execution speed is often limited by the high computational cost of action inference. In this work, we investigate what can be achieved at the control level without modifying the underlying policy learning process. We introduce an asynchronous inference and control framework that enables fast task execution while maintaining smooth and stable robot motions. By formulating the generation of continuous target positions from discontinuous model predictions as a tracking control problem, our method makes asynchronous inference practical for real robots. We further accelerate execution through adaptive action skipping based on the variance of predicted positions. Experiments with Action Chunking Transformer and OpenVLA-OFT on a bimanual robot demonstrate substantial speedups while preserving high task success rates.
2611.11089.comment: 8th Robot Learning Workshop: Is Physical AI Going Zero-Shot? at NeurIPS 2026

llm.title_ja: 高速実行に向けたビジョンベース方策のための非同期制御・行動推論のための制御考慮型コマンド生成
llm.tldr_ja: ポリシー学習プロセスを変更することなく、不連続な予測モデル出力を追跡制御問題として定式化し、適応的なアクションスキップを組み合わせることで非同期推論を実ロボットで実用化するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: ビジョンベースの制御方策やVLAモデルはタスクの複雑さを向上させたが、行動推論の計算コストが高く実行速度が制限されていた。
llm.method: 連続的な目標位置の生成を追跡制御問題として定式化し、予測位置の分散に基づく適応型アクションスキップによって実行を加速する非同期推論・制御フレームワークを導入した。
llm.result: 両腕ロボットを用いたAction Chunking TransformerとOpenVLA-OFTの実験により、高いタスク成功率を維持しながら大幅な高速化を実現した。

2611.11089.tldr_en: This work introduces an asynchronous inference and control framework that enables fast task execution while maintaining smooth and stable robot motions, and formulates the generation of continuous target positions from discontinuous model predictions as a tracking control problem.

2611.11087.title: SoftPAT3D: Physics-Augmented Text-to-3D Scene Generation with Deformables
2611.11087.abstract: We present SoftPAT3D, a physics-augmented framework for text-to-3D scene generation in which deformable objects, such as cloth, stuffed toys and ropes, are generated as physically valid, simulation-ready bodies and placed in intersection-free contact with the furniture that supports them, with one another and with themselves. Existing physics-augmented pipelines simulate rigid bodies only and cannot accommodate a generated deformable object, which text-to-3D generation returns as a geometrically invalid mesh, sometimes self-intersecting, that has no rest shape, no material model and no admissible initial state. These are the inputs a deformable simulation requires, and we construct each from information already in the pipeline. The rest shape comes from how the object is manufactured rather than from the generated physically inconsistent deformed configuration, and a material library assigns each deformable object its initial elastic parameters, which can then be optimized. The occluded support is regenerated and converted into a watertight collision mesh, each object is released from an optimizable placement above the supporting part that the prompt specifies, and the complete scene is driven to static equilibrium under one unified contact model, with completion verified by geometric checks and a vision-language model. When a scene fails the prompt, a grid search over placements corrects it, and the adjoint of a differentiable simulation of the same contact energy reaches the targets the grid does not, places several bodies jointly and recovers and optimizes material parameters. Multi-body scenes equilibrate in a single simulation, and the pipeline also runs from the text prompt alone. On all sixty-five prompts, SoftPAT3D produces no undesired interpenetration of any kind, whereas every other system does, and its scenes directly support scene editing and robotic manipulation.

llm.title_ja: SoftPAT3D: 変形可能オブジェクトを伴う物理拡張型Text-to-3Dシーン生成
llm.tldr_ja: 布やぬいぐるみなどの変形可能オブジェクトを物理的に妥当かつシミュレーション可能な状態で生成し、交差のない接触を維持して家具や他のオブジェクトと配置する物理拡張型フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 従来のテキストからの3D生成パイプラインは剛体のみをシミュレートし、変形可能オブジェクトの幾何学的不整合や接触の未解決に対応できない。
llm.method: 生成されたメッシュから復元形状や材質を構築し、衝突メッシュの再生成と最適化可能な初期配置を経て、接触モデルで静的平衡を達成する。
llm.result: 65個のすべてのプロンプトにおいて、望ましくない相互貫通のないシーンの生成に成功した。
keywords_ja: 変形可能オブジェクト
物理シミュレーション

2611.11087.tldr_en: SoftPAT3D, a physics-augmented framework for text-to-3D scene generation in which deformable objects are generated as physically valid, simulation-ready bodies and placed in intersection-free contact with the furniture that supports them, with one another and with themselves.

2611.11085.title: ObjectWorld: Scaling Object-Centric World Models with A Large-Scale 3D Full-Object Flow Dataset
2611.11085.abstract: Generative world modeling from large-scale visual data offers a promising path toward scalable robot manipulation. This calls for an intermediate representation that can be supervised at scale and remains actionable for downstream control. We propose 3D full-object flow, an object-centric motion representation that assigns dense 3D trajectories to points across the complete surface of a target object, including its occluded regions. By extending visible-surface object flow to the full object geometry, this representation makes complete object motion explicit and applies uniformly to both rigid and deformable objects. To realize the potential of this representation at scale, we introduce a 1210-hour full-object flow dataset that addresses the scarcity of large-scale supervision for complete 3D object motion. The dataset integrates diverse real-world videos and physical simulations, with a scalable annotation pipeline for recovering full-object motion from real-world observations and quality metrics for systematically assessing annotation quality. We then train a world model that takes an image and a task description as input and predicts dense full-object flow over the reconstructed object geometry. Experiments show reliable annotation quality, data-scalable flow prediction, and effective downstream manipulation across novel scenes and robot embodiments. Project website with additional results and videos: https://nus-lins-lab.github.io/ObjectWorld/.

llm.title_ja: ObjectWorld: 大規模3D全オブジェクトフローデータセットを用いたオブジェクト中心型世界モデルのスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 隠蔽領域を含むオブジェクト表面全体の点に高密度の3D軌跡を割り当てる表現「3Dフルオブジェクトフロー」を提案し、多様なデータからなる大規模データセットとそれを用いた世界モデルを構築した。
llm.problem: 大規模な視覚データからの生成的世界モデルには、大規模に監督可能で下流の制御に活用できる中間表現が不足している。
llm.method: 隠蔽領域を含む完全なオブジェクト表面の3D軌跡を定義する3Dフルオブジェクトフロー表現を導入し、実世界動画と物理シミュレーションを統合した1210時間のデータセットとそれを用いた予測モデルを構築した。
llm.result: 信頼性の高いアノテーション品質、データスケーラブルなフロー予測、および新しいシーンやロボット実機における効果的な下流マニピュレーションを実現した。

2611.11085.tldr_en: 3D full-object flow is proposed, an object-centric motion representation that assigns dense 3D trajectories to points across the complete surface of a target object, including its occluded regions, by extending visible-surface object flow to the full object geometry.

2611.11050.title: Floquet-Parameterized Koopman-MPC for Tracking Periodic Orbits
2611.11050.abstract: Designing real-time control for nonlinear systems to track periodic orbits can be challenging, especially for complex and coupled dynamical systems (e.g., tethered kites), where the true model parameters are hard to obtain. To address this, we propose a physics-informed Koopman learning approach that incorporates periodic-orbit stability directly into the learned linear predictor. The approach combines the underlying periodic structure of the dynamics along with periodic state-input trajectory data to learn physically consistent linear predictors (in lifted/observable space). We leverage Floquet theory, which studies the stability of periodic orbits in nonlinear systems, to obtain the periodic stability information of a given orbit via a monodromy matrix (i.e., the state transition matrix over an entire period). Subsequently, we impose open-loop monodromy constraints to learn Floquet-parameterized linear predictors using a least-squares Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (EDMD) formulation, thereby constraining the search space and aiding in Koopman learning. We then utilize these linear predictors to design a model predictive control (MPC) law for tracking periodic references. Finally, we evaluate the designed framework on a cartpole system under periodic forcing and compare it against a purely data-driven baseline.

llm.title_ja: 周期軌道追従のためのフロケパラメータ化Koopman-MPC
llm.tldr_ja: 周期軌道の安定性を学習済み線形予測器に直接組み込む物理情報に基づくKoopman学習アプローチを提案し、モデル予測制御により周期参照の追従を実現する。
llm.problem: 複雑で連成した非線形システムにおいて、真のモデルパラメータの取得が困難であり、周期軌道を追従するリアルタイム制御の設計が難しい。
llm.method: フロケ理論を活用してモノドロミー行列から周期安定性を取得し、拡張動的モード分解（EDMD）定式化を用いてフロケパラメータ化された線形予測器を学習し、MPCを設計する。
llm.result: 周期強制を受けるカートポールシステムにおいて評価され、純粋なデータ駆動型ベースラインと比較して有効性を示した。

2611.11023.title: Where Should Models Run? A Collaborative Inference Framework for Embodied Intelligence in 6G
2611.11023.abstract: Embodied intelligence systems rely on fast and reliable inference to enable real-time perception, reasoning, and control. Recent advances in large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) models, including Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, have significantly enhanced the capabilities of embodied agents in complex environments. However, deploying these models remains challenging due to the limited computational resources and energy budgets of robotic platforms. A fundamental question is where inference should be executed. Collaborative inference, which partitions models across end devices, edge servers, and the cloud, has emerged as a promising solution. Yet determining the optimal partitioning point remains an open problem, as it depends on wireless network conditions, model structure, and privacy requirements. This article reviews the state of the art in collaborative inference for embodied intelligence and proposes an edge-centric framework in which the edge coordinates model partitioning and execution. Through both simulation and real-world experiments over WiFi and 5G networks, we demonstrate that the optimal partitioning strategy varies with network conditions and model structure. We further identify latency-minimizing partition points for ResNet-101, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and OpenVLA-7B in collaborative inference between NVIDIA Jetson Nano or AGX Xavier devices and an AGX Thor edge server under varying wireless conditions. Finally, we discuss the future directions for collaborative inference in 6G-empowered embodied intelligence systems.

llm.title_ja: モデルはどこで実行すべきか：6Gにおける身体性知能のための協調推論フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: エンドデバイス、エッジサーバー、クラウド間でモデルを分割する協調推論に焦点を当て、エッジがモデルの分割と実行を調整するエッジ中心型フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットプラットフォームの限られた計算資源とエネルギー予算のため、大規模AIモデル（LLMやVLAなど）のデプロイが困難である。
llm.method: 無線ネットワーク条件、モデル構造、プライバシー要件に応じて最適な分割点を決定するエッジ中心型フレームワークを提案し、Wi-Fiと5G環境で評価する。
llm.result: 最適な分割戦略はネットワーク条件とモデル構造によって異なり、各種デバイスとサーバー間の協調推論における遅延最小化パーティションを特定した。
keywords_ja: エッジコンピューティング

2611.11023.tldr_en: This article reviews the state of the art in collaborative inference for embodied intelligence and proposes an edge-centric framework in which the edge coordinates model partitioning and execution and demonstrates that the optimal partitioning strategy varies with network conditions and model structure.

2611.11011.title: Learning Actionable Information Landscapes for Multimodal Active Sensing in Hawkmoths
2611.11011.abstract: Animals integrate information across sensory modalities to guide exploration, suggesting that they maintain internal estimates of where actions are expected to reduce uncertainty. However, how such action-conditioned information maps are learned from multimodal sensory experience remains unclear, as previous studies have been largely confined to unimodal sensing frameworks. We introduce a multimodal predictive-coding framework for learning uncertainty-reduction maps from visual and mechanosensory observations in hawkmoth flower interaction tasks. A variational generative model trained on simulated environments recovers modality-specific information landscapes over the action space, capturing how visual patterns, surface geometry, and mechanosensory cues shape the value of exploratory actions. These learned maps are consistent with several features of hawkmoth behavior, including nonzero tracking offsets, probing along visual patterns, and geometry-dependent exploration. Applying the model to behavioral data from flower tracking and nectary search, we find that natural trajectories tend to occupy regions of high uncertainty reduction in these learned maps. Building on these observations, we develop an uncertainty-gated lexicographic algorithm that switches between information gathering and reward exploitation based on perceptual uncertainty. In nectary search, uncertainty gating improves learning relative to exploit-only, $ε$-greedy, fixed-time, and uncertainty-calibrated non-lexicographic controls, with better generalization and robustness to sensory and curvature shifts. These results link information landscapes learned through generative modeling to biological sensing and embodied exploration.

llm.title_ja: スズメガにおけるマルチモーダル能動的センシングのための実行可能な情報ランドスケープの学習
llm.tldr_ja: スズメガの花への相互作用タスクにおける視覚および機械受容の観測から不確実性低減マップを学習するマルチモーダル予測符号化フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: マルチモーダルな感覚経験から、行動条件付きの情報マップがどのように学習されるかは、従来単一モダリティに限定されており不明確であった。
llm.method: シミュレーション環境で訓練された変分生成モデルを用いて行動空間全体の情報ランドスケープを復元し、不uncertaintyに駆動される辞書式アルゴリズムを開発した。
llm.result: 自然な軌跡が学習されたマップの高い不確実性低減領域を占める傾向があり、不確実性ゲーティングにより学習と一般化が向上することを示した。

2611.11011.tldr_en: This work introduces a multimodal predictive-coding framework for learning uncertainty-reduction maps from visual and mechanosensory observations in hawkmoth flower interaction tasks, and develops an uncertainty-gated lexicographic algorithm that switches between information gathering and reward exploitation based on perceptual uncertainty.

2611.11009.title: PIA: Agentic Physics-Informed Runtime Anomaly Detection
2611.11009.abstract: Runtime anomaly detectors for cyber-physical systems are either learned as black boxes from normal data, which miss stealthy manipulations that keep every signal inside its normal range, or derived by hand from physical models, which requires expert effort for every plant. We introduce physicsinformed agents (PIA), in which a large language model agent writes the detector itself as a set of physical residuals, such as pump characteristics, tank mass balances, and controller logic, and refines every candidate against normal operating data through an evaluation workbench before deployment. The result is a compact, human-readable detector that runs in milliseconds and names the component behind each alarm. On the BATADAL water distribution attack benchmark, PIA with Claude Opus 5.5 reaches an F1 of 0.878 on the test attacks against 0.504 for the strongest of six statistical and deep baselines, keeps detecting attacks concealed by replayed and offset sensor readings, and attributes every detected test attack to the attacked component. Ablations show that testing hypotheses against data is decisive: agents that write residuals from the plant description alone lose up to 0.28 F1, whereas agents that see only anonymized signals recover most of the physical structure.

llm.title_ja: PIA: エージェント型物理情報に基づくランタイム異常検知
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模言語モデルエージェントが物理的残差のセットとして検出器自体を記述し、正常な動作データに対して評価ワークベンチで洗練させる物理情報エージェント（PIA）を提案する。
llm.problem: サイバーフィジカルシステムのランタイム異常検知器は、ブラックボックスとして学習されるか、プラントごとに専門家の手作業による物理モデルの導出が必要である。
llm.method: LLMエージェントがポンプ特性やタンクの質量バランスなどの物理的残差を記述し、正常データを用いた評価ベンチマークで候補を洗練させるフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: BATADALの水配分攻撃ベンチマークにおいてF1スコア0.878を達成し、既存の統計的・ディープラーニングベースラインを大きく上回った。
keywords_ja: サイバーフィジカルシステム

2611.10994.title: RoboMoCap: A Large-Scale Whole-Body Motion Capture Dataset with Egocentric Vision for Robot Learning
2611.10994.abstract: Humanoid robots must coordinate locomotion and manipulation to navigate complex environments and perform everyday tasks. Learning such behaviours from human demonstrations requires accurate whole-body motion paired with egocentric vision, particularly for lower-body movements and foot placements that are frequently invisible from a first-person perspective. However, existing egocentric datasets often lack high-fidelity optical motion capture or systematic coverage of diverse loco-manipulation behaviours. To address this gap, we introduce RoboMoCap, a large-scale multimodal dataset combining egocentric vision with marker-based optical motion capture, specifically designed for locomotion-centric humanoid learning. RoboMoCap comprises over 200 hours of recordings from 14 participants, featuring six head-mounted cameras, wrist-mounted visual and inertial sensing, and optical full-body motion capture at 120 Hz. The dataset systematically covers diverse locomotion primitives, dynamic whole-body movements, and loco-manipulation tasks, including variable-speed walking, turning, constrained navigation, terrain traversal, object transportation, and manipulation during locomotion. It provides temporally aligned multimodal observations and metric whole-body motion representations, enabling the study of human movement beyond directly observable body regions. We systematically evaluate existing methods on three benchmark tasks: egocentric full-body motion reconstruction, foot contact and placement estimation, and human-to-humanoid motion retargeting. By pairing egocentric vision with high-fidelity human motion across diverse locomotion and interaction scenarios, RoboMoCap provides a foundation for egocentric motion understanding and humanoid learning from human demonstrations.

llm.title_ja: RoboMoCap: ロボット学習のための一人称視点を持つ大規模全身モーションキャプチャデータセット
llm.tldr_ja: 移動中心のヒューマノイド学習のために、一人称視点映像とマーカーベースの光学式モーションキャプチャを組み合わせた大規模マルチモーダルデータセットRoboMoCapを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の一人称視点データセットは、高精度な光学式モーションキャプチャや多様な移動・操作動作の体系的な網羅が不足している。
llm.method: 6つの頭部装着型カメラ、手首の視覚・慣性センサー、120Hzの光学式全身モーションキャプチャを統合し、14人の参加者による200時間以上の記録からなるデータセットを構築した。
llm.result: 一人称全身モーション復元、足の接触・配置推定、ヒューマン・ツー・ヒューマノイドモーションリターゲティングの3つのベンチマークタスクで既存手法を評価した。
keywords_ja: モーションキャプチャ
ヒューマノイドロボット

2611.10994.tldr_en: RoboMoCap is introduced, a large-scale multimodal dataset combining egocentric vision with marker-based optical motion capture, specifically designed for locomotion-centric humanoid learning and systematic coverage of diverse loco-manipulation behaviours.

2611.10967.title: BAT-WAM: Bridging Action and Touch in World-Action Models for Dexterous Hands
2611.10967.abstract: Dexterous manipulation with world action models (WAMs) relies on hand configuration and contact information, yet joint-state and whole-hand tactile observations may be partially or entirely missing. RGB images provide scene context and hand-object geometry but are insufficient to reliably recover these missing modalities. We further observe a correlation between hand state and tactile information. Motivated by this observation, we introduce BAT-WAM, a framework that bridges visual, joint-state, and tactile representations for WAMs. BAT-WAM learns separate codebooks and decoders for the tactile and action streams. An RGB-conditioned continuous latent bridge connects the two streams for bidirectional learning, while visual information serves as continuous context. Under the HTBench evaluation protocol, BAT-WAM reduces the root mean squared error (RMSE) of tactile reconstruction by 34.73% under fully masked conditions and 38.84% under partially masked conditions, relative to an image-conditioned HandTouch checkpoint. For future tactile prediction conditioned on target-time RGB and historical actions, it reduces mean RMSE by 85.56% relative to OpenWAM with HandTouch. Real-robot experiments further show that BAT-WAM consistently outperforms related WAM baselines in dexterous manipulation. Generalization experiments on unseen objects and scenes also demonstrate substantial improvements over baseline models. These findings support joint modeling of visual context, hand state, and touch as a representation approach for multimodal WAMs.

llm.title_ja: BAT-WAM: 器用な手の世界行動モデルにおける行動と触覚の橋渡し
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚、関節状態、触覚の表現を統合し、RGB画像を連続的なコンテキストとして用いて双方向学習を行うフレームワーク「BAT-WAM」を提案する。
llm.problem: 器用なマニピュレーションにおける世界行動モデル（WAMs）では、関節状態や全身の触覚観測が部分または完全に欠落することがあり、RGB画像だけでは十分に復元できない。
llm.method: 触覚と行動のストリームに対して個別のコードブックとデコーダーを学習し、RGB条件付きの連続潜在ブリッジで両ストリームを接続する。
llm.result: HTBenchプロトコルにおいて触覚再構成のRMSEを大幅に削減し、実機実験および未知のオブジェクトに対する一般化において関連するWAMベースラインを一貫して上回った。
keywords_ja: 器用なマニピュレーション

2611.10967.tldr_en: Joint modeling of visual context, hand state, and touch as a representation approach for multimodal WAMs is supported and BAT-WAM is introduced, a framework that bridges visual, joint-state, and tactile representations for WAMs.

2611.10950.title: Interpretable Cyber-Physical Attack Detection in Smart Grids: A Leakage-Controlled Multi-Testbed Evaluation of Fusion, Robustness, and Observability Limits
2611.10950.abstract: Cyber-physical smart-grid detectors are typically treated as black boxes and validated exclusively on clean, temporally shuffled datasets, which risk overly optimistic performance claims. This work presents a multi-testbed evaluation study built around an interpretable, time-windowed fusion Random Forest, adopting the pessimistic result whenever evaluation protocols disagree. (i) On a public paired cyber-physical dataset, shuffled cross-validation is optimistic: macro-F1 falls from 0.96 to 0.88 +/- 0.06 under rolling-origin temporal evaluation. A topology-free graph convolutional network (GCN) serving as a control confirms that this lightweight model is competitive on these splits. (ii) The adaptive and adaptive-joint feature-space attacks, which are infeasible as realistic grid manipulations, degrade macro-F1 to 0.67 and 0.34, respectively. Adversarial training and randomized smoothing partially restore performance, and a physics-constrained evolution-strategy evasion on the IEEE 14-Bus testbed shows the same vulnerability pattern. (iii) On real IEC-104 traffic, the cyber view reliably catches structural attacks (recall of 0.87 to 0.98) but largely fails on semantic value manipulation (recall of 0.11 to 0.35). An observability taxonomy on the IEEE 14-Bus system reveals that stealthy false data injection defeats all three observation views. (iv) On a full AC weighted least-squares state-estimation testbed, a forecasting-aided temporal test is evaded by slow ramps precisely where a rate-invariant physics-manifold test sustains detection at a common 5% false-alarm target. A full end-to-end evaluation on IEEE 118-Bus confirms the ordering but bounds its strength: the manifold test detects every trial down to 0.05 degree/step and 0.48 at 0.02 degree/step, against 0.14 for the temporal test. All code and benchmarks are released.

llm.title_ja: スマートグリッドにおける解釈可能なサイバーフィジカル攻撃検知：融合、ロバスト性、および観測可能性限界のリーク制御型マルチテストベッド評価
llm.tldr_ja: 解釈可能な時間窓付き融合ランダムフォレストを中心に据え、サイバーフィジカルスマートグリッド検出器の性能や頑健性を複数のテストベッドで評価する。
llm.problem: スマートグリッドの検出器は通常ブラックボックスとして扱われ、クリーンで時間的にシャッフルされたデータセットで検証されるため、過度に楽観的な性能評価につながるリスクがある。
llm.method: ローリングオリジン時間評価、適応型特徴空間攻撃、実交通データ、AC重み付き最小二乗状態推定テストベッドを用いて、検出器の脆弱性と検出限界を多角的に評価する。
llm.result: シャッフルされた交差検証は過度に楽観的であり、レート不変の物理マニホールドテストが一貫して攻撃を検出できることを示した。
keywords_ja: サイバーセキュリティ

2611.10950.tldr_en: This work presents a multi-testbed evaluation study built around an interpretable, time-windowed fusion Random Forest, adopting the pessimistic result whenever evaluation protocols disagree.

2611.10949.title: Explicitly capturing demonstrator multi-modality for distillation into diffusion policies
2611.10949.abstract: The diversity of a distilled diffusion policy's outputs matters beyond how it impacts the policy's success rate. In particular, downstream applications like test-time search and policy improvement require exploration. Thus, we want to distill multi-modal demonstrators into diffusion policies which reproduce their conditional action distributions. Standard data collection for behavior cloning applies a sliding window to demonstration episodes, which pairs unique observation histories with actions. These datasets can be fit by a policy that is either multi-modal, or unimodal with high Lipschitz constant to capture a diversity of actions seen at nearby observation samples. Prior work finds that diffusion policies trained on sparse data learn the latter, memorizing one action per observation. We adapt vine sampling to behavior cloning data collection to resolve this ambiguity: at some states the demonstrator visits, query it $k$ times from exactly the same observation. On a synthetic task, we study how the number of actions per observation, $k$, affects the learned policy, and find that larger $k$ yields a policy that better matches the demonstrator's conditional distribution, including its multi-modality and diversity. On a 2D truck unloading task, vine sampling likewise leads to a policy closer to the demonstrator and substantially improves both best-of-$N$ and expert iteration performance.
2611.10949.comment: Presented at Pretrain to Adapt Workshop at the 10th Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026). Project website: https://shaoyuan.cc/research/vine/

llm.title_ja: 拡散ポリシーへの蒸留に向けた実演者のマルチモダリティの明示的キャプチャ
llm.tldr_ja: 行動クローンデータの収集にブドウサンプリング（vine sampling）を適用し、同一の観測から複数回クエリを行うことで、実演者の条件付き分布やマルチモダリティに合致したポリシーを学習する。
llm.problem: 拡散ポリシーの学習において、標準的なスライドウィンドウによるデータ収集では、観測ごとの行動の多様性を学習できず、単峰性に陥るか過剰適合しやすい。
llm.method: 実演者が訪れた特定の状態で同じ観測から $k$ 回クエリを行うブドウサンプリングを行動クローンに適用し、条件付き分布への適合度を高める。
llm.result: 合成タスクおよび2Dトラック荷降ろしタスクにおいて、より実演者に近いポリシーが得られ、best-of-$N$やエキスパート反復の性能が大幅に向上した。

2611.10949.tldr_en: On a synthetic task, vine sampling leads to a policy closer to the demonstrator and substantially improves both best-of-N$ and expert iteration performance, and a policy that better matches the demonstrator's conditional distribution, including its multi-modality and diversity.

2611.10938.title: BRACE: Belief-guided Residual Adaptive Control for Safe Navigation under Unknown Disturbances
2611.10938.abstract: Disturbances encountered during autonomous navigation generally vary across space, often discontinuously, as obstacles redirect wind and changing terrain alters traction. Tracking controllers typically assume sufficient control authority to mitigate disturbances and maintain safety; the regime where this assumption fails remains underexplored. We present Belief-guided Residual Adaptive Control (BRACE), a hierarchical reinforcement learning (RL) framework for reach-avoid navigation under unknown, bounded, spatially varying disturbances. BRACE infers a disturbance belief from model prediction errors and uses that to condition a high-level policy that adapts the reference trajectory. The policy combines a nominal and a belief-guided residual term, trained jointly with a likelihood-ratio advantage reweighting heuristic. We evaluate BRACE in three simulated quadcopter environments with abruptly switching wind fields, and validate it on Crazyflie hardware with fan-generated disturbances. Across these settings, BRACE improves reach-avoid performance over model predictive control and RL baselines.

llm.title_ja: BRACE: 未知の外乱下での安全なナビゲーションのための信念誘導型残差適応制御
llm.tldr_ja: 空間的に変動する未知の外乱下での到達回避ナビゲーションを実現するため、モデル予測誤差から外乱信念を推論して参照軌道を適応させる階層型強化学習フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 自律ナビゲーションで遭遇する外乱は空間的に不連続に変動し、従来の追従コントローラは外乱を軽減する制御権の仮定が破綻する領域での制御が未踏である。
llm.method: モデル予測誤差から外乱信念を推論し、それを基に高レベルポリシーを条件付けて基準軌道を適応させる、尤度比アドバンテージ再重み付けヒューリスティックを用いた階層型RLフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: 風向きが急変するシミュレーション環境およびCrazyflie実機を用いたファン外乱環境において、MPCやRLベースラインを上回る到達回避性能を示した。

2611.10938.tldr_en: Belief-guided Residual Adaptive Control (BRACE), a hierarchical reinforcement learning (RL) framework for reach-avoid navigation under unknown, bounded, spatially varying disturbances, and improves reach-avoid performance over model predictive control and RL baselines.

2611.10932.title: Beating the Pool, Not the Game: A White-Box Equilibrium Agent for Language-Based Economic Games
2611.10932.abstract: We describe sudsho, a rule-based agent for the GLEE Competition that plays bargaining, negotiation, and persuasion with zero inference-time LLM calls. Games are scored as payoff percentiles against an empirical pool of prior play on the same configuration, so pool percentiles set our demand targets while clamped equilibrium shares bound demands and acceptance. Every move is a deterministic function of the visible state (persuasion mixing aside), so alignment is verified by replaying the post-freeze move log through the policy. Across 117,280 games the agent reached an overall rating of 2056 at $0 inference cost, and the account, ranked by its best agent (a same-policy replica), placed 26th of 71 ranked accounts. A replay against three frozen snapshots of the opponent pool credits the pool-aware clamp with 274 to 330 points of mean per-game bargaining rating, an effect that holds where logged opponent decisions fix the replay.

llm.title_ja: ゲームに勝つのではなくプールに勝つ：言語ベースの経済ゲームのためのホワイトボックス均衡エージェント
llm.tldr_ja: 推論時のLLM呼び出しを一切行わず、目に見える状態の決定論的関数として交渉・説得を行うルールベースのエージェントを提案する。
llm.problem: 言語ベースの経済ゲームにおいて、推論時に大規模言語モデルを毎回呼び出すアプローチは計算コストや効率性の面で課題がある。
llm.method: 過去のプレイの経験的プールに対するペイオフパーセンタイルをターゲットとし、均衡シェアによって要求と受容を制限する、可視状態の決定論的関数に基づくルールベースエージェントを設計した。
llm.result: 117,280ゲームにわたり推論コスト0で総合レーティング2056に到達し、プール対応の制限手法が平均バーゲニングレーティングを大幅に向上させることを確認した。

2611.10917.title: Remembering to Reason: Structured Memory for Scene and Workflow Understanding in Robot-Assisted Surgery
2611.10917.abstract: Surgical video understanding is an important foundation for intelligent assistance in robot-assisted surgery. Similar surgical views can reflect different actions or procedural stages. Interpreting these views requires access to earlier observations, yet frame-centric prompting leaves this history unavailable. We introduce MemSurg, a framework that remembers surgical observations before reasoning over them. Its structured memory graph stores timestamped entity categories, locations, motion cues, and interaction summaries. Chronological links preserve recent context, while entity-associated links connect recurring observations across the procedure. Task-adaptive retrieval then supplies evidence-grounded prompts for scene and workflow reasoning, supporting both frozen inference and memory-conditioned supervised fine-tuning. Evaluation on robot-assisted prostatectomy and two complementary surgical benchmarks shows a 10.43-percentage-point gain over SurgRAW with GPT-4o. Memory conditioning adds 6.52 points under matched Qwen3-VL-8B fine-tuning, and an inference-time plug-in adds 7.04 points to EndoChat. These results support structured memory as a reusable source of procedural evidence for surgical video understanding. Our code will be publicly released.

llm.title_ja: 推論のための記憶：ロボット支援手術におけるシーンとワークフロー理解のための構造化記憶
llm.tldr_ja: タイムスタンプ付きのエンティティや相互作用の要約を記憶する構造化メモリグラフを用い、過去の観察にアクセスして手術映像を解釈するフレームワーク「MemSurg」を提案する。
llm.problem: 手術映像の理解において、類似した視点が異なるアクションや段階を反映し得るため過去の観察へのアクセスが必要だが、フレーム中心のプロンプトではそれが不可能である。
llm.method: エンティティカテゴリや場所、モーションの手がかり、相互作用の要約を格納する構造化メモリグラフを構築し、タスク適応的な検索によって証拠に基づいたプロンプトを生成する。
llm.result: 前立腺切除術などの手術ベンチマークにおいて、GPT-4oを用いたSurgRAWベースラインを大幅に上回る精度を達成した。

2611.10908.title: Beyond Real or Fake: A Dual-Channel Authenticity and Reasoning Protocol for Photographic Assessment
2611.10908.abstract: Forensic verification has converged on a binary "real vs. fake" label that confates fully synthetic, tampered, and AI-retouched images despite their very different consequences. We argue that GenAI manipulations decompose along two complementary channels: a camera channel of sensor fingerprints (destroyed by neural processing), and a semantic channel of scene-level coherence (disrupted by content edits). Each manipulation type leaves a distinctive two-channel signature. We instantiate this taxonomy in 2CAP (2-Channel Authenticity Protocol), pairing a contrastively-trained camera encoder with a frozen semantic encoder to serve two applications on a shared backbone: (i) four-class authenticity classification via cross-attention fusion with learnable reliability weights; and (ii) evidence generation, where an authentic image serves as a reference for a query and the two encoders produce per-channel alignment scores together with a patch-level saliency map. These signals are supplied as privileged context to a frozen Vision-Language Model (VLM) through an Observe-Generate-Refine loop, yielding explanations with localization without forensic fine-tuning. On a multi-source benchmark, 2CAP attains the best classification performance, including strong retouching detection where existing methods fail, and improves explanation quality.

llm.title_ja: リアルかフェイクかを超えて：写真評価のための2チャネル真正性と推論プロトコル
llm.tldr_ja: センサー指紋を捉えるカメラチャネルとシーンの文脈を捉えるセマンティックチャネルの2つを組み合わせ、真正性の分類と根拠生成を行う2CAPプロトコルを提案する。
llm.problem: 法医学的検証は「リアルかフェイクか」の二値ラベルに収束しており、完全に合成された画像、改ざんされた画像、AIレタッチされた画像を混同している。
llm.method: 対照学習されたカメラエンコーダーと凍結されたセマンティックエンコーダーを組み合わせ、クロスアテンション融合による4クラス真正性分類と、VLMを用いた説明生成を行う2CAPを構築した。
llm.result: マルチソースベンチマークにおいて最高の分類性能を達成し、既存手法が失敗するレタッチ検出や説明品質の向上を実現した。

2611.10908.tldr_en: 2CAP (2-Channel Authenticity Protocol), pairing a contrastively-trained camera encoder with a frozen semantic encoder to serve two applications on a shared backbone, attains the best classification performance, including strong retouching detection where existing methods fail, and improves explanation quality.

2611.10894.title: Zero-Shot VLA Adaptation with Retrieved Guidance
2611.10894.abstract: Pre-training large parametric "Vision-Language-Action" (VLA) models on large demonstration datasets has recently yielded promising results for general-purpose manipulation. However, these models still struggle under even small domain shifts relative to the training data, such as changes in camera viewpoint, background, object identity, or robot morphology. Motivated by the success of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in language models, we pursue retrieval to boost VLA performance. Specifically, we seek to leverage retrieval from domain-mismatched, "in-the-wild" demonstration datasets like DROID to guide a VLA's behavior in a new target domain. To achieve this, we introduce RAGu, which overcomes robotics-specific challenges for RAG: (1) It incorporates simple geometric calibration to transform source demonstrations into the target setup and reduce cross-domain differences. (2) It uses a coarse-to-fine retrieval strategy that selects, from a large pool of pre-warped candidates, the trajectory most compatible with the base VLA. (3) It guides the VLA's flow-matching inference procedure rather than seeking to retrain the base model or expand its limited context window. We evaluate RAGu across real-world, simulation, sim-to-real transfer, and cross-embodiment humanoid manipulation. We find it improves real-world VLA success rates from 20% to 80% and outperforms the closest-related baselines in sim. Project website: raguvla.github.io

llm.title_ja: 取得したガイダンスを用いたゼロショットVLA適応
llm.tldr_ja: カメラ視点や背景、ロボット形態などのドメインシフトに対応するため、オープンな実演データセットからの検索を活用してVLAモデルの推論を誘導するフレームワーク「RAGu」を提案する。
llm.problem: 大規模な視覚言語行動（VLA）モデルは一般的なマニピュレーションに有効であるものの、カメラ視点や背景などのわずかなドメインシフトに対しても性能が低下する。
llm.method: 簡単な幾何学的較正によりソース実演をターゲット設定に変換し、大規模な候補からVLAに最も適合する軌跡を選択する粗密検索戦略を用いてフローマッチング推論を誘導する。
llm.result: 実世界でのVLAの成功率を20%から80%に向上させ、シミュレーションにおいても既存のベースラインを上回った。

2611.10894.tldr_en: RAGu, which overcomes robotics-specific challenges for RAG, is introduced, which improves real-world VLA success rates from 20% to 80% and outperforms the closest-related baselines in sim.

2611.10877.title: Sampling-based Model Predictive Control as Sequential Monte Carlo Inference
2611.10877.abstract: Sampling-based model predictive control (MPC) is treated as a family of distinct algorithms: predictive sampling, MPPI, the cross-entropy method, and their biased, colored-noise, and annealed variants all sample control sequences and reweight them by cost. We show a single Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) inference algorithm implements them all, specified by three independent axes: the proposal, the update rule that reduces cost-weighted particles to a nominal plan, and the effective-sample-size threshold for resampling. We evaluate SMC-based planning on MuJoCo non-linear control, open-loop navigation through obstacle fields, 7-DoF motion planning, and non-prehensile push-T, in simulation and on a Franka FR3. Resampling combats particle degeneracy at long horizons. At a 28-knot horizon in our navigation domain it cut the collision rate by 30% over non-resampling baselines. Programmable proposals improve push-T success over perturbative baselines, improving from 1% to 100% in simulation and 10% to 90% on hardware.
2611.10877.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L). Code: https://github.com/CoMMALab/PFMP

llm.title_ja: 順次モンテカルロ推論としてのサンプリングベースモデル予測制御
llm.tldr_ja: 予測サンプリングやMPPIなどの多様なサンプリングベースのMPCアルゴリズムを、3つの独立した軸（提案分布、更新ルール、リサンプリングの閾値）で規定される単一の順次モンテカルロ（SMC）推論アルゴリズムとして統一的に示す。
llm.problem: サンプリングベースのモデル予測制御（MPC）は、多様な個別アルゴリズムとして扱われており、その背後にある共通の推論構造が整理されていなかった。
llm.method: 制御シーケンスをサンプリングしコストで再重み付けする一連の手法を、プロポーザル、更新ルール、リサンプリングの有効サンプルサイズ閾値を持つSMC推論として定式化し評価した。
llm.result: ナビゲーション領域における長ホライズンでの衝突率を30%削減し、プッシュTタスクにおいてシミュレーションおよび実機で成功率を大幅に向上させた。

2611.10877.tldr_en: This work shows a single Sequential Monte Carlo inference algorithm implements a family of distinct algorithms: predictive sampling, MPPI, the cross-entropy method, and their biased, colored-noise, and annealed variants all sample control sequences and reweight them by cost.

2611.10872.title: DreamVLA: From Generated Human Motions to Humanoid Vision-Language-Action Policies
2611.10872.abstract: Training vision-language-action (VLA) policies typically depends on substantial robot demonstration data, making human teleoperation a costly and cumbersome bottleneck, particularly for whole-body humanoid interaction. Reinforcement learning in simulation offers an alternative for scaling this data, but designing task-specific rewards remains challenging. To address this, we propose DreamVLA, which uses generated motion trajectories to guide reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation, converting them into reliable task execution trajectories. These trajectories train VLA models in simulation without new task-specific teleoperation data. Our central contribution is a reference-conditioned DAgger distillation procedure: after a failed learner rollout, we restart the RL expert from a sampled learner state with the same reference suffix and aggregate successful corrective trajectories, addressing the distribution shift left by offline imitation. We evaluate picking from a platform, opening a drawer, pressing a button, and walking and picking from a platform, with ablations of DAgger iterations, residual RL, and generated dataset scale. Project website: ember-center-berkeley.github.io/DreamVLA.
2611.10872.comment: Accepted to CoRL 2026 workshops G2A: From Generative Models to Robot Actions and Open Problems in Contact-Rich Loco-Manipulation

llm.title_ja: DreamVLA: 生成された人間のモーションからヒューマノイドビジョン言語行動ポリシーへ
llm.tldr_ja: 生成されたモーション軌道を利用してシミュレーション内での強化学習を誘導し、新たなタスク固有の遠隔操作データなしでVLAモデルを訓練するフレームワーク「DreamVLA」を提案する。
llm.problem: VLAポリシーの訓練は大量のロボット実演データに依存しており、特に全身ヒューマノイドの相互作用において人間の遠隔操作が大きなボトルネックとなっている。
llm.method: 生成されたモーション軌道でシミュレーション内の強化学習をガイドし、失敗したロールアウトからリスタートして成功した修正軌道を集成する参照条件付きDAgger蒸留手順を導入する。
llm.result: プラットフォームからのピッキング、引き出しの開閉、ボタン押しなどのタスクにおいて、アブレーション評価やデータスケールの検証を通じて有効性を実証した。

2611.10872.tldr_en: This work proposes DreamVLA, which uses generated motion trajectories to guide reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation, converting them into reliable task execution trajectories, and evaluates picking from a platform, opening a drawer, pressing a button, and walking and picking from a platform.

2611.10825.title: MoE-DAgger: Transition-Aware Router-Entropy Gating for Selective Human Correction in Phase-Structured Manipulation
2611.10825.abstract: Selective data acquisition in Dataset Aggregation (DAgger) on robots requires deciding which learner rollouts to correct and when to intervene. In manipulation with ordered phases, router entropy from a phase-supervised soft mixture-of-experts (MoE) is insufficient: the same value can reflect either a normal adjacent-phase handoff or support for nonadjacent or earlier phases. We propose MoE-DAgger, which uses causal router history to distinguish these cases without providing the policy with a phase label, progress variable, or hard phase command during execution. The acquisition rule allows an adjacent transition to settle, but requests correction when high entropy persists outside such a transition, the transition times out, or routing persistently favors an earlier phase. Under matched active human-control budgets, MoE-DAgger achieves 84.0% task success on Green and 78.0% on Red, exceeding phase-unaware filtered entropy by 22 percentage points on Green and 26 points on Red, with no observed collisions in 50 rollouts per task. On 50 shared intervention-free traces per task, 83.3% and 80.0% of its first proposals fall on failed rollouts within predefined failure windows when 15 and 25 traces are selected, compared with 70.0% and 72.0% for temporal action-chunk disagreement and 63.3% and 60.0% for ensemble disagreement. Shadow replay and an active no-veto ablation indicate that suppressing queries at normal adjacent handoffs is a key contributor to the improved allocation.
2611.10825.comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Project page: https://SJ824.github.io/MoE-DAgger/

llm.title_ja: MoE-DAgger: 相構造化マニピュレーションにおける選択的人間の修正に向けた遷移認識型ルーターエントロピーゲーティング
llm.tldr_ja: 順序付けられたフェーズを持つマニピュレーションにおいて、因果ルーター履歴を用いて通常のエントロピー変動と異常を区別し、選択的な人間の介入を決定する「MoE-DAgger」を提案する。
llm.problem: DAggerにおける能動的なデータ収集では、どの学習者ロールアウトを修正し、いつ介入すべきかを決定する必要があるが、単純な混合専門モデル（MoE）のエントロピーだけでは隣接フェーズの移行と他の異常を区別できない。
llm.method: 因果ルーター履歴を利用して、通常の隣接フェーズ移行が落ち着くのを待ちつつ、移行時間切れや過去のフェーズへの偏りなど高エントロピーが持続する場合に修正を要求する取得ルールを設計した。
llm.result: 限られた人間の介入予算のもとで、GreenおよびRedタスクにおいてフェーズ非認識のフィルタリング済みエントロピーを大きく上回る成功率を達成し、50回のロールアウトで衝突が観測されなかった。

2611.10825.tldr_en: MoE-DAgger is proposed, which uses causal router history to distinguish cases without providing the policy with a phase label, progress variable, or hard phase command during execution and indicates that suppressing queries at normal adjacent handoffs is a key contributor to the improved allocation.

2611.10822.title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Internal Computation for Reinforcement Learning
2611.10822.abstract: Iterative neural policies usually spend the same computation on every decision, although the benefit of additional processing varies across states. We introduce Adaptive Internal Computation (AIC), an iterative policy that learns when to stop refining its latent representation and act. In AIC, we train action selection and stopping jointly, an expected-depth penalty values computation and intermediate value predictions provide auxiliary supervision. We show that when only some states benefit from further refinement, an ideal state-dependent allocator outperforms every state-independent stopping schedule at the same expected depth. With at most eight refinement steps per decision, AIC executes 3.3 steps on average across twelve benchmark tasks and lowers per-decision latency by 31--44% relative to a fixed eight-step policy on four control and robotics tasks. Its mean reward exceeds the best fixed-depth policy on seven tasks and trails it on four. Ablating adaptive stopping and value supervision separately shows that stopping accounts for most of the reward gain on PickCube and AntMaze, where it also executes more refinement steps and that supervision accounts for most of it on RareEvent.

llm.title_ja: 思考のタイミングの学習：強化学習のための適応的内部計算
llm.tldr_ja: 状態ごとに潜在表現の洗練をいつ停止して行動すべきかを適応的に学習する反復ポリシー「Adaptive Internal Computation（AIC）」を提案する。
llm.problem: 反復的なニューラルポリシーは、状態間で追加処理の利点が異なるにもかかわらず、すべての決定に同じ計算量を費やしている。
llm.method: 行動選択と停止を共同で訓練し、計算量にペナルティを与える期待深度ペナルティと中間値予測による補助的監督を組み合わせた適応型ポリシーを構築した。
llm.result: 12のベンチマークタスクにおいて平均3.3ステップの計算で実行し、固定ステップのポリシーと比較して決定ごとの遅延を31〜44%削減しつつ、多くのタスクで報酬を上回った。

2611.10822.tldr_en: Adaptive Internal Computation (AIC), an iterative policy that learns when to stop refining its latent representation and act is introduced, which shows that stopping accounts for most of the reward gain on PickCube and AntMaze and that supervision accounts for most of it on RareEvent.

2611.10819.title: Selective Cooperative Perception via Blind Spot Reasoning and Agentic Dialogue with Vision-Language Models
2611.10819.abstract: Real-time cooperative perception (CP) in multi-agent traffic environments is highly resource-intensive, which posing scalability challenges for large-scale deployment. Efficiency can be significantly improved by selectively performing CP only in safety-critical scenarios and for key occluding objects. Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are well-suited for complex reasoning in dynamic and uncertain environments, making them a promising tool for this selective CP task. This study proposes a VLM-driven agentic framework for blind spot reasoning and dialogue-based CP. A mixed-model architecture is designed that integrates conventional object detection for stable perception, vision-language reasoning for identifying impactful occlusions, and a physics-based geometric module to align reasoning with real-world visibility constraints. The framework also incorporates a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting mechanism to enhance interpretability and intent-aware decision-making. We collect real-world data from connected vehicles operating in urban traffic and compare the driving-critical blind spot identification and dialogue performance of four state-of-the-art VLMs. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves over 80% accuracy in driving-critical blind spot detection and over 90% success in dialogue-driven perception sharing. This work provides a scalable, interpretable, and bandwidth-efficient alternative to conventional CP pipelines, and offers new insights into agentic communication design for future connected traffic systems.

llm.title_ja: 死角推論とビジョン言語モデルを用いたエージェント型対話による選択的協調知覚
llm.tldr_ja: 安全上クリティカルなシナリオや主要な遮蔽オブジェクトに限定して協調知覚を選択的に実行するため、VLM駆動型のエージェントフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: マルチエージェント交通環境におけるリアルタイム協調知覚（CP）は非常に計算集約的であり、大規模展開に向けたスケーラビリティの課題がある。
llm.method: 従来の物体検出と、影響力のある遮蔽を特定するビジョン言語推論、実世界の可視性制約に整合させる物理ベースの幾何学的モジュール、および思考連鎖（CoT）プロンプティングを統合したアーキテクチャを設計した。
llm.result: 運転上クリティカルな死角検出において80%以上の精度を達成し、対話駆動型の知覚共有において90%以上の成功率を示した。

2611.10819.tldr_en: A VLM-driven agentic framework for blind spot reasoning and dialogue-based CP, which provides a scalable, interpretable, and bandwidth-efficient alternative to conventional CP pipelines, and offers new insights into agentic communication design for future connected traffic systems.

2611.10778.title: Passivity-Guaranteed Variable Impedance and Compliance Control via Online Parameter Optimization
2611.10778.abstract: Variable impedance control enhances the interaction capability of robot manipulators by adapting impedance parameters online. However, time-varying impedance parameters may inject energy into the system and violate passivity, particularly when tasks demand rapid stiffness changes. Existing methods address this by increasing damping or limiting the stiffness profile, which often degrades the dynamic response. In this work, we propose a quadratic programming-based parameter optimization framework that guarantees passivity by modulating the desired inertia to compensate for energy injected by stiffness variations, while preserving a critically damped system. For the case of diagonal impedance matrices, we optimize the rates of change of inertia and stiffness subject to a passivity constraint formulated as a convex quadratic program. We extend the framework to compliance control, where the desired inertia is coupled to the robot's configuration-dependent inertia matrix. We use an eigendecomposition based on Cholesky factorization to optimize the spectral weights while maintaining passivity. Experiments on the Kinova Gen3 7-degree-of-freedom manipulator validate both methods with human interaction perturbations. Comparisons with an energy tank approach and a nonpassivity-based method demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves less conservative stiffness tracking without requiring an energy reservoir or damping overhead.

llm.title_ja: オンラインパラメータ最適化による受動性保証付き可変インピーダンス・コンプライアンス制御
llm.tldr_ja: 所望の慣性を変調して剛性変化によって注入されるエネルギーを補償し、受動性を保証する二次計画法ベースのパラメータ最適化フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 時間変動するインピーダンスパラメータがシステムにエネルギーを注入し受動性を破る課題がある。
llm.method: 所望の慣性を変調して剛性変動によるエネルギーを補償する、二次計画法ベースのパラメータ最適化フレームワークの提案。
llm.result: エネルギーリザーブやダンピングのオーバーヘッドなしに、より保守的でない剛性追従を実現した。

2611.10778.tldr_en: This work proposes a quadratic programming-based parameter optimization framework that guarantees passivity by modulating the desired inertia to compensate for energy injected by stiffness variations, while preserving a critically damped system.

2611.10771.title: WorldFoundry: Towards Unified Infrastructure for World Intelligence
2611.10771.abstract: Visual generative models increasingly blur the line between synthesizing observations and simulating environments. Yet visual plausibility alone does not constitute successful world modeling: compelling outputs may lack persistent state, physical dynamics, or causally consistent responses to interactions. We define a generative world model as a predictive dynamical system that maintains a persistent, history-conditioned representation of an environment, updates that representation in response to actions or interventions, and generates temporally coherent trajectories that reflect outcomes under observed and counterfactual interventions. From this definition, we derive an intelligence-oriented framework spanning perceptual grounding, persistent state modeling, controllable transformation, dynamics-aware prediction, and closed-loop interaction. We present WorldFoundry, open-source infrastructure for reproducible inference and evaluation across video, 3D and 4D, embodied action, and interactive world systems. WorldFoundry unifies model and benchmark discovery, runtime and asset preparation, execution orchestration, artifact management, and interactive visualization, while modality-specific adapters preserve native inputs, execution semantics, output representations, and evaluation protocols. Explicit manifests, durable artifact contracts, and evidence-aware scorecards separate execution readiness from evaluative claims, making each claim traceable to its supporting artifacts. The catalog contains 270 model entries, 74 benchmarks, and 62 registered metric entries, with readiness and execution evidence recorded separately. WorldFoundry enables reproducible comparison of persistent, controllable dynamics across heterogeneous systems, advancing the field from perceptual synthesis toward measurable world intelligence.
2611.10771.comment: 39 pages, 10 figures. This technical report will be updated periodically
2611.10771.hf_summary_en: WorldFoundry offers open-source infrastructure for reproducible inference and evaluation of generative world models across video, 3D/4D, embodied action, and interactive systems, with traceable evidence and benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: WorldFoundry：世界知能のための統合インフラストラクチャに向けて
llm.tldr_ja: WorldFoundryは、ビデオ、3D/4D、身体化された行動、インタラクティブシステムにわたる生成世界モデルの再現可能な推論と評価のためのオープンソースインフラを提供する。
llm.problem: 生成世界モデルには、永続的状態、物理ダイナミクス、因果的に一貫した応答が欠けている場合がある。
llm.method: ビデオ、3D/4D、身体的行動にわたる再現可能な推論と評価のためのオープンソースインフラWorldFoundryの構築。
llm.result: 270のモデルエントリ、74のベンチマーク、62の登録済みメトリックエントリを含むカタログを実現した。

2611.10769.title: Look Ahead: Search-Driven Reasoning in Embodied AI
2611.10769.abstract: Search allows a robotic policy to evaluate candidate futures before committing to an action. Motivated by test-time planning for vision-language action (VLA) models, we study selective search over action chunks in PushT using a frozen Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) policy. Beam search generates perturbed alternatives around the policy prediction and scores them through rollouts from cloned simulator states. Across 50 evaluation episodes, beam search raises task success from 0% to 18% and increases average cumulative reward from 39.44 to 103.2. We introduce One Step Ahead (OSA), a gate that simulates the nominal policy chunk and invokes full search only when its predicted coverage drop exceeds a threshold. In the reported ablations, OSA preserves or improves success while reducing runtime by approximately 3x relative to full beam search. Ablations over tree depth, branching factor, beam width, and replanning frequency show that larger search budgets do not consistently improve performance. The results support selective test-time search for action-chunking policies; evaluation on language-conditioned VLAs and physical robots remains future work.

llm.title_ja: 先読み：身体性AIにおける探索駆動型推論
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結したACTポリシーを用いたPushTにおいて、アクションチャンクに対する選択的探索がタスク成功率と累積報酬を向上させることを示した。
llm.problem: VLAモデルのテスト時計画において、アクション決定前に候補となる未来を評価する必要がある。
llm.method: 凍結されたACTポリシーを用いたPushTにおいて、アクションチャンクに対する選択的ビーム探索とOne Step Ahead（OSA）ゲートの導入。
llm.result: ビーム探索によりタスク成功率が0%から18%に向上し、OSAによりフル探索に比べ実行時間が約3倍削減された。
llm.limitation: 言語条件付きVLAや実機ロボットでの評価は今後の課題である。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.10769.tldr_en: This work introduces One Step Ahead (OSA), a gate that simulates the nominal policy chunk and invokes full search only when its predicted coverage drop exceeds a threshold, and introduces One Step Ahead (OSA), a gate that preserves or improves success while reducing runtime by approximately 3x relative to full beam search.

2611.10748.title: REINS: A Self-Evolving Agent Harness for Real-Time Trajectory Planning
2611.10748.abstract: Agent harnesses -- runtime scaffolds that wrap an LLM's reasoning loop with tool dispatch, verification, and persistent memory -- have become the standard substrate for deploying LLMs as autonomous agents, as demonstrated by Claude Code and Codex in software engineering. In trajectory planning, however, this paradigm has not taken hold: existing LLM-based trajectory planning methods either keep the LLM in the decision loop, exceeding the millisecond-level control budget, or offload it to offline rules or training-time supervision -- leaving the runtime planner non-evolving. Intermediate hybrids still lack the verification-and-consolidation loop that makes harnesses reliable. We ask: what runtime harness would let an LLM planner meet real-time constraints while self-evolving into a deployable one? We propose REINS, a harness built on three LLM-planner couplings: LLM outputs are (i) grounded to a learned variable-level dynamics model, (ii) verified via calibrated predicates and forward rollout, and (iii) consolidated into an indexed rule memory that serves future scenes in O(log n) without re-invoking the LLM. The harness closes a self-evolution loop: familiar scenes resolve by memory lookup; novel scenes invoke the LLM, whose verified outputs enrich the memory. Without modifying LLM weights, REINS attains 98%+ compliance, nearly 50% collision reduction, and 1.9-4.6 ms latency on simulated and real-world benchmarks at the tactical decision layer, with LLM invocation rate monotonically declining as memory matures. Code: https://github.com/ZhihongCui/REINS
2611.10748.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Main Track). 36 pages, 7 figures, 20 tables. Code: https://github.com/ZhihongCui/REINS

llm.title_ja: REINS：リアルタイム軌道計画のための自己進化型エージェントハーネス
llm.tldr_ja: LLMの出力をダイナミクスモデルへの接地、検証、ルールメモリへの統合によって結合し、実時間制約を満たしながら自己進化するREINSを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のLLMベースの軌道計画法はミリ秒単位の制御予算を超過するか、非進化的なままである。
llm.method: LLM出力を動的モデルへの接地、検証、索引付きルールメモリへの統合を行うREINSハーネスの提案。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界のベンチマークで98%以上の準拠率、約50%の衝突削減、1.9〜4.6 msのレイテンシを達成した。
keywords_ja: エージェントハーネス

2611.10748.tldr_en: REINS is proposed, a harness built on three LLM-planner couplings: LLM outputs are grounded to a learned variable-level dynamics model, verified via calibrated predicates and forward rollout, and consolidated into an indexed rule memory that serves future scenes in O(log n) without re-invoking the LLM.

2611.10721.title: Behavioral Evaluation of Large Language Models Under Cognitive Biases in HAZOP Studies
2611.10721.abstract: Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) studies safeguard industrial processes against catastrophic accidents. Large language models (LLMs) increasingly assist HAZOP drafting, yet evaluations rely on lexical overlap. Because LLMs internalize human heuristics, prompts may trigger biased judgments. Whether frontier LLMs withstand cognitive perturbations in safety-critical workflows remains unknown. Here we show across 420 trials that three frontier LLMs resisted 96.8% of cognitive manipulations, rendering overall susceptibility statistically inconclusive. Contrary to assumed broad fragility, models rejected confirmation and availability cues. However, safety-critical risk downgrades emerged under low anchors and gain frames. Thus, automated hazard analysis requires disciplined human-in-the-loop validation.
2611.10721.comment: 8 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables. Submitted to IFAC for possible publication. Supplementary material available at https://github.com/ViniMelloeMuller/psyhazop-supplementary-material

llm.title_ja: HAZOPスタディにおける認知バイアス下での大規模言語モデルの行動評価
llm.tldr_ja: 3つのフロンティアLLMは認知的操作の96.8%に抵抗したが、低アンカーおよび利得フレームの下で安全性に関わるリスク格下げが発生した。
llm.problem: 安全性が重要なワークフローにおいて、フロンティアLLMが認知的摂動に耐えられるか不明である。
llm.method: 420回の試行を通じて3つのフロンティアLLMの認知バイアスに対する頑健性を評価。
llm.result: モデルは96.8%の認知操作に抵抗したが、低アンカーや利得フレームではリスク格下げが発生した。

2611.10720.title: Locating and Repairing Domain Shift in VLM Trajectory Planning
2611.10720.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are increasingly adopted as end-to-end driving planners, yet they suffer from cross-city domain shift. Existing methods treat this shift as a single quantity addressed by uniform alignment or single-site editing. We challenge this view on two counts: (i) domain shift in VLM trajectory planners is inherently structured across modality and layer, and (ii) a locate-then-repair recipe matched to this structure outperforms every uniform-objective baseline. We analyse domain shift via activation patching and uncover two regularities. (F1) Modality axis. Image and text tokens exhibit distinct shift patterns in each VLM. (F2) Layer axis. The layer-wise shift partition is architecture-dependent and dataset-stable. These findings recast domain shift as a two-dimensional tensor indexed by modality (image vs. text tokens) and layer, motivating a simple principle: locate where shift occurs, and repair only there. We instantiate this principle in MoLaRx (Modality-Layer Repair), a locate-then-repair framework. The Causal Importance Score (CIS) estimates the domain shift as a modality-layer tensor and partitions the layers into functional zones. CIS-Guided Selective Repair (CISR) then applies a matched operator (Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) / low-rank adaptation (LoRA) / freezing) to repair each zone, with the composition adapting automatically to each architecture. We evaluate MoLaRx on three architecturally distinct VLMs (LFM2-VL-1.6B, Qwen2-VL-2B, and PaliGemma2-3B) across two cross-city benchmarks (nuScenes and Argoverse 2). MoLaRx attains the lowest cross-city trajectory-error gap among adaptation methods in all six main-table settings, while using 50-60% fewer trainable parameters and 8.4-10.9 ms lower inference latency. In contrast, uniform MMD-only adaptation collapses in all six settings, highlighting the importance of structure-guided repair.
2611.10720.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Main Track). 30 pages, 7 figures, 16 tables. Code: https://github.com/ZhihongCui/MoLaRx

llm.title_ja: VLM軌道計画におけるドメインシフトの特定と修復
llm.tldr_ja: モダリティとレイヤーに構造化されたドメインシフトを特定し、該当箇所のみを修復するMoLaRxフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: VLAやVLMを用いたエンドツーエンドの運転プランナーは都市間のドメインシフトに悩まされている。
llm.method: 因果重要度スコア（CIS）を用いてドメインシフトを特定し、選択的に修復を行うMoLaRxフレームワークの提案。
llm.result: 3つのVLMと2つの都市間ベンチマークにおいて、クロスシティの軌道誤差ギャップを最小化しつつ、パラメータ数とレイテンシを削減した。

2611.10720.tldr_en: MoLaRx attains the lowest cross-city trajectory-error gap among adaptation methods in all six main-table settings, while using 50-60% fewer trainable parameters and 8.4-10.9 ms lower inference latency, highlighting the importance of structure-guided repair.

2611.10699.title: PLS-GS: Probabilistic Lidar Scaffolds for Compact, Surface-Aligned Gaussian Splatting
2611.10699.abstract: While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is typically optimized from images only, many robotics and mapping applications provide both camera and high-definition LiDAR data, combining rich visual appearance with accurate geometric structure. We introduce PLS-GS, a probabilistic LiDAR scaffold for Gaussian Splatting that exploits this complementary sensing setting to construct a compact 3DGS representation aligned to the measured surface. PLS-GS fits a Hierarchical Gaussian Mixture Model jointly over position and color, yielding a continuous and adaptive scaffold that eliminates the need for discrete scene partitioning such as voxel grids or octrees. The fitted mixture then guides the renderable 3DGS Gaussians: each rendering Gaussian is associated with a GMM component and constrained in the local surface frame induced by that component's covariance. A Mahalanobis support loss bounds the deviation of the rendering Gaussians from the corresponding LiDAR-derived surface. Across five large outdoor scenes, PLS-GS places primitives markedly closer to the LiDAR measurements than both image- and LiDAR-initialized baselines, while employing substantially fewer primitives, yielding a considerably more compact model and faster rendering. At matched capacity, PLS-GS places primitives closer to the LiDAR measurements, with comparable rendering quality. Code is available at https://github.com/k-harikumar/PLS-GS.
2611.10699.comment: Accepted to WACV 2027. Main paper and supplementary material. Code: https://github.com/k-harikumar/PLS-GS

llm.title_ja: PLS-GS：コンパクトで表面に整列したガウススプラッティングのための確率的LiDARスキャッフォールド
llm.tldr_ja: カメラとLiDARのデータを活用し、測定された表面に整列したコンパクトな3DGS表現を構築する確率的LiDARスキャッフォールド（PLS-GS）を提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の3Dガウススプラッティングは画像のみから最適化されることが多く、離散的なシーン分割が必要になる。
llm.method: 位置と色の両方に対して階層的ガウス混合モデルを共同でフィッティングし、レンダリング用3DGSをガイドするPLS-GSの提案。
llm.result: 5つの大規模屋外シーンにおいて、従来の初期化手法よりもLiDAR測定値に近い位置にプリミティブを配置し、よりコンパクトなモデルを実現した。
keywords_ja: ガウススプラッティング

2611.10699.tldr_en: PLS-GS is introduced, a probabilistic LiDAR scaffold for Gaussian Splatting that exploits this complementary sensing setting to construct a compact 3DGS representation aligned to the measured surface, yielding a considerably more compact model and faster rendering.

2611.10682.title: Burden, Bounty, or Bliss? Muscle-Aware Retargeting and Null-Space Exploration for Whole-Body Musculoskeletal Control
2611.10682.abstract: Learning whole-body musculoskeletal control from human motion is important for developing human-like robots, assistive devices, and rehabilitation systems. This task presents two main challenges, namely reference trajectories that are kinematically plausible but difficult to reproduce through muscle-driven dynamics, and a highly redundant 700-dimensional action space in which unstructured exploration can easily disrupt the target motion. In this paper, we propose a motion-to-policy pipeline that exploits muscle redundancy in two complementary stages. First, muscle-aware retargeting (MAR) performs bounded adaptation of kinematic trajectories subject to hard semantic, anatomical, and contact constraints. We motivate the constraint bounds by analyzing how reference-trajectory artifacts affect muscle-driven tracking. Second, null-space exploration (NSE) estimates a one-control-frame mapping from muscle excitations to generalized forces and injects bounded, anatomically structured perturbations along its null space into the actions of a value-guided flow policy. On a 24-clip motion-capture benchmark, MAR and NSE together solve every reference, reach the full horizon with half the samples of the baseline pipeline, and lower joint-center error by 44% without late collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first end-to-end pipeline that transforms monocular video into a trained whole-body imitation policy controlling 700 muscles.
2611.10682.comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to IEEE ICRA 2027

llm.title_ja: 負担、恵み、それとも至福？全身筋骨格制御のための筋肉考慮型リターゲットとnull空間探索
llm.tldr_ja: 筋肉の冗長性を活用して運動データをポリシーに変換する、筋肉考慮型リターゲットとnull空間探索を組み合わせたパイプラインを提案した。
llm.problem: 人間の運動からの全身筋骨格制御の学習には、動的に再現困難な基準軌道と700次元の高冗長な行動空間という課題がある。
llm.method: 筋肉考慮型リターゲット（MAR）とnull空間探索（NSE）を組み合わせたモーション・ツー・ポリシーパイプラインの提案。
llm.result: すべての基準軌道を達成し、ベースラインの半分のサンプルで完全なホライゾンに到達し、関節中心誤差を44%削減した。
keywords_ja: モーションキャプチャ

2611.10682.tldr_en: This is the first end-to-end pipeline that transforms monocular video into a trained whole-body imitation policy controlling 700 muscles and motivates the constraint bounds by analyzing how reference-trajectory artifacts affect muscle-driven tracking.

2611.10664.title: Task-Critical Part Alignment Improves Imitation of Object Interactions
2611.10664.abstract: This paper presents enhancements to the DINOBot framework for imitation learning of object-object interactions. We introduce two key contributions aimed at improving the accuracy and efficiency of alignment in imitation-based robotic tasks. First, we integrate RANdom SAmple Consensus (RANSAC) for outlier rejection during the alignment phase, effectively mitigating the impact of noisy depth data and spurious feature matches. This improves robustness when transferring demonstrations to real-world applications. Second, we refine the semantic correspondence process by focusing on task-relevant interaction regions, ensuring that the learned representation prioritizes critical object features that influence successful manipulation. We evaluated our approach in a range of real-world manipulation tasks, including picking, insertion, shaking, and pouring, using a robotic system. The experimental results demonstrate an overall improvement of 13.8% in task success rates compared to the baseline, along with faster convergence in the alignment process. These results highlight the effectiveness of our enhancements in improving precision and efficiency for object-object interaction imitation in robotics.
2611.10664.comment: 6 pages, 6 figures. Accepted at ICAR 2025. This is the preprint version; the published version may differ slightly
2611.10664.journal_ref: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Robotics (ICAR), pp. 329-334

llm.title_ja: タスククリティカルなパーツアライメントによる物体間相互作用の模倣の改善
llm.tldr_ja: RANSACを用いた外れ値除去とタスク関連の相互作用領域への注力により、物体間相互作用の模倣学習における精度と効率を向上させた。
llm.problem: 模倣学習における物体間相互作用の転送において、ノイズの多い深度データや不正確な特徴マッチングが課題となる。
llm.method: アライメント時の外れ値除去のためのRANSACの統合と、タスク関連の相互作用領域に焦点を当てたセマンティック対応の洗練。
llm.result: 実世界のマニピュレーションタスクにおいて、ベースラインと比較してタスク成功率が13.8%向上し、アライメントの収束が高速化した。

2611.10664.tldr_en: Improvements to the DI-NOBot framework for imitation learning of object-object interactions integrate RANdom SAmple Consensus for outlier rejection during the alignment phase, effectively mitigating the impact of noisy depth data and spurious feature matches.

2611.10660.title: Dynamics-Informed Action Learning for Goal-Conditioned Latent Planning
2611.10660.abstract: Latent world models enable visual control by planning action sequences in compact representation spaces, but a gap remains between how latent dynamics are learned and how they are used for planning. First, teacher-forced training does not expose the dynamics model to the recursively predicted latent states encountered during planning. Second, sampling-based planners typically initialize action search from goal-agnostic proposals, without exploiting the action-conditioned dynamics learned by the world model. We introduce Dynamics-Informed Action Learning (DIAL) to bridge these two gaps. During training, rollout alignment exposes the forward model to its own autoregressive latent predictions, while multi-step inverse supervision trains a lightweight inverse dynamics head to infer actions from latent-state transitions. We further apply the inverse head to model-generated transitions with its parameters held fixed, encouraging predicted rollouts to retain action-relevant information. At test time, DIAL autoregressively couples the inverse and forward dynamics to construct a dynamics-informed action sequence toward the goal, which initializes the mean of the Cross-Entropy Method (CEM) proposal distribution. The subsequent CEM search then refines this initialization using the standard sampling and updating procedure. Experiments across four visual control benchmarks demonstrate that DIAL outperforms existing latent world models and planning baselines in both standard and long-horizon scenarios.

llm.title_ja: ゴール条件付き潜在計画のためのダイナミクス情報に基づく行動学習
llm.tldr_ja: 教師強制訓練のギャップを埋めるため、ロールアウト整合性とマルチステップ逆モデルを用いたダイナミクス情報に基づく行動学習（DIAL）を提案した。
llm.problem: 潜在世界モデルにおいて、潜在ダイナミクスの学習方法と計画での利用方法の間に乖離が存在する。
llm.method: ロールアウト整合性と軽量な逆ダイナミクスヘッドを組み合わせたダイナミクス情報に基づく行動学習（DIAL）の提案。
llm.result: 4つの視覚制御ベンチマークにおいて、既存の潜在世界モデルや計画ベースラインを上回る性能を達成した。

2611.10660.tldr_en: Experiments across four visual control benchmarks demonstrate that DIAL outperforms existing latent world models and planning baselines in both standard and long-horizon scenarios.

2611.10650.title: Trajectory Inversion for a Rudderless Dual Vectored-Thrust Flying Wing
2611.10650.abstract: A rudderless dual vectored-thrust flying wing combines vertical takeoff and landing with efficient for- ward flight in a compact tailless configuration. Without aerodynamic control surfaces, vectored thrust couples translation and pitch control. Therefore, generating dy- namically compatible trajectories remains an open chal- lenge. To address this challenge, this study proposes a trajectory generation method that jointly optimizes path geometry and timing. Trajectory inversion yields state and control histories that satisfy the coupled equations of motion. The optimization balances curvature-induced acceleration against aerodynamic support, lowering thrust- vectoring demand while retaining the defining maneuver features. Representative looping and rolling sequences are tracked in closed-loop simulations. These results provide a basis for planning autonomous aerobatic maneuvers with rudderless vectored-thrust aircraft.

llm.title_ja: ラダーなし二重推力偏向全翼機のための軌道反転
llm.tldr_ja: パスの幾何学形状とタイミングを共同で最適化する軌道生成手法を提案し、結合された運動方程式を満たす状態および制御履歴を導出した。
llm.problem: ラダーなしの推力偏向全翼機では、空力制御面がないため推力偏向が並進とピッチ制御を結合させ、動的に適合する軌道生成が困難である。
llm.method: パスの幾何学形状とタイミングを共同最適化する軌道生成手法の提案。
llm.result: 閉ループシミュレーションにおいて代表的なルーリングやローリングシーケンスの追従に成功した。

2611.10647.title: Which Taxels, Not How Many: Tactile Sensor Placement for Dexterous Policies
2611.10647.abstract: Policies for dexterous manipulation depend on design choices made before training: which sensors enter the observation, where they are placed, and how their readings are arranged for the encoder. These choices are rarely examined. For tactile sensing, simulation studies place taxels uniformly over the hand, and this placement has become a default without being tested. We test this default under a single controlled protocol. The protocol holds the teacher, the training procedure, and the candidate taxels fixed and varies only the sensor configuration and the representation. We evaluate it on in-palm rotation and grasping with three robot hands. A small set of taxels selected from contact statistics matches a far larger uniform set. Taxels at rarely contacted sites are equivalent to no tactile input. With all candidate taxels, their layout in the input tensor does not affect performance, even for a convolutional encoder. Uniform placement therefore overestimates the number of taxels a task requires. We distill these results into lessons for designing tactile policies and into a minimal set of design choices that a tactile policy study should report.
2611.10647.comment: Accepted at the Workshop on Everything Beneath the Policy, CoRL 2026. 8 pages, 5 figures, 12 tables

llm.title_ja: タクセル数ではなくどのタクセルか：器用なポリシーのための触覚センサ配置
llm.tldr_ja: 接触統計から選択された少数のタクセルが、より大規模な一様なタクセルセットと同等の性能を発揮することを実証した。
llm.problem: 器用なマニピュレーションポリシーにおける触覚センサの配置や選択の基準が十分に検証されていない。
llm.method: 教師、訓練手順、候補タクセルを固定し、センサ構成と表現のみを変更する制御プロトコルによる評価。
llm.result: 接触統計から選択された少数のタクセルが大規模な一様セットと同等であり、一様配置は必要なタクセル数を過大評価していることを示した。

2611.10647.tldr_en: This work distills lessons for designing tactile policies and a minimal set of design choices that a tactile policy study should report into a minimal set of design choices that a tactile policy study should report.

2611.10635.title: Model-Based Imitation Learning For Monocular Vision-Based Navigation
2611.10635.abstract: Reliable navigation with a single monocular limited field-of-view camera is challenging because the lack of depth measurements and limited spatial awareness complicate collision checking. Existing approaches to tackle these challenges fall into two categories. Model-based planners can incorporate explicit collision-avoidance guidance which leads to better generalization but are often computationally expensive and require manual tuning of the algorithmic parameters. In contrast, end-to-end approaches trained by imitation learning can be flexible but typically encode safety only implicitly and thus can suffer from high collision rates in novel scenarios. In this paper, we present a middle ground through model-based imitation learning. The model-based part is a learned collision model that can map a sequence of past images and a candidate control sequence to a distribution of worst-case obstacle clearance. This predictive distribution in turn is used to define a collision-risk cost in a trajectory optimization formulation. The imitation component uses human demonstrations to learn scene-dependent balancing of collision risk with other task costs such as goal progress. We also use it to learn the algorithmic parameters (e.g., a warm start) of our optimizer to accelerate the solution process. We show that our approach can demonstrate highly reliable navigation in cluttered environments on robots with different embodiments. We also demonstrate a substantial reduction in collision rate over recent end-to-end and model-based baselines.

llm.title_ja: 単眼ビジョンベースナビゲーションのためのモデルベース模倣学習
llm.tldr_ja: 最悪の障害物クリアランスの予測分布を用いて衝突リスクコストを定義し、人間のデモンストレーションから学習するモデルベース模倣学習を提案した。
llm.problem: 単眼カメラのみを用いた信頼性の高いナビゲーションは、深度測定の欠如と限られた空間認識により困難である。
llm.method: 学習された衝突モデルと軌道最適化を組み合わせたモデルベース模倣学習フレームワークの提案。
llm.result: 様々なロボットの形態において cluttered な環境での高信頼なナビゲーションを実現し、ベースラインと比較して衝突率を大幅に削減した。

2611.10635.tldr_en: This paper presents a middle ground through model-based imitation learning that can demonstrate highly reliable navigation in cluttered environments on robots with different embodiments and demonstrates a substantial reduction in collision rate over recent end-to-end and model-based baselines.

2611.09892.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
