We introduce Augmentron, a geometry-aware pipeline that generates reusable scene representations and renders them through recorded camera poses. This produces temporally and multi-view consistent environ- ment and workspace variations while preserving the robot, task objects, actions, and annotations. Across three physical manipulation tasks, replacing half of the real world training dataset with Augmentron data improves model success across three tasks for both in out-of-distribution distractor objects, and out-of-distribution workspace variation evaluations. In a separate comparison against alternate augmentation techniques, Augmentron achieves the highest pooled success in all three conditions. The results show that introducing augmented data to a data training recipe can help policies generalize to dynamic real-world settings.
2611.09145.comment: Accepted to the 8th Robot Learning Workshop (WRL), NeurIPS 2026

llm.title_ja: Augmentron：ロボット学習のためのスケーラブルなマルチビュー視覚的拡張
llm.tldr_ja: 記録されたカメラポーズを通じてシーン表現をレンダリングし、時間的・マルチビューで一貫した環境変異を生成するジオメトリ認識型パイプラインAugmentronを提案した。
llm.problem: 視覚的に狭いデモンストレーションで訓練されたロボットポリシーは、タスクに関係のない環境特徴に過敏になりやすい。
llm.method: ロボット、タスクオブジェクト、アクションを保持しながら、シーン表現を生成して記録されたカメラポーズでレンダリングするジオメトリ認識型パイプラインを用いる。
llm.result: 3つの物理的マニピュレーションタスクにおいて、訓練データの半分をAugmentronデータに置き換えることで、未見の環境や外乱に対する汎化性能が向上した。

2611.09145.tldr_en: Across three physical manipulation tasks, replacing half of the real world training dataset with Augmentron data improves model success across three tasks for both in out-of-distribution distractor objects, and out-of-distribution workspace variation evaluations.

2611.09130.title: Auditing Grasp Feasibility Predictors with Planner-Verified Counterfactuals
2611.09130.abstract: Grasp-feasibility predictors report near-perfect accuracy on Task and Motion Planning benchmarks, but high accuracy on these benchmarks does not verify that a predictor uses the collision geometry that the motion planner checks. We propose a planner-verified counterfactual (CF) test: holding the grasp pose fixed, we insert a solid obstacle into the approach corridor, add its points to the model input, and let a planner re-derive the label, which flips from feasible to infeasible. Across eight predictors spanning point clouds, voxels, depth, and object tokens, CF-pair AUROC falls from high natural AUROC (0.920-0.996) to chance (0.470-0.504), and the flip holds across four planners, two arms, and a real-object obstacle. Predictors fail at different resolutions, from a bounding box to a 12.5 cm voxel. In the point-cloud models we dissect, the obstacle either moves the representation in a direction unrelated to whether it blocks the grasp or is not registered at all. A clearance-aware read of the corridor points, trained on the unmodified benchmark with no counterfactual scenes, reaches 0.983 CF-pair AUROC, but it remains bound to its trained obstacle placements; a placement-invariant clearance representation is still open. We release the counterfactual labels, metrics, datasheet, and relabeling pipeline at https://github.com/codewithsajid/graspfc-cf.
2611.09130.comment: Accepted to WACV 2027. 10 pages main paper + 8 pages supplementary

llm.title_ja: プランナー検証済み反事実を用いた把持可能性予測器の監査
llm.tldr_ja: 把持姿勢を固定したままアプローチ回廊に障害物を挿入し、プランナーによるラベルの反転を利用して把持可能性予測器の妥当性を検証するテストを提案した。
llm.problem: 把持可能性予測器はベンチマークで高精度を示すが、モーションプランナーがチェックする衝突ジオメトリを実際に用いているかは検証されていない。
llm.method: 把持姿勢を固定した状態でアプローチ回廊に固体の障害物を挿入し、モデルへの入力に追加してプランナーにラベルを再導出させる反事実テストを実施する。
llm.result: 自然なベンチマークでの高精度にもかかわらず、障害物が追加された反事実テストでは予測器の性能が偶然レベルにまで低下することが判明した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2611.09130.tldr_en: A planner-verified counterfactual (CF) test is proposed: holding the grasp pose fixed, a solid obstacle is inserted into the approach corridor, add its points to the model input, and let a planner re-derive the label, which flips from feasible to infeasible.

2611.09129.title: TouchAnnotator: Multi-Source Tactile Supervision with Privileged-View Distillation
2611.09129.abstract: Egocentric video captures human-object interaction at scale but rarely includes tactile labels for hidden contact and pressure. We introduce TouchAnnotator, an ego-only bimanual tactile annotator trained with multi-source tactile supervision and privileged-view distillation. A canonical hand field unifies glove pressure, geometry-derived human contact, and robot fingertip deformation from six datasets and three embodiments, while source-aware masks preserve valid targets. During training, an EMA teacher observes synchronized ego and wrist views and distills hand-local representations and tactile predictions into a student that uses only ego video and estimated pose at inference. Compact past-clip memory supplies temporal context. We evaluate on EgoTouch, zero-shot FPHA transfer, and 860 synchronized glove recordings. The model transfers to bare-hand contact and produces qualitatively coherent tactile responses across bare-hand, gloved-hand, and robot embodiments. On measured recordings, it improves temporal accuracy by 5.38 points and Volumetric IoU by 5.02 points under a shared protocol. These results show that heterogeneous human--robot supervision and privileged training views can turn egocentric video into dense tactile annotations.

llm.title_ja: TouchAnnotator：特権ビュー蒸留によるマルチソース触覚教師あり学習
llm.tldr_ja: マルチソースの触覚教師あり学習と特権ビュー蒸留を用いて、一人称視点動画から隠れた接触や圧力を密に注釈するTouchAnnotatorを提案した。
llm.problem: 一人称視点動画は人間と物の相互作用を大規模に捉えられるものの、接触や圧力に関する触覚ラベルがほとんど含まれていない。
llm.method: グローブの圧力や幾何学的接触、ロボットの指先の変形を正規化された手のフィールドで統合し、EMA教師モデルから一人称視点動画のみを使用する学生モデルへ知識を蒸留する。
llm.result: ベアハンド、グローブ装着手、ロボットの多様な身体において一貫した触覚応答を生成し、時間的精度と体積IoUが向上した。

2611.09129.tldr_en: TouchAnnotator, an ego-only bimanual tactile annotator trained with multi-source tactile supervision and privileged-view distillation, shows that heterogeneous human--robot supervision and privileged training views can turn egocentric video into dense tactile annotations.

2611.09124.title: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence
2611.09124.abstract: Foundation models increasingly guide robot actions, yet sustained autonomy requires efficient control and failure recovery. We introduce A2-MEAS, an embodied multi-agent framework built around code as a scaling interface. Learned correction codes combine corrective language, spatial evidence, execution history, and action proposals. MetaBrain provides training supervision and runtime guidance. A correction encoder and adapter absorb this knowledge into policy weights during training, while fresh codes adapt behavior with frozen weights at deployment. The action model, A2-WLA, adds motion-aware history and a latent world model to a vision-language-action policy. Surprisingly, this simple design with action pretraining and task specialization reaches 0.5755 Q-score on the 50-task BEHAVIOR 2026 public subset before online correction, 2.21x the 2025 winner's reported 0.2605 across different benchmark editions and training configurations. On all 100 BEHAVIOR 2026 public tasks, A2-MEAS achieves 0.6411 Q-score and 45.40% task success. On RoboTwin 2.0, A2-WLA achieves 93.98% average success, rising to 95.05% with the complete system. Across 12 real-robot tasks in five household settings, A2-WLA achieves 57.92% average success versus 26.67% for pi0.5. In long-horizon pour-over coffee preparation, a history-conditioned adapter raises post-failure completion at two filter-handling steps from 14% to 94% and from 8% to 82%, compared with A2-WLA retries. Our training infrastructure delivers 427.1 samples per second, 4.03x the throughput of a pi0.5 reference implementation on matched hardware. We will release the system, models, training scripts, and infrastructure to support efficient embodied learning.

llm.title_ja: エージェント型身体性知能の時代に向けて
llm.tldr_ja: コードをスケーリングインターフェースとして構築された身体性マルチエージェントフレームワークA2-MEASを提案し、効率的な制御と障害からの復旧を実現した。
llm.problem: 基盤モデルがロボットの行動を導くようになる中、持続的な自律性のために効率的な制御と失敗からの回復が必要とされている。
llm.method: 訂正コードを組み合わせた学習済み修正機構と、動作を認識する履歴および潜在世界モデルをVLAポリシーに追加した行動モデルA2-WLAを組み合わせる。
llm.result: BEHAVIOR 2026ベンチマークやRoboTwin 2.0、および実機における12のタスクで優れた成功率とコーヒー準備タスクでの高い復旧率を達成した。

2611.09124.tldr_en: This work introduces A2-MEAS, an embodied multi-agent framework built around code as a scaling interface that combines corrective language, spatial evidence, execution history, and action proposals to support efficient embodied learning.
2611.09124.hf_summary_en: An embodied multi-agent framework uses learned correction codes and a vision-language-action model with motion-aware history and latent world modeling to improve robot control, failure recovery, and training efficiency.

2611.08462.title: OopsieRecover: Learning Transferable VLA Corrections from Semantic Interventions
2611.08462.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform a wide range of robotic manipulation tasks, but often fail during deployment. Teaching them to recover from these failures requires substantial corrective data: existing approaches learn to recover from failures by directly associating corrective actions with the observations in which they were demonstrated. For instance, DAgger-like fine-tuning can require tens to hundreds of interactions, yet the resulting policy may still fail to generalize the learned corrections beyond the demonstrated scenarios. We hypothesize that semantics can capture the underlying reasons for failures and their corrections, enabling policies to learn from only a handful of corrective demonstrations and generalize those corrections to novel objects, and scene variations. We propose OopsieRecover, a framework that uses abduction to infer the intent behind a small set of corrective demonstrations and encodes the inferred knowledge as dense spatial representations and conditional costs. These costs capture when a behavior is undesirable and steer the policy toward more desirable action regions. We experiment across 6 tasks and variations in object poses, scenes, and related tasks, and find that only a handful of corrective demonstrations can enable a VLA to overcome failures across a broad range of novel situations, without requiring new corrective data for each variation. Please refer to https://robin-lab.cs.utexas.edu/oopsierecover for videos.

llm.title_ja: OopsieRecover: セマンティックな介入による転移可能なVLA修正の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 意味的介入からの転移可能なVLA修正を学習するフレームワークOopsieRecoverを提案し、少数の修正デモからVLAが幅広い新規状況での失敗を克服できるようにする。
llm.problem: VLAモデルのデプロイ時の失敗からの復旧には膨大な修正データが必要であり、学習した修正の汎化性能が低いこと。
llm.method: アブダクションを用いて少数の修正デモの意図を推論し、知識を密な空間表現と条件付きコストとしてエンコードするフレームワーク。
llm.result: わずか少数の修正デモにより、追加データなしで広範な新規状況においてVLAの失敗克服を可能にした。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.08462.tldr_en: OoopsieRecover is proposed, a framework that uses abduction to infer the intent behind a small set of corrective demonstrations and encodes the inferred knowledge as dense spatial representations and conditional costs that steer the policy toward more desirable action regions.

2611.08458.title: Latent RL Priors for Data-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation
2611.08458.abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation from limited visual demonstrations is challenging because policies must acquire both perceptual grounding and precise control, while reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation can acquire rich control behaviors from large-scale interaction with privileged information. We introduce \textbf{Latent RL Prior}, a two-stage framework that reuses this control knowledge for data-efficient visual policy learning. During privileged pretraining, we distill large-scale RL rollouts into a flow-matching action decoder conditioned on proprioception and latent task context. During visual adaptation, we freeze the decoder and learn a visual interface that maps images to its latent context using action supervision alone, without privileged labels or latent targets. The same decoder can further be shared across arms by learning coordinated visual contexts for bimanual manipulation. Across three simulated tasks, our method outperforms full-parameter fine-tuning of $π_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7 in the low-data regime; on door lifting and bimanual assembly, it surpasses full-data baselines using $10\times$ and $5\times$ fewer demonstrations, respectively. Further analysis shows that direct visual-to-latent conditioning improves adaptation performance and training stability over routing visual predictions through the pretrained state encoder. Robustness to unseen mass variation and greater linear accessibility of contact-force information in decoder representations further provide evidence of retained RL-acquired control knowledge. Project website: https://yixiaowang7.github.io/latent-rl-prior-page/.

llm.title_ja: データ効率の高い器用な操作のための潜在RL事前分布
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模RLの制御知識をフロースマッチング行動デコーダに蒸留し、視覚的適応を行う二段階フレームワークLatent RL Priorを提案し、少ないデモンストレーションでの器用な操作学習を実現する。
llm.problem: 限られた視覚的デモンストレーションからの器用な操作の学習が、知覚の基礎付けと精密な制御の双方を必要とするため困難であること。
llm.method: 特権的事前学習により大規模RLのロールアウトを潜在タスク文脈に条件付けられた行動デコーダに蒸留し、視覚インタフェースを学習する。
llm.result: 低データ環境においてベースラインを凌駕し、ドア持ち上げや両手組立において5〜10倍少ないデモでベースラインを上回った。

2611.08458.tldr_en: Analysis shows that direct visual-to-latent conditioning improves adaptation performance and training stability over routing visual predictions through the pretrained state encoder, and robustness to unseen mass variation and greater linear accessibility of contact-force information in decoder representations further provide evidence of retained RL-acquired control knowledge.

2611.08449.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
2611.08449.abstract: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding. VFlash exploits the known structure of visual primitives to predict their coordinates jointly, using a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass. The layout adapts to the primitive's type, dimensionality, and length, supporting compact boxes and long, variable-length trajectories. Crucially, spatial accuracy need not require reproducing an autoregressive model's exact token sequence. VFlash therefore trains on annotated primitives and directly accepts structurally valid predictions without target-token agreement. Across the evaluated 2D and 3D robot trajectory tasks, VFlash consistently reduces prediction errors relative to autoregressive decoding. Preliminary single-rollout measurements indicate approximately 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting. A world action model conditioned on VFlash plans achieves 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites, compared with 62.6% for the baseline.
2611.08449.hf_summary_en: VFlash employs Flash Primitive Decoding to predict visual primitive coordinates jointly via a lightweight drafter, reducing trajectory prediction error and generation time while improving downstream world action model success.

llm.title_ja: VFlash: フラッシュプリミティブデコーディングによる高速で正確な視覚的計画
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚プリミティブの構造を利用して座標を共同予測し、生成を大幅に高速化するVFlashを提案し、予測誤差の削減と成功率の向上を実現する。
llm.problem: 自己回帰型ビジョン言語モデルが視覚計画を1座標トークンずつ生成するため、予測コストが高くなること。
llm.method: 軽量なドラフターを用いて1回のフォワードパスでプリミティブ全体を予測するFlash Primitive Decodingの導入。
llm.result: 3Dポイント動作予測において約25倍高速な生成を実現し、タスクスイートで平均成功率70.2%を達成した。

2611.08449.tldr_en: VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding, which trains on annotated primitives and directly accepts structurally valid predictions without target-token agreement, and consistently reduces prediction errors relative to autoregressive decoding.

2611.08425.title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
2611.08425.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people. Deploying VLAs in real-world systems therefore requires a runtime monitor that is timely, calibrated, and informative while being efficient enough to run on the edge. Existing methods fail to fulfill these requirements. We present VLA-Tug, a lightweight probe over the latent layers of a VLA backbone that improves early failure detection and bounds the missed-detection and false-alarm rates, with minimal inference overhead. We show that supervising on the pre-failure segment of a trajectory increases early failure detection at matched false-positive rates by up to 30% over the strongest learned baseline. Under shift to unseen tasks, the bounds on missed-detection and false-alarm rates remain valid in up to 86% of runs, versus at most 21% for baselines. Unlike existing methods, VLA-Tug predicts the failure mode to enable corrective actions, raising top-3 accuracy on unseen tasks by up to 44% over a majority baseline. VLA-Tug enables real-time monitoring where the well-timed and informative probe supports lightweight steering that improves task success. We release a dataset of 3,180 annotated manipulation episodes to support future work on latent failure detection in VLAs at https://vla-tug.github.io.
2611.08425.comment: Code, videos, and dataset available at https://vla-tug.github.io

llm.title_ja: 校正された潜在プローブによるVision-Language-Actionモデルの失敗予測と分類
llm.tldr_ja: VLAバックボーンの潜在層に対する軽量プローブVLA-Tugにより、推論オーバーヘッドを抑えながら早期の失敗検出と誤検知率の抑制を実現する。
llm.problem: VLAは分布シフトに対して脆弱であり、実世界システムへのデプロイには適時かつ校正された実行時モニタリングが必要であること。
llm.method: VLAバックボーンの潜在層に対する軽量プローブを構築し、失敗前の軌跡で教師あり学習を行う。
llm.result: 早期失敗検出率を最大30%向上させ、未見タスクの失敗モード予測におけるtop-3精度を最大44%向上させた。
keywords_ja: リアルタイムモニタリング

2611.08425.tldr_en: VLA-Tug is presented, a lightweight probe over the latent layers of a VLA backbone that improves early failure detection and bounds the missed-detection and false-alarm rates, with minimal inference overhead and enables real-time monitoring where the well-timed and informative probe supports lightweight steering that improves task success.

2611.08413.title: T3R: Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement Towards Efficient and Robust VLA Models
2611.08413.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable end-to-end robot control, but inference is increasingly expensive. Each decision processes hundreds of visual tokens, often across multiple cameras, leading to substantial computation while allowing irrelevant background content to distract action prediction under distribution shift. We argue that these issues stem from two complementary forms of redundancy: many visual tokens are spatially irrelevant, while attention over the remaining tokens is often misallocated. Based on this observation, we propose T3R, a Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement framework. In the first stage, segmentation-guided token pruning removes irrelevant visual patches to reduce computation and eliminate distracting context. In the second stage, saliency-guided attention biasing reallocates attention toward action-critical visual regions and language instructions within the retained tokens. Together, pruning produces a cleaner candidate set, while attention biasing further emphasizes the most decision-relevant evidence, yielding a better accuracy-efficiency frontier than either stage alone. On LIBERO-Spatial, T3R removes 85% of scene-camera visual tokens while essentially matching the unpruned success rate, and improves success by up to 7 percentage points under out-of-distribution object-placement perturbations. The timing comparison attributes 7.8 ms per inference call to pruning and attention-bias application. As input resolution increases, LLM-forward profiling shows up to a 3.3x speedup over the unpruned baseline. Evaluations across LIBERO, SIMPLER, and RoboTwin with three VLA backbones show the strongest accuracy-efficiency benefits in multi-camera settings. These results demonstrate that training-free token refinement is a practical approach to efficient and robust VLA inference.

llm.title_ja: T3R: 効率的で頑健なVLAモデルに向けたトレーニング不要の2段階トークンリファインメント
llm.tldr_ja: セグメンテーションに基づくトークンプルーニングとサリエンシーに基づくアテンションバイアスを組み合わせたトレーニング不要の2段階トークンリファインメントフレームワークT3Rにより、計算効率と頑健性を向上させる。
llm.problem: VLAモデルの推論において、無関係な背景トークンやアテンションの不適切な割り当てによる高い計算コストと性能低下が生じること。
llm.method: 第1ステージで無関係な視覚パッチをプルーニングし、第2ステージで行動クリティカルな視覚領域と指示にアテンションを再配分する。
llm.result: LIBERO-Spatialで85%の視覚トークンを削除しつつ成功率を維持し、最大3.3倍の高速化を達成した。

2611.08413.tldr_en: Evaluations across LIBERO, SIMPLER, and RoboTwin with three VLA backbones show the strongest accuracy-efficiency benefits in multi-camera settings, demonstrating that training-free token refinement is a practical approach to efficient and robust VLA inference.

2611.08407.title: Social Humanoid: Socially Responsive Human-Humanoid Interaction
2611.08407.abstract: Humanoid robots are typically trained as solitary agents, leaving them unable to coordinate physically with human partners who naturally anticipate and adjust to one another. To bridge this gap, we present Social Humanoid, a hierarchical system that generates and executes socially responsive whole-body motion on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 conditioned on a human partner's motion. Its high-level policy performs flexible sequence modeling of human and humanoid motion through a shared tokenized representation, generating reactive humanoid motion and anticipating the partner's motion when they are occluded, while a low-level whole-body tracking controller executes the generated motion on the robot. To train the system, we introduce a two-phase adaptive retargeting procedure that retargets one interaction partner to the robot while morphing the other partner to preserve contact dynamics, reachability, and relative body scale. We apply this procedure across five motion-capture datasets to produce a new Human-Humanoid Interaction (HHI) benchmark of 260 hours of human-humanoid interactions. Our results demonstrate that Social Humanoid produces coordinated, human-aligned behavior across diverse interaction types in simulation and the real world. Project page: https://von31.github.io/social-humanoid/

llm.title_ja: Social Humanoid: 社会的に応答性の高いヒューマン・ヒューマノイドインタラクション
llm.tldr_ja: 人間のパートナーの動作に条件付けられて社会的応答性の高い全身運動を生成・実行する階層型システムSocial Humanoidを提案し、シミュレーションと実世界で協調的行動を実現する。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドロボットが単独のエージェントとして訓練されており、物理的に協調する人間と自然に適応できないこと。
llm.method: 共有されたトークン化表現を用いて人間とヒューマノイドの動作をモデリングする高次元ポリシーと、全身トラッキングコントローラによる階層システム。
llm.result: 多様なインタラクションタイプにわたり、シミュレーションおよび実世界で人間と協調した一貫性のある行動を生成できた。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット
ヒューマンロボットインタラクション
モーションキャプチャ

2611.08407.tldr_en: Social Humanoid is a hierarchical system that generates and executes socially responsive whole-body motion on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 conditioned on a human partner's motion, and produces coordinated, human-aligned behavior across diverse interaction types in simulation and the real world.

2611.08398.title: A Multimodal Haptic Interface for Simultaneous Softness and Thermal Modulation
2611.08398.abstract: Haptic interactions, such as touching an object in virtual reality, involve detecting a plethora of sensations through the skin. Whilst tactile displays exist to simulate and manipulate all of these cues individually, little progress has been made constructing devices that can control multiple cues simultaneously. This paper presents a tactile display technology that offers both softness and temperature change. A prototype display, based on particle jamming and the thermal transfer of heated and cooled water, is evaluated in terms of its ability to change both stiffness and temperature. Mechanical evaluations demonstrate controllable stiffness increase of 300%, whilst thermal characterisation showed strong surface uniformity and a range of achievable temperatures from 10°C up to 50°C, with closed-loop control maintaining a 0.2°C error from a setpoint. This work advances the design of multimodal tactile displays with applications to perceptual research, medical simulation, and affective haptics.

llm.title_ja: 柔らかさと温度の同時変調のためのマルチモーダル触覚インターフェース
llm.tldr_ja: 粒子ジャーミングと温水・冷水の熱伝達を利用して柔らかさと温度の両方を制御する触覚ディスプレイのプロトタイプを開発し、剛性と温度の可変性を実証する。
llm.problem: 触覚ディスプレイは個別のキューをシミュレートできるが、複数のキューを同時に制御するデバイスの開発が進んでいないこと。
llm.method: 粒子ジャーミングと水温制御を組み合わせたマルチモーダル触覚ディスプレイの試作と機械的・熱的評価。
llm.result: 剛性の300%の制御可能な向上と、10°C〜50°Cの温度範囲で0.2°Cの誤差を維持する閉ループ制御を実証した。
keywords_ja: 触覚インターフェース
バーチャルリアリティ

2611.08390.title: SCALE: Real-Time Latent Communication for Cyber-Physical Agents
2611.08390.abstract: Latent communication enables agents to collaborate efficiently by directly exchanging intermediate model representations rather than raw sensor data or text messages. Existing approaches, however, are primarily designed for LLM agents and do not consider the bandwidth constraints and heterogeneous task deadlines faced by cyber-physical agents. In this work, we propose SCALE, a real-time latent communication method tailored for cyber-physical agents. Motivated by the spatio-temporal continuity of the physical world, SCALE matches tokens across consecutive latent messages using similarity scores to identify reusable information and avoid redundant transmission. It then profiles the semantic gain and communication cost of transmitting different amounts of latent information. Based on these profiles, SCALE employs a real-time scheduler that jointly determines which pending messages to transmit and how many latent tokens to send, subject to available bandwidth and task deadlines. We evaluate SCALE across three cyber-physical benchmarks and a physical spider robot case study under diverse network conditions and heterogeneous task deadlines. Our results show that SCALE significantly improves both task performance and on-time delivery in bandwidth-constrained networks. Our code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SCALE-4E80/.

llm.title_ja: SCALE: サイバー・フィジカル・エージェントのためのリアルタイム潜在通信
llm.tldr_ja: 物理世界の時空間的連続性を利用して連続する潜在メッセージ間のトークンをマッチングし、帯域幅と期限に合わせて送信を制御するリアルタイム潜在通信手法SCALEを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の潜在通信手法はLLMエージェント向けに設計されており、サイバー・フィジカル・エージェントが直面する帯域幅の制約や異種タスクの期限を考慮していないこと。
llm.method: 類似度スコアを用いたトークンのマッチングによる冗長送信の回避と、帯域幅・期限に応じたリアルタイムスケジューラーの導入。
llm.result: 帯域幅の限られたネットワークにおいて、タスク性能と期限内配信率を大幅に向上させた。
keywords_ja: サイバー・フィジカル・システム

2611.08390.tldr_en: The proposed SCALE employs a real-time scheduler that jointly determines which pending messages to transmit and how many latent tokens to send, subject to available bandwidth and task deadlines, and significantly improves both task performance and on-time delivery in bandwidth-constrained networks.

2611.08373.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
2611.08373.abstract: Reliable robotic manipulation requires both semantic understanding and precise control in three-dimensional space. However, vision-language-action (VLA) foundations largely inherit visual representations from 2D vision-language pre-training, while spatial supervision is often introduced only during task-specific adaptation. Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. We present SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action Model that scales implicit spatial alignment to continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training. Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, SLA jointly optimizes action prediction and alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and spatial representations from a frozen 3D perception model. We curate and unify heterogeneous robot datasets to support spatial learning across diverse embodiments, tasks, and scenes. To accommodate this diversity, we introduce feature-dependent gates that adaptively aggregate visual embeddings from multiple VLA layers for spatial supervision. The teacher further exploits partially available depth and camera calibration alongside RGB observations, enabling effective use of heterogeneous geometric annotations. Probabilistic state dropout encourages reliance on visual cues and mitigates overfitting to demonstration trajectories. All auxiliary components are used only during training, allowing direct reuse of pretrained VLA weights and preserving the original inference architecture.
2611.08373.hf_summary_en: The SLA model enhances spatial understanding in Vision-Language-Action systems by aligning visual embeddings with 3D spatial representations through continual pre-training and feature-dependent gating.

llm.title_ja: SLA: 継続的事前学習による空間・言語・行動モデルの拡張
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結された3D知覚モデルとの空間的アライメントを組み込んだ継続的事前学習により、多様なロボットデータで空間理解を向上させるSLAモデルを提案する。
llm.problem: VLA基盤モデルは2D視覚表現を継承しており、空間的監督がタスク特化型適応の段階でのみ導入されること。
llm.method: 事前学習済みポリシーを初期値とし、行動予測と、中間視覚埋め込みと凍結3D知覚モデルからの空間表現とのアライメントを共同最適化する。
llm.result: 多様なロボットデータ、タスク、シーンにわたって空間理解を向上させ、推論アーキテクチャをそのまま維持できることを示した。

2611.08373.tldr_en: This work presents SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action Model that scales implicit spatial alignment to continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training and curate and unify heterogeneous robot datasets to support spatial learning across diverse embodiments, tasks, and scenes.

2611.08372.title: MOMASPLAT: Dynamic Novel-View Demonstration Augmentation for Mobile Manipulation
2611.08372.abstract: Visuomotor policies trained through imitation learning are highly sensitive to changes in camera viewpoint. This is particularly problematic for mobile manipulation (MoMa), where robots rarely execute manipulation from the exact same base pose used during demonstration collection due to navigation uncertainty, localization drift, and environmental constraints. Recent approaches use novel-view synthesis (NVS) to augment demonstrations with unseen viewpoints, but they assume static scenes and therefore fail to re-render the manipulated object during the post-contact interaction phase, leaving the most critical parts of the demonstration unaugmented. We present MOMASPLAT, a novel-view demonstration augmentation framework for mobile manipulation that synthesizes full manipulation trajectories from unseen robot base poses, including dynamic object interactions. Our key insight is that standard MoMa data collection naturally provides the multiview observations needed to reconstruct both the static scene and the manipulated object in 3D. MOMASPLAT combines 3D Gaussian Splatting, feed-forward 3D foundation models, and kinematics-based action retargeting to separately reconstruct the scene and manipulated object, render them from novel viewpoints, and generate geometrically consistent synthetic demonstrations paired with transformed actions. We evaluate MOMASPLAT on five real-world mobile manipulation tasks involving both rigid and articulated objects across three scenes, and validate the fidelity of its synthesized demonstrations against ground truth in simulation. MOMASPLAT substantially improves robustness to unseen base poses, more than doubling the average success rate of the strongest baseline and maintaining non-trivial success at large base displacements where all baselines fail, while reducing the need for largescale real-world data collection.

llm.title_ja: MOMASPLAT: モバイルマニピュレーションのための動的新規視点デモンストレーション拡張
llm.tldr_ja: 3Dガウススプラッティングと基盤モデルを組み合わせて、動的オブジェクトの相互作用を含む新規ロボット基準姿勢からの完全な操作軌跡を合成するフレームワークMOMASPLATを提案する。
llm.problem: モバイルマニピュレーションにおいて、ナビゲーションの不確実性等によりデモ時と異なるカメラ視点や基準姿勢の変化が生じるが、既存の新規視点合成は静的シーンを仮定しており動的相互作用を扱えないこと。
llm.method: 3Dガウススプラッティング、3D基盤モデル、および運動学ベースの行動リタイージェティングを組み合わせてシーンと操作対象を個別に再構築し合成する。
llm.result: 未見の基準姿勢に対する頑健性が大幅に向上し、最強のベースラインの平均成功率の2倍以上を達成した。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレーション

2611.08372.tldr_en: MOMASPLAT substantially improves robustness to unseen base poses, more than doubling the average success rate of the strongest baseline and maintaining non-trivial success at large base displacements where all baselines fail, while reducing the need for largescale real-world data collection.

2611.08368.title: VisionSIM: Beyond Idealized Sensors - A Multi-Modal Simulator for Robot Perception
2611.08368.abstract: Robotic perception increasingly relies on heterogeneous sensor suites combining cameras with emerging modalities (event, SPAD, iToF/dToF, and thermal). Yet existing simulators idealize these sensors, hiding critical modality-specific failure modes that limit real-world deployment. We present VisionSIM, a unified, physically grounded simulation platform that elevates sensor realism to a first-class concern by modeling the raw physical measurement process for diverse conventional and emerging modalities. We expose fine-grained control over physical sensor parameters, reproducing failure modes overlooked by general-purpose simulators: pileup and glare for LiDAR; phase wrapping, saturation, and motion artifacts for iToF; refractory drops for event cameras; and history-dependent emission for thermal cameras. This enables principled cross-modality comparison on identical scenes and trajectories. We release the platform and a large indoor dataset with synchronized raw measurements and rich ground-truth annotations.

llm.title_ja: VisionSIM: 理想化されたセンサーを超えて - ロボット知覚のためのマルチモーダルシミュレーター
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な従来型および新興センサーの生物理学的測定プロセスをモデル化し、センサー特有の失敗モードを再現する統合シミュレーションプラットフォームVisionSIMを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のシミュレーターはセンサーを理想化しており、実世界展開を制限する重要なモダリティ固有の失敗モードを隠蔽していること。
llm.method: LiDAR、iToF、イベントカメラ、サーマルカメラなどの生物理学的測定プロセスと失敗モードを物理ベースで詳細にモデル化する。
llm.result: 同一シーンと軌跡におけるクロスモダリティの比較を可能にし、豊富な正解注釈付きの大規模屋内データセットとプラットフォームを公開した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダルセンサー
物理ベースシミュレーション

2611.08368.tldr_en: VisionSIM is presented, a unified, physically grounded simulation platform that elevates sensor realism to a first-class concern by modeling the raw physical measurement process for diverse conventional and emerging modalities.

2611.08364.title: SHORE: Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Online Bin Packing
2611.08364.abstract: Online 3D bin packing with a processing buffer requires choosing which box to pack, its orientation, and its placement while keeping the stack stable under unknown future arrivals. A collapse ends the episode and forfeits the remaining volume. Existing methods use geometric rules or hard stability masks, limiting how risk can influence the joint choice of box, orientation, and placement. We propose Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning (SHORE), which combines a learned stability probability of a placement with an on-policy estimate of its return conditional on stability. A 3D U-Net learns stability from executed outcomes and simulated alternatives, revealing outcomes of actions underrepresented in early rollouts. A discrete on-policy actor--critic uses stability predictions in both its action values and policy prior, with gates that limit the effect of an untrained or changing model. In deployment, SHORE does not require additional search or simulation overhead. In Isaac Gym, SHORE reaches 73\% space utilization by 0.4M environment steps, while the same learner without stability modeling reaches that level at about 1M. On the expanded 60-box set, SHORE achieves 0.734 space utilization versus 0.588 for the GOPT state-of-the-art baseline, with a higher placement-failure frequency (1.03\% vs. 0.63\%), trading more risk for greater packed volume. The results show faster learning and higher utilization on the more demanding realistic box arrival set. Ablations suggest that simulated alternatives provide useful early supervision, while executed outcomes alone sustain later performance. We also demonstrate the method on a real robot to verify the simplicity of integrating the method to real bin packing pipelines.

llm.title_ja: SHORE: オンライン箱詰めのための安定性ハイブリッドオンポリシー強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 配置の学習済み安定性確率と安定性条件付きリターンのオンポリシー推定を組み合わせ、リアルタイムの箱詰め効率を高めるSHOREを提案する。
llm.problem: オンライン3D箱詰めにおいて、幾何学的ルールやハードな安定性マスクを使用することが、箱の選択、向き、配置の共同最適化へのリスクの影響を制限していること。
llm.method: 3D U-Netによる配置の安定性学習と、安定性予測を行動価値とポリシー事前分布の両方に利用する離散オンポリシーアクター・クリティックの組み合わせ。
llm.result: Isaac Gymにおいて0.4Mステップで73%の空間利用率を達成し、従来ベースラインを上回る効率と学習速度を示した。

2611.08364.tldr_en: This work proposes Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning (SHORE), which combines a learned stability probability of a placement with an on-policy estimate of its return conditional on stability, and shows faster learning and higher utilization on the more demanding realistic box arrival set.

2611.08361.title: Radio-to-Pose Information for Gauge-Drift Correction in Cooperative Localization
2611.08361.abstract: Cooperative localization uses odometry and inter-robot measurements to estimate the motion of a robot team. These measurements describe only relative geometry, but the team's estimated position and orientation can drift together over time, i.e., gauge drift. In this work, we study correction of this gauge drift using a radio attenuation map registered in the same world coordinate frame used for robot poses. Specifically, we propose Radio-to-Pose Information (RPI), an interface that converts power residuals and their pose derivatives into a Gaussian information matrix and vector pair. RPI builds on the insight that received power is sensitive to shared displacement in the world map. The pose estimator uses the interface together with odometry and inter-robot measurements to update poses and minimize uncertainty. We characterize the shared motions detectable from the map and observed links. For an uncertain shared map, RPI keeps correlations across robots and time and reproduces joint Gaussian pose estimates and covariances. Across $1000$ simulated Gaussian trials, RPI matches the results of joint estimation. Across 32 paired trials with a registered map, RPI reduces common-position RMSE from $0.542$m to $0.140$m in a $50\times50$m arena compared with a baseline that uses radio only to weight relative measurements.

llm.title_ja: 協調型自己位置推定におけるゲージドリフト補正のためのラジオ・ツー・ポーズ情報
llm.tldr_ja: 世界座標系に登録された電波減衰マップを用いて相対測定値の更新を行い、ロボットチームのゲージドリフトを効果的に補正するRadio-to-Pose Information (RPI)を提案する。
llm.problem: 協調型自己位置推定において、オドメトリーとロボット間測定は相対幾何学のみを記述するため、推定位置と方位が時間の経過とともに一緒にドリフト（ゲージドリフト）すること。
llm.method: 受信電力の残差とその姿勢微分をガウス情報行列とベクトルペアに変換するインターフェースRPIの構築。
llm.result: 1000回のシミュレーション試行で共同推定の結果と一致し、32回の実試行で共通位置RMSEを0.542mから0.140mに削減した。
keywords_ja: 協調ローカリゼーション

2611.08361.tldr_en: Radio-to-Pose Information is proposed, an interface that converts power residuals and their pose derivatives into a Gaussian information matrix and vector pair and reproduces joint Gaussian pose estimates and covariances for an uncertain shared map.

2611.08352.title: USB Gym: A Gymnasium Testbed for Closed-Loop Ultrasound View Matching
2611.08352.abstract: Background and Objective: Our main goal is ultrasound guidance: moving a probe until its image matches a target view. Published methods for each part of a guide are evaluated in separate simulators. We asked whether these methods, combined into one guide, are good enough. Methods: We built USB Gym, a testbed whose standard engine simulates ultrasound from public patient CT, with a network drawing organ textures from CT labels. Its guide has three replaceable parts (slots), an organ segmenter, a controller and a reward, which received 20 published methods, each run on the same 60 episodes of six held-out patients. In each slot, a published method replaced ours only if detectably better on these patients. The better of this combination and our original guide on 20 new CTs is the benchmark baseline. A pose oracle, reading the exact probe pose available only in simulation, set the reference. The results below are exploratory. Results: On these CTs, the probe started on average 16.0 mm from the target view; the pose oracle brought it to 1.5 mm. Of the results known when the combination was fixed, only an image-similarity reward (SSIM) was slightly but detectably better, so the combination was our guide with that reward. This combination was the benchmark baseline, ending at 13.7 mm (16% of the oracle's progress). Conclusions: Combining untuned published methods with ours did not guide the probe near the target view; the task remains under-explored. The testbed accepts new methods; no guide was tested on hardware.
2611.08352.comment: 75 pages; supplementary material (62 pages) as an ancillary file. Submitted to Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine. Code: https://github.com/tohnperfect/USBGym

llm.title_ja: USB Gym: 閉ループ超音波ビューマッチングのためのGymnasiumテストベッド
llm.tldr_ja: パブリックな患者CTから超音波をシミュレートし、器官セグメンター、コントローラー、報酬を評価できる標準化されたテストベッドUSB Gymを構築し、公開手法の統合評価を行った。
llm.problem: 超音波ガイドの各部分に対する既存手法が個別のシミュレーターで評価されており、統合された性能が十分に検証されていないこと。
llm.method: パブリックCTから器官テクスチャを描画するネットワークと標準エンジンを用いた超音波シミュレーションテストベッドの構築。
llm.result: 未調整の公開手法を組み合わせたガイドではターゲットビュー付近への誘導が不十分であり、タスクが未開拓であることを示した。
llm.limitation: ハードウェア上でのガイドテストは実施されていない
keywords_ja: シミュレーションテストベッド

2611.08352.tldr_en: Conclusions: Combining untuned published methods with the authors' did not guide the probe near the target view; the task remains under-explored.

2611.08338.title: GPWM: Modeling the World as 3D Particle Motion
2611.08338.abstract: We introduce GPWM, a Generative Particle World Model that predicts how 3D scenes evolve by generating the motion of particles and rigid bodies over time. Unlike video world models that generate scene appearance, GPWM operates directly in 3D physical space. A single representation and architecture cover rigid, deformable, cloth, and granular materials, in both passive physics and robotic interaction. GPWM is an object-aware multi-resolution transformer that combines flow matching with diffusion forcing to generate coherent physical trajectories far beyond its training horizon. We train and evaluate GPWM on ParticleWorlds, a 25.5-million-frame corpus spanning diverse geometries, materials, interactions, and robot embodiments. GPWM outperforms the best prior learned-dynamics baseline in each of six physical domains, reducing prediction error by 31% on average. Breaking from the domain-specific setting of prior methods, a single Unified GPWM models these heterogeneous regimes with one set of weights, largely outperforming per-domain baselines and even surpassing our own specialist models in two domains. GPWM further generalizes to unseen geometries, physical properties, object counts, and rollout horizons. Beyond prediction, GPWM enables contact-rich planning by learning a generative prior over joint actuator-object motion. Instead of searching over unconstrained actions, planning searches the model's latent noise for interactions that achieve a desired object-space goal. With the same world model, noise-space planning substantially outperforms action-space search on pushing and picking, where complex contact sequences are hard to discover. Executed open-loop in simulation, the resulting plans achieve goal-directed manipulation without reference action trajectories or goal-specific policies.
2611.08338.comment: 39 pages, 27 figures, 7 tables. Robert Ren and Matthew Bronars contributed equally (ordered by coin flip). Project page: https://robertren1122.github.io/gpwm/

llm.title_ja: GPWM: 3Dパーティクルモーションとしての世界モデル化
llm.tldr_ja: パーティクルと剛体の動きを3D物理空間で直接生成し、多様な材質やタスクを単一の表現でモデル化する生成型パーティクル世界モデル(GPWM)を提案する。
llm.problem: 動画ベースの世界モデルはシーンの見た目を生成するのみであり、3D物理空間での多様な材質やロボット相互作用を直接扱えないこと。
llm.method: フロースマッチングと拡散フォーシングを組み合わせた、オブジェクト認識型マルチ解像度トランスフォーマーによるパーティクルモーション予測。
llm.result: 6つの物理ドメインすべてで従来手法を凌駕し、予測誤差を平均31%削減、接触を伴うプランニングでの優れた性能を実証した。
keywords_ja: パーティクルモーション
物理シミュレーション

2611.08338.tldr_en: A single Unified GPWM is introduced that predicts how 3D scenes evolve by generating the motion of particles and rigid bodies over time by largely outperforming per-domain baselines and even surpassing its own specialist models in two domains.

2611.08318.title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
2611.08318.abstract: Self-improving embodied agents are increasingly being developed and compared on robot simulation benchmarks. Several recent works expose the benchmark's success criteria to the learning agent, a practice we call Criteria Exposure (CE). These criteria, originally written to verify policies trained by imitation learning, often demand more than the corresponding language instructions, so a score from such a verifier may not faithfully reflect whether the instructed task was completed, especially for robot-control programs written by an agent. As embodied coding agents report ever higher benchmark scores, a natural question arises: when a coding agent is exposed to the benchmark's criteria, does it generate code that better performs the instructed task, or code that simply overfits to the verification criteria? We conduct controlled experiments with a self-improving agent with and without CE, and find that with CE the agent quickly produces code with a higher success rate under the given criteria, but this advantage disappears when the criteria are changed slightly without departing from the original instructions. More importantly, the skills the agent develops under CE transfer poorly across tasks. We further propose instruction-faithful criteria and show that they better reflect the performance of agent-generated programs.

llm.title_ja: タスクの学習か、検証器の学習か？: 身体性自己改善における基準曝露の再考
llm.tldr_ja: 身体性エージェントの自己改善ベンチマークにおいて成功基準をエージェントに公開する「基準曝露（CE）」が汎化性能やスキル転移に与える影響を制御実験により検証した。
llm.problem: ベンチマークの成功基準を学習エージェントに公開するプラクティス（CE）により、指示されたタスクではなく検証基準に過剰適合してしまう懸念があること。
llm.method: セルフ改善型エージェントを用いて、基準曝露あり／なしでのタスク成功率やスキル転移性能を比較する制御実験の実施。
llm.result: CEありの環境では特定基準での成功率は上がるものの、基準がわずかに変更された際に優位性が消失し、スキル転移が不十分であることを示した。

2611.08318.tldr_en: This work conducts controlled experiments with a self-improving agent with and without Criteria Exposure (CE), and finds that with CE the agent quickly produces code with a higher success rate under the given criteria, but this advantage disappears when the criteria are changed slightly without departing from the original instructions.

2611.08308.title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines
2611.08308.abstract: Reward machines (RMs) have been proposed as a reward formulation in reinforcement learning (RL) to capture non-Markovian tasks where credit assignment depends on history. By representing reward functions as automata, RMs expose the task's temporal structure and allow such rewards to be handled within a Markovian framework. However, they assume a labelling function, a proposition-grounding oracle for observations, which must be manually engineered for each environment, limiting their wider applicability. In this work, we address this limitation by proposing RM-VLM, a novel approach in which a large language model (LLM) generates an RM from a natural-language task description, and a vision-language model (VLM) acts as the labelling function, grounding the RM's propositions over image-based observations during RM-guided policy learning. A VLM-based value function estimator is used to assess the agent's progress towards each RM transition and derive a dense reward signal. We evaluate RM-VLM on three domains covering non-Markovian grid-world navigation, robotic manipulation, and 3D object collection. Our experimental results show that RM-VLM consistently achieves higher task success rates than existing VLM-based reward methods across all tested domains.

llm.title_ja: RM-VLM: 自然言語タスク記述から視覚的グラウンディングされたリワードマシンへ
llm.tldr_ja: LLMからリワードマシンを生成し、VLMをラベリング関数として用いて画像観測上のプロポジションをグラウンディングするRM-VLMを提案し、タスク成功率の向上を実現する。
llm.problem: 強化学習における報酬マシン（RM）の適用には、環境ごとに手動で設計されたラベリング関数が必要であり、適用範囲が制限されること。
llm.method: 大規模言語モデルによるリワードマシンの生成と、視覚言語モデルによる画像ベース観測のプロポジションのグラウンディングの統合。
llm.result: 非マルコフ的グリッドワールド、ロボット操作、3Dオブジェクト収集の3つのドメインで、既存のVLMベースの報酬手法よりも高いタスク成功率を達成した。

2611.08308.tldr_en: This work proposes RM-VLM, a novel approach in which a large language model generates an RM from a natural-language task description, and a vision-language model acts as the labelling function, grounding the RM's propositions over image-based observations during RM-guided policy learning.

2611.08295.title: Transformer-Based Trajectory Prescription for sEMG-Optimizing Robot-Mediated Rehabilitation
2611.08295.abstract: Robot-mediated rehabilitation has the potential to deliver high-intensity, individualized therapy, but existing systems (which have not consistently improved outcomes) typically prescribe kinematic trajectories rather than explicitly targeting the neuromotor activations thought to support recovery. To address this gap, and ultimately enable activation-optimizing rehabilitation robot behavior, we present a personalizable transformer-based model mapping individuals' muscle activations (as measured via surface electromyography) to prescribed contact force trajectories when interacting with an end-effector rehabilitation robot. The model uses a transformer encoder-decoder leveraging rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) to generate a latent representation of trajectory-relevant and user-specific neuromotor factors, and augments trajectory prediction with flow matching to produce a distribution over plausible prescriptions biased toward the training distribution. Using data from 16 healthy participants completing 15 isometric trajectory tracking tasks, we evaluate generalization across held-out tasks and users, as well as the feasibility of user-specific fine-tuning within a therapy-session timescale. The model achieves mean trajectory prediction errors of <8% on held out tasks and users, with effectively instantaneous deterministic inference and sub-second sampling of trajectory distributions. An initial test using the model during live rehabilitation tasks demonstrates that, on average, participants reach the target neuromotor activations with just 15% error accumulated throughout the task. These results provide a proof of concept for data-driven, activation-targeted trajectory prescription in robot-mediated rehabilitation and establish a foundation for future validation in clinical populations. Data and code have been open-sourced as part of the OpenRobotRehab project on SimTK.
2611.08295.comment: Accepted for presentation and publication in the 2026 Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL). PMLR, 2026

llm.title_ja: 筋電図を最適化するロボット支援リハビリテーションのためのトランスフォーマーベース軌道処方
llm.tldr_ja: 筋電図（sEMG）で測定された個人の筋肉の活性化を所定の接触力軌道にマッピングするトランスフォーマーベースのモデルを提案し、リハビリテーションの個別最適化を実現する。
llm.problem: 既存のリハビリテーションロボットは運動学的軌道を処方するのみであり、回復を支える神経運動活性化を直接ターゲットにしていないこと。
llm.method: ロータリー位置埋め込みを用いたトランスフォーマーエンコーダ・デコーダとフロースマッチングを組み合わせた軌道処方モデルの構築。
llm.result: 未見のタスクやユーザーに対する平均軌道予測誤差が8%未満であり、ライブリハビリでのターゲット神経運動活性化の達成を実証した。
keywords_ja: ロボット支援リハビリテーション

2611.08295.tldr_en: A personalizable transformer-based model mapping individuals'muscle activations to prescribed contact force trajectories when interacting with an end-effector rehabilitation robot to establish a foundation for future validation in clinical populations and provide a proof of concept for data-driven, activation-targeted trajectory prescription in robot-mediated rehabilitation.

2611.08286.title: Interactive Visual Gym: Evaluating Visual Interaction Models with Simulated Users in Interactive Worlds
2611.08286.abstract: Visual interaction models that support users during ongoing physical tasks require evaluation in closed loop, where assistant responses can change subsequent user behavior and task outcomes. Existing benchmarks largely rely on offline replay and therefore cannot capture these effects. We introduce Interactive Visual Gym, a framework for closed-loop evaluation and training of visual interaction models through joint simulation of executable task environments and human users. We contribute three simulators that recreate everyday tasks and human-aligned action spaces across cooking, household manipulation, and mobile-interface domains, together with a persona-conditioned user simulation harness that collaborates with the assistant while incorporating controlled execution errors and other out-of-plan behaviors. We instantiate the framework as IVG-Bench, a benchmark with 315 interaction scenarios. Evaluating state-of-the-art VLMs as visual interaction models reveals substantial limitations: the best-performing model, Gemini 4 Argon, completes only 53.4% of tasks within the time limit, exhibits significant weaknesses in factual grounding and actionable guidance, and is often too slow to prevent errors when response latency is considered. We verify our evaluation protocol with a human study which finds 78.5% agreement between our interaction-quality metric and participant preferences. We further show that the environments provide useful learning signals: in a proof-of-concept GRPO experiment, closed-loop training improves both task success and interaction quality for Qwen3.5-4B model in our cooking environment.

llm.title_ja: Interactive Visual Gym: インタラクティブ世界におけるシミュレーションされたユーザーを用いた視覚的インタラクションモデルの評価
llm.tldr_ja: 実行可能なタスク環境と人間のユーザーの共同シミュレーションにより、視覚的インタラクションモデルの閉ループ評価と訓練を行うフレームワークInteractive Visual Gymを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークはオフラインリプレイに依存しており、アシスタントの応答がその後のユーザー行動やタスク結果に与える影響を捉えられないこと。
llm.method: 調理、家庭内操作、モバイルインターフェースのタスク環境と、制御された実行エラーを持つペルソナ条件付きユーザーシミュレーションハーネスの構築。
llm.result: 最先端VLMの評価により、タスク完了率の限界や応答遅延の課題が明らかになり、閉ループ訓練による性能向上の有効性を示した。
keywords_ja: 視覚的インタラクション
ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2611.08286.tldr_en: Interactive Visual Gym is introduced, a framework for closed-loop evaluation and training of visual interaction models through joint simulation of executable task environments and human users, and shows that the environments provide useful learning signals.
2611.08286.hf_summary_en: Interactive Visual Gym enables closed-loop evaluation and training of visual interaction models by jointly simulating task environments and human users, exposing limitations in state-of-the-art VLMs and improving performance through closed-loop training.

2611.08275.title: Aligning Policy Encoders with a Shape Teacher
2611.08275.abstract: 3D-aware representations can improve robotic manipulation by providing geometric information that is robust to changes in viewpoint, object position, and occlusion. However, using 3D inputs at deployment requires additional sensing and processing, making image-based policies more practical. We ask whether an image-based policy can acquire 3D shape information during training while retaining a purely image-based interface at deployment. We propose shape-teacher alignment, a training-time mechanism that uses a pretrained 3D shape representation as an alignment target for an image-based policy encoder. Specifically, we use Point-MAE features from individual objects as targets for corresponding image patches, transferring geometric structure to the policy without changing its deployment inputs or architecture. On LIBERO, shape-teacher alignment produces image representations that are more structured around object shape and corresponding parts, while substantially accelerating policy convergence and improving success rates. For pretrained policies, convergence is accelerated by 4.7x and 5.6x on the Object and Spatial suites, respectively, without requiring the shape teacher or depth input at deployment.

llm.title_ja: ポリシーエンコーダと形状ティーチャーのアライメント
llm.tldr_ja: 画像ベースのポリシーエンコーダの学習時に事前学習済みの3D形状表現をアライメントターゲットとして用いる形状ティーチャーアライメントを提案し、ポリシーの収束と成功率を向上させる。
llm.problem: 3D認識表現はロボット操作に有効だが、デプロイ時に追加のセンシングと処理が必要となり画像ベースポリシーの方が実用的であること。
llm.method: 個々のオブジェクトからのPoint-MAE特徴を対応する画像パッチのターゲットとして利用し、デプロイ時の入力を変更せずに幾何学的構造を転送する訓練手法。
llm.result: LIBEROにおいて、オブジェクト形状と対応部分に焦点を当てた表現を獲得させ、ポリシーの収束を4.7倍〜5.6倍加速し成功率を向上させた。

2611.08275.tldr_en: This work proposes shape-teacher alignment, a training-time mechanism that uses a pretrained 3D shape representation as an alignment target for an image-based policy encoder, substantially accelerating policy convergence and improving success rates on LIBERO.

2611.08259.title: Fault-Geometry-Aware Control Allocation for Emergency Quadrotor Landing under Single-Motor Loss of Effectiveness
2611.08259.abstract: Partial single-motor loss of effectiveness (LoE) changes the remaining control-authority geometry of a quadrotor and can change which control allocator performs best during emergency landing[cite: 11]. We compare three allocators in Crazyflie software-in-the-loop simulation: bounded weighted least squares (reported as PINV), a finite-candidate residual allocator (QP-lite), and the same residual allocator with scoring parameters tuned offline by the Cross-Entropy Method (CEM)[cite: 11]. For this study, fault geometry is represented by the known failed-motor index[cite: 11]. At $η=0.496$ remaining effectiveness, matched development trials select CEM for M1, M3, and M4 and PINV for M2; the M3 selection is a one-trial margin (29/30 versus 28/30)[cite: 11]. After freezing this routing map, the policy achieves 117/120 safe first-contact touchdowns on fresh seeds and 115/120 in a separate randomized-order integrated-supervisor evaluation[cite: 11]. For the critical M2/PINV branch, Firth regression gives a nominal $η_{50}\approx0.4956$ with a within-model 95% bootstrap interval of approximately [0.4955, 0.4956][cite: 11]. One-factor-at-a-time $\pm10\%$ plant perturbations shift $η_{50}$ by up to 0.05495 for thrust coefficient and 0.04974 for mass; the most frequent violated first-contact criterion also changes from vertical speed in many conditions to angular rate for mass -10% and thrust-coefficient +10%[cite: 11]. At fixed $η=0.496$, PINV has a higher M2 safe count than frozen CEM in 9/11 tested plant states and ties in 2/11; the two ties are both 0/30[cite: 11]. The experiments therefore distinguish motor-conditioned allocator selection from sensitivity to plant-model mismatch[cite: 11].

llm.title_ja: 単一モーター効率低下時の緊急クアッドコプター着陸に向けた故障形状を考慮した制御配分
llm.tldr_ja: 単一モーターの効率低下が生じたクアッドコプターの緊急着陸において、残存する制御権の形状に基づいたモーター条件付きのアロケータ選択手法を評価し、プラントモデルの不確実性に対する感度との違いを実証した。
llm.problem: 部分的なモーター効率低下がクアッドコプターの残存制御権の幾何学を変化させ、緊急着陸時の最適な制御配分を変動させる課題。
llm.method: 制約付き重み付き最小二乗法、有限候補残差アロケータ、クロスエントロピー法でチューニングされた残差アロケータの3つをソフトウェアインザループシミュレーションで比較。
llm.result: 固定されたルーティングマップを用いた評価で、新規シードにおいて120回中117回の安全な接地を達成し、モーター条件付きアロケータ選択の有効性を示した。

2611.08259.tldr_en: Three allocators in Crazyflie software-in-the-loop simulation are compared: bounded weighted least squares, a finite-candidate residual allocator (QP-lite), and the same residual allocator with scoring parameters tuned offline by the Cross-Entropy Method.

2611.08209.title: RoboARCade: Benchmarking Agentic Robot Control
2611.08209.abstract: Improvements in multi-modal capabilities have enabled agents to act directly as robot policies, a setting we refer to as agentic robot control (ARC). We introduce RoboARCade, a benchmark of long-horizon manipulation tasks across three embodiments designed to test in-context adaptation, memory, and reasoning for precise control. The tasks build on existing open-source benchmarks, which we make harder by widening the range of initial conditions. RoboARCade is easy to use and extend: all tasks run on a single simulation backend, MuJoCo, each task is a self-contained data pack, and agents connect through interchangeable interfaces, so new tasks, agents, and interfaces can be added independently. The benchmark separates leading agents: GPT-6 Astra achieves 49.8% compared with 43.6% for Claude Fable 5.1, leaving substantial room for improvement. Comparing two interfaces, we find that a richer visual interface adds only 1.5 to 6.8 points at 1.7 to 2.3 times the cost. Failures stem mostly from choosing a poor manipulation strategy or executing a good one imprecisely, rarely from misunderstanding the scene, and agents incorrectly claim success on 24% to 39% of attempted subtasks. Agents can also improve without human input: one successful demonstration in context raises Astra's score from 53.5% to 73.0% on a five-task subset, and a prompt the agent writes and revises itself reaches 72.0%. Code, videos and full traces are available at roboarcade.org.

llm.title_ja: RoboARCade：エージェント型ロボット制御のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: エージェント型ロボット制御（ARC）の評価に向け、初期条件の範囲を広げた長期マニピュレーションタスクのベンチマークRoboARCadeを提案し、主要なマルチモデルエージェントの性能を比較した。
llm.problem: マルチモーダル能力の向上によりロボットポリシーを直接駆動するエージェント型ロボット制御の体系的な評価ベンチマークが不足していること。
llm.method: MuJoCoベースの単一シミュレーション環境上で動作する、3つの実体を持つ長期マニピュレーションタスク群のデータパックと交換可能なインターフェースを構築。
llm.result: GPT-6 Astraが49.8%、Claude Fable 5.1が43.6%を記録し性能差を示したほか、文脈内での1回の成功実演によりAstraのスコアが向上することを確認。

2611.08209.tldr_en: RoboARCade is introduced, a benchmark of long-horizon manipulation tasks across three embodiments designed to test in-context adaptation, memory, and reasoning for precise control of agentic robot control.

2611.08156.title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling
2611.08156.abstract: World-action models adapt pretrained video generators, and vision-language-action models build on pretrained vision-language backbones; both tie policy architecture and inference cost to large transformers designed for generation rather than control. It remains unclear how much these generation-oriented choices affect control. In this work, we introduce Latent Action JEPA (La-JEPA), a compact world-action model whose policy transformer is trained from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder. Following Fast-WAM, La-JEPA learns to predict future features jointly with actions during training and generates only actions at inference. Among policies without embodied pretraining, La-JEPA achieves state-of-the-art performance in clean and randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes and on LIBERO-Plus with correct instructions, while using far fewer parameters than the strongest competing policies. It runs substantially faster than Fast-WAM at comparable performance and outperforms the closest JEPA-based methods, LeapBot-WA and JEPA-WAM, on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0 without their pretrained policy backbones. On four real-robot tasks, its average success is comparable to pi0.5 and above non-embodied-pretrained baselines. Through a design study of the choices behind La-JEPA, we show that JEPA features outperform video VAE latents, most clearly out of distribution, and that training-time future prediction choices significantly impact the policy even when future prediction is skipped at inference. We correct the LIBERO-Plus instructions, as the officially released evaluator corrupts them for most variants, and re-evaluate several strong open baselines. Without a generative pretrained policy backbone, La-JEPA is better and faster than far larger policies, suggesting that robot foundation models may benefit from architectures designed for control rather than inherited from generation.

llm.title_ja: La-JEPA：潜在世界モデルを用いたコンパクトなロボットポリシー
llm.tldr_ja: 生成指向の大型トランスフォーマーとは異なり、事前学習済みV-JEPA 2.1エンコーダの潜在空間内でポリシーをスクラッチから訓練するコンパクトな世界行動モデルLa-JEPAを提案し、優れた性能と高速性を実証した。
llm.problem: 生成指向の既存の動画・視覚言語行動モデルはポリシーのアーキテクチャや推論コストが大きすぎる課題があること。
llm.method: 事前学習済みV-JEPA 2.1エンコーダの潜在空間でポリシーを学習させ、訓練時に将来予測を行いながら推論時は行動のみを生成するLa-JEPAを構築。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0やLIBERO-Plusにおいて既存の競合ポリシーよりもはるかに少ないパラメータ数で最高水準の性能を達成し、実機タスクでもpi0.5と同等の成功率を記録。

2611.08156.tldr_en: It is shown that JEPA features outperform video VAE latents, most clearly out of distribution, and that training-time future prediction choices significantly impact the policy even when future prediction is skipped at inference, suggesting that robot foundation models may benefit from architectures designed for control rather than inherited from generation.

2611.08144.title: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment-Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
2611.08144.abstract: Robot reinforcement learning increasingly runs environments outside the trainer: in another process, on another machine, in another language. Many faults at this boundary raise no error. We make the boundary a wire protocol and ask what notices a fault in it. On Pendulum, HalfCheetah, Hopper and a 7-joint arm (Pusher), we injected up to 23 faults into what crosses the wire and 2 into the trainer's log, from one value to every value. Unless every value was wrong, a learning-curve threshold caught at most one run in ten, and a comparison with ten fault-free seeds at most 21%. A clean evaluation of all 1,060 final policies agreed with the curves: of the 728 boundary-fault runs both curve checks passed, 723 scored no more than three standard deviations below fault-free seeds, though nearly all ended on other weights and, for reward faults, logged other returns. Checks of the run itself, not of its outcome, saw every fault. A step ledger kept on both sides and compared step by step caught and located every fault that crossed, on Pendulum, Hopper and Pusher on one machine and on Pendulum across two, with no fault-free run and, on Pendulum, a median 3% more training time. An episode record kept at the environment caught the faults in the trainer's log. We list such faults found in practice, in Gymnasium 1.3 and our own code and, reported by others, in five multi-agent libraries, and recommend a step ledger and episode counts kept at the environment.
2611.08144.comment: 7 pages, 6 figures, 6 tables. Accepted to the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Everything Beneath the Policy. Code, specification, and every experiment's protocol, logs and findings: https://github.com/PlugRL

llm.title_ja: 強化学習における環境・トレーナー境界でのサイレント故障の検出
llm.tldr_ja: 強化学習の環境とトレーナーの境界でエラーを発生させずに生じるサイレント故障を検出するため、通信プロトコル上にステップ台帳とエピソード記録を導入する手法を提案し、あらゆる通過故障の検出に成功した。
llm.problem: 強化学習において環境が別プロセスや別マシンで実行される際に生じる、エラーを伴わないサイレント故障が従来の学習曲線の閾値では検出しにくいこと。
llm.method: 境界をワイヤプロトコル化し、双方の側で維持・比較されるステップ台帳と環境側でのエピソード記録の保持を導入して故障を検出。
llm.result: Pendulum、Hopper、Pusherを用いた実験で、通過したすべての故障をステップ台帳によって検出・特定できることを実証した。

2611.08144.tldr_en: This work makes the boundary a wire protocol and asks what notices a fault in it, and lists such faults found in practice, in Gymnasium 1.3 and its own code and, reported by others, in five multi-agent libraries, and recommends a step ledger and episode counts kept at the environment.

2611.08142.title: Educational robotics beyond ROS: a custom library for direct transfer of Webots controllers in the Turtlebot3
2611.08142.abstract: Robot Operating System (ROS) is becoming a standard in robotics courses at higher education, but its installation, configuration and distributed programming model can introduce a significant entry barrier in the new landscape of AI-based master and degree studies, where many students do not have a strong informatics background. This paper presents an educational experience that enables students to program a TurtleBot3 Burger directly in Python, while preserving a direct transfer path from simulation to the physical robot. The approach is based on a custom library that mirrors the Webots API, allowing the same controller code to be executed in the simulator and on the real TurtleBot3 with minimal modification. The library provides access to the robot motors, wheel encoders, inertial sensors and LiDAR, and is complemented by scripts that automate deployment and execution on the physical platform. It was used in a master-level course on introductory autonomous vehicles, and initial student feedback suggests that the approach reduces the perceived complexity of ROS-related infrastructure and helps learners focus on algorithmic logic and real-world behaviour.
2611.08142.tldr_en: An educational experience that enables students to program a TurtleBot3 Burger directly in Python, while preserving a direct transfer path from simulation to the physical robot.

2611.08139.title: H-TRIP: Exact Many-to-Many Distance Index for Multi-Robot Exploration
2611.08139.abstract: Frontier-based exploration systems repeatedly evaluate geodesic travel costs between robot poses and candidate viewpoints, and tour-based planners consume the full pairwise distance matrix built from them. Recomputing these matrices with one graph search per source scales with the explored map size, whereas distance caches that refresh only locally affected or newly created frontiers can retain stale costs between surviving pairs when newly discovered free space creates a global shortcut. We present H-TRIP (Hierarchical Tropical Rank-one Incremental Propagation), an exact distance index grounded in Kleene algebra over the min-plus semiring for monotonically growing occupancy grids. H-TRIP partitions the known map into a spatial hierarchy with fixed boundary ports. Each unknown-to-free revelation is decomposed into efficient rank-one min-plus edge insertions at the affected leaf, and only decreased port-to-port summaries are propagated along its ancestor chain. A shared hierarchical lift evaluates the dense many-to-many matrix of shortest distances for all active query points on the occupancy map. We prove that sequential insertions preserve exact shortest-path distances on the grid. Benchmark experiments confirm exact agreement with reference searches on fully built maps and show that dense many-to-many queries at a few dozen viewpoints are up to two orders of magnitude faster than sequential k x BFS. On exploration runs with sixteen robots, in-loop queries on the growing occupancy graph are 2.21x-8.59x faster than co-scheduled k x BFS on maps with side 256, 512, and 1024 cells.

llm.title_ja: H-TRIP：マルチロボット探索のための厳密な多対多距離インデックス
llm.tldr_ja: 単調増加する占有グリッドマップに対し、min-plus半環上のクリーネ代数に基づいた厳密な距離インデックスH-TRIPを提案し、複数の視点間における多くの最短距離クエリを高速化した。
llm.problem: フロンティアベースの探索システムにおける複数視点間の測地旅行コストやペアワイズ距離行列の再計算が、マップサイズの拡大に伴いスケールしないこと。
llm.method: マップを境界ポートを持つ空間階層に分割し、未知領域から自由領域への変化をランク1のmin-plus辺挿入として効率的に処理・伝播するH-TRIPアルゴリズムを設計。
llm.result: ベンチマーク実験により、完全なマップ上の基準検索と完全に一致し、数十の視点での密な多対多クエリが従来の逐次BFSに比べて最大2桁高速化されることを確認。

2611.08139.tldr_en: H-TRIP (Hierarchical Tropical Rank-one Incremental Propagation), an exact distance index grounded in Kleene algebra over the min-plus semiring for monotonically growing occupancy grids, and proves that sequential insertions preserve exact shortest-path distances on the grid.

2611.08119.title: H-BRICK: Hierarchical Boundary Reachability Index with Compressed Kleene Closure for Directed Grid Graphs
2611.08119.abstract: Repeated directed reachability queries arise in online path planning, task-agent allocation, and swarm control on static grid maps, where reachability is asymmetric and full transitive closure is storage-prohibitive. We introduce H-BRICK, a Hierarchical Boundary Reachability Index with Compressed Kleene closure for exact cell-to-cell queries on directed grid graphs. H-BRICK partitions the graph into tiles, computes a local Boolean Kleene closure within each tile, and projects it onto the tile's boundary ports. The resulting directed port-to-port summaries are then composed recursively across shared interfaces up to a single root covering the graph. We prove algebraically that the construction is exact: in the Boolean Kleene algebra of binary relations, every composed summary equals the boundary projection of the regional reflexive transitive closure, and every cell-to-cell query agrees with reachability in the original graph. Experiments on directed grid graphs across diverse map topologies compare H-BRICK against directed search and component-based baselines, and compare its storage requirements against full transitive closure. A batched reachability evaluation further demonstrates that sharing endpoint lifts across many-source/many-target queries amortizes hierarchical traversal and, at k=64, yields a 5.0x-22.9x throughput improvement over the scalar query loop. The results show that hierarchical boundary compression is most advantageous in query-intensive spatial graphs where online search traverses large reachable regions and the hierarchy maintains compact boundary interfaces.

llm.title_ja: H-BRICK：有向グリッドグラフのための圧縮クリーネ閉包を用いた階層型境界到達可能性インデックス
llm.tldr_ja: 静的グリッドマップ上のオンライン経路計画等における非対称な有向到達可能性クエリを高速化するため、空間をタイルに分割し局所的なブール・クリーネ閉包を再帰的に組み合わせるH-BRICKを提案した。
llm.problem: 静的グリッドマップ上での有向到達可能性クエリにおいて、非対称性のため完全な推移閉包の記憶容量が膨大になり処理が困難になること。
llm.method: グラフをタイルに分割して局所的なブール・クリーネ閉包を計算し、境界ポート上に射影して共有インターフェース間で再帰的に合成する階層型インデックス構築手法。
llm.result: 多様なマップトポロジーでの実験において、バッチ処理された到達可能性評価により従来のスカラ式クエリーループと比較して5.0倍から22.9倍のスループット向上を達成。

2611.08119.tldr_en: The results show that hierarchical Boundary Reachability Index with Compressed Kleene closure is most advantageous in query-intensive spatial graphs where online search traverses large reachable regions and the hierarchy maintains compact boundary interfaces.

2611.08111.title: Reinforcing End-to-End Autonomous Driving Safety via Negative-Aware Planning in a Unified World-Action Model
2611.08111.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) jointly model future traffic states and driving actions for end-to-end autonomous driving in intelligent transportation systems. However, their action learning remains dominated by expert-trajectory imitation, leaving unsafe alternatives close to expert trajectories insufficiently constrained. To improve WAM robustness in safety-critical scenarios, we propose NegWAM, a safety post-training framework for unified WAMs that learns explicit safety boundaries from near-expert failure trajectories. NegWAM constructs negative trajectories that are geometrically close to the expert trajectory yet carry safety risks, uses them as repulsive anchors to steer predictions away from dangerous behavior, and encodes them as scene-conditioned rider tokens to learn scene--trajectory compatibility. During training, NegWAM jointly optimizes the flow-matching and near-expert negative objectives, while the auxiliary rider branch is discarded at inference, incurring no additional overhead. On NAVSIM v2, NegWAM achieves 40.4 EPDMS on navhard, a 4.1% relative improvement over the strongest compared scorer-free WAM baseline, and achieves 93.3 EPDMS on navtest. These results demonstrate that NegWAM achieves strong performance in safety-critical scenarios while preserving routine-driving performance. Zero-shot closed-loop evaluation on HUGSIM further demonstrates cross-benchmark generalization. The code is available at https://github.com/Zizizi-hao/NegWAM.

llm.title_ja: 統合世界行動モデルにおけるネガティブアウェア計画を通じたエンドツーエンド自動運転の安全性強化
llm.tldr_ja: 自動運転向け世界行動モデルの安全性を向上させるため、専門家の失敗軌跡から得られた近接失敗例を反発アンカーとして明示的な安全境界を学習するポストトレーニングフレームワークNegWAMを提案した。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデルの行動学習が専門家の軌跡模倣に依存しており、専門家軌跡に近い不安全な代替案に対する制約が不十分であること。
llm.method: 専門家に近いが安全リスクを伴うネガティブ軌跡を構築し、それらを反発アンカーとして予測を危険な行動から遠ざけつつシーンと軌跡の適合性を学習するNegWAMを設計。
llm.result: NAVSIM v2のnavhardで40.4 EPDMSを達成し既存の最強ベースラインに対して4.1%の相対的改善を示し、通常運転性能を維持しつつ安全性を向上させた。

2611.08111.tldr_en: NegWAM, a safety post-training framework for unified WAMs that learns explicit safety boundaries from near-expert failure trajectories, is proposed, demonstrating that NegWAM achieves strong performance in safety-critical scenarios while preserving routine-driving performance.

2611.08100.title: An Integrated Open-Source Stack for Vision-Based Autonomous Navigation of Wheeled Rovers
2611.08100.abstract: Vision-based rover autonomy requires integrating perception, localization, planning and platform-specific control under limited sensing and computing resources. We present an open-source ROS 2 stack for following directional arrows, reaching a terminal cone and returning autonomously to the start. It connects YOLOv8n detection and geometric direction, range and bearing estimation with RGB-D SLAM, wheel-inertial state estimation, kinematics-aware planning, behavior-tree mission management and STM32 actuation. Standard interfaces separate reusable autonomy from the hardware layer; a proportional path-following plugin supports low-speed rover motion. Public resources include software, configuration, a labeled dataset, trained weights and evaluation logs. On 478 held-out images, the detector achieves mAP@0.5 of 0.720 under the Ultralytics evaluator and outperforms a classical OpenCV baseline under a shared evaluation protocol. The reported perception latency is 25 ms on a Jetson Orin NX. Three missions, one indoor and two outdoor, demonstrate marker-guided navigation and autonomous return without operator motion commands or reported collisions. Field results document integration failures and corrective choices; repeated instrumented trials remain necessary to quantify physical navigation errors and reliability.

llm.title_ja: 車輪型ローバーのビジョンベース自律ナビゲーションのための統合オープンソース・スタック
llm.tldr_ja: 限られた計算・センシング資源の下で矢印追従や終端コーンへの到達、自律帰還を行う車輪型ローバー向けに、知覚・局所化・計画・制御を統合したROS 2オープンソーススタックを開発した。
llm.problem: ビジョンベースのローバー自律移動において、知覚・局所化・計画・プラットフォーム制御を限られたリソースで統合する必要があること。
llm.method: YOLOv8nによる検出・幾何学的推定とRGB-D SLAM、車輪慣性状態推定、運動学を考慮した計画、振る舞いツリーによるミッション管理をROS 2上で統合。
llm.result: 478枚のホールドアウト画像でmAP@0.5が0.720を達成し、屋内および屋外の実ミッションにおいてマーカー誘導ナビゲーションと衝突なき自律帰還を実証。
llm.limitation: 物理的なナビゲーション誤差や信頼性を定量化するために反復的な実機検証が必要である点。
keywords_ja: ビジョンベースナビゲーション

2611.08100.tldr_en: An open-source ROS 2 stack for following directional arrows, reaching a terminal cone and returning autonomously to the start, which connects YOLOv8n detection and geometric direction, range and bearing estimation with RGB-D SLAM, wheel-inertial state estimation, kinematics-aware planning, behavior-tree mission management and STM32 actuation.

2611.08097.title: STEP: Spatiotemporal Training with Explicit Prediction for Perceptive Humanoid Locomotion
2611.08097.abstract: For perceptive humanoid locomotion, the relevance of terrain geometry depends on the robot's body state and how both evolve under its actions. Existing work has advanced terrain-aware sensory fusion and cross-modal prediction, improving how visual and proprioceptive information is combined and related. However, feature aggregation alone does not specify which cross-modal relationships should be learned, while prediction between simultaneous observations does not explicitly constrain their action-dependent evolution. We present Spatiotemporal Training with Explicit Prediction (STEP), a one-stage framework that jointly supervises cross-modal relationships and action-dependent state evolution within a shared control representation. Multiple learned queries aggregate depth and proprioceptive tokens into a compact policy state. Bidirectional masked prediction uses each visible modality to predict latent features of the omitted modality, explicitly supervising terrain-body relationships. An action-conditioned predictor maps the current policy state and executed action to the next fused state, with an exponential-moving-average target defined directly in the policy representation space. Simulation comparisons show overall improvements in terrain traversal over evaluated fusion alternatives and ablations, while depth-dropout and delay experiments demonstrate the benefits of both predictive objectives under degraded visual input. Deployed on a 23-DoF Noetix E1 humanoid with onboard sensing, STEP succeeds in 98 of 100 hardware trials across stairs, a 40\,cm platform, a 70\,cm gap, stepping stones, and backward stair traversal without rearward terrain visibility.

llm.title_ja: STEP：知覚的ヒューマノイド歩行のための明示的予測を伴う時空間トレーニング
llm.tldr_ja: 知覚的ヒューマノイド歩行において、クロスモダリティの関係性と行動に依存した状態進化を共通の制御表現内で同時に監督する1ステージのフレームワークSTEPを提案し、実機での優れた不整地走破性を実証した。
llm.problem: 不整地歩行において単なる特徴集約では学習すべきクロスモダリティの関係が指定されず、同時観測間の予測では行動依存の進化が明示的に制約されないこと。
llm.method: 深さと固有感覚のトークンを統合する学習済みクエリを用い、双方向のマスク予測と行動条件付き予測器によって地形と身体の関係性および状態進化を同時に監督するSTEPを構築。
llm.result: 23自由度のNoetix E1ヒューマノイドを用いた実機実験において、階段や段差、ギャップなど100試行中98試行で走破に成功。

2611.08097.tldr_en: Spatiotemporal Training with Explicit Prediction (STEP), a one-stage framework that jointly supervises cross-modal relationships and action-dependent state evolution within a shared control representation, is presented.

2611.08075.title: Leave It Better Than Found: Value-Guided Cooperation in Sequential Tasks
2611.08075.abstract: We consider the problem of sequential task continuation, where one robot acts in a workspace that has been affected by a previous robot.
